body:
Closes #153, closes #159, closes #89. Three independent issues batched on one branch; no shared files between them apart from `tests/unit/ui-button.test.tsx` (#159 only) and `Makefile` (#89 only). ## #153 — optional props spell `| undefined` Consumers compiling with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (`website` does) could not pass a `T | undefined` value into a prop declared `foo?: T`. Every optional member of an exported interface or type alias under `src/components` (156 members across 36 files, including the MUI theme augmentations in `types.d.ts`) now reads `foo?: T | undefined`. Two `onChange?: (v) => void | undefined` handlers, which had the `undefined` on the return type, are corrected to `((v) => void) | undefined`. `tests/unit/optional-props-accept-undefined.test.ts` is the drift guard: it walks `src/components` with the TypeScript compiler API and fails for the first optional member of an exported declaration that lacks `undefined`. Internal, non-exported shapes (a MUI-facing `slotProps` object type, say) are out of scope on purpose — they must match MUI's own `foo?: T` signatures — and the guard proves its own matcher against the type forms the codebase uses. ## #159 — bordered pills share the filled pill's box Measured in Storybook before / after, against the Figma frames: | Pill | Figma | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `outlined` / `small` (439:19257) | 137×50 | 52 tall | **50** | | `name="danger"` (439:19822) | 98×42 | 44 tall | **42** (97.9 wide with the story label) | | `name="socialButton"` (439:19329) | 189×58 | 56 tall | **58** | | `outlined` / `medium` (439:19253) | 171×62 | 62 (fixed in #137) | 62, unchanged | Each bordered rule now spends 1px of the Figma inset on the border and the rest on padding (15/23, 11/23, 17), the same compensation the medium CTA, `ui-add-button`, `ui-filter-chip`, `ui-task-card` and `ui-integration-card` already apply. The social button also declares the 22px line box its 18px DemiBold label measures in Figma instead of the small button's 18px. The shared outlined preset and the social button keep a transparent 1px border when disabled so the box cannot jitter between states; the unit tier pins the arithmetic for all three pills the way it already did for the medium CTA. Eleven chromium baselines regenerated in the pinned Playwright image: the outlined small button's hover/active/focus states and story (the disabled shot is byte-identical), the danger pill's four states and story, the social button story, and the Figma-parity board that hosts the danger tiles. ## #89 — ESLint complexity backstop; lint fails on warnings - `eslint.config.mjs` mirrors the RCA hard policy at looser thresholds for `src/**` and `scripts/**`: `complexity 12`, `max-lines-per-function 60`, `max-lines 400`, `max-depth 4`, `max-params 3`. Zero existing violations in `src` (the RCA gate already enforces tighter numbers); `scripts/**` had been globally ignored and is linted again — three 4-parameter functions and two import-group gaps fixed, `no-console` allowed there as for the k6 scripts, `scripts/**` added to the devDependency importers. - `react/jsx-no-bind`, `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` and `no-await-in-loop` are errors. The three `src` sites are fixed rather than disabled: `use-copied-latch` routes the cleanup's `timer.current` read through a stable callback (the cleanup has to clear whichever reset is armed *at* unmount), `ui-text-field-form` composes the RHF + consumer handlers in a memoised `ControlledInput`, and the items-list story gives each accordion row its own `useCallback`. `jsx-no-bind` is off for test files — a test's inline handler renders once and has no consumer. - `no-restricted-syntax` (the `*ByTestId` nudge in tests) is an error too; the 29 sites were all mock stand-ins, which now carry real semantics (`swiper-mock` is an APG carousel region with slide groups, the card mocks are `
`/`
` landmarks) and are queried by role. - `import/prefer-default-export` is off: named exports through per-component barrels are this package's export contract (`export-contract-integrity.test.ts`), so 52 stylistic warnings were noise. - `make lint-next` runs `eslint --max-warnings 0` and also lints `*.mjs`. Bats: the existing `lint-next` test asserts the flag; `tests/bats/eslint_complexity_backstop.bats` writes an 80-statement / 4-param / 5-deep / 13-branch fixture under `src/`, runs the real ESLint, and asserts every backstop rule fires (and that a within-policy function passes, and that the thresholds sit above `config/metrics-policy.json`). ## Triage notes - #152 and #155 were closed as superseded: both are already on `main` (case-folded `target`, exported `Ui*Props`, no bare `Golos`) — see the closing comments. - `tests/bats/unused_dependency_gate.bats:403` fails on a host that has `/usr/bin/git` (it assumes the git-less bun image); pre-existing and unrelated. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_018dqdFKN5j7iJP4V1QufaWo --- ## Summary by cubic Batches three independent fixes: optional component props now accept `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, bordered pill buttons render at their Figma height, and ESLint blocks complexity regressions so `make lint-next` fails on warnings. **Bug Fixes** - All 156 optional members of exported types under `src/components` now spell `| undefined`; author: karol-blaszczyk
body:
`PRIVACY.md` names **OpenRunner** as one of the LLM sub-processors that receives memory content. It is not one, and never was.

Checked across every `.py`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.yaml`, `.env*` and `.toml` in the platform: zero hits. No client, no base URL, no API key in any environment. The entry on the public sub-processor list came from an early drafting note listing inference candidates, and a docs PR removing it is what surfaced this.

## Where it came from

I added it on 11 September, in the same pass that corrected three other privacy claims — encryption being opt-in, delete being a soft delete, and the fact that the service does use LLM sub-processors — each by checking the backend. For this one I read the published sub-processor list instead of the code. It is the only claim in that pass I sourced from a page, and it is the one that was wrong.

## What it says now

Names **Groq**, which is what the code shows on these paths (`compression_pipeline.py`, `user_context_service.py`), and points at the [sub-processor list](https://docs.sekondbrain.ai/subprocessors/) as the authoritative record rather than restating a snapshot of it — a copy of a list is a copy that goes stale, which is exactly what happened here.

Verified: no remaining mention of OpenRunner anywhere in the repo, `check.sh` passes, 85 tests.

This matters more than a normal docs fix because the repo is public and the plugin is going to the Claude directory, where the privacy disclosure is a review criterion.

author: p-tite-tete
body:
Same family as #40394 and #40396, both merged yesterday. This one is the VAT declaration payment page, and it has no access check at all.

## The defect

`htdocs/compta/paiement_vat.php` contains **zero** `restrictedArea()` or `accessforbidden()` call — on 18.0, 21.0, 22.0, 23.0, 24.0 and develop, checked on each branch. `main.inc.php` only checks that a session exists.

**Read.** `if ($action == 'create')` does `$tva->fetch($chid)` and displays the amount, the label, the payment mode and the bank account of the declaration. `Tva::fetch()` selects `WHERE rowid = <id>` with no entity filter, and the page tests no right whatsoever before displaying. So any authenticated user — including an external portal user — reads any VAT declaration by changing `id` in the URL. This is the company's tax data, and unlike the supplier invoice case in #40394 it does not even require a right on another module to reach.

**Write.** The payment action is gated by `$permissiontoadd = $user->hasRight('tax', 'charges', 'creer')`, but by nothing else: a user holding that right can record a payment against a declaration of another entity and close it with `closepaidvat`.

## The change

The call `compta/tva/card.php` already makes on the declaration itself, line 105:

```php
restrictedArea($user, 'tax', $object->id, 'tva', 'charges');
```

placed after `$chid` is resolved and before the actions section, so it covers the display as well as the write.

## Scope

Targeting 24.0 following your guidance on #40394. The file has no guard on any branch from 18.0 up, so tell me if you would rather have it lower and I will redo it — forward merges will not carry it down.

body:
## Summary

Migrate InvestigationContinuityPanel from legacy MovablePanel/CanvasTexture to SpatialPanel + @pmndrs/uikit while preserving InvestigationContinuityController authority, action enablement, save/checkpoint/recover semantics, and explicit portable-file open/export behavior.

## Programme / finding

P1-UXR / UXR1 interaction and UI substrate de-customisation, following #720-#736.

## Risk surface

- [ ] Analytical / statistical correctness
- [ ] Rust ↔ WASM ↔ TypeScript boundary
- [x] Dataset ingest, identity, serialization, or reproducibility
- [x] WebXR / VR interaction or spatial UI
- [ ] Rendering performance or large-dataset performance
- [x] Security, privacy, permissions, or untrusted input
- [ ] Build, CI, deployment, dependencies, or supply chain
- [x] Documentation / engineering governance
- [ ] None of the above

Primary failure modes: disabled restore/recovery actions become invokable, the UI mutates continuity state directly, busy-state double actions race the controller, file-open cancellation mutates the active investigation, or export/open semantics diverge from desktop continuity.

## Adversarial implementation contract

- [x] **High-risk change:** recovery and portable-investigation boundaries are affected.
- [ ] **Standard-risk change:** behavior changes without crossing a high-risk authority/evidence boundary.
- [ ] **Low-risk exemption:** purely editorial/mechanical.

### High-risk pre-implementation adversarial contract

- **Invariant:** InvestigationContinuityController remains the sole authority for save/checkpoint/restore/recovery/export/open operations; the panel may only request actions and present status.
- **Authority / production path:** UIKit button -> activate(action) -> InvestigationContinuityController method -> existing continuity/recovery path.
- **Primary failure modes:** disabled actions dispatched anyway; direct archive/autosave mutation in UI; concurrent action races; cancelled file picker changes the active investigation; open/export action bypasses controller validation.
- **Falsifying evidence:** disabled-action regression, shared-controller XR continuity test, session roundtrip, WorldUIManager integration, and full production build.
- **Non-goals / dependencies:** no continuity-controller implementation change, no persistence schema change, no new durability claim, no bypass of portable package verification.

## Architecture governance

- [x] Existing continuity authority ownership is preserved; UIKit is presentation and dispatch only.
- [ ] An existing ADR governs this change.
- [ ] This change requires/implements an RFC or new ADR.

## Focused verification

- [x] Typecheck / compile checks relevant to changed code
- [x] Focused affected tests
- [x] Production build
- [x] WorldUIManager / session-roundtrip / panel-layout integration
- [ ] Physical Quest smoke for this surface
- [ ] Benchmark/performance evidence when a hot path materially changed

Exact checks:
- npx vitest run tests/pt5d-continuity-ui.test.ts tests/world-ui-manager.test.ts tests/session-roundtrip.test.ts tests/panel-layout.test.ts -> 48 passed
- npm run typecheck -> passed
- npm run build -> passed
- npx eslint src/vr/ui/InvestigationContinuityPanel.ts tests/pt5d-continuity-ui.test.ts -> passed
- git diff --check -> passed

## Correctness evidence

InvestigationContinuityPanel no longer imports or extends MovablePanel. Button enablement is projected from continuity summary/busy state. activate() rejects missing/disabled actions before dispatch. Save/checkpoint/restore/recover/export/open operations all remain delegated to InvestigationContinuityController. File-open cancellation only updates human-readable status and never invokes openPortable.

## Post-implementation adversarial review

**Exact reviewed head:** 8c408aed5f31bb99cf9f7882bb8e06652b9e0789

author: kvnlng
body:
## Summary

Two remediation-pass defects, fixed in one PR because the second depends on the first.

- **#569. SHIFT_DATE re-created a date that was gone or changed.** The arm shifted the value recorded at `audit()` and wrote it back whatever the target now held. That covered a deleted tag (re-created and exported), a blanked or edited value (overwritten), a deleted nested item attribute, and a Study whose `study_date` was set to None. The arm now checks the live target first. It shifts only when the target still holds the audited original, or already holds the shifted value, which is the re-run case. Otherwise it declines with a `REMEDIATION_DECLINED` row that names the tag and carries no value, logs a WARNING, and D's statuses demote the entity.
- **#576. A mixed REMOVE/REPLACE chain inflated the owner row's fold count.** `_foldable_instance_findings` deduplicated on `(uid, path, attr, removed)`, but the apply loop deduplicates on `_remediation_key`, which has no action in it. The owner row could therefore claim "1 instance-level finding on this tag folded into it" over a pass that folded none. The count now follows the loop's key. A value copy counts when the key's first finding is not a REMOVE. A removed copy counts when any finding on the key is a REMOVE, because every non-REMOVE before it declines on the absent copy: #547 for REPLACE, and #569 for SHIFT. **Only row text changes.**

Fixes #569
Fixes #576

## Review round 1 (on e52ead4), addressed in bfc1dd4

The branch is rebased onto d721141, through 619e0b7 (#615) and then #606. Each time the only conflict was in `mutation_probe.py` TARGETS, and both sides were kept. The CHANGELOG and `remediation.py` hunks merged cleanly. After the rebase the five `mark_modified` pins sit at 291/382/432/453/461, and the citation and invariants tests pass.

- **F1: a reused report re-created a removed private date, and it was exported.** The #569 guard already closed this; round 1 pins it.
  - **Shape.** JPEG2000.dcm with the default private-tag removal and `0009,1042` under JITTER. REMOVE and SHIFT share one key, and `anonymize(report)` runs twice.
  - **Killer.** `test_a_private_date_the_first_call_removed_is_not_recreated_by_the_second[threads|processes]`, end to end through export. It is red on 57400d1: the tag is back after the second call (`dev-E3/r2_f1_red_base_312.log`). It is also red on head with the guard call deleted (m1-F1-only). CHANGELOG sub-bullet added under #569.
- **F2(a): a REMOVE that raises on a value copy.** **Docstring only, not restored.**
  - **Why not restored.** Before the pass, owner REPLACE plus instance `[REMOVE (will raise), REPLACE]` has exactly the same inputs as #576's own case, owner REPLACE plus `[REMOVE (will apply), REPLACE]`. The first folds 1 and the second folds 0. Counting the raise case again is the #576 over-claim.
  - **What changed.** The docstring now states the one-row under-claim, and that 57400d1 counted it. It uses the reviewer's text plus one sentence on why it is not restored.
- **F2(b): two entities sharing a UID.** Docstring only, and the inline "as the loop's is" is corrected. Behaviour is unchanged from base, so there is no killer. Mutant R8 (the copy taken from the last finding) stays unpinned on purpose, because pinning it would pin an under-claim.
- **F3.**
  - **R1** (Study `present = True`) is killed by `test_a_study_date_cleared_after_the_audit_is_not_recreated`, which now asserts "is no longer on the Study".
  - **R3b** (the `is None` exemption dropped) is killed by the new `test_a_shift_built_with_no_original_writes_no_row`: `applied == 0`, no rows, value unchanged.
- **P4:** the audited Study value is now `normalize_study_date(str(value).strip())`, a one-line change. Killer: the new `test_a_padded_study_date_is_the_date_the_study_holds`, red on head before the change.
- **P5:** the item branch now reads `present = entity.attributes.get(attr) is not None`, a one-line change. Killer: the new `test_a_date_key_holding_none_is_no_longer_on_the_item`, red on head before the change.
- **P8:** the CHANGELOG and T5 docstring now say "on 3.12 in threads and processes, and on 3.14t for the deleted case".
- **P1, P2 and P6** are being filed by the coordinator. **P3 and P7** are noted only.

## Step-0 addendum findings (57400d1)

The designs still fit, so there was no stop. Full addendum: `.agent/scratch-098/brief-E3-addendum.md`.

- **#569 premise.** Reproduced on 3.12.14, threads and processes, for all five variants (deleted, blank, edited, nested, study None). Reproduced on 3.14.7t for deleted/threads. Before the fix, every variant ended with a `REMEDIATION_SHIFT_DATE` row, a remediated status and a shifted export.
- **Re-runs.** `anonymize(report)` twice was idempotent before and is idempotent after.
- **Ordinary path.** On ten files, 13 shifts (floor) and 42 shifts (jitter-all) had 0 targets absent or differing, so the guard never fires there.
- **#576 premise.** 4 of 28 patient cases and 27 of 117 study cases were wrong.
- **`__remediated__` record (#574).** SHIFT records through `record_date_shift`. A decline returns before that call and before W3, so it records nothing and writes nothing, which is accurate. #576 changes no write, so W1-W3 are untouched. T6 asserts that the record vouches for the copy in every case.
- **D (#577).** A decline goes through `_record_decline`, so `_declined_entities` feeds `_settle_statuses`. The key is not in `processed_entities`, `folded_keys` or `_satisfied_keys`, so the tally settles False. It is a decline, not `_satisfied`, because the end state is not present. #576 does not touch the tally.

## Design notes and deviations from the brief

1. **A blank original passes the guard.** Brief §3.9 called "absent target with an empty original" a decline. That turned `test_declined_remediation_is_recorded.py::test_an_empty_date_is_not_a_decline` red, because that test pins no row for an empty date. The arm's existing empty-date branch is unchanged: it returns a bare `False` with no row, which is the one exception review-D sanctioned. Nothing can be re-created from a blank. This is m10, killed by that test, which is unedited.
2. **Study comparison uses `normalize_study_date`, not `format_study_date`.** `Study.__setattr__` stores values through `normalize_study_date`, so an ISO-spelled original (`2004-01-19`) is the same date. `format_study_date` would falsely decline it (m7).
3. **Item lookup uses `_canonical_tag`.** `set_attr` lowercases, so a hand-built `0008,002A` is the tag the item holds (m6).
4. **The helper logs the WARNING itself.** An in-arm log line would break the #310 line budget. The text is `Date shift declined for <subject>: <reason>`, and the reason names only the tag and the entity type.
5. **An unparseable original on a deleted target declines as "is no longer on".** It no longer claims "invalid date format ... unchanged" about a value that is not there (m9, new test).
6. **Line budget.** The five `mark_modified` pins stay at 291/382/432/453/461. The +4 guard lines are paid for above 382 by rejoining the unresolvable-PatientID `logger.warning`/`_record_decline` calls, whose text is byte-identical. `# Deterministic Date Shifting` was kept, not deleted as the brief proposed.
7. **The #576-on-#569 dependency is 7 study cases, not 20.** With the new count and the guard removed, 7 cases fail (n4). The 20 is "#569 alone with the old count".
8. **`scripts/mutation_probe.py` TARGETS.** T5 is added to the privacy, remediation, session and entities rows. T6 is added to privacy, remediation and entities.

**Residual, stated in the `_foldable_instance_findings` docstring, not fixed.** A finding that *raises* claims no key, the same as a decline.

**Pre-existing observation, not filed.** In the `study_date = None` case the Study declines and the instance's own 0008,0020 finding still shifts its copy. Export then stamps `StudyDate=''` from the Study, per the #492/#189 design. Before this PR it exported a shift of the aud

author: monglong0214
body:
Release 1.3.15. `stale` reported two references as dangling that point at records declared in the very same block.

## The reported symptom is real; the reported mechanism is not

The issue diagnosed `stale` re-reading its own output out of a fenced code block in a commit message. Three checks say otherwise:

1. Every `Follows` value stored in the index is a clean id — none carries prose.
2. `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:only,unfold)'` on the quoted commit yields nothing from that block.
3. `r-238475016983  want an existing Record-Id in history` is not a trailer value. It is the report's own column layout, `Follows: <value>  want <text>`.

Both suspected ids were declared and reachable, exactly as the issue said. So the symptom needed a different explanation.

## Every `Record-Id` in a block is a declaration

`findDanglingRefs` built its declared set with `trailerValue`, which returns **one** value per key per record. A record here is a *block*, and a block carries several declarations whenever squash inheritance writes each preserved record's trailers with no blank line between them — git folds the lot into a single trailer block.

```
055ac9e4  blk0 : 16 Record-Ids   (Follows: r-238475016983 → the 4th)
e44f621c  blk0 :  3 Record-Ids   (Follows: r-aab1c91aacf4 → the 2nd)
```

**The asymmetry is what made it certain.** `e44f621c` carries two `Follows:` lines in one block:

| reference | position of the id | result |
|---|---|---|
| `Follows: r-3d106dced1f0` | the **first** id | resolves |
| `Follows: r-aab1c91aacf4` | the **second** id | dangling |

Same message, same block, same scan. Only position separated them, which is the signature of reading one value where there are several.

`declaredAnywhere` — the fallback for a truncated window — already collected every trailer this way. The complete-scan path was the wrong one, which is why it survived: the repair written for a partial scan was correct, and nobody asked the same question of the whole scan.

## Both suggestions in the issue were considered and neither applied

- **Skip trailer-shaped lines inside fenced code blocks.** Measured: git's trailer atom already yields nothing from that block, so the rule would guard a path nothing takes while moving a boundary git owns (SPEC §2.1 B3).
- **Refuse a `Follows:` value that does not match the id grammar.** `findDanglingRefs` already skips those (`RECORD_ID_RE`), and `validateRecord` reports them as `format`. Reporting one line under two rules makes the repair loop chase it twice. A test now pins that this stays as it is.

## What is deliberately left open

The same one-id-per-record assumption lives in the lifecycle fold, and that half is untouched:

```
commit-sourced distinct Record-Ids   52
stale totalRecords                   32
blocks carrying >1 Record-Id          7   (16, 8, 4, 4, 3, ...)
```

About twenty records have no lifecycle at all — they cannot be reported superseded, expired, or for review. Fixing it means either splitting a block at each `Record-Id` or making squash inheritance separate its blocks, and SPEC states neither. That is a decision, not a repair, so it is filed rather than guessed at.

Closes #1012

## Verification

- Reproduced as a unit case: a reference to the second id in a block is reported, one to the first is not.
- After the change, `commitlore stale` on the reporting repository reports no dangling refs where it reported two.
- 3 of the 5 new cases fail with the collection reverted. The other two are controls — an undeclared id is still caught, and a malformed value is still left to the `format` rule.
- 198 test files, 4,323 tests, 4 skipped; typecheck clean.
- Source only. `dist/` and `installer/canonical-artifact.json` are left to the canonical rebuild.

body:
## 🤖 AI-Submitted Pull Request

This PR was **created and submitted by AI**. A human did not manually write or submit this PR.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Submitted by** | `hos-worker-hos[bot]` |
| **Model** | `claude-sonnet-5` |
| **Submitted** | 2026-09-14 |
| **Human review required** | yes — overseer reviews; human authorization required for MEDIUM+ risk |

## Summary

Implements #1340: a release-scoped execution mode on the existing panel engine (`run_panel.sh --release-range <base>..<head>`), plus a thin entry point (`scripts/run_release_panel.sh`) that owns range derivation, the verdict contract, and `--verify` — which recomputes head SHA, base SHA, exclusion-file hash, and post-exclusion file digest against a posted verdict rather than trusting it outright.

This PR (ADR-1340 PR 1) is **deliberately inert**: nothing in the repository invokes the new suite yet. A follow-up PR arms `worker.md`'s R2 after a real execution produces a verdict `--verify` accepts. Full design rationale, rejected alternatives, and residual gaps are in the DECISIONS.md entry this PR adds.

## Review history (this PR went through two rounds of adversarial security review before being opened)

- code-reviewer: approved, no blocking findings (two non-blocking suggestions filed for follow-up).
- security-reviewer (round 1): found a **HIGH** finding — `select_verdict`'s tie-break trusted a self-reported `completed_at` field from inside the verdict JSON payload rather than the comment's GitHub-authenticated `created_at`, and nothing rejected a comment containing more than one verdict marker. Combined, this allowed a forged verdict block (planted via injected free text in the same bot comment as a genuine verdict — an LLM-reviewer-echo injection vector) to win selection and pass all `--verify` checks, without needing the worker's bot token.
- Fix applied: `extract_verdicts` now refuses any comment with more than one marker outright; `select_verdict` ties-break only on GitHub's authenticated `created_at`. Regression tests added (`test_ts5b`, `test_ts5c`, `test_ts6b`, and an end-to-end `test_ts3b` through the real `--verify` CLI).
- security-reviewer (round 2, targeted re-verification): confirmed the fix closes the finding, attempted several bypasses (author-filter evasion, multi-comment splitting, marker mimicry, off-by-one), all closed. **APPROVED.**

body:
## Objetivo

Corrige o fluxo de bloqueio de sites para manter o navegador aberto e redirecionar o site bloqueado para o Google na mesma aba.

## Novo fluxo

1. Ao detectar um site bloqueado, a cortina de bloqueio entra imediatamente.
2. A cortina permanece visível por no mínimo 1 segundo.
3. Enquanto a cortina está por cima, o serviço tenta substituir a URL da aba atual por `https://www.google.com` e submetê-la na mesma janela do navegador.
4. A edição e a submissão da barra de endereço agora toleram pequenos atrasos da UI, com tentativas curtas e limitadas.
5. O fluxo não fecha mais a aba e não manda o navegador para HOME como fallback.
6. Se a reescrita na mesma aba não puder ser confirmada, o navegador permanece aberto; o próximo evento do site bloqueado pode iniciar nova tentativa.

## Segurança do fluxo

- A reescrita continua vinculada ao pacote e ao `windowId` exatos detectados.
- Antes de tocar na barra, o serviço ainda confirma que a janela mostra o alvo bloqueado detectado.
- Depois que a barra é ativada, eventos normais gerados pelo próprio editor do navegador não invalidam mais a tentativa prematuramente.
- Nenhum `ACTION_VIEW` genérico foi reintroduzido, pois isso poderia abrir outra aba.

## Testes

Atualiza `WebsiteBlockNavigationTest` para cobrir:
- cortina mínima de 1 segundo;
- tolerância a eventos de UI na mesma janela durante edição/submissão;
- falha de sanitização sem fechamento/saída do navegador;
- ausência de ação `EVACUATE_HOME` na máquina de transição de sites.

## ปัญหา

ในฟอร์มแก้ไขเมนู ส่วน "อยู่ในหมวดเพิ่มเติม" ชื่อหมวดถูกบีบจนเหลือบรรทัดละตัวอักษร อ่านไม่ออกทั้งหน้า

ต้นเหตุอยู่ที่ `src/components/admin/Admin.css` — กฎ `.admin-form-group input { width: 100% }` ตั้งใจไว้สำหรับช่องกรอกข้อความ แต่ไปโดน `input[type="checkbox"]` ด้วย ช่องติ๊กจึงกว้างเท่ากล่องทั้งใบและไม่ยอมหด บีบข้อความข้าง ๆ จนแทบไม่เหลือที่

(PR ก่อนหน้าแก้ด้วยการจัดกริดใหม่ ซึ่งไม่ได้แตะต้นเหตุ อาการจึงยังอยู่)

## วิธีแก้

**1. หมวดเพิ่มเติมเปลี่ยนเป็น dropdown** (`ManageMenu.jsx`)

- เลือกทีละหมวดจาก dropdown — หมวดหลักและหมวดที่เลือกไปแล้วจะไม่โผล่ในรายการซ้ำ
- หมวดที่เลือกแล้วแสดงเป็นป้าย กดกากบาทเอาออกได้
- ชื่อหมวดยาวแค่ไหนก็อ่านออกเต็ม ๆ และเห็นทันทีว่าตอนนี้เลือกอะไรไว้บ้าง
- ยังไม่เลือกอะไรจะมีข้อความบอกว่าเมนูนี้จะขึ้นเฉพาะหมวดหลัก

**2. แก้ต้นเหตุที่ CSS** (`Admin.css`)

ยกเว้น `input[type="checkbox"]` และ `input[type="radio"]` จากกฎความกว้าง 100% — แก้ช่องติ๊กอีก 8 จุดในหน้าจัดการเมนูและหมวดหมู่ที่โดนปัญหาเดียวกันไปด้วย

author: canelamoraguezandyjesus-bot
body:
Cierra la incidencia #632. **Esto desbloquea el motor**: sin este cambio,
ninguna decisión nueva puede fusionarse.

## El hecho

La guarda de ADR-171 se puso en rojo al regenerar `MEMORIA.md`:

```
AssertionError: MEMORIA.md pesa 120207 bytes: por encima de 120000 deja de
leerse entera de una vez y vuelve a ser un corpus (ADR-171, criterio (c))
```

**No fue culpa del cambio que la destapó.** Sobre `main` el fichero pesaba ya
**119.370 bytes**: quedaban **630** de margen. Y cada ADR fusionado añade, medido
sobre las cinco fusiones de esta misma noche, **unos 1.350 bytes**:

| Fusión | `MEMORIA.md` | Crecimiento |
|---|---|---|
| ADR-191 | 113.969 | — |
| ADR-192 | 115.170 | +1.201 |
| ADR-190 | 116.766 | +1.596 |
| ADR-193 | 118.047 | +1.281 |
| ADR-194 | 119.370 | +1.323 |

El siguiente ADR, **fuera cual fuera**, rompía Quality.

## Dónde vive el fallo

No en `MEMORIA.md`, que es generado. No en la guarda, que hizo exactamente su
trabajo: avisar **antes** de que la vista dejara de ser una vista.

Vive en **lo que la vista decide llevar**. El generador copiaba, por cada ADR y
para siempre, el primer párrafo entero de su sección «Decisión». Esa sección
pesaba **81.037 de los 119.370 bytes: el 68 % del fichero.** Eso no es un índice,
es el corpus del que ADR-171 venía huyendo.

## La decisión

**El índice se queda entero; la copia del resumen, no.**

- La tabla sigue listando **todos** los ADR, con número, fecha, estado, título y
  enlace. Nada desaparece de la vista.
- La columna «Resumen» la llevan los ADR **desde `PRIMER_ADR_CON_LECCION`**. De
  los anteriores queda `—`, y su resumen está **en el ADR que la propia fila
  enlaza**, a un clic.

La frontera no es un número a ojo: es la constante que ya gobierna qué ADR forman
el corpus vivo del método. Se reutiliza en vez de inventar otra, y por eso no
puede desincronizarse de aquella.

**No es podar.** El resumen es una *copia* del primer párrafo del ADR; el
original no se toca.

## Lo que se gana, medido sobre el mismo árbol

| | |
|---|---|
| `main`, antes de tocar nada | 119.370 bytes, **630** de margen |
| Este árbol **sin** el arreglo | **121.022** bytes: por encima del límite |
| Este árbol **con** el arreglo | **90.142** bytes, **29.858** de margen |
| Ahorro | **30.880** bytes, de 168 filas |
| A 1.350 bytes por ADR | **unos 22 ADR de margen** |

La fila del medio es la que importa: **este ADR, con su evidencia y su entrada en
el registro, habría roto la guarda él solo.**

## Y aquí está su fecha de caducidad, que el criterio de parada exigía declarar

Esto compra **unos 22 ADR**, no un techo. El siguiente corte, cuando vuelva a
apretar, es el índice de `docs/audits` —83 filas, 11.026 bytes, y crece a dos
filas por ADR—. Lo que cerraría el problema del todo —que la vista lleve
recuentos y punteros y el detalle viva en vistas generadas aparte, como ADR-171
ya hace con `DESENLACES.md`— es más caro y cambia lo que un lector encuentra al
entrar: queda declarado, sin hacerse.

**Lo que no se hará nunca aquí:** subir el límite. Mover una frontera para que
una guarda deje de morder es la mutación que ADR-192 documentó como la
peligrosa: la regla deja de existir en silencio.

## Comprobación

Dos guardas nuevas, y el árbol de prueba pasa a tener **un ADR por encima de la
frontera**: sin él, «ninguno lleva resumen» habría pasado igual y la regla solo
se mediría por un lado.

- `test_el_indice_de_decisiones_esta_completo_aunque_el_resumen_no`
- `test_solo_las_decisiones_desde_la_frontera_llevan_resumen_en_la_vista`

**Tres mutaciones, las tres vistas caer:**

| | Mutación | Resultado |
|---|---|---|

author: itrekr
body:
Preserved the CalDAV resource identity of newly created recurrence exceptions so an occurrence can be moved more than once.

The first move of a recurring occurrence writes an override into the same VCALENDAR resource as its parent series. Previously, the event returned to the cache contained the series UID and RECURRENCE-ID but omitted the CalDAV href and ETag inherited from the parent. The initial write therefore succeeded, but a later update could derive its target from the UID instead of addressing the actual shared server resource.

Copy the parent CalDAV href and ETag into the newly created override so all subsequent mutations continue targeting the original series resource.

Also canonicalize the returned RECURRENCE-ID using the TZID stored on the serialized iCalendar property. The previous floating value depended on the machine's local timezone. It could match by coincidence when the system and event timezones were equal, but failed on UTC systems because the cached identity and persisted recurrence identity had different offsets.

The original task-to-event regression was caused by the general CalDAV provider serializing task-shaped updates with the generic VEVENT formatter. An initial fix protected only updates where `oldEvent` was already a task, so it fixed moves of imported VTODO resources but missed event-to-task conversion, where only `newEvent` has task semantics.

Current upstream main now handles that component transition: task writes use the VTODO codec, imported VTODO resources are patched in place, and explicit event-to-task conversion creates a VTODO. Retain an integration regression test that persists an all-day conversion and reparses it through a later CalDAV refresh, verifying that it remains a task rather than reverting to a VEVENT.

Add regression coverage for repeated recurrence-exception moves and for RECURRENCE-ID matching when the host timezone is UTC. Update the CalDAV user documentation to describe the resulting task and recurrence behavior.

## Filled PR template

## Description

Fix CalDAV identity handling for individual occurrences moved out of a recurring series, and strengthen regression coverage for persisted task conversion.

### Recurring-event regression

Moving one occurrence of a recurring event creates an exception inside the same remote `VCALENDAR` resource as the parent series. The first move succeeded, but the returned exception did not retain the parent resource's CalDAV href and ETag. A later attempt to move that exception could therefore target a UID-derived URL instead of the actual shared server resource.

The created exception now inherits the parent's CalDAV href and ETag, allowing the same occurrence to be moved repeatedly without modifying the rest of the series.

The returned `RECURRENCE-ID` is also derived from the serialized iCalendar property, including its `TZID`. Previously, a floating recurrence ID was interpreted using the machine's local timezone. It worked when the system and event timezones happened to match, but failed on UTC systems because the cached identity no longer matched the offset-bearing identity stored in CalDAV.

### Task regression and previous fixes

The original task regression occurred because task state was updated optimistically in memory while the general CalDAV provider serialized the resource through the generic event formatter, producing a `VEVENT`. The task checkbox appeared immediately, but the next CalDAV refresh parsed the persisted `VEVENT` as an ordinary event and replaced the temporary task state.

The first attempted fix checked only whether `oldEvent` was already a task. That protected imported `VTODO` resources during moves and edits, but it did not cover event-to-task conversion. During conversion, `oldEvent` is still an event and only `newEvent` has task semantics.

Current upstream `main` already contains the corrected component-selection behavior:

* Creating or converting an item marked as a task writes a `VTODO`.
* Editing an imported `VTODO` patches the existing task component.
* Existing server-specific VTODO properties are preserved.

This PR retains an integration regression test that converts an all-day event into a task, captures the persisted VTODO, feeds it through a later CalDAV refresh, and verifies that it remains a task.

### Regression coverage

The added tests verify:

* A newly created recurring exception retains the parent CalDAV href and ETag.
* The same recurring occurrence can be moved more than once.
* A timed `RECURRENCE-ID` is canonicalized using its `TZID`.
* Recurrence lookup works when the host timezone is UTC.
* An all-day event converted into a task is persisted as `VTODO`.
* The converted task remains a task after a subsequent CalDAV refresh.

The CalDAV user guide now documents task component conversion and repeated recurring-exception moves.

## Type of Change

* [x] Bug fix
* [ ] New feature
* [ ] Refactor
* [x] Documentation
* [ ] Chore / maintenance

  * [x] Kept provider logic and UI views decoupled.
  * [x] Extended the existing recurrence helper instead of duplicating provider logic.
* **Internationalization (i18n)**:

* **Documentation Sync**:

  * [x] Updated the corresponding CalDAV documentation under `docs/user/`.

* **Code Integrity & Type Safety**:

author: ayushexel
body:
## What

A minimal, reproducible example of pretraining a GPT where one Lance table is the whole data layer: raw text, curation flags, token ids, the training dataloader and post-training retrieval all work on the same table. Sequence packing and shuffling happen inside `lancedb.streaming.StreamingDataset` (lancedb >= 0.38). This is the code behind the sequence-packing blog post; the numbers live in the post.

## Contents (`examples/llm_pretraining/`, 15 files)

- **Pipeline**: `ingest.py` (FineWeb-Edu or synthetic), `curate.py` (SQL EDA, FTS index, dedup flag as a new column), `tokenize_data.py`, `geneva_backfill.py` (the same columns as distributed, checkpointed Geneva backfills, plus a GPU embedding column), `model.py`, `common.py`, `train.py` (torchrun-ready, `--pack`, `--resume auto` across world sizes, `--blocks-mode` for the loader A/B), `sample.py`, `forensics.py`.
- **A/B controls**: `build_packed_datasets.py` writes identical pre-packed blocks as Parquet, pre-shuffled Parquet, MDS shards and a Lance table; `blocks_loaders.py` holds the Parquet loaders. `mosaicml-streaming` is the optional `ab` extra.
- **`loader_gil_repro.py`**: standalone, CPU-only reproduction of why fewer loader threads are faster (the single packer thread is starved of the GIL by read-ahead and transform threads). Needs nothing else from the repo.
- Root `README.md`: one row added to the examples table.

## Verification

- README smoke path (synthetic ingest -> curate -> byte tokenize -> tiny packed train, 40 steps) runs to completion on CPU.
- Geneva `is_dup` backfill on a synthetic table flags the same ids as the single-process path.
- `loader_gil_repro.py` on a 4-core box: `io_queue_depth` 1 -> 8 takes one packed iterator from 1.00M to 271k tok/s while the raw queue grows 61k -> 169k rows and process CPU rises, i.e. the readers are neither idle nor storage-bound.

## Notes for review

The branch was deliberately slimmed to a repro: the blog-length README, tuning notes, run-harness scripts, raw result files, the offline assertion suite and the elasticity/Mosaic check harnesses were removed. Docstrings and argparse help are limited to what each thing does.

author: duplighost
body:
Players could reach the Holdfast without understanding how supplies, power, rest, road lights and boss marks fit together. The station now demonstrates that sequence with a rewarding supply chest, a physical cable to its breaker, one current-step cue, completed-rest feedback and a real lamp using the supplied bulb. The pause menu keeps the whole route available, including existing-save and ending states.

Bosses now complete attack chains before exposing their hearts. Their machines drive committed, visible attacks; destroying machines removes that pressure and improves earned openings. Rapid machine destruction no longer interrupts every attack or repeatedly resets recovery. Charge and sweep hit areas match their warnings.

Also fixes respawning behind an unopened Holdfast gate, adds safe held-E descent and its prompt, aligns the starting car and signs with the road, moves ponds clear of roads/yards, gives field fences matching collision and breakage, and clears the station doorway of overlapping placards. Refuge doors pause against the player instead of pushing them through the threshold. Shared supply chests have hinged lids and visible contents; boss victories and supplies show saved reward amounts and world-space tokens.

Validation: fresh-start mouse/keyboard supplies, breaker, close door, rest, leave and replace bulb sequence; actual Space ascent/E descent without damage; focused combat, reward persistence, ledger, water, door and checkpoint checks; renderer smoke (12 passed, 80 shader programs); generated-site boot. Computer-assisted input won both the road boss and Bellwether with staged equipment, while constant aimed strafing lost. These probes do not establish human balance or full-campaign completion.

author: sqrt-of-2
body:
This PR turns the Jacobian of Cholesky reconstruction into an identity of measures: it proves that `TauCeti.symmetricLebesgue p`, restricted to the positive-definite cone, is the image under `L ↦ L * Lᵀ` of Lebesgue measure on the positive-diagonal lower-triangular matrices weighted by `2 ^ p * ∏ i, (L i i) ^ (p - i)`, and records the Lebesgue- and Bochner-integral forms of that change of variables.

<!--tauceti-target:v1 {"focus":"StandardDistributions","id":"cholesky-change-of-variables-symmetric-lebesgue"}-->

Roadmap: StandardDistributions

The target is the last change-of-variables bullet of Layer 6 item 2 ("Cholesky decomposition") of `StandardDistributions/README.md`: "Prove that the restriction of `symmetricLebesgue p` to the positive-definite cone is the pushforward, under `L ↦ L * Lᵀ`, of the positive-diagonal coordinate region weighted by `2 ^ p * ∏ i : Fin p, (L i i) ^ (p - i.1)`. The multivariate-Gamma integral and Bartlett decomposition must use this Jacobian in these exact coordinates." The statement, the two measures it is phrased with and the name `map_cholesky_symmetricLebesgue` follow the skeleton pinned in `StandardDistributions/Suggested.lean`, as the existing Cholesky files do.

The milestone is Layer 6, symmetric matrices and Wishart distributions. Its item 1 (the symmetric carrier, `symmetricLebesgue`, the congruence Jacobian), the Cholesky package of item 2 through the Jacobian determinant `abs_det_fderiv_choleskyReconstructionCoordinates` (TauCeti#6538), and the elementary multivariate Gamma function of item 3 (TauCeti#6565) are on `main`; this PR supplies the missing measure-level step that links them, which is exactly what `integral_posDef_multivariateGamma` needs to turn the cone integral into a product of independent triangular-coordinate integrals — only its `p = 0` case is currently proved. After this PR, Layer 6 still needs that cone integral for general `p`, the nonsingular real-degree Wishart density family with its probability, moment and transform theorems, Bartlett decomposition, and the inverse-Wishart family.

The proof reads both sides in the on-or-below-diagonal coordinates, where reconstruction is the self-map `choleskyReconstructionCoordinates` of a Euclidean space whose derivative is already computed. That needs a second coordinate system on the symmetric subspace, `symmetricLowerCoordinates`, which is `symmetricCoordinates` composed with the transposition of index pairs; permuting coordinates preserves product Lebesgue measure, so the normalisation of `symmetricLebesgue` is unchanged. On the positive-diagonal region the coordinate reconstruction is injective, because Cholesky factors are unique, and its image is the coordinate image of the positive-definite cone; Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar` then gives the change of variables there, and the coordinate equivalences carry it back. Nothing is vendored; the classical statement is Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, Theorem 2.1.9, cited in the new file.

Three files change. The new `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/SymmetricMatrix/Cholesky.lean` holds the lower coordinates, the two Lebesgue measures on the Cholesky factors, the Jacobian density and the change of variables with its integral forms; `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/SymmetricMatrix.lean` re-exports it. `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/WithDensity.lean` gains one general lemma it uses, `MeasureTheory.Measure.map_withDensity_comap_subtype_coe`: weighting the comap of a measure to a measurable set and pushing it back along the inclusion gives the weighted restriction. That file is the canonical home for transporting a density along a map, and Mathlib has no such lemma (its Jacobian file weights before comapping instead).

🤖 Prepared with Claude Code

author: bobjansen
body:
Exact fixed-point decimals, up to 38 digits, stored as a signed 128-bit count of 10^-s units. Precision and scale live on the column (ColumnMeta::decimal) and travel through every operator; scalars and literals carry their own type. Semantics: plans/decimal-plan.md, SPEC sections 2.4, 3.1 and 3.5.

- Language: decimal"12.30" literals, Decimal(p, s) types, and the Decimal(x, p, s) cast, through the lexer, parser, lowering, IR schema and codegen.
- Arithmetic is exact and checked: overflow is an error. Scale loss rounds half away from zero. / yields Float64; % is refused. Comparisons are exact across scales. Decimal mixes with Int64 and float literals, not with Float64 columns.
- Filter, sort, group-by, distinct, and inner/left/semi/anti joins. Join keys at different scales are refused.
- Aggregates: sum (Decimal(38, s), checked), min/max/first/last, mean from the exact sum, count_distinct. Statistical aggregates are refused.
- I/O: Arrow C Data d:p,s (zero-copy decimal128), Parquet in every physical encoding, and CSV decimal(p,s) hints that parse and write exactly. Decimal256 and precision above 38 are refused by name.
- ibex_bench --suite decimal compares kernels against Int64/Float64. The monetary example is examples/decimal_money.ibex.

body:
## Summary

Defines the frozen **A: Core Model Domain** contract for the staged model-system refactor. This PR does not migrate Runtime/Fleet, Image, Transcription, Subagent/Dream, WebUI, or the root Config.

### Canonical identity

Three concepts are explicitly separated:

- `model_id`: stable Nanobot machine identity (registry dict key)
- `display_name`: mutable human-facing name
- `model`: upstream model string sent to the Provider API

`ModelConfig.provider` is mandatory canonical state and must be a concrete Provider ID. `provider="auto"` is rejected; auto-detection may only exist later at model-creation input parsing before a canonical `ModelConfig` is produced.

### ModelConfig

The canonical type contains:

- `display_name`
- concrete `provider`
- upstream `model`
- `capabilities`
- `context_window_tokens`
- `pricing`
- `generation_defaults`
- `offering_id`
- `pools`
- `max_concurrent_requests`

There is no legacy flat/proxy compatibility surface in `ModelConfig` and no `ModelPresetConfig = ModelConfig` alias.

### Capabilities

Only capabilities with current Nanobot consumers are modeled:

- `text`
- `vision`
- `image_generation`
- `transcription`

Generic `audio`, `video`, `tools`, and `reasoning` capability flags are intentionally not included. Provider registry remains adapter/protocol/transport metadata; no duplicate Provider capability truth source is introduced.

### Fleet-facing model facts

Current Fleet-consumed facts remain on the configured model route:

- `pools`
- `offering_id`
- `input` / `output` / `cache_read` pricing
- `max_concurrent_requests`
- context/capability facts

No `fleet.allowed_models` center is introduced. Unused `cache_write` pricing is not modeled.

### Shared lookup contract

`nanobot.model_domain` exposes the small common API later consumer PRs must use:

- `validate_model_id(model_id)`
- `get_model(models, model_id)`
- `require_model_capability(models, model_id, capability)`

The registry contract is `Mapping[str, ModelConfig]`, so B/C/D/E can migrate independently without each reimplementing model lookup.

Canonical model IDs use the stable slug rule:

`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`

### Follow-up split

- B Runtime + Fleet
- C Image
- D Transcription
- E Subagent + Dream
- final integration: switch root schema to `models` / consumer `model_id`, migrate current config, then delete `ModelPresetConfig`, `model_presets`, synthetic default handling, duplicated AgentDefaults model facts, and obsolete migration paths

### Explicit non-goals

- no Runtime/Fleet consumer migration
- no Image consumer migration
- no Transcription consumer migration
- no Subagent/Dream migration
- no WebUI redesign
- no root Config schema switch in this PR

author: lvl0lvl
body:
`scripts/guard-sweep.ts` mutates a file in place and restores it with `git checkout -- <file>`. #66 closed the symlink case; a HARD LINK is the same defect with the index saying nothing: a regular file whose inode has another name passes every gate — mode `100644`, porcelain clean, the path resolving inside the tree — and `writeFileString` truncates the shared inode, so every other name holds the mutation while the restore unlinks and recreates only the tree's own name. Measured `--in-place` on a file with a twin outside the tree: `killed by 1` at exit 0, the twin left holding `if (false) {`; refusal 3 ("it never mutates a tree it did not create") did not hold for a shared inode. Reached by the install a fresh worktree has to run — pnpm hard-links what a `file:`-protocol package publishes — and also by a `setupCommand` that runs `ln`, or `--in-place` on a `cp -al` / `rsync --link-dest` checkout. Found by #66's review (SEC-1, executed on head and base; also bug66 and qa66), deferred as pre-existing. Closes t3_bot-43k.

## What changed

- `linkRefusal` stats the file after the index-mode test and refuses a regular file whose link count exceeds one: `<file> has N links — a write lands in every name of its inode, and git checkout -- recreates only this one. Find the others with find . -inum <inode>; in a workspace node_modules is where to look first`. Only a `File` is judged — a directory shares no inode with another name whatever its link count is — so a directory row still falls through to the read gate. A stat that fails is left to the read gate too, the tree's rule for an unreadable file.
- The index mode is asked FIRST and the order is load-bearing: `fs.stat` follows a link and Effect has no `lstat`, so with the order swapped a tracked dangling link fails the stat and falls to the read gate as "could not read" — the wrong gate's reason.
- Header refusal 7 names both shapes; `Mutation.file`'s doc and `exitCodeFor`'s enumeration follow; the pre-flight's link-gate comment notes that a hard-linked file reads fine and would pay the baseline.
- `guard-sweep.symlink.test.ts`'s ONE CLAIM widens to "a file whose write would land somewhere the restore does not reach", stated as the two shapes it delivers rather than as the general property.

## Tests

`scripts/guard-sweep.symlink.test.ts` 4 → 10, end-to-end against the real tool in scratch git repos:

- `--in-place` on a file with a second name for its inode outside the tree — NOT RUN with the link count, the twin's bytes untouched, porcelain clean, exit 3 (on the unfixed tool: `killed by 1`, exit 0, the twin mutated).
- worktree mode with a `setupCommand` that replaces the tracked file by `ln` to an outside inode — NOT RUN, the outside file untouched, exit 3.
- two TRACKED names for one inode: the tree asserted first (porcelain empty, both files at HEAD's bytes), then the report — the observable an outside twin cannot produce.
- a tracked dangling link named as a symlink rather than an unreadable file, pinning the index-mode-before-stat order.
- a tracked file under a mode-000 parent handed to the read gate, pinning the stat-failure fall-through.
- **the pre-flight call site**: a hard-linked file whose anchor is ABSENT. `linkRefusal` is wired at two sites — the pre-flight skip and the row loop — and every other hard-link fixture reaches only the row loop, because each one's file holds the anchor. With the pre-flight `continue` removed this row refuses the whole config at exit 1 blaming a stale anchor instead of exit 3 naming the link count.

Both directions on every executable branch this diff introduces, with one exception stated below.

| property | mutant | result |
|---|---|---|
| a shared inode is refused | the link-count test never fires | reds the hard-link tests |
| only a regular file is judged by its link count | the `File` guard dropped | reds "judges a directory row by its own index entry…" |
| the index mode decides before the stat | the stat block hoisted above the `120000` test | reds "names a dangling link a symlink, not an unreadable file" — observable `NOT RUN — could not read src/dangle.ts` |
| the stat-failure branch reaches the read gate | the branch returns a reason / the branch deleted | reds "hands a tracked file its stat cannot see to the read gate…" (both directions) |
| the pre-flight skips a hard-linked row | the pre-flight `continue` removed | reds "names the link count, not the anchor, when a hard-linked file lacks the anchor" |
| the admit side is real | `links > 1` → `links > 0` | reds 4 tests asserting `killed by 1` |

The one exception: the `Option.isNone(nlink)` refusal is pinned by nothing, because no constructible input reaches it — measured against the real Node layer on darwin, `nlink` comes back `Some` for a File, a Directory and a CharacterDevice. It refuses rather than admits, so it fails safe. Deleting it reds nothing, and that is disclosed rather than hidden.

`tsc --noEmit` exit 0 for `scripts`.

## Merge gates

Blocking conditions live here rather than in a chat log, because one of them lived only in a chat log and was walked past. The three gates with artifacts that night were discharged; the one without an artifact was lost.

- [x] Count gate @ `7d540e045` — exit 0
- [x] Guard sweep @ `7d540e045` — 18/18 killed, exit 0 measured
- [x] `#66` mutants vs the widened suite — 5/5 still red, none lost
- [x] Claim audit over the diff's prose — found a third and a fourth
- [x] Blind bugs / security / tests lanes — all returned by name and outcome
- [x] Reachability corrected, then the claims deleted
- [x] Targeted lane against the corrections — 4 findings, all acted on
- [x] `#66` mutants @ final head `31bb69a7ec` — 5/5 red, counts unchanged
- [x] Count gate @ final head `31bb69a7ec` — exit 0. Machine summary: *"Measured 14 workspace(s) against origin/main@4d8f02d82: 4 lost name(s), each explained by --allow above."* The four are the #66 tests under the old describe title (`scripts/guard-sweep.symlink.test.ts`, base 4 → head 10); QUAL-3 widened the suite's ONE CLAIM and renamed them, every it-title is present under the new prefix, and #66's five mutants re-run red at this head.

The gate prints its own limit and it is worth repeating rather than leaving implicit: *"This does not see a test REWRITTEN UNDER THE SAME NAME — a green gate is not the Tests rule discharged."* That is what #66's five mutants at this head are for.
- [x] Guard sweep @ final head `31bb69a7ec` — 18/18 killed, 741-test baseline, 0 survivors, 0 NOT RUN, exit 0 measured
- [x] CI green @ `31bb69a7ec` — Fork Check + Test Server 1/2/3 all `success`, read per-SHA from the check-runs API (not `gh pr checks`, which answers about the PR and can report a previous run)

## Review record

**The first review round ran before a crash and its triage record did not survive.** Six lanes landed at 05:04 EDT on 2026-09-14; triage and the SE fixes completed — they are four commits on this branch — and the session died at 06:22 before the blind verification pass was recorded. The scratch worktree holding the triage and verify artifacts was under `/tmp` and is gone.

Reconstructing findings from the commits that fixed them cannot fail: a finding recovered from its own fix is shaped by that fix, so every verification passes by construction. The record was re-established two other ways instead.

Every lane line states what the lane was **given** as well as what it found. A record listing only findings cannot tell independent corroboration from an echo, and the merge record is the worst place for that ambiguity — findings get re-checked, the sentence describing how they were obtained does not.

Fresh worktree, mutants applied from HEAD and restored with `git checkout`, tree verified byte-identical afterwards, each mutant typechecked before its result was believed.

body:
実機でのフィードバックに対応しました。

## ① ピンチ操作のちらつき (不具合)

原因が**3つ重なって**いました。ご報告いただいた「小さい表示と大きな表示を切り替え続ける」「最終的に絵がおかしくなる」「小さくなって上下反転する」がそれぞれ別の原因に対応します。

| 症状 | 原因 | 対応 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 大小が切り替わり続ける | 表示領域の高さをJSで測って決めていた。高さが変わる → ページのスクロールバーの有無が変わる → 幅が変わる → また高さが変わる、という往復が起きていた | CSS の `aspect-ratio` に任せ、JSでの測定をやめた |
| 絵が壊れる・上下反転する | 表示倍率が変わるたびに描き直していた。ピンチ中は毎フレーム倍率が変わるので、**同じキャンバスに何重にも描いて**いた | 描画に使う解像度を整数段階に丸め、操作が終わってから反映するようにした。不要になった描画は打ち切る |
| 一瞬白くなる | 表示中のキャンバスへ直接描いていた | 画面外のキャンバスへ描いてから一度に転送する形にした |

## ② 操作導線 (ご指摘は「整理」でしたが、テンプレートとページ送りは墨消しの機能なので、そちらとして対応しました)

- **ページ送りとテンプレートをツールバーへ移動**しました。PDFを通り越してスワイプする必要がなくなります
- テンプレートの保存と呼び出しを**1つのダイアログにまとめ**、サイドバーのカードを整理しました
- 読み込み後は**前置きを畳み**、注意書きを書き出しの手前へ移しました
- **PDFの高さに上限**を設けました (スマホで画面の62%まで)。小さく見えるときは拡大で補えます

結果として、スマホでPDFが見え始める位置が画面のかなり上に来て、ツールバーも常に手の届く場所にあります。

## ③ 何もないところから始める

画像や空白ページだけでも新しいPDFを作れる旨を明示し、**「空白ページから始める」**ボタンを置きました (画像からの開始は以前から動いていましたが、分かりにくい状態でした)。

## ⑤ 一括墨消しの適用前プレビュー

ご提案どおり**代表1件**を開いて、テンプレートがどこに当たるかを確かめられるようにしました。ページ送りもできます。2件目以降を選んで確認することも可能です。

## ⑥ 分割・結合について

ロードマップから外しました。代わりに v0.4 は「テンプレートの自動位置合わせ」「ページ番号付与」を置いています。

## テスト

**57項目すべて通過**。今回追加したもの:

- **ちらつきの検証** — ピンチ中に表示領域の大きさが揺れないこと、描き直しが繰り返されないこと、拡大後も絵の縦横比が保たれること (上下反転や潰れの検出)
- 一括墨消しの適用前プレビュー

テストを書く過程で、貼り付くアプリバー/ツールバー/下部ナビの下に隠れた位置を操作しようとして空振りする問題があったため、「実際に触れる位置」を返すヘルパーを用意しました。

author: rimioai
body:
## Context This PR is an upgrade pass on the built-in Pi adapter. It checks the adapter against the refreshed `pi-reference.md` for Pi 0.85.1 (the earlier reference was for 0.84.3). The installed CLI and the upstream source prove each claim. The third-party pins also moved: `rpiv-ask-user-question` 2.10.1, nicobailon `pi-subagents` v0.67.0, and tintinweb v0.19.0. ## Implementation - **Extension dialogs raise Waiting (new, Pi 0.84.4+).** Pi puts `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` around each extension `ctx.ui` dialog. The RimZ extension sends a dialog only while a run is active and a UI exists. It does not send idle dialogs, RPC mode, or the questionnaire's own dialog. Each dialog gets a `ui_prompt:` key. Rust maps the start to `AwaitingInput { detail: title, native_key }` and the end to an unnamed `ToolUsed` with the same key. The end thus clears only its own wait. `agent_settled` drops an open key, so a dialog that closes after the settle does not open the turn again. Each dialog is a generic `Question` because Pi sends no body or options. `rimz answer` refuses these dialogs and tells the user to answer in the pane. Pi before 0.84.4 does not send the pair, so behaviour on those releases does not change. - **Subagent label (fix).** nicobailon `pi-subagents` v0.65+ no longer sets `PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD_AGENT`. It names the child session in the child's `before_agent_start`, after the row has started. The extension now sends `subagent_started` again when the child's label changes, and the store keeps the newest label. The environment variable stays as a fallback for releases before 0.65. - **Subagents capability changes from Full to Partial.** nicobailon v0.65+ foreground children run in the parent process and do not load global extensions. These children are visible only when the user adds the RimZ extension path to `subagents.defaultExtensions` or to the agent's `extensions`. The README matrix, `agent-support.md`, and `adapter_pi.md` show this change. - **`session_info_changed`** now reads only `ev.name`, which is the upstream event shape. The two guessed nested shapes are removed. - **Launch reminders stay unsupported, with a corrected reason.** Pi has `--append-system-prompt`, but any use of it replaces the discovered `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` (installed 0.85.1 `dist/core/resource-loader.js`). RimZ reminders would thus remove the user's own file without a warning. The reference row is corrected. A channel through the extension is a follow-up. - Out of scope: labels for the new OAuth provider IDs (`xai`, `openrouter`, `radius`, `kimi-coding`). They live in the shared `delegated_account.rs` and are filed as a follow-up. Verification: `cargo xtask gate` passes on current `main` (6805 tests pass). A Rust unit test sends the dialog start and end through the real lifecycle `step`: Running, then Waiting, a sibling tool end that keeps Waiting, and back to Running. The Node extension harness checks dialog filtering, the settle case, and the relabel on the native-settled path and the pre-0.80.4 path. ## Advisories - If the user types an extension slash command during a run and the command opens a dialog, the row shows Waiting for a dialog that the user opened. Pi runs extension commands immediately during a run, and the dialog context cannot tell a command from a tool. `adapter_pi.md` documents this limit. - The store test does not cover the relabel directly. The relabel depends on `store/snapshot/project.rs`, where the event task replaces the earlier task. Review confirmed this by reading the code. - No automatic setup is added for foreground nicobailon children. The user must add the extension path. - A Pi release that does not send `ui_prompt_end` when a turn is aborted leaves the wait until the turn end clears it. No test covers this case.

author: iribarnesy
body:
**Empilée sur #63**, elle-même sur #56 — à rebaser sur `main` une fois celles-ci mergées.

Lève le premier des deux préalables que #55 (les tempêtes) s'était fixés.

## Le défaut

Le coefficient d'élancement H/D est **l'**indicateur du risque de chablis en sylviculture française : au-dessus de 80 un peuplement est réputé fragile, en dessous de 70 stable. Le moteur le fixait à **50 pour tout arbre, toujours**, parce que le diamètre se déduisait de la seule hauteur.

## Le principe

Le diamètre devient une grandeur portée par l'**individu**. Il s'épaissit à la mesure de ce que l'arbre monte, divisé par l'élancement que la lumière lui impose : 35 au large, 100 sous couvert.

Un arbre garde ainsi la **mémoire de son histoire** — ce qu'il a poussé à l'ombre reste élancé même s'il est dégagé ensuite, ce qui est précisément ce qu'on observe après une éclaircie trop tardive.

## E10 émerge, et c'était tout l'intérêt

Aucune règle ne dit « serré = élancé ». Les parties tournent avec les mêmes espèces, les mêmes constantes et la même graine ; seul l'écartement change.

| écartement | plantés | H dom | D dom | **H/D** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 m | 784 | 13,1 m | 30,7 cm | **43,8** |
| 4 m | 169 | 14,7 m | 34,6 cm | **43,2** |
| 6 m | 64 | 14,5 m | 37,8 cm | **38,6** |
| 10 m | 16 | 12,9 m | 36,3 cm | **35,5** |

## Ce que le moteur n'atteint pas, et pourquoi

La sylviculture mesure 25–40 au large et 90–100 en perche. Le moteur ne couvre que 35–44 : le bon **ordre**, une amplitude trop faible.

Mon premier diagnostic — « le signal de lumière est le mauvais » — était faux : `extinctionAt` compte déjà l'ombrage latéral entre codominants, et c'est lui qui produit l'écart mesuré. La cause réelle est **antérieure à ce lot** : ce poids latéral vaut 0,4 contre 1 pour un voisin dominant, or en plantation régulière tout le monde est codominant de tout le monde — exactement la situation que ce coefficient atténue. Les deux écartements les plus serrés sont d'ailleurs à égalité (43,8 et 43,2) : sous un certain espacement, le terme sature.

**Je n'y touche pas ici.** Ce 0,4 gouverne aussi l'auto-éclaircie, la succession et le tri des espèces ; le bouger déplacerait toutes les conclusions écologiques du dépôt. C'est écrit dans le test, mesures à l'appui, et ça mérite son propre lot.

## Trois décisions de modélisation

- Un arbre **brouté** garde son tronc : la dent raccourcit, elle n'amincit pas. Un semis abrouti devient trapu — ce qui est observé.
- Un **rejet de souche** repart à l'élancement de référence, le tronc de l'ancienne tige partant au bois mort. Garder le diamètre de la souche ferait d'un taillis recépé une tige de plus en plus grosse à chaque coupe.
- Le champ est **optionnel** : son absence vaut l'élancement de référence, donc exactement le comportement d'avant pour toute partie ou tout test existant.

## La conservation a fait son travail

Une fuite de 0,133 kg C est apparue dans le trajet du feu. Ce n'était pas le moteur : c'était le grand livre **du test**, qui recalculait le carbone en suspens sans le diamètre — le même arbre mesuré deux fois avec deux règles.

## Trois tests ont cédé, aucun sur le mécanisme

- Le **rapport ravageurs** chaud/figé a été rabaissé trois fois (×2, puis 1,6, puis 1,27), chaque fois pour une cause réelle. On cesse de le poursuivre : il enregistre le moteur au lieu de le contraindre. Le test exige désormais la direction sur **chaque** partie.
- La **banque de hêtres** de la succession basculait sur **un** individu (18 contre 19). Dix-neuf sujets ne portent pas une exigence de monotonie stricte ; ce qui fait la succession, c'est le contraste avec les vieux bouleaux, qui perdent neuf dixièmes de leur effectif.
- Le **gain du BRF** a changé de forme pour la troisième fois en une journée :

| état du moteur | 16 ans | 35 ans | lecture |
|---|---|---|---|
| allométrie gonflée | 0,99 | 1,09 | bénéfice différé |
| allométrie corrigée | 1,068 | 1,038 | bénéfice qui s'estompe |
| élancement individualisé | 1,035 | 1,039 | bénéfice plat |

J'avais affirmé la deuxième lecture comme une propriété écologique, assertion sur la forme de la courbe à l'appui. **Elle n'a pas tenu une heure.** Le test n'affirme plus que le signe, qui a résisté aux trois états.

## Une section nouvelle dans `realisme.md`

« Ce qu'un test écologique a le droit d'affirmer » — trois pièges qui se sont refermés assez souvent pour être écrits une fois pour toutes : un rapport entre deux quantités composites n'est pas une propriété du monde ; une ancre écrite d'après le moteur n'est pas une ancre ; la conservation ne valide rien. Avec son corollaire, subi deux fois aujourd'hui : **un seuil mesuré au milieu d'un lot périme avant la fin du lot.**

E10 passe de ❌ à 🟡, B10 gagne le tronc : **76 %**.

Le diamètre voyage jusqu'au rendu (`SnapshotTree.diametreCm`) : une perche et un sujet de plein vent ne se dessinent pas pareil.

Suite complète verte, 778 tests.

author: greluc
body:
Closes #1891.

> [!important] This is #1892 re-landed against `main`
> #1892 carried this work but was opened against `feat/lager-location-filter`, the tip of the
> #1870 → #1873 → #1888 → #1884 → #1887 chain. #1887 squash-merged into `main` at 08:23:31Z and
> #1892 merged into the now-dead base **47 seconds later**, so commit `9c356a0d` never reached
> `main` — it lives only on `origin/feat/lager-location-filter`.
>
> This PR is that commit cherry-picked onto `main`, unchanged. `main`'s tree is byte-identical to
> the commit's original parent (`git diff origin/main 9c356a0d^` is empty), so the pick was
> conflict-free and the diff here is exactly the diff that was reviewed on #1892. The full gate was
> re-run on the new base — see Verification.

## What this does

The app rendered dialogs in **three** shapes and only one was the design system's:

| Shape | Root / box | Dialogs | Opened by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| canonical | `.krt-modal-overlay` / `.krt-modal` | 42 | `krtm-modal-open` over a default `display: none` |
| legacy A | `.modal` / `.modal-content` | 47 | inline `display`, over a default **`flex`** |
| legacy B | `.modal-overlay` / `.modal-box` | 7 | an `active` class |

All **54** legacy dialogs are ported onto the canonical shell and **both legacy shapes are
deleted** — markup, CSS rule sets and open/close contracts, not merely call sites. The app now has
96 canonical dialogs and nothing else.

The defaults were *inverted* between the families, which is the trap: legacy A's root was visible
unless a class hid it. Visibility is now the shared `krtm-modal-open` / `krtm-hidden` pair
everywhere; the `active` toggle and the now-unreferenced `open-modal` / `close-modal` handlers in
`common-handlers.js` are gone, as are 34 `krtm-*` utilities whose only call sites were legacy
dialogs.

## Why it is worth doing

Every dialog defect had to be fixed once per shape. The two instances the issue names are both
from one evening: the 44 px touch floor needed four extra `.seg button` fixes after being made a
default, and teaching `.krt-modal` to scroll had to be written a second time for `.modal-content`
when `#storeModal` came out 881 px tall in an 800 px viewport.

**The multiplier reached past CSS, which the issue did not know.** `krt-live-sync.js`'s "is any
dialog open?" guard — the thing that stops a peer's change from swapping the DOM out from under an
open form and 409-ing the next submit — queries `.krt-modal-overlay` only. **54 of 96 dialogs had
no such protection**, and org-chart hand-rolled its own `busyTest` to compensate. That is the same
defect as the duplicated CSS fix in different clothes: a behaviour keyed on the root class,
silently absent from every shape that does not carry it. It is fixed here by construction — no new
code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] No `.modal`, `.modal-content`, `.modal-overlay` or `.modal-box` in `templates/` or the
      stylesheets; every dialog uses the canonical shape
- [x] `MODAL_SHAPES` holds exactly one shape, and the touch sweep is green on all five device
      classes
- [x] The interim `.modal-content` cap is deleted, not left behind
- [x] Every ported dialog still opens, closes and submits — including the live-sync fragment seams
      (`refinery-orders-details.html`'s `?fragment=store`) and the `admin/mission-data.html` trio
- [x] Tests in place — `SingleModalShapeTest` plus the browser-side sweep
- [x] `./gradlew check` passes green
- [x] CHANGELOG entry added

## Fixes to the canonical shape itself

The shape everything moved onto was incomplete, so two of these had to land with the port:

- **The head styled `h2`, but the shared `modal-wrapper` fragment emits `h3`.** A fragment-rendered
  title fell through to the global heading rule and came out orange at the browser's default `h3`
  size instead of white at `0.85rem` — so the shared shell never matched the hand-written markup it
  exists to replace.
- **`bank.a11y.closeModal` labelled the close button on fifteen pages** with nothing to do with the
  Bank, because the shared fragment hard-coded a Bank-namespaced key. Now `general.a11y.closeModal`.
- **`.krt-modal-close`** gains `flex-shrink: 0` (a long German title would otherwise squeeze the ✕
  narrower than its glyph in the flex head) and a `:focus-visible` ring (it is the first Tab stop
  inside a dialog, which the org-chart focus-trap test asserts). #1884 had already found the larger
  half of this — the class carried **no rule in any stylesheet** — and its treatment is kept
  unchanged. Worth noting that the same defect was reached from two directions: #1884 by measuring,
  this by porting onto it, since the legacy `.close-modal` it replaces *was* styled.

## Two guards, and why both

`MODAL_SHAPES` drives the **browser sweep**: reveal each dialog, measure its real geometry at five
widths, photograph it. It answers *"does this dialog lay out correctly?"* — and can only ask that of
a shape somebody entered in the list, which is the drift its own Javadoc named and could not close.

`SingleModalShapeTest` (new, frontend `test` source set, no browser) asks *"is there a second shape
at all?"* from the template and stylesheet text, on **every push** rather than only on a PR carrying
the `e2e` label. It fails if a legacy dialog class reappears, if an overlay does not carry exactly
one frame, or if a footer's submit button sits outside the form it submits.

That last assertion caught **two real defects in this very change** — a submit button outside its
form does nothing when clicked, silently, and looks perfect in a screenshot. Both halves of the
guard were verified to fail by reintroducing a legacy root, a legacy CSS rule and a detached footer
before this was called done.

## Also cleaned up on the way

The touch block's close-button rule listed `.close-modal` and `.btn-close`, both now deleted. Its
comment called the markup behind one of them *"the real defect there … but that is a separate
change"* — a `<span>` dismiss control in `admin/mission-data.html` that no keyboard could reach.
**This is that change**: every dismiss control in the app is a `<button>` now.

## Verification

Re-run on the `main` base for this PR:

- `./gradlew spotlessApply` — no changes
- `./gradlew check` — **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, and `SingleModalShapeTest` actually ran (4 tests,
  0 failures — not an UP-TO-DATE false green)
- `:frontend:lintCss` / `lintJs` / `lintHtml` / `typecheckJs` — green
- ADR-0177 re-checked against `origin/main` and every remote branch at push time — uncontested

Carried over from #1892 on the identical tree:

- `:frontend:e2eTest` — **231 tests, 0 failures**, including the reduced-`MODAL_SHAPES` touch sweep
- Scripted checks: no dialog lost a trigger, a button id or its submit; every dialog keeps an
  accessible name and a close control; every JS class selector still resolves to markup

## User-visible effect

Every dialog now caps at `90vh` and scrolls its body, so the buttons at the bottom stay reachable on
a short viewport — noticeable on the 54 ported ones, which is why a refactor carries a CHANGELOG
entry. Confirm dialogs lose their centred text and gain a right-aligned footer row, which is what
the canonical shape does. Both are in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Notes for review

- `.krt-modal--xwide` (800 px) is added as the third and last sanctioned width, for dialogs whose
  body carries a *table* rather than a form. The per-dialog `krtm-max-width-*` utilities are deleted
  rather than re-pointed.
- `.krt-modal-flow` is new: a wrapper sitting between the frame and its `<form>` — the refinery
  store dialog's live-sync swap container — would otherwise absorb the frame's column layout and
  leave the body unscrollable, the exact defect the cap exists to prevent.
- Two `krtm-*` utilities that were already dead before this change are deliberately left alone as
  out of scope.
- The knowledge base is updated in the same unit of work: `Frontend.md`'s "three modal shapes"
  section is corrected and

author: prafiles
body:
## What

Two fixes to canon primitives in `registry/netix/ui`, both ported from `prism-ui`'s copies:

- `select.tsx` — a closed `Select` shows the selected item's label instead of its raw value.
- `dialog.tsx` — adds `DialogBody`, a scrollable middle region, and makes `DialogContent` a
  bounded flex column.

## Why

**Select shows raw values.** `registry/netix/ui/select.tsx:9` is
`const Select = SelectPrimitive.Root`. Base UI renders the *value* in a closed trigger — it has
no way to know the label while `SelectContent` is unmounted — so a closed select reads `active`
or `__all__` where the Radix-era component read the item's text. Base UI's documented answer is
an explicit `items` map, which would mean editing every call site. `prism-ui` instead derives
the map from the `SelectItem` children the caller already wrote
(`frontend/prism-ui/app/components/ui/select.tsx:19-46`), which keeps the component API
unchanged; an explicit `items` prop still wins and skips the walk entirely. That is what is
ported here.

**Dialog has no scrollable body.** `registry/netix/ui/dialog.tsx:51` made `DialogContent` an
unbounded `grid`, so a dialog with a long form grows past the viewport with nothing to scroll.
Ported from `frontend/prism-ui/app/components/ui/dialog.tsx:77,134`: `DialogContent` becomes
`flex flex-col` with `max-h-[85dvh]` and `overflow-hidden`, `DialogHeader`/`DialogFooter` are
`flex-none`, and the new `DialogBody` is the `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` scroller (exported
from the item).

`DialogBody` is additive — `confirm-modal` and `form-modal` keep their own inner
`max-h-[80vh] overflow-y-auto` wrappers and are unchanged here.

## How verified

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check` clean.
- `pnpm vitest run registry` — 12 files, 95 tests pass, including two new test files
  (`registry/netix/ui/select.test.tsx`, `registry/netix/ui/dialog.test.tsx`; the first tests
  under `registry/netix/ui`, which had none).
- The select test was confirmed to be a real regression guard: reverting `Select` to
  `SelectPrimitive.Root` makes it fail with `Received: active▼` against `Expected: Active`.
- Test files are not shipped — `registry.json` lists each item's files explicitly, so
  `r/select.json` and `r/dialog.json` carry only the components.
- `pnpm build` + `pnpm registry:build` per `docs/AGENTS.md`; `dist/` is byte-identical (primitives
  are not bundled), `r/select.json` and `r/dialog.json` regenerated and committed.
- Whole-suite `pnpm test` shows the same 35 pre-existing `localStorage`-undefined failures in
  `src/tokens/theme-init.test.ts` that `main` has locally (Node 26 / jsdom artefact); nothing
  under `src/` is touched here.

Note: `frontend-template`'s verbatim copies are refreshed by the release step's
`pnpm sync:template`, owned by that repo — not done here.
