author: platreth
body:
### 📣 Summary

Data exports no longer include the `_notes` and `_tags` columns.

### 📖 Description

Notes and tags on submissions came from the legacy KoboCAT API, which is gone, so nobody can fill them in anymore. Exports kept the two columns anyway, which was confusing. They are removed from CSV, XLSX and SPSS labels exports, along with the `_submission__notes` and `_submission__tags` columns on repeat group sheets.

### 💭 Notes

- The change is in kpi only. formpack still defines `NotesCopyField` and `TagsCopyField`; kpi simply stops listing them in `SubmissionExportTaskBase.COPY_FIELDS`. There is no API or schema change and no migration.
- Old submissions may still carry `_notes` and `_tags` keys in Mongo. The data API already strips them in `_inject_properties`, exports were the last place still showing them. The test fixtures keep those keys on purpose so the tests prove the columns stay out.
- The copy columns now come out as `_id, _uuid, _submission_time, _validation_status, _status, _submitted_by, __version__, meta/rootUuid, _index`. A script that reads an export by column position instead of by header will be off by one from `_status` on and by two after `__version__`.

### 👀 Preview steps

1. ℹ️ have a deployed project with at least one submission
2. in DATA, open the Downloads tab, export as CSV and open the file
3. 🔴 [on release/2.026.33] the header row has `_notes` between `_validation_status` and `_status`, and `_tags` between `__version__` and `meta/rootUuid`
4. 🟢 [on PR] neither column is there and `_status` directly follows `_validation_status`
5. 🟢 [on PR] with a repeat group, the repeat sheet of an XLSX export has no `_submission__notes` or `_submission__tags` column either

Automated dependency-group upgrade for `app:holmes-gpt`.

| PR | dep | file:line | from → to | bump |
|----|-----|-----------|-----------|------|
| https://github.com/niklasfrick/homelab/pull/266 | `holmes` | `apps/argocd-apps/settings/zendo/zendo-argocd-apps-helm-values.yaml:53` | 0.33.0 → 0.41.0 | minor |

Revert: `git revert <this commit>` — ArgoCD selfHeal returns the cluster to the previous versions on the next sync.

## Impact report

# Impact report — `app:holmes-gpt`

Verdict: **SAFE TO MERGE**
Scope: holmes-gpt on zendo, repo: homelab
Bump class: minor — worst of: holmes chart 0.33.0 -> 0.41.0

## What is changing

| dep | from -> to | kind | release notes read |
|-----|-----------|------|--------------------|
| `holmes` | `0.33.0 -> 0.41.0` | helm chart (HolmesGPT 0.33.0 -> 0.41.0) | https://github.com/HolmesGPT/holmesgpt/releases (0.34.0 ... 0.41.0) |

## Breaking changes found in the notes

- no release in 0.34.0-0.41.0 labels itself a breaking change; the chart has no CHANGELOG. The removal-style entries are: 0.34.0 "Remove deprecated Tool._is_restricted() mechanism"; 0.36.0 "ROB-415 remove KRR resource recommendation features"; 0.40.0 "Remove experimental Azure SQL toolset" and "Remove MariaDB MCP integration, consolidate to native MariaDB datasource".
- 0.40.0 also carries security hardening with behavioural effect on toolsets: "Fix command injection vulnerability in Kubernetes toolset", "Fix SSRF in internet/fetch_webpage and connectivity_check toolsets (ROB-896)", "Require an allowlist before tcp_check probes private networks (ROB-1114)".

## Does it hit our config

| finding | our config | affected? |
|---|---|---|
| KRR / Azure SQL / MariaDB removal | `apps/holmes-gpt/settings/zendo/zendo-holmes-gpt-helm-values.yaml` sets one `modelList` entry (`claude-sonnet`) and one `mcpAddons` entry: `github` with `toolsets: "pull_requests,actions"` | no |
| kubectl-run / internet / tcp_check hardening | not used — the only addon enabled is `github` | no |
| values keys renamed/removed | none documented; 0.36.0 adds `extraEnvVarsSecrets`/`envRef`, 0.40.0 wires MCP bearer-token auth | no |

## Expected impact

Single Deployment roll. Holmes is an interactive troubleshooting assistant, not on any request path; the only observable change is that some toolsets it used to expose locally are gone upstream and some probes are now allowlisted. The pinned `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret reference and the GitHub PAT addon are untouched.

## Rollback

Commit: `<merge sha>` — `renovate-apply.py revert --repo homelab --sha <sha>`
Estimated rollback risk: low. Stateless Deployment, no CRDs, no storage.

## Decision

merge.

author: lexoliu
body:
The safe-area rule from #112 makes every stack inset its own content, but the AppKit roots (`WaterUI.swift` `layout()` and `WindowContentContainer.layout()` in `WuiWindowManager.swift`) still published the toolbar inset to Rust whenever the content managed the safe area, so content under a toolbar window was inset twice.

Both roots now lay their content out through `wuiContentFrame(of:in:)`, exactly as the UIKit root already does after #112. With every root applying the insets natively, the environment's safe-area signal never leaves zero, so the publish path (`updateSafeArea`, the signal's `setValue`, and the platform-inset initializers) is removed.

Verified on macOS with `examples/navigation` (`water run --platform macos`): the mail list extends under the toolbar with the toolbar blurred over the first row, and no second toolbar-height gap above the content.

Follows water-rs/waterui#810.

author: defurniture2025
body:
## What does this PR do?

A cron run whose turn ends `empty_response_exhausted` (retries and fallback all returned empty replies) is recorded as **failed** instead of "ok".

In that case the agent substitutes leaked reasoning or an explainer as `final_response`, so the scheduler's empty-`final_response` soft-failure check never fires. The job keeps `last_status: ok` in jobs.json although nothing useful was delivered, and the failure is invisible to anyone watching cron health. We saw this on a scheduled job whose model returned empty content twice in a row.

## Related Issue

No existing issue or PR found (searched open and closed PRs and issues for `empty_response_exhausted` and cron empty-response failures).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `cron/scheduler.py`: `_final_response_from_result` raises for `turn_exit_reason == "empty_response_exhausted"`, like the existing `failed` / `completed=False` path.
- `tests/cron/test_cron_empty_response_failure.py`: covers the raise, normal delivery, and the max-iteration summary path (which must still deliver).

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/cron/test_cron_empty_response_failure.py -q`
2. `pytest tests/cron -q`

author: darrinbaldwindev
body:
## Franchise App review fix

Targeted follow-up to PR #6 exact-head review. This branch starts from PR #6 head `768d624a149e383939791406dcf8ced1ac271662` and fixes one fail-closed ambiguity only.

### Finding
When a requested franchise scope has more than one active membership row for the authenticated user, `resolveAuthorizedFranchiseContext` previously used `Array.find()` and silently selected the first row. That makes authorization role resolution dependent on row ordering/corrupt duplicate data.

### Change
- require exactly one active membership match for an explicitly requested franchise;
- reject duplicate matches with `AMBIGUOUS_FRANCHISE_MEMBERSHIP`;
- add focused regression coverage using duplicate rows with conflicting roles.

### Evidence on exact head `ac208a07c40e99ee1c1f70f67a1a857d8207fa6e`
- Franchise App independent static review: bounded repair is correct by inspection.
- Amazon Q Developer check run completed successfully as a **code review** check.
- No GitHub Actions test/typecheck/build run is present for this exact head.

The Amazon Q success is review evidence only and must **not** be interpreted as runtime/CI test GREEN.

### Boundary
This does **not** complete P0 tenancy. It does not add persistence, schema/migrations, DB-backed request context, tenant-scoped repository methods, A/B persistence isolation, deployment, or production migration. Those remain with Manus App under Issues #15/#18.

No merge/ready/deploy action is requested. Exact-head runtime test/typecheck/build evidence is required before this bounded fix can be considered runtime verified.

## What are the changes about?
[SST-784](https://saldi-team.atlassian.net/browse/SST-784): Shared `skriv()` escapes parentheses before emitting both PostScript and HTML, so HTML/PDF shows literal backslashes. Escape parentheses and existing backslashes only at the PostScript output boundary; keep the HTML text unchanged.

This implements the confirmed escaping defect. The ticket’s premature-wrapping report remains open pending confirmation of manual line breaks and template width.

## Validation
- `php tests/integration/printTextEscaping.php`: five text fixtures across left/right/center alignment, checking actual HTML output and PDFs rendered with Ghostscript. Includes nested/unbalanced parentheses, literal backslashes and ordinary text. All 15 cases pass with warnings enabled.

- PHP syntax and whitespace checks pass.

Six full-application PDF cases passed with PostgreSQL and real converters: quote, order confirmation and invoice, each in HTML and PostScript mode. All preserve literal parentheses and Windows-style backslashes, with the expected page/line count. The baseline HTML confirmation reproduces the unwanted escaped parentheses. The 15 integration cases also pass. The separate wrapping question and customer-template validation remain open.

- `includes/formfunk.php::skriv`, called by order printing and shared form text: print an order confirmation containing parentheses, a Windows-style path and nested parentheses with HTML generation on and off; compare visible text, alignment and page breaks.
- Exercise a long description crossing a page boundary and bold/italic text in quotes, invoices and confirmations; verify headers/footers and totals remain unchanged.

author: mastersingh24
body:
Closes #974.

Compaction had two dependencies a long unattended run can lose, and it lost both silently. Neither is visible while anything is going well, which is how both survived into a milestone about proving autonomy.

## The two defects

**1. An uncatalogued model disabled compaction outright.** `DefaultCompactor.ShouldCompact` divides used tokens by the model's context window. `usage.Tracker.ContextWindowSize()` returns `0` for a model the pricing catalogue has never heard of — a Vertex publication name, a proxy id, a model newer than the build — and the ratio read that as *not full yet*. Compaction therefore never fired at all: absent, silent, and observable only when the provider eventually hard-failed on an oversized request several thousand turns later, at which point nothing in the daemon log points at compaction.

**2. A dead summarizer meant unbounded history.** Compaction summarizes by *calling the model*, so the same 429 shed that is breaking turns breaks compaction too; the failure backoff doubles out to 32 turns and history grows the whole time. The only strategy depended on the resource that was already failing.

## What this does

- **`AssumedContextWindowSize = 128_000`.** An unknown window is measured against it and announced once, naming the model id — the operator's fix is either to pin a catalogued id or to accept the guess, and neither is choosable from "compaction is degraded" alone. `size == 0` (no turn has landed) is still false: that is an empty session, not a degraded one.
- **`MechanicalCompactionAfterFailures = 2`.** Two consecutive summarizer failures escalate to mechanical truncation: no model call, a deterministic digest — a ledger of the tool calls that ran, with arguments but not results, most recent first and capped at 40; plus the conversation tail verbatim inside a 6,000-character budget. The header tells the model in plain terms that it is reading a truncation, that detail *has* been lost, and that it should re-run a tool rather than guess at a dropped result (the #710/#1031 lesson: prose next to the data at the moment of the decision).
- **It reuses the existing boundary mechanism.** Same `CompactionEventTag`, same `sliceFromBoundary` path, same next-turn framing. Nothing new on the read side. The extra `compaction_mechanical` key marks it for a post-mortem that needs to know which kind of boundary it has.
- **Success clears the cooldown but keeps the failure count.** That leaves exactly one summarizer attempt per context-refill cycle, which is simultaneously the cost and the recovery probe. If the mechanical path fails too, *that* is a `context-reduction-failed` row — both strategies are down.
- **A new `context-reduction-degraded` event**, at most once per process per condition.

## Adversarial review

**128,000 is a judgement call, not a measurement.** There is no principled derivation; it is chosen to be wrong in the safe direction. Guessing too large lands the threshold past a wall the provider enforces and kills the session — precisely the #974 symptom. Guessing too small only buys extra compactions: real work and real money, but the run survives and every one of them is visible and priced. 128K is at or below the window of every model either supported provider currently serves. The day a provider ships a *smaller*-windowed model that is not in the catalogue, this will be wrong in the unsafe direction. I took that trade knowingly; the alternative on offer was the status quo, which is no bound at all. I also rejected double-conservatism: 128K against the small-tier 0.35 threshold is ~45K, which would be destructive for no gain.

**The assumption deliberately does not go into `usage.ContextWindowSizeFor`.** That would have been a one-line fix and it would have been wrong. There, `0` means "unknown" and `/context` renders it as unknown, which is honest; a tracker reporting a fabricated window makes every consumer display a made-up percentage as though it were measured. The assumption belongs to the component that has to act without the answer.

**Mechanical truncation is lossy by design.** It drops tool *results* entirely and keeps only the call ledger. That is a real loss of information a summary would have preserved — it is the thing that keeps an unattended run alive until someone looks at it, not a steady state. The digest says so to the model, and the degraded row says so to the operator. If you read a degraded row on a session you care about, intervene.

**Degraded is not failed, and sharing the author had a cost.** "Did not run" and "ran, but worse" read oppositely during an incident, so this is a new event rather than a new `operation` value on `context-reduction-failed`. The author is shared on purpose (a client already matching on it sees both), but that meant `attach.ContextReductionFailure` — which matched on **author alone** — would have reported a degraded row as a failure, i.e. exactly backwards. Caught during implementation; fixed by adding an `InvocationID` check with a comment naming why. This is the sharpest edge in the change and the one most worth a second pair of eyes.

**A test was deleted, not fixed.** `TestDefaultCompactor_ShouldCompact_UnknownWindowSkips` asserted `ShouldCompact == false` on an unknown window — it pinned the defect as though it were the intent. Its replacement carries the comment saying so. Three tests stand in its place (uses the assumed window / still respects the threshold / no turn yet is not degraded).

**Emitting an event from inside a predicate.** `compactionWindowSize` is called from `ShouldCompact`, a per-turn predicate, and it writes an eventlog row. The alternative is making every caller remember to announce it, and the caller that forgets is the one running unattended at 3am. It is latched to once per process and is a queue append.

**Pre-fix failure verification.** Both production files were patched back to the old *behaviour* (leaving every new symbol in place so the package still compiles — reverting them outright makes the tests uncompilable, which proves nothing) and the suite re-run. Six tests failed, exactly the predicted set and no others:

- `TestUnknownContextWindow_AnnouncesItselfOnTheEventLog` — `ShouldCompact = false on an unknown model far past the assumed window`
- `TestUnknownContextWindow_AnnouncedOncePerSession` — `degraded rows after 5 threshold checks = 0, want 1`
- `TestDefaultCompactor_ShouldCompact_UnknownWindowUsesTheAssumedOne` — `ShouldCompact = false at 999999 tokens on an unknown model`
- `TestPersistentSummarizerFailure_FallsBackToMechanicalTruncation` — `no compaction boundary was written; history is still unbounded after a dead summarizer`
- `TestMechanicalFallback_ClearsTheCooldownButNotTheFailureCount` — `cooldown after a mechanical fallback = 4, want 0`
- `TestMechanicalFallback_AnnouncesItselfOnTheEventLog` — `no context-reduction degraded row in the event log`

Declared as passing both before and after, by design: the three `TestMechanicalSummary_*` pure-function tests (determinism, boundedness, oversized-final-message), `TestKnownContextWindow_IsNotDegraded`, `TestSingleSummarizerFailure_DoesNotTruncateMechanically`, `..._UnknownWindowStillRespectsTheThreshold`, `..._NoTurnYetIsNotDegraded`, and `TestMechanicalCompact_EmptyWindowIsNotReportedAsAFailure`. Those pin the *boundaries* of the new behaviour rather than the behaviour itself, so a pre-fix pass is the correct result for them.

`TestRunPendingCompaction_BacksOffOnFailure` (#356) still passes unchanged at 2 LLM calls across 4 turns, even though the mechanical path now fires inside it — the fallback makes no model call, which is the point.

**Not verified on a cluster.** Both paths are exercised by unit tests with a failing mock summarizer and an uncatalogued model id. Neither has been seen in a live GKE run, because both require conditions we do not deliberately create. The 8-hour unattended run this unblocks (box A1 of #1042) is where either would actually

author: cainiao33
body:
An explicit `data=` override was silently discarded when resuming from a checkpoint whose saved dataset still existed. Reproduced on current main with a real interrupted training run: `train(resume=True, data="b.yaml")` continued using `a.yaml`.

Update the existing checkpoint-data condition to honor explicit data, and avoid inserting the task-default dataset for path resumes. Without an override, the checkpoint dataset remains in use. Boolean resume from a non-resumable checkpoint still starts new training.

Scope: two existing production files, **4 lines added / 2 removed**. No new arguments, helpers, files, or tests.

Validation: real training reproduced the bug on main and verified six boolean/path resume cases (different dataset, no override, explicit task-default dataset). Additional real-training checks passed for config-file overrides with both resume forms, path resume from a different base model, and non-resumable checkpoint fallback. No new Ruff diagnostics relative to the original PR head. Existing CI provides cross-platform and Python-floor resume coverage.

author: gilgardosh
body:
Adds a comprehensive evaluation document for a proposed extension to `@accounter/mcp-server` that would expose a filtered GraphQL schema and a schema-navigation tool through MCP.

## Summary

This is a research and proposal document that evaluates three requirements:
1. A filtered schema surface — expose a deliberately small subset of queries, types and fields
2. Automated exposure — derive tool definitions from the schema without per-capability code
3. A schema-navigation tool — help agents discover schema paths through prose intent

## Key sections

- **Open source survey** (§2): Examines 7 projects; none are directly adoptable. Key finding: every mature option curates at the **operation** level (persisted documents), not the **schema-subset** level that requirement 1 proposes.
- **Self-implementation cost** (§4): Estimates 1,000–1,400 lines across four pieces (subset definition, builder, execution tool, discovery tools) — roughly the cost of three curated tools, with payback around the fourth tool not written.
- **Detailed feedback** (§5): Identifies gaps and blindspots:
  - Schema documents types (100%) but barely documents root fields (15%) and arguments (2%)
  - No query-cost control exists anywhere in the server
  - The subset is not the security boundary; RLS and auth directives are
  - Requirement 3 (schema navigation) has the strongest ecosystem validation and should ship first
  - An alternative design (operations-as-tools via `@mcpTool` directives) is worth explicit consideration
- **Suggested phasing** (§6): Five phases from A (search tool alone) through E (evidence-based widening), with A–C carrying no new exposure risk.

## Notable findings

- **Requirement 3 is the strongest part**: It has clear external validation (Apollo MCP Server, ChilliCream's Semantic Introspection RFC) and pays off independently, even without the execution tool.
- **The subset is not a security boundary**: The 410 auth directives and RLS upstream are the actual boundary. The subset controls context and blast radius, not authorization.
- **Documentation is the biggest gap**: The proposal assumes descriptions exist to drive automation, but only 16 of 108 Query root fields and 9 of 373 arguments have descriptions. This converts the work from "write a tool" into "write a tool and document the subset."
- **An overlooked alternative**: Every project with real adoption chose operations-as-tools (persisted documents with `@mcpTool` directives) over schema-subset exposure. This is worth explicit decision-making rather than default.

## No runtime changes

This is a documentation-only addition. No code changes to the server or connector.

body: ## Bug and impact `classify()` in `frontend/advisor_desk.html` used bare English words as intents. That is not a style issue: it served the wrong kind of answer, or refused a lookup the advisor is licensed to make. Concrete triggers: 1. **“Can I ask what NVDA is trading at?”** matched `\bask\b` and returned **INDETERMINATE** about bid/ask/spread being unavailable. The last print (`226.040000`) was never shown. The desk is labelled *Ask the desk*; the verb *ask* is how a rep phrases a quote request. 2. **“What’s my client’s NVDA position worth?”** matched `\bclient\b` and returned **INTERNAL USE ONLY** (BLK-005). The Wilson 1,200-share position was never shown. This is the primary phrasing on an advisor desk. 3. **“What’s the forward PE on NVDA?”** matched `\bforward\b` and was treated as a client-facing send. BLK-005 is *output formatted to send, forward, or show to a client*. Mentioning a client, or using *ask* as a verb, is not that. This is a different defect from PRs #2–#5 (wrong-issuer `resolve()`). Those remain open and are not touched here. ## Root cause ```js /\b(email|send|forward|client|draft.*(note|letter))\b/ /\b(bid|ask|spread|book|nbbo)\b/ ``` `ask`, `client`, and `forward` are ordinary English on this desk. They were treated as quote-book and BLK-005 tokens. ## Fix - Quote-book intent requires bid / *the ask* / ask price / spread / book / nbbo / bid-and-ask. The seed *Give me the bid and ask on NVDA* still matches `bid`. - BLK-005 requires a communication verb (`email|send|forward|draft|show`) **and** `client|customer`, or `draft` a note/letter/email. *Draft this as an email to my client* still blocks. *Should my client buy more NVDA?* still hits advice first. ## Validation `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` — **155 passed** (live-schema tests skipped; no local Postgres). New cases in `tests/test_desk_classify.py` run the same `classify()` / `answer()` extracted from the page.

author: osolmaz
body:
## Summary

The test suite leaked one workflow server per extension test home, and each leaked server held about 80 MB for the life of the machine. This change makes the harness stop the servers its run started before it removes the temporary root.

## What the leak cost

The suite creates one temporary root per run (`test/global-setup.ts`). Some tests point `HOME` at a temporary home, and the extension's client starts a workflow server there. The per-case stop request in `test/extension.test.ts` misses a server that is still starting when the request arrives.

A missed server becomes an orphan (its parent is 1), never exits, and keeps writing into the temporary root, so the root also survives the cleanup step. In this working tree that accumulated 208 servers and 16.3 GB of resident memory over five days, and the memory pressure caused `earlyoom` to kill the browser.

## The fix

`test/temp-workflow-servers.ts` walks the run root for `server/server.lock.json`, checks the recorded process start identity with the existing `matchesProcessIdentity` helper, sends `SIGTERM`, waits up to five seconds, and escalates to `SIGKILL` for a survivor. `test/global-setup.ts` calls it in `teardown` before `fs.rmSync`, and reports the number of servers it stopped on stderr.

The start-identity check is deliberate: a recorded process identifier alone can belong to a stranger by the time the run ends.

## Tests

`test/temp-workflow-servers.test.ts` covers the four paths: a recorded live process with a matching identity is stopped, a stale identity leaves the process alone, a record for a process that already exited reports nothing, and a root without a server store reports nothing.

## Verification

- `npm run check`: 112 files, 1366 tests, 90.94% statements and 85.47% branches.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 3 files, 14 tests.
- `npx slophammer-ts@latest dry .`: 0 candidates.
- `npx slophammer-ts@latest check . --only ts.dependency-boundaries-required`: no findings.
- Measured effect: `npx vitest run test/extension.test.ts` left two servers alive before the change and none after it. The full check run reports `test harness stopped 2 workflow server(s) left behind by this run` and leaves one server, the one that serves the live state database.

## Boundary

A run that is killed cannot clean up, so an interrupted run can still leave a server behind. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` states that and tells the reader to check `ps` after an interrupted run.

author: slimbuck
body:
A plain click with the brush or sphere brush selected nothing in Safari; only a drag worked. Chromium and Firefox were unaffected.

Both tools rasterise the stroke into the shared mask canvas as `moveTo(prev)`, `lineTo(x, y)`, `stroke()` with round caps. On pointerdown `prev` is the current point and `update()` runs immediately, so a click, which has no pointermove, produces a single zero-length segment. Chromium and Firefox render a zero-length round-capped line as a filled dot. Safari draws nothing, which is what the HTML spec asks for, so the mask stayed empty. The 2D brush selects straight from that mask, so the `set` op cleared the selection. The sphere brush is gated on the same mask texture in the intersect shader at footprint 0, so its capsule test never ran either.

Both tools now fill a circle of the brush radius at the pointerdown position with `arc` and `fill` before continuing into the stroke path, so the click no longer depends on the browser's stroking rules. Drags are unchanged: the filled dot coincides with the round cap the stroke draws anyway.

Verified with real pointer input in Chromium and Firefox (click and drag select with both brushes, mask pixel coverage unchanged), and the Safari root cause confirmed with a canvas probe on Safari 26.6.2. A manual click in Safari is still worth doing before merging.

body:
> **Ready for review.** `configservice-sdk` **0.21.0** is released (tag `configservice-sdk-0.21.0`, from Cantara/ConfigService-SDK#929) and this PR now uses it; the verification below was re-run against the released artifact. It still needs an owner to review the configuration class before merging.

## Why

#1537 reverted master to Spring 5.3.39 to get it building again, which leaves the Dashboard on **GHSA-4wrc-f8pq-fpqp** (critical, spring-web < 6.0.0). Moving forward was blocked on `constretto-spring`: 2.2.3 is its only release, and it references a class Spring 6 deleted. Same crossing as Cantara/ConfigService#1830 and Cantara/microservice-baseline#611: constretto only layered two properties files.

## What changed

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Spring (incl. webmvc) | 5.3.39 | 6.2.19 |
| Jersey | 2.48 | 3.1.12 |
| Jetty | 9.4.58 `jetty-servlet` | 12.1.13 `jetty-ee10-servlet` |
| `javax.servlet` / `javax.ws.rs` / `javax.xml.bind` | javax | jakarta |
| constretto-spring | 2.2.3 | removed |
| Java level | 1.8 (from parent) | 17 |
| configservice-sdk | 0.20.22 | 0.21.0 |

- **`Configuration`** keeps its name, API and load order: classpath `cs_application.properties`, then `./config_override/application_override.properties` if present, overrides win. **Please review this class.**
- **`Main`**: Jetty 12 security classes are in `ee10` packages; the role constraint is `Constraint.from(user, admin)`, health is `Constraint.ALLOWED`. The `(server, contextPath)` constructor no longer exists, so the context is attached with `server.setHandler`.
- **`SpringMVCGlocalExceptionHandler`**: Spring 6.1+ throws `NoResourceFoundException` for a missing static file where Spring 5 answered 404, and the catch-all `Throwable` handler turned that into a 500. It is now sent back as the same 404.
- **`mvc-config.xml`**: version-less schema locations instead of `spring-*-3.0.xsd`.

## Verification

This repo has **no tests**, so the migrated jar was started next to master's jar and both were probed identically (JDK 22, local):

| request | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/health` | 200 | 200 |
| `GET /dashboard/` (FreeMarker index) | 200 | 200 |
| `GET /dashboard/js/app.js`, `/css/main.css` | 200 (same bytes) | 200 (same bytes) |
| `GET /dashboard/js/`, `/img/`, `/images/favicon.ico` | 404 | 404 |
| `GET /dashboard/application/` no auth / bad password / read user / admin | 403 / 403 / 403 / 403 | 403 / 403 / 403 / 403 |
| `GET /dashboard/client/` no auth | 403 | 403 |
| `POST /dashboard/authenticate` good / bad credentials | 200 / 401 | 200 / 401 |
| `GET /dashboard/doesnotexist`, `/nope/missing.js` | 500 | 500 |

Dependency tree: a single version each of Jakarta Servlet 6.0, JAX-RS 3.1, Jersey 3.1.12, Jetty 12.1.13 and Spring 6.2.19. Not verified: pages that call a live ConfigService.

## Two things on master this PR deliberately does NOT change

1. **`/application/*` and `/client/*` answer 403 to everyone, including the admin user.** `Main` never sets an authenticator, so Jetty logs `No authenticator for: RoleInfo{[user, admin]}` and refuses every request. Adding `BasicAuthenticator` would open those endpoints to anyone with the configured credentials, which is a security decision for the owner, not something to slip into a dependency migration.
2. **Unmapped paths answer 500, not 404.** `<mvc:default-servlet-handler default-servlet-name="org.springframework...DefaultServletHttpRequestHandler"/>` names a servlet that does not exist, so the fallback forward fails.

Cantara Jenkins only builds master, so nothing will run on this PR.

author: marius-kilocode
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A full Agent Manager sync resolved each worktree with 2 to 3 `gh` calls:

- worktree with a PR: `gh pr view` plus a `reviewThreads` GraphQL query
- worktree without a PR: `gh pr view`, `gh pr view <branch>`, `gh pr list --search <sha>`

With N worktrees that scales linearly in GraphQL points and process spawns against a 5,000 point/hour budget shared with every agent session that also runs `gh`. GraphQL requests are `POST`, so ETag and `304` revalidation do not apply, which is why caching alone cannot reduce this cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batching is the available lever while staying on `gh`. One aliased GraphQL document resolves every worktree by `headRefName`, with a HEAD-SHA alias for same-repo PRs whose local branch was renamed. The response is reshaped into the `gh pr view --json` shape so `parsePRResult`, `checks`, and `parseReviewers` are reused unchanged, and so full-sync and active-tick results hash identically, which avoids badge flicker.

Selection mirrors gh's own finder because the naive query produces wrong badges:

- states `[OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED]`, newest first, open preferred, so a merged PR keeps its badge instead of disappearing
- a fork PR is only attributed when the local HEAD matches, since `headRefName: "main"` on this repository alone matches 76 fork PRs
- a SHA-associated PR only counts when open with an exact head match, because a fresh branch off `main` sits on the last merged PR's squash commit
- a default-branch worktree does not show its latest merged PR, matching gh

Anything the batch cannot decide stays unresolved so the existing per-worktree path runs: ambiguous candidates, `refs/pull/N/head` tracking refs, GraphQL errors, and unknown fields. A failed batch is never worse than the previous behavior.

The seed orchestration lives in `pr/am-pr-seed.ts` behind a small callback host. `PRStatusPoller.ts` grows only by the call site, a host adapter, and one optional `fetchOne` parameter.

## User Impact

PR badges stay correct with fewer GitHub API calls and fewer `gh` process spawns. The selected worktree keeps its 15s refresh, the all-worktree sweep stays at 2 minutes, and multi-project is unaffected because each project already has its own poller batching only its own repository.

## Evidence

Measured against `Kilo-Org/kilocode` with `GH_DEBUG=api` and `rateLimit { cost }`:

- one rich `gh pr view` costs 1 GraphQL point; one `reviewThreads` query costs 1 point
- 10 branches batched: 1 request, `cost: 2` to `3`, 0 errors, all 10 resolved including 6 fork PRs and an ambiguous fork pair

Isolated VS Code on a disposable fixture with two open PRs, one merged PR whose remote branch was deleted, and one fresh branch off `main`, counting only children of the extension host during one full sync:

- 1 batched `gh api graphql`, 3 `reviewThreads` follow-ups, 0 `gh pr view` or `gh pr list`
- `Batched PR lookup cost: 1` logged each 2 minutes
- with `gh` unauthenticated: one batch failure logged, then the legacy path reported the same auth state as before

Checks: `tests/unit/` 5,620 pass, 0 fail; `typecheck`, `lint`, `knip`, `check-kilocode-change`, and `format` clean.

Limitations: the per-PR `reviewThreads` query and the 15s active tick are unchanged, so at 10 worktrees the hourly reduction is roughly a quarter and grows with worktree count.

(`tmux new-session` forks a daemon that inherits stderr; under uvloop a PIPE
stderr hangs `communicate()` on EOF) with no comment, so an editor of that
file could swap the file back for a PIPE and reintroduce the new-session hang.
`pty_common._run_tmux` now owns the spawn mechanics for both callers — the
`capture` flag covers claude-sub's stdout contract, `check` keeps
pty_common's raise contract — and claude-sub's `_run_tmux` is deleted;
`_tmux_checked` calls the shared runner. The signature-mirror fakes in
`tests/conftest.py` and `tests/test_terminal_backend.py` gain the `capture`
parameter to stay faithful mirrors, and the env-behavior fake moves from
`wait()` to `communicate()` to match the merged body.

Deleted symbol: `_run_tmux` in `src/cli/claude_sub.py` (its references fold
into the pty_common definition imported by the same module).

## Evidence

Probe 1 — the two copies before the change (whole-repo grep for the runner):

```
$ rg -n "async def _run_tmux" src/
src/agents/backends/pty_common.py:  async def _run_tmux(*args: str, check: bool = False) -> tuple[int, str]:
src/cli/claude_sub.py:  async def _run_tmux(*args: str, capture: bool = False) -> tuple[int, str]:
```

Probe 2 — claude-sub already imported five helpers from the natural owner, so
the spawn mechanics were the only unshared piece:

```
$ rg -n "from src.agents.backends.pty_common import" -A6 src/cli/claude_sub.py
from src.agents.backends.pty_common import (
    _TMUX_SOCKET,
    _tmux_binary,
    _tmux_client_env,
    tmux_session_exists,
    tmux_session_name,
)
```

Probe 3 — vulture over the production tree (both copies are called, so this
cleanup came from the clone scan, not the dead-code probe; listed for the
record that no symbol was deleted on static-tool evidence):

```
$ vulture src/ server.py --min-confidence 90
(no output)
```

Probe 4 — full test suite green after the change:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q -m "not local_only"
5542 passed, 11 deselected in 332.76s
```

Fixes #1235.

## What
Narrows the preview totals promise to tracked changes (option 3 from the issue). Untracked provider-directory files are dropped in `untrackedFilesList` before any diff exists, so they are neither listed nor counted. Counting them (options 1/2) would mean reading every file under an untracked `node_modules/`/`target/` on every review, not just `--preview`, since that list feeds the normal workspace path too. author: tsatsuamable
body:
## Summary

Migrate InputTelemetry, the final production consumer of MovablePanel outside src/vr/ui, to SpatialPanel + @pmndrs/uikit. Preserve live WebXR input-state projection, hand/controller matching, world-context diagnostics and PanelManager lifecycle.

## Programme / finding

P1-UXR / UXR1 final production-surface migration after #742. A post-merge substrate audit found InputTelemetry still extended MovablePanel even though all src/vr/ui production panels had migrated.

## Risk surface

- [ ] Analytical / statistical correctness
- [ ] Rust ↔ WASM ↔ TypeScript boundary
- [ ] Dataset ingest, identity, serialization, or reproducibility
- [x] WebXR / VR interaction or spatial UI
- [ ] Rendering performance or large-dataset performance
- [ ] Security, privacy, permissions, or untrusted input
- [ ] Build, CI, deployment, dependencies, or supply chain
- [x] Documentation / engineering governance

Primary failure modes: source-to-hand/controller matching changes, transient XR pose errors become fatal, telemetry begins mutating input authority, PanelManager lifecycle breaks, or the new UIKit surface fails to update in headset.

## Adversarial implementation contract

- [ ] **High-risk change**
- [x] **Standard-risk change:** a developer-facing XR diagnostic surface is migrated without changing input authority.
- [ ] **Low-risk exemption**

### Standard-risk pre-implementation adversarial contract

- **Invariant:** InputTelemetry remains projection-only. Engine input, XRInputSource data, WorldSpatialContext and controller/hand state remain authoritative.
- **Authority / production path:** engine/XR state -> InputTelemetry projection -> UIKit Text only.
- **Primary failure modes:** handedness matching drift; missing-source fallback regression; getPose transient exception escapes; panel update/render lifecycle regression.
- **Falsifying evidence:** InputTelemetry source matching tests, untracked-hand regression, constructor null-safety, WorldUIManager integration, typecheck and production build.
- **Non-goals / dependencies:** no input-routing, gesture, XR provider, spatial-context, selection or device-validation behavior changes. Depends on existing engine input/XR APIs.

## Focused verification

- [x] InputTelemetry interaction tests
- [x] Constructor null-safety
- [x] WorldUIManager integration
- [x] Panel layout integration
- [x] Typecheck
- [x] Production build
- [x] ESLint / diff integrity

Exact checks:
- npx vitest run tests/vr-interactions.test.ts tests/panel-rendering-null-safety.test.ts tests/world-ui-manager.test.ts tests/panel-layout.test.ts -> 65 passed
- npm run typecheck -> passed
- npm run build -> passed
- npx eslint src/vr/InputTelemetry.ts tests/vr-interactions.test.ts -> passed
- git diff --check -> passed

## Correctness evidence

InputTelemetry no longer imports or extends MovablePanel and no longer owns a CanvasTexture renderer. It extends SpatialPanel, projects its bounded diagnostic lines through a UIKit Text component, and remains registered through the existing PanelManager/input/update lifecycle.

The source matching logic is preserved: handedness is preferred for hand/controller association, with source-order fallback. XR getPose failures remain non-fatal and return unavailable rather than throwing through the panel update loop.

A new regression explicitly proves InputTelemetry is a SpatialPanel/UIKit surface.

## Post-implementation adversarial review

**Exact reviewed head:** 1dedbdc77e51b149014bac6eae0d8ed5780dffd4

- **Production path attacked:** engine XR/session/input state -> source matching -> WorldSpatialContext snapshot -> bounded telemetry lines -> UIKit projection.
- **Failure mode exercised:** handedness mismatch, missing source, transient pose failure, constructor state order and migration-induced authority mutation.
- **Observed result:** existing matching/untracked-source tests remain green; constructor null-safety remains green; panel is now explicitly asserted as SpatialPanel; no input state is written by the panel.
- **Test falsifiability:** changing matching order, allowing pose exceptions to escape, or restoring canvas/Mo​​vablePanel inheritance breaks focused regressions.
- **Completion/status check:** PASS. Exact-head migration and adversarial review are complete for InputTelemetry.

**Disposition:** PASS

## Review disposition

PASS. Exact-head local verification is complete; required CI checks adjudicate promotion independently.

author: pinoeer-kingxi
body:
Related to #43587.

## Scope

The original 4-image -> 5-image reproducer now gets a prefix-cache hit on vLLM 0.29.0 in my TP=2 GPU validation (details below). A narrower first-sibling miss remains when the producer continues for more than one Mamba block after its final multimodal feature: full attention can identify the shared prefix, but align-mode Mamba has no materialized state at that boundary.

This PR:

- exposes the final multimodal feature end on `Request`;
- stops align-mode Mamba prefill once at that cache-aligned boundary;
- retains the boundary as a possible replay point; and
- adds an end-to-end coordinator regression where a consumer appends a second MM item and changes from a 0-token hit to a 528/1600-token hit.

The automatic checkpoint is deliberately limited to the final MM item, so it adds at most one prefill split per multimodal request.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR directly references #43587. #55873 and its follow-ups implement application-directed semantic checkpoint tokens; this PR does not add or duplicate that API. It provides one bounded automatic boundary for the common incremental-MM case.

## Validation

- `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`: 48 passed, including producer -> consumer regressions for 528- and 1600-token Mamba blocks.
- `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py`: 48 passed.
- Three related hybrid Mamba prefix-cache tests in `test_prefix_caching.py`: passed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent code-review pass: no remaining findings. An earlier encoder-rescheduling approach was removed after review found stateful cache-accounting risk.

## GPU baseline

On vLLM 0.29.0 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, TP=2, the issue's 4 -> 5 image pattern (padded above one Mamba block) produced:

```text
4 images, first request:  cached=0
4 images, identical replay: cached=1632
5 images after 4 images:    cached=1632
```

This confirms that the original v0.19 failure is no longer universal on the latest release. The exact Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16 checkpoints were not available locally, and the patched source checkout could not use a matching precompiled wheel, so the PR remains draft pending exact-model and human-author review.

## Model evaluation

Not run. This changes scheduler/cache checkpoint placement, not model math or output semantics.

## AI assistance

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance, including regression construction and an independent review pass. Human author review is still required before marking the PR ready.

author: amazing-source
body:
Fin du premier point de la phase 5 : le banc d'essai a maintenant ses projets mis de côté. La case est cochée dans ROADMAP.md.

## Le choix

click et cobra ont servi à tous les résultats du banc d'essai : ils restent des projets de développement. Pour mesurer ailleurs que là où l'on règle, il faut un nouveau projet par lanceur, et il ne doit pas être choisi au goût. La règle, consignée dans l'ADR 0013 : parcourir les dépôts GitHub les plus étoilés du langage (recherche du 2026-09-14) et prendre le premier qui remplit les critères de l'ADR 0011 :

1. licence permissive, dépôt ni archivé ni fork ;
2. fichier de verrouillage à la racine des 200 commits de la fenêtre (`uv.lock` avec pytest, ou `go.mod`) ;
3. suite complète qui passe au dernier commit, dans l'image du banc d'essai, en moins d'une minute avec les caches chauds (la collecte garde `~/.cache` dans un volume).

| Langage | Projet | Résultat |
|---|---|---|
| Python | NousResearch/hermes-agent | écarté : 6 jobs de CI d'environ 4 min |
| Python | TheAlgorithms/Python | écarté : voir plus bas |
| Python | langflow-ai/langflow | écarté : 5 jobs de CI de 17 à 24 min |
| Python | harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo | écarté : 330 s |
| Python | Graphify-Labs/graphify | écarté : 423 s et 11 échecs |
| Python | **fastapi/fastapi** | **mis de côté** : 3 348 tests réussis en 34 s |
| Go | avelino/awesome-go | écarté : encore en cours après 25 min |
| Go | **ollama/ollama** | **mis de côté** : 7 931 tests (dont 305 sautés) en 23 s, caches chauds |

**Un seul écart est un jugement.** TheAlgorithms/Python n'a que 22 fichiers de test pour 1 507 fichiers Python ; ses autres tests sont des doctests dans les fichiers d'algorithmes eux-mêmes. Les tests d'un changement se trouvent donc dans le fichier modifié, retrouvés par son nom sans rien prédire. Le garder aurait fait paraître la correspondance de noms meilleure qu'elle ne l'est. L'ADR le dit.

## Le code

- `benchmarks/harness/collect.py` : les deux projets, avec leur commit de fin épinglé.
- `benchmarks/harness/images/fastapi` : image uv Python 3.11 épinglée par digest, avec `git`, qu'un test appelle et que les runners GitHub fournissent. `images/ollama` reprend la chaîne d'outils de cobra, avec son propre volume de cache.
- `benchmarks/split.py` : `HARNESS_DEVELOPMENT` et `HARNESS_HELD_OUT`.
- `python -m benchmarks.harness evaluate` refuse un projet mis de côté sans `--held-out`. La collecte ne classe rien, elle reste donc libre.

## Vérifié

- Les fenêtres des deux projets ont été lues commit par commit : pour fastapi, `.python-version` vaut 3.11, `scripts/test.sh` existe, et le groupe `tests` comme l'extra `all` sont présents aux 200 commits. Pour ollama, `go.mod` indique `go 1.26.0` aux 200 commits.
- La vraie collecte, limitée à un commit (`--limit 1`), a été lancée sur les deux projets : le plus ancien commit de chaque fenêtre se construit et sa suite passe : fastapi `e24d44c` en 44 s, ollama `681dfae` en 130 s, caches froids (6 581 tests). Aucun mutant dans ces deux commits : celui de fastapi ne touche aucun fichier de `fastapi/`, et celui d'ollama ne fait que supprimer des lignes, alors que les mutants portent sur les lignes ajoutées (ADR 0012).
- Un test vérifie que chaque projet du banc d'essai est soit de développement, soit mis de côté ; un autre, que l'évaluation refuse un projet mis de côté avant de cloner quoi que ce soit.
- ruff, mypy : OK. 255 tests passent en local ; 28 sont sautés (Postgres et Docker).

author: tamnd
body:
papers extract read one paper at a time while the routing table offered sixteen lanes for a page image, so the backlog of thirty two papers left for M4 was going to take as long as the sum of them. papers translate already solved this and this borrows its answer.

A worker pool across the list, one worker per lane the fleet has for a picture, plus a --jobs flag for a run that should be gentler than the routing table says, or to hold a layout run down to one heavy process. A machine with no routing table reads one paper at a time, which is what a native run wants anyway.

Across papers and never within one. The pages of a paper are read in order because each page teaches the next one what a page of this paper looks like: rule A5 judges a page against how long this paper pages usually are, rule A6 against where its printed numbering starts, and the folio learner is fed page by page as the answers come back.

The lane count comes out of the route file rather than off the fleet, so it can be known before the fleet is built. Fleet does no network work, but it refuses a table with no vision route, and a native run on a machine with no table at all has to keep working.

Three tests: that several papers really are in flight at once, that every paper is reported exactly once with its own error, and that a cancelled run closes the channel instead of hanging. go test -race is clean.

author: vytautasp
body:
Records the design for the **report** — an ended session written out in full and taken out of the
app, as a PDF. Documentation only; nothing is implemented yet. Design for #99.

## `CONTEXT.md`

Gains a **Report** section after "The table". The `_Avoid_` list does real work: **record** was
already a competitor's W–T–L, **standings** the table, **score sheet** one match's two numbers, and
**session history** the list of ended evenings. "Tournament report" was never available — the
glossary avoids "tournament" outright.

## ADR-0038, "The report is a document, not the screen"

Marked as **refining** ADR-0021 §4 rather than superseding it: the screen's typography is untouched.

The load-bearing decision is the typeface. Verdana was chosen precisely *because* it is installed
everywhere and therefore costs no bytes and no round trip — which is exactly what makes it
unembeddable, since there is no Verdana file in this repo and there could not legally be one. The
fallback a PDF offers instead is the core-14 fonts, and those are WinAnsi: `ė į ų ū ą č` have no
codepoint there, so Helvetica cannot spell `Deimantė`. Half this app's audience reads Lithuanian, so
this is a wall rather than a compromise. The report is set in **Roboto** and looks like a document
rather than like the app.

Also recorded:

- **No `DIFF` column**, despite the reference PDF having one. Point difference is computed nowhere
  in `padel-engine`, deliberately — decision #8 resolves ties on head-to-head and then stops. A
  difference column beside the ranking would look like the tie-break and would not be it, on the one
  artefact where no reader can tap anything to find out.
- **No medals**, because Roboto has no emoji and drawing them would spend the report's one flourish
  on what the Standings tab calls "the one warm thing on the screen". **Joint positions are marked**
  though — two `2`s followed by a `4`, unexplained on a page nobody can question, reads as a bug.
- **A pure `buildReport` with pdfmake behind a `PDF_MAKER` token**, mirroring `QR_ENCODER`. The seam
  is what stops the report becoming a second, drifting rendering of the standings.
- **No automated tests**, deferred on ADR-0021 §6's reasoning and written down as a deferral rather
  than left as a silence.

## Review notes

The two places I'd most expect pushback are the ones I argued hardest in the ADR: dropping `DIFF`

## ELI5

OMP launched from Orca should find the same sessions and settings as OMP launched from your login shell. Orca now carries the shell's directory settings into local and daemon launches, while explicit pane settings still win.

## Change

Reuse the cached login-shell environment probe for OMP and bare-shell launches on macOS/Linux. Copy only XDG directory variables and `PI_CONFIG_DIR`, preserving explicit empty values. Pass explicit pane-env provenance separately from already-merged local process values so local and daemon precedence agree. Install OMP's managed extensions under its selected config root without setting `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` or collapsing config and data roots.

Addresses #20140. OMP v18.1.17 (the reported version) and current read-only source both keep config at `join(homedir(), PI_CONFIG_DIR || '.omp')`; XDG data/state/cache redirect independently when the corresponding OMP root exists. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` does not directly choose that config root. Moving all config/extensions into `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp` as suggested in the issue would conflict with this contract.

## Proof

Rebuilt hidden Orca, installed OMP 18.1.18 on macOS, and a disposable login profile. Orca itself began without `XDG_DATA_HOME`. The opt-in runtime test passed in 11.6s and verified actual session paths and `agent.db` creation:

| Launch | Config/extensions | Session/data root |
|---|---|---|
| Orca with login-profile settings | `<home>/.omp-profile-proof/agent` | `<home>/xdg-data/omp` |
| Explicit pane overrides | `<home>/.omp-pane-config/agent` | `<home>/pane-data/omp` |
| Plain login shell with inherited Orca directory settings removed | `.omp-profile-proof` | `<home>/xdg-data/omp` |

This checks storage routing, so actual runtime paths and filesystem assertions are the proof; an OMP startup screenshot would not establish them. No model turn is required.

The test writes its profile only in its disposable output directory, refuses an absent/non-isolated E2E home, and explicitly isolates nested login shells. The final run left the real-home profile hash unchanged and created no real-home test roots.

## Validation and review

- 134 tests passed across launch inheritance, extension materialization, local-provider, WSL, and zsh launch suites.
- Node typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent implementation review found no blocking findings; independently ran 67 focused tests.
- Native Windows and client-side WSL probes are skipped. SSH execution stays on its existing host boundary; folder workspaces use the same launch environment.
- A cold bare-shell launch may wait up to the existing five-second environment-probe timeout; subsequent calls share its cached result.

OMP source at `~/projects/oh-my-pi` was read only. This does not migrate existing split storage trees or change named-profile selection.

- [x] No upstream skill source was copied or translated.

author: lazynet
body:
Step 1 of the implementation sequence in `specs/designs/2026-09-13-multi-agent-harness-design.md`. Step 0 landed in #265.

## What it adds

The vocabulary every adapter translates into, in `agents/base.py`: `Verdict`, `Operation`, `Signal`, `FileEdit`, `ToolCall`, `HookEvent`, `HookDecision`, `HookOutput`, `HookSupport`, `ConfigArtifact`, `WriteOp`.

`AgentAdapter` gains `hook_events()`, `parse_hook_input()` and `format_hook_output()`. `ClaudeCodeAdapter` implements them as pass-throughs — no field renamed, no value reinterpreted — and `NullAdapter` with it, so the existing protocol-conformance test keeps covering both.

## The two defaults that carry the weight

**`HookDecision.verdict` defaults to `None`, not `ALLOW`.** `pre_tool_use_security` exits 0 with no output for every command it merely fails to object to. With `ALLOW` as the default, migrating that branch would convert each of those into an explicit, prompt-skipping approval — the regression delivered entirely by a default value.

**`HookSupport` declares a verdict *set*, not a `can_block` flag.** An agent that logs `unsupported permissionDecision:ask` and runs the tool anyway is not distinguishable by a boolean. With the set declared, deploy can refuse a configuration rather than discover it while a tool call is pending.

## Verdict sets are gated on evidence from this repo

Only two verdicts have been observed being honoured here: `DENY` at `pre_tool_use` (`pre_tool_use_security` — stderr + exit 2) and `BLOCK` at `session_stop` (`stop_verify_guard` — `{"decision": "block"}`). Every other event declares an empty set, which makes deploy refuse a blocking hook there. That is the false-negative direction, and the set grows when a verdict is actually exercised — not when a vendor doc names one.

## One deviation from the design's step-1 list

The design lists `config_targets()` / `plan_config()` among step 1's Protocol methods. They land here as a separate optional `ConfigPlanner` Protocol, in the idiom `HeadlessAgent` and `SessionPinningAgent` already set, rather than on `AgentAdapter`. Putting them on `AgentAdapter` would either ship methods no adapter satisfies — breaking the `isinstance` conformance test — or ship bodies that raise, which is the "promise with no implementation" the design itself rules out. The signatures are frozen either way, which is what step 1 is for; step 3 implements them.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` — 2515 passed, no new warnings
- `uv run ruff check src tests` — clean
- `uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict` — clean
- Both load-bearing guards mutation-tested: flipping the default verdict to `ALLOW` fails `test_abstaining_is_not_approving` and `test_abstaining_emits_nothing_at_all`; dropping `DENY` from `pre_tool_use` fails two more. Restored by hand-editing back, not `git checkout`.

author: kilbot
body:
Step 3 of the checkout logging audit (wcpos/roadmap#293, ticket wcpos/roadmap#296). This is the vocabulary the action rows of step 4 are written against.

The event registry covered sync, print, product and client, plus one lone checkout entry. Everything else a sale does fell back to its raw developer string in Store health → Logs, which is what a merchant saw.

## What lands

21 types in the `CHECKOUT` domain, grouped as the audit found them:

| group | types |
|---|---|
| Taking money | `payment.recorded`, `payment.recorded-offline`, `payment.captured`, `payment.authorized-offline`, `payment.settlement`, `payment.not-mirrored` |
| Refused or returned | `payment.refused`, `payment.declined`, `payment.cancelled`, `payment.released`, `payment.voided`, `payment.void-refused` |
| The sale | `checkout.opened`, `checkout.split-planned`, `checkout.completed`, `checkout.cancelled`, `checkout.order-refresh`, `checkout.provenance-skipped` |
| The reader | `reader.connected`, `reader.disconnected`, `reader.battery-low` |

Each carries a merchant-readable label, and a description wherever the label alone would leave someone guessing. Both are translated at **render** time, so a payment taken on a Spanish till reads in whatever language the till runs later. That is why the registry exists instead of English strings at the call site.

The labels say who did what rather than naming a status, because that is the distinction a cashier actually needs at the end of a busy day:

- `payment.refused` — "Your store refused a payment"
- `payment.declined` — "The terminal did not take the payment"
- `payment.not-mirrored` — "Payment saved on your store but not on this till"

## Two of them are live immediately

`payment.refused` and `payment.settlement` already have emitters, so those rows gain titles the moment this lands:

- `payment.refused` — the manual payment refusal in `use-record-manual-payment`.
- `payment.settlement` — all three rows of an offline card settlement in the terminal-payments service: the per-attempt row, the row written when the retries run out, and the clearing row when it later settles. The attempt row was missing its type until Codex caught it; it has it now, so the three read as one story.

The other nineteen are what step 4 writes against.

Unused types are a warning, not a failure. The gate becomes enforcing for each one the moment it is emitted.

## Scoped directories

`check-event-labels.mjs` gains `packages/core/src/screens/main/pos/checkout` and `packages/core/src/services/terminal-payments`, following the precedent set by the receipt-email queue: scoped to the directories that emit by design, so the gate stays enforcing rather than degrading to an unused-label warning once the call sites land.

Worth knowing for review: the gate only treats a `type:` property as an event when the same object literal carries a `level:` of `debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error`. Checkout is full of `type:` keys that are not events — reducer actions, and `context.type` values — and none of them are picked up.

## Overlap with #2009

#2009 adds the REGISTER half of the same work and touches three of the same files: `event-registry.json`, the test's seed assertions, and the generated label artifacts. It is the earlier PR and has right of way — whichever of us lands second merges `next` and resolves, regenerating the artifacts rather than hand-merging them. A note to that effect is on #2009.

## Validation

- `packages/utils` `event-registry.test.ts` — **11 passed**, including two new cases pinning the money vocabulary and the refusal wording
- `packages/utils` logger suites — **185 passed**
- `packages/core` logs suites — **110 passed**
- `node scripts/check-event-labels.mjs` — 94 types labelled, 19 unemitted (expected)
- `node scripts/check-sync-event-types.mjs` — every emitted type covered
- `node scripts/extract-js-strings.js --check` — complete

## Not in this PR

The call sites. Writing them is step 4 (wcpos/roadmap#297), which also adds `actor` to the money rows and makes checkout the first producer of the Logs screen's Actions chip.

author: mevilbhojani
body:
Step 2 of task 029 (ADR 003 phase 3, migration half). Builds on #713.

`digest.ceo` and `project.guide` were built-in JavaScript modules the engine ran bespoke `gather`, `buildUserPrompt`, `verify` and `toChanges` functions for. They are now **documents in the closed vocabulary**, and `Modules/Agents/skills/digest.js` and `Modules/Agents/skills/projectGuide.js` are deleted.

## How they became data

`compile()` moved out of `skillRecord.js` into `skills/compile.js`, so one function turns a document — a company's own or a built-in one — into the generic-skill contract. `skills/index.js` compiles the seeds instead of requiring code modules. There is no branch on which kind a skill is; the special path is gone rather than widened.

Resolution is now **company row → built-in seed → code skill**. The middle step is what makes deleting the code files safe: a migration record is written once globally, so a workspace created after 022 runs would never be seeded and would otherwise have lost both skills. `qa-review` and `pr.summary` stay code, as ADR 003 §3 requires.

Migration `022` writes both documents into every existing company so an admin can open and edit them; a company that already holds either key keeps its own copy.

## Three catalogue additions the migration needed

| Addition | Why |
|---|---|
| `fallback` | A template rendered from gathered data alone, posted when the model answered nothing. Where the reporter's deterministic digest went — without it a run whose provider is down proposes nothing. |
| `grounded` | `{ keys, numbers, fields, mustNameKey, allowHours }` — the reporter's hand-written ground-truth check, generalised in `skills/grounding.js` so any skill can hold answer fields to the tasks and counts its readers measured. |
| Board readers | `project.tasks` gained `dueSoon`, `inReview`, `moved`, the five bucket lists, `plan` by sprint, `next`, and `keys`/`counts`; `project` gained `requireGuide`. |

All three are declarable by a skill an admin writes, and `SkillEditor.vue` exposes them, so step 1's "the editor exposes the whole vocabulary" still holds.

## Not regressed

- **The `agent` label semantics are untouched.** Both skills declare `project_task`, whose scope is `project`, so neither is ever the agent for one task.
- **`project.guide` still reads `agent-after`**, as step 1 deliberately recorded. `tests/agent-split.test.js` and `tests/ai-project-execute-agents.test.js` passed **untouched** — step 1's evidence pattern — and a new test pins the guide's `agent-after` explicitly so it cannot move silently again.
- The reporter is still reachable by the `risk.today` alias an agent may already hold.

## Model pin

Already satisfied by #713 and **not rebuilt**: the editor exposes the per-skill pin, `validateSkill` checks it through `AICore/modelPin`, and `compile()` carries it. Recorded separately in progress.md: the pin is stored and validated but not yet forwarded to the provider — `askModel` never reads `skill.model`, and nor does the agent-level pin. That is the cost-and-routing half of phase 3.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `jest --selectProjects unit conventions` | 303 suites, 4398 tests, green (302 / 4381 before) |
| `vitest run` | 47 files, 384 tests, green |
| `i18n-backfill` then `i18n-check` | 9 keys in 10 locales; 8036/8036, 0 missing, exit 0; baseline unchanged |
| eslint (backend + frontend) | 0 errors |
| `vue-cli-service build` | complete |
| In-process sweep, real database | read-only, no model, no writes |

**Revert checks.** `fallback` and `grounded` unwired in `compile()` → 5 failures. `project.guide`'s declared `inputs` emptied → 3 failures, including the guide's `agent-after`.

**Real-data sweep** (company `6a8ee973…`, project AlianHub Platform): 58 tasks, 38 open, 20 done, 10 unassigned, grouped by sprint. With no provider `digest.ceo` proposed one comment — "38 open task(s): 0 overdue, 0 blocked, 0 in review, 10 unassigned." author: prajuaba
body:
A property declared `[SensitiveData(Protection = Mask)]` was only ever protected if it was a `string`. Three gaps, each of which made the declaration read as a control while performing less than it claimed. Found while closing Resourcify's FRS 7.5 gap, where the eight fields needing protection are all `decimal`.

## The read path returned the unmasked value

`EntityEncryptionService.MaskSensitiveFields` computed the masked value for a non-string property and then threw it away — the branch did nothing, so the **original** value was returned to a caller the schema says may not see it. It now writes the property type's default.

## A masked decimal was indistinguishable from a real one

That default is `0`, so a masked cost rate reads as a free resource. `SensitiveDataAttribute` gains `StateProperty`, naming another property on the same entity that the masker sets to a canonical masked state — `true` for a `bool`, or the member named `Masked` for an enum. A schema naming a property that is not there is left alone rather than throwing at read time.

## The write path lost data rather than leaking it

`PreserveMaskedFieldsCallerCannotRead` had the matching hole, and this is the dangerous one. It skipped everything but `string`, so:

1. An unentitled caller GETs an entity; the masked `decimal` arrives as `0`.
2. They edit an unrelated field and PUT the whole document back.
3. The guard hits `continue`, and the stored real value is replaced by `0`.

Silently — `Range(0, 100000)` accepts `0`, and no exception is raised anywhere.

It now decides on **entitlement before type**: a caller who may not read a property cannot change it, whatever its type, because restoring is a plain property copy and needs no string operations. The mask-echo guard stays string-only and now says why — a masked `0` and a genuine `0` are the same value, so applying it to a value type would reject a privileged caller legitimately setting a field to its default.

## The Roles list was unreachable from any schema

`EntityAccessPolicy.ShouldMask` already honoured a `Roles` list on the attribute, letting a role stand in for the `view:{category}` scope. The compiler had no way to emit one, so no schema could use it. `Property` gains `sensitiveRoles` and `sensitiveStateProperty`.

Both are additive: a schema declaring neither regenerates byte-identically. Confirmed against Resourcify — 173 files written, 47 scaffolds preserved, `api-manifest.json` byte-identical, and only the entities whose properties actually changed showed a diff.

## Verification

Verified by mutation, not by green. Restoring the `!= typeof(string)` skip turns the two write-path tests red:

```
CallerWithoutScopeSubmittingMaskedDecimalZero_PreservesStoredValue [FAIL]
  Expected: 123.45
  Actual:   0
CallerWithoutScopeSubmittingNewDecimalValue_PreservesStoredValue [FAIL]
  Expected: 123.45
  Actual:   999.99
```

and leaves `CallerWithScopeSettingDecimalToZero_ValueSurvivesWithoutException` green — the correct signature, since the privileged path was never affected.

`Foundry.Mongo` masking **35/35**, `Foundry.Schema.Compiler` **407/407**. The archival and partitioning suites need a standalone `mongod` and a replica set on 27018; they were not run locally and are left to CI.

author: danielkjellid
body:
Stacked on #40 (`ds/theme`), which is stacked on #39. This diff is only the plugin work.

The overlays coming next need two things the bundle did not have:

- **`x-trap`** (`@alpinejs/focus`) — moves focus into a modal, returns it to the trigger on
  close, and marks the rest of the page inert. Dialog, Drawer and Command all depend on it.
- **`x-anchor`** (`@alpinejs/anchor`) — positions panels that float beside a trigger
  (Popover, DropdownMenu, Select, Combobox, Tooltip) and flips or shifts them to stay in the
  viewport. That collision handling is what keeps a menu near the screen edge from forcing a
  horizontal scrollbar; the alternative was hand-rolling the same thing in every panel.

Both are exposed through the chainable API, with modifiers built into the attribute name so
the call site reads as `x_trap("open", inert=True, noscroll=True)` and mypy catches a bad
placement rather than it silently doing nothing at runtime.

`x-teleport` is deliberately left out until something needs it — it has to sit on a
`<template>`, and that is a design decision better made next to its first real use.

## On bundle size

Two plugins would have taken the bundle from 116kB to **223kB** on every page load, so this
also turns on esbuild's minifier: the result is **97kB**, smaller than before the plugins
were added (34kB gzipped). Only the build flag changed; esbuild preserves the export names,
which I checked on the output.

## Verification

`make lint` + tests pass in both packages (273 / 96). Nine new cases in `test_base.py` pin
the attribute-name construction for every modifier combination, including rendering. I also
confirmed against the built bundle that `trap` and `anchor` register as real directives and
`$focus` as a magic — they were previously only entries in Alpine's "missing plugin" warning
table.

author: igorshevchik
body:
## Что было видно

Владелец трижды сказал одно и то же: «открывается слайдер от UI, а нужен от jsSDK». И привёл решающее сравнение:

- **«Квалифицировано в сделку»** (список лидов) — открывает **хорошо**;
- **«Успешные сделки из лидов»** (9 записей) — открывает **плохо**.

## Почему

Слайдер всё это время был настоящий, от jsSDK. Но выглядел он модальным окошком посреди экрана — и отличить это от чужого компонента на глаз нельзя.

Высоту фрейма слайдера задавали **мы сами**: страница детализации звала `fitWindow`, тот меряет содержимое, и портал сжимал окно до его размера.

Девять успешных сделок → окно на треть экрана. Сотня лидов → окно нормальное.

Отсюда и «лиды хорошо, сделки плохо»: разница была не в механизме открытия, а в **длине списка**.

## Что сделано

- **в режиме детализации `fitWindow` не зовётся вовсе** — ни при открытии, ни после доклеенной страницы, ни на плашке «Список не открылся»;
- **список занимает весь экран и листается внутри себя.** Наблюдатель конца списка смотрит в контейнер прокрутки, а не в экран, — иначе «показать ещё» не срабатывало бы никогда;
- **оглавлению приложения подгонка остаётся**: там три плитки, и фрейм в целый экран оставил бы под ними пустое поле;
- **класс `.drill-frame` с минимальной высотой 600 px удалён.** Это была заплатка из прошлого PR — она лечила симптом того же дефекта (короткий экран схлопывался), а причина была в подгонке.

## Новый тест сразу нашёл ещё одно место

Заведён `tests/nuxt/appIndexPage.nuxt.test.ts` — у главной приложения два лица, и высота фрейма это ровно то, что ломалось на боевом **трижды**.

Первым же прогоном он поймал: экран **«Список не открылся»** тоже звал подгонку и сжимал слайдер до двух строк. То есть человек, нажавший на число, вместо объяснения получал полоску. Исправлено.

⚠ Заметить возврат этого дефекта мог бы только человек на боевом портале: на демо-наборе детализации нет вовсе, а `fitWindow` вне фрейма — пустая операция. Поэтому тест здесь, а не «проверим глазами».

## Проверено

- `pnpm check` — 1320 тестов; `generate` + смоук, 9 проверок под боевым CSP.

author: siddharth705
body:
## Summary

### 1. Pin the greeting hero above Getting Started / Your Journey

The greeting hero rendered *after* the Getting Started checklist and Your Journey widgets, both of which only appear conditionally — so the hero, the one element that's always on the page, visually jumped up or down depending on which of the other two happened to render for a given user. Moved the hero's JSX above both so it's pinned first, always.

### 2. Getting Started (and Your Journey) popping in with no loading indicator

Reported separately: "Getting Started" takes too long to appear. Investigated the actual cause before changing anything:

- **Checked the backend first.** `OnboardingService.getChecklist()` makes five sequential lookups (user, checklist events, latest import job, budgets, goals). Checked every one against its migration — all five are backed by an appropriate index (`idx_user_checklist_events_user_id`, `idx_import_jobs_user`, `idx_budgets_user_active`, `idx_goals_user_active`). No missing-index issue there.
- **The real, verifiable gap is on the frontend.** Both `ChecklistWidget` and `JourneyWidget` rendered nothing at all — not even a skeleton — while their own query was in flight, so each one silently popped into existence whenever its fetch took long enough to notice (Getting Started's query is one of ~9 Dashboard fires in parallel on mount, competing for the same backend — routinely the slowest to settle). Every other independently-loaded Dashboard section (Accounts/Recent Transactions/Budget/Goals) already reserves its space with a `useDelayedLoading`-gated skeleton; these two were the only ones that didn't.

Added the same skeleton pattern to both. Also added a 5-minute `staleTime` to `ChecklistWidget`'s query, so a plain Dashboard revisit doesn't pay the same wait again for data that almost certainly hasn't changed — every action that actually could change it already explicitly invalidates the `['onboarding']` cache itself, so this only skips needless refetches, never risks a stale checkmark.

## Test plan
- [x] Hero-order regression test (DOM order), confirmed to **fail** against the pre-fix ordering
- [x] Skeleton regression tests for both widgets (fake-timer-driven, mirroring `Ledger.test.tsx`'s existing pattern for this hook), each confirmed to **fail** against the pre-fix code
- [x] Full frontend suite: 1367 tests passed, 0 failures
