body:
## Summary

The notary knows nothing about JWKS. One commit, stacked on `feat/ws-attestations` (#6).

Replaces #7 and #8. #7's branch carried five pre-force-push copies of #6's commits alongside its
own work and needed a merge commit to become mergeable; this is the same intent rebuilt on the
current base as a single clean commit — and narrower, because the prover-side helpers leave the
notary entirely instead of staying as a library module.

## What changes

**Deleted** — the JWKS duty and everything only it used:

- `src/jwks/` in full: the Merkle `JwksRotationProof` path (`notary.rs`, `transcript.rs`,
  `sol_types.rs`, `crypto.rs`) *and* the prover helpers and mock (`mod.rs`, `prover.rs`, `mock.rs`)
- the `--jwks-enabled` flag and `NotaryState::jwks_enabled`
- the server-name dispatch in `handle_verified_session` (and the `CertBinding` imports only it used)
- the `Jwks` / `Http` / `Base64` error variants
- dependencies: `alloy-primitives`, `alloy-sol-types`, `serde_with`, `base64`, `k256`, and the
  non-test `reqwest` (the smoke tests keep their dev-dependency)

**Kept** — the notary signs the section 9.1 record for every session; the host it observed is in
the record, and the contract that reads it pins the host. `libid_transcript::AttestationWire` stays
the wire struct, as on the base. The crate still builds as a library so the smoke tests can embed
`run`.

**Docs** — `lib.rs`, `server.rs` and the README no longer describe two duties or a dispatch. The
comment at the former dispatch site keeps the reason it is gone: the notary deciding what a session
is for is the profile-specific decision REQ-COMMON-33 forbids.

Diffstat: 14 files, +50 / −1241.

## Why the helpers leave

The notary is client-agnostic; `run_jwks_prover` / `notarize_jwks` / `MockProver` were keeper code
hosted here for reuse. Hosting them here made the keeper depend on this whole crate (axum, tlsn,
mpz, the server) and pin the notary's exact libid-rs revision so cargo kept one copy of the types —
the coupling behind #8 and the keeper's repeated re-pins. Everything they use lives in libid-rs
(`libid_tlsn::prover_generic`, `libid_transcript::{Layout, AttestationWire, read_msg}`,
`libid_ceremony::AttestedData`), so they move to the keeper (libid-org/keeper#7) and
the keeper's `notary` dependency goes away.

## Verification

- `cargo check --all-targets` — 0 errors
- `cargo +nightly fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --all` — all pass, including `proxy_protocol_returns_attestation_on_the_reclaimed_websocket`
  and `mpc_protocol_returns_attestation_on_the_recovered_socket`

## Operational note

`--jwks-enabled` becomes a clap usage error and `NOTARY_JWKS_ENABLED` is inert. No deployment passes
the flag; grndd-systems/deployment sets the env var in `kustomize/overlays/libid-testnet/identity-notary.env`
and `kustomize/overlays/testnet/notary.env` — those pods keep starting (the var is ignored), and the
two lines should be dropped when this rolls out.

## Sequencing

Pairs with libid-org/keeper#7. The keeper's current branch still pins `notary @ 67dd1fe` (#7's
head) until keeper#7 merges, so #7's branch stays in place until then; #7 and #8 are closed.

---

## Real path verified (2026-09-14)

A notary built from this tree, started with anvil's #0 key, and the keeper's `examples/notarize_jwks`
(keeper#7 build) driving a genuine MPC-TLS session against `www.googleapis.com`:

- prover: TLS handshake, `GET /oauth2/v3/certs`, 1033-byte response, MPC-TLS proof complete
- notary: `Verified server: www.googleapis.com` → `Ceremony attestation sent to prover` (136 sent / 1557 recv bytes) — no dispatch, no JWKS code on the path
- keeper read the frame back: 1797 bytes of attested data, 65-byte signature, recovered address
  `0xf39f…9266` = anvil #0; `authority_id` matches `keccak256("www.googleapis.com")`

The wire-frame contract (`attestation_frame` on the notary, `libid_transcript::read_msg` on the keeper)
and prover/verifier compatibility on the shared tlsn `550220e` / mpz `4db9454` pins hold with no crate
shared between the two sides.


---

## Release image

So other repos' CI can pull a current, production-shaped image off this branch.

**Changes**

- `tower-http` 0.6→0.7, `tokio-tungstenite` 0.29→0.30, `reqwest` 0.12→0.13 — the only direct deps whose requirement no longer reached the newest release.
- Test client takes no TLS backend: it GETs `/info` over loopback HTTP, so `rustls` would only add rustls-platform-verifier, quinn and an Android JNI tree. Lockfile is 17 packages smaller than before the bump.
- Image runs as uid 10001, not root.
- Builder drops `pkg-config`/`libssl-dev`; runtime stops naming `libssl3` — nothing in the graph links OpenSSL.
- `HEALTHCHECK` probes `${NOTARY_PORT:-7047}` instead of a literal 7047, which `--port` would have made permanently unhealthy.
- OCI `source`/`description`/`licenses` labels.
- README: tag policy, and that a consumer's CI needs no login step.

**Verified**

- `cargo test --all` 7/7; `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean; `cargo +nightly-2026-08-10 fmt --check` clean.
- `ghcr.io/libid-org/notary:custom-1f54c19` pulled with an **empty docker config**, no credentials: runs, logs `notary signer ready` at `0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8`, accepts TCP on 7047, reports `healthy` on both 7047 and `NOTARY_PORT=9999`. 125MB, linux/amd64, uid 10001.

**Not verified / known issues**

- Every healthcheck probe logs one ERROR (`MPC-TLS failed: Broken pipe`), 1:1 — ~2880/day. Pre-existing; wants a server-side log-level fix, not a Dockerfile one.
- `libssl3` still arrives via `ca-certificates`→`openssl`; the image size is unchanged.
- amd64 only. arm64 hosts need `--platform linux/amd64`; native multi-arch is cheap now (public repo ⇒ free `ubuntu-24.04-arm`) but is a workflow change for its own PR.


---

## Multi-arch images

Consumers span architectures — amd64 runners and x86 nodes, arm64 runners and Graviton, Apple
Silicon — while every image published so far is amd64 only.

**Changes**

- `docker-custom.yml`, `release.yml`: one build job per platform on a runner of its own architecture
  (`ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`), pushing by digest; a merge job joins the digests into the tag.
- Tag semantics unchanged — `:<version>` and `:latest` from a release, `:custom-<suffix>` from a
  dispatch — each now a manifest list over both platforms.
- `oci-mediatypes=false` with provenance and SBOM off: a classic Docker manifest list, exactly two
  platform entries, readable by pre-23 Docker clients.
- `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.1 and `actions/download-artifact` v8.0.1 pinned by commit SHA.
- README: the "amd64 only" note replaced by what the tags now carry.

**Verified**

- `ghcr.io/libid-org/notary:custom-c957999`: `docker manifest inspect` lists `linux/amd64` and
  `linux/arm64`.
- arm64 variant pulled and run natively on Apple Silicon — `--help`, then `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 7047
  --ws-port 0`, logging `notary signer ready notary=0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8`,
  listener accepting, `uname -m` aarch64, uid 10001, no emulation warning.
- Build wall clock: amd64 4m35s, arm64 4m27s, manifest 6s (single-arch amd64 was 4m17s).

**Not verified / known issues**

- `release.yml` is unexercised until a release is published; the identical build/merge shape ran
  through `docker-custom.yml`.
- Digest-only pushes leave untagged versions in the ghcr package; a "delete untagged" retention
  policy would break every tag.
- `custom-3d74656`, an intermediate build, is an OCI index that `docker manifest inspect` before
  Docker 23 cannot read. Pin `custom-c957999`.

author: strzhao
body:
# test(gateway): keep the runner's system proxy out of the media-retry connect guard

`TestCacheImageFromUrlConnectGuard::test_blocks_private_dns_answer_at_connect_time` fails
deterministically on any runner whose macOS System Configuration carries a proxy, even
though the test already clears every proxy environment variable it can find.

## What happens

The test unsets `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` and their lowercase forms
before calling `cache_image_from_url`, so it expects the SSRF connect guard to be the only
thing standing between the call and the rebinding host. On macOS that expectation does not
hold: `urllib.request.getproxies()` falls back to the System Configuration when no proxy
environment variable is set, and httpx (with the default `trust_env=True`) uses that result
to pick a proxy. The request then dials the proxy address instead of the host under test, and
the guard assertion reports a connect to `('127.0.0.1', 7890)`.

## How to reproduce

```
$ scutil --proxy            # HTTPEnable/HTTPSEnable/SOCKSEnable = 1, proxy 127.0.0.1:7890
$ python3 -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.getproxies())"
{'http': 'http://127.0.0.1:7890', 'https': 'http://127.0.0.1:7890'}
$ pytest tests/gateway/test_media_download_retry.py -q
1 failed, 13 passed
```

## The change

One line in the test, blocking that one environment source for the duration of the test:

```python
monkeypatch.setattr("httpx._utils.getproxies", lambda: {})
```

The obvious spelling — patching `urllib.request.getproxies` — does not work: `httpx/_utils.py`
binds the name at import time (`from urllib.request import getproxies`), so httpx keeps
calling the original. Patching httpx's own binding is the point that actually takes effect.

Production behaviour is untouched. Respecting the system proxy is correct for a real client;
the bug is that this test never isolated itself from the ambient environment.

## Verification

- Before: `1 failed, 13 passed`. After: `14 passed` (same worktree, same interpreter).
- Mutation check: gutting the connect guard in `tools/url_safety.py` makes the test fail
  again, so it is still asserting the guard rather than having been hollowed out.
- Neighbourhood: `pytest tests/gateway -k "media_download or connect_guard"` → 15 passed,
  1 skipped. Full `tests/gateway` run compared A/B against the same tree at `origin/main`:
  the failing-id sets differ by one known-flaky timing test only.
- No behaviour change outside the test: the diff is one file, five added lines.

## Relationship to the other open work

#110728 is an umbrella report listing several files whose gateway tests do not isolate
themselves from ambient runner state. The two open cars for it fix different files and
different causes — #110732 (update / Desktop cold-start liveness) and #110750 (local-models
quickstart isolation) — and neither touches `tests/gateway/test_media_download_retry.py`.
This change is the system-proxy leg of that report and is complementary to both.

Closes #110728 (system-proxy leg).

author: kevindetry-milaboratories
body:
Bump every pframes-rs artifact the SDK pins to 1.1.60, and the Python runenv that bundles the matching wheel. ## Why - pframes-rs 1.1.59 folds same-axis n-ary joins as a balanced tree, so tables with hundreds of per-sample columns no longer overflow the Tokio worker stack and kill the host process ([MILAB-6925](https://app.notion.com/p/3db3a83ff4af8165942bd6de9cd10afd), [pframes-rs#296](https://github.com/milaboratory/pframes-rs/pull/296)). - pframes-rs 1.1.60 adds the outer join fix for primary-less axis groups (MILAB-6852, [pframes-rs#293](https://github.com/milaboratory/pframes-rs/pull/293)). Both are bug fixes with no new API, so `REQUIRES_PFRAMES_VERSION` stays unchanged. Blocks built against this SDK still load on older desktop apps. ## Changes | File | Change | |---|---| | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | `@milaboratories/pframes-rs-node` 1.1.56 to 1.1.60 (exec plane: `pf-driver`, `pl-middle-layer`). `@milaboratories/pframes-rs-wasip2` 1.1.56 to 1.1.60 (spec plane: `pf-spec`, `workflow-tengo`). `@platforma-open/milaboratories.runenv-python-3` 1.11.4 to 1.13.1. | | `lib/ptabler/software/src/requirements.txt` | `polars-pf` 1.1.56 to 1.1.60, the Python wheel built from the same engine. | | `package.json` | `better-sqlite3` added to `pnpm.neverBuiltDependencies`. See below. | | `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Refreshed. Also resolves `pframes-rs-serv` 1.1.60 and `better-sqlite3` 13.0.3. | | `.changeset/balanced-join-fold.md` | Patch for `pf-driver`, `pl-middle-layer`, `pf-spec`, `workflow-tengo`, `software-ptabler`. | ## Why the runenv bump ptabler pins `polars-pf` in its requirements and installs it offline from the wheels bundled in the `runenv-python-3` package. The first CI run of this PR failed all 92 ptabler-based workflow tests with: ``` ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement polars-pf==1.1.59 (from versions: 1.1.56) ``` [runenv-python-3#107](https://github.com/platforma-open/runenv-python-3/pull/107) moved the runenv to `polars-pf` 1.1.60 and was released as 1.13.1 (`python-3.12.10` 1.3.25). This PR pins that release. The jump from 1.11.4 also picks up the 1.12 and 1.13 runenv releases. ## Why `neverBuiltDependencies` The new `pframes-rs-serv` pins `better-sqlite3` 13.0.3. That version ships prebuilt N-API binaries, sets `gypfile: false`, and has no install script, but pnpm 9 still runs `node-gyp rebuild` because a `binding.gyp` is present. Without the entry, `pnpm install` fails with `node-gyp: command not found` on a machine without node-gyp. The prebuilt binary loads and runs on Node 22 and 24. ## Verification - Full monorepo build passes. - `pf-driver` vitest: 54 passed, including the tests that drive the native addon. - `pf-spec` vitest: 17 passed against the 1.1.60 WASM component. - ptabler Python suite with the 1.1.60 wheel: 315 passed. - The desktop app bump of `pframes-rs-node` is tracked separately, together with the removal of `pframes-rs-wasm`.

Greptile Summary

This PR updates the SDK’s JavaScript, WASI, and Python pframes-rs packages to 1.1.60. The release adds balanced same-axis joins and an outer-join fix, while the matching Python run environment keeps offline ptabler installs working. - Updates native and WASI pframes-rs packages from 1.1.56 to 1.1.60. - Pins ptabler to the matching `polars-pf` 1.1.60 wheel and run environment 1.13.1. - Lets pnpm use the prebuilt `better-sqlite3` binary without running a local build.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 The PR appears safe to merge. The engine pins and Python wheel stay aligned at `1.1.60`. The lockfile matches the catalog and runenv changes.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | pnpm-workspace.yaml | Moves the Node, WASI, and Python runenv catalog pins to matching releases. | | lib/ptabler/software/src/requirements.txt | Pins `polars-pf` to `1.1.60`, matching the updated offline runenv. | | package.json | Adds `better-sqlite3` to `neverBuiltDependencies` so pnpm does not try an unneeded native rebuild. | | pnpm-lock.yaml | Locks the pframes packages, matching runenv artifacts, and `better-sqlite3` at their new versions. | | .changeset/balanced-join-fold.md | Adds patch releases for all packages that ship or use the updated engines. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant App as SDK caller participant Node as pframes-rs-node 1.1.60 participant Serv as pframes-rs-serv 1.1.60 participant DB as better-sqlite3 13.0.3 participant Py as ptabler participant Env as runenv-python-3 1.13.1 App->>Node: Run pframes work Node->>Serv: Start engine service Serv->>DB: Use shipped native binary App->>Py: Run table workflow Py->>Env: Install offline requirements Env-->>Py: Supply polars-pf 1.1.60 Py-->>App: Return table result ```

author: tamnd
body:
The scan hands out one morsel per row group since #487, and the next thing on the roadmap is a driver that reads several of them at once. The moment that lands, a plain SELECT with no ORDER BY returns its rows in whatever order the threads happened to finish in, and it returns a different one on the next run. SQL does not promise an order, so it is not wrong, but every engine anybody actually uses gives back the file order for a query like that and a user who sees the rows move around reports it as a bug. This is the piece that stops the scheduler from having to care.

A chunk arriving at the sink came from exactly one morsel, because every streaming operator transforms a chunk in place and none of them merges chunks across morsels. So the morsel number and the position within the morsel totally order the output in source order, and the only thing missing was for the sink to be told which morsel it is being fed from. That is the new Sink::at, called once per morsel by the driver on the instance that took it, with a default that does nothing because every sink in the tree but one has no use for it.

The one that has a use for it is the root. root_in_order sits next to root and holds chunks whose turn has not come, releasing them once no instance is still reading a morsel cut before theirs. That is DuckDB's minimum batch index scheme under another name. root keeps today's behaviour and is what a query with an ORDER BY under it wants, because the operator below has already put the rows where it wants them and holding them back would only add latency.

The capacity bound needed one rule to not become a deadlock. An instance is told to wait on held chunks only when a morsel cut before its own is still being read, so the instance holding the earliest morsel is never told to wait and there is always somebody who can make progress. There is a test for exactly that, because it is the sort of thing that works on one thread and hangs on sixteen.

The tests drive two instances by hand with morsels finishing out of order, since there is no parallel driver yet to do it for real. No speed change on one thread and none expected: run_serial takes one morsel at a time, so the ordered root holds one morsel's chunks and hands them over when the next morsel starts.

run_serial is still not on the execution path, so this is machinery ahead of its consumer. Worth landing now anyway, because items 6 and 7 of the roadmap would otherwise produce wrong answers first and get this retrofitted afterwards.

Part of #486, stage one. Milestone F4, #349.

author: 0x1abin
body:
## Summary

On touch devices, completing a WeRead download could leave the activity in `OpenBook`: `silentRestartToReader()` stopped Wi-Fi and returned without opening the reader. If the download had already exceeded the inactivity timeout, the next loop could enter sleep with the previous progress screen retained.

Remove the touch-only early return so reader-targeted restarts always set the RTC destination, display the loading popup, and reboot into the book. Rebooting also starts a fresh inactivity timer. The deep-sleep guard and ordinary `silentRestart()` touch behavior remain intact. The shared reader restart is also used by font download, KOReader sync, and WeRead progress sync; those callers were inspected. This pre-existing defect was identified while investigating reports following #298; it was not introduced by that PR.

## Validation

- Added a host test that compiles the actual restart functions with platform stubs. It fails on the original touch branch and passes after the fix, covering both touch capability configurations, reader/font-prompt targets, the sleep guard, and unchanged touch behavior for ordinary home restarts.
- All 55 Python discovery tests passed.
- `./bin/ci-check` passed: formatting, cppcheck, all 549 host tests, and builds for default (X3/X4), Sticky, X4 Pro, EEGO A4, Murphy M4, Waveshare 3.97, and Paper Mono.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Hardware verification remains pending. The WeRead README records acceptance steps for downloads longer than the sleep timeout, disabled auto-sleep, preserved EPUB/progress, and reopening on touch devices and X3/X4.

## Scope Check

- [x] Read SCOPE.md and ROADMAP.md; this fixes an existing download-to-reader transition.
- [x] No new theme, connector, application, dependency, setting, public API, or cache format.
- No SDK, HAL, bootloader, OTA, or recovery changes. The application restart helper now honors its reader destination on touch devices too.
- No new heap allocations; production code only removes the three-line early-return branch. No measured performance or memory improvement is claimed.

### AI Usage

YES — implementation, review, and validation were assisted by Codex.

author: chesedd
body:
### Motivation

- The full-viewport `backdrop-filter: blur(...)` on the tutorial journal forces the browser to composite and blur the entire viewport and is the prime suspect for input lag when the journal is open.
- The success animation used `transform` on the whole journal spread which also risks triggering expensive layer work on editor content.
- The change aims to remove costly compositing triggers while preserving the book look and layout so Monaco/`player.py` input remains smooth.

### Description

- Remove `backdrop-filter: blur(4px)` from `.journal-backdrop` and keep the darkened background color (`background: rgb(3 9 13 / 78%)`).
- Replace the spread success feedback to only use opacity (remove `transform: scale(...)` and the `transform` transition) so the success state no longer transforms the entire spread.
- Keep visual book details (paper color, texture gradients, central fold, tabs, and box-shadow) intact and only avoid viewport-filtering effects that force full-viewport recompositing.
- Add a CSS regression test `frontend/tests/journalEffects.test.mjs` that asserts `.journal-backdrop` contains a `background` declaration and does not contain `filter`/`backdrop-filter`, and that `.journal-spread`/`.journal-success` do not use `transform`-based transitions.

### Testing

- Ran `npm test` and all test subtests (including the new `journalEffects` tests) passed successfully.
- Ran `npm run lint` with no lint failures reported.
- Ran `npm run build` and the build completed successfully (build warnings only about chunk size and externalized modules were observed). 
- Ran `git diff --check` and repository checks passed; the patch commited as a single change removing the expensive backdrop and transform usage.

## מה זה עושה
מאפשר למנהל להוסיף משתמש **בלי לשלוח מייל הזמנה**. בחלון הוספת המשתמשים (הגדרות → משתמשים) נוספה תיבת סימון **"שליחת קישור הזמנה במייל עכשיו"** — **מסומנת כברירת מחדל**.

- **מסומנת** → התנהגות קיימת: נשלח קישור הזמנה בדוא״ל.

author: wiktorstarczewski
body:
Fixes #878. A signed write (send, claim, swap, account creation) no longer strands a WASM client and an IndexedDB connection: each realm keeps one `MidenClientInterface` for every read and write, and its SDK keystore routes to callbacks the realm installs once instead of rebuilding the client to carry them.

- `installRealmKeystore` / `uninstallRealmKeystore` (`src/lib/miden/sdk/miden-client.ts`) hold the realm's `sign`, `insertKey` and `getKey` callbacks, typed with the SDK's own aliases; `getMidenClient()` takes no options and is never rebuilt for a call.
- The client's SDK keystore holds stable trampolines: a sign reaching a replaced client is refused with `WasmClientPoisonedError`; an insert reaching one lands only while the installed sink is the one that client's build was retired against (a per-sink id the build's trampolines carry, so no closure over a vault key is retained; the SDK has persisted the account by the time it asks); `getKey` has no installer and is refused by name; a call made before the realm installed a callback fails with a named error, and `MidenClientInterface.create` fills any keystore member its caller left out with a refusal that names it. A refusal on a replaced client also logs its kind and the two generations, since only the message crosses the SDK boundary.
- `Actions.init` installs the vault signer in every realm that writes (service worker, mobile, desktop); the popup never runs it and never signs. The four proxy writes, the guardian pipeline and the E2E swap hooks no longer carry a signer of their own (the proxy's `signCallback` argument is the flag-ON op's reverse-IPC signer and is unused inline).
- A vault installs its insert-key sink when it takes its key; `lock()` retires only the vault it locks (a spawn's or an in-flight unlock's sink survives a lock), and when a flow that constructed a vault ends, adopted or not, the realm's sink is re-derived from the store (`syncRealmInsertKeySink` in `actions.ts`); each slot transition leaves one log line with the sink id. Wallet creation and import ride the accounts write queue, like unlock, and every flow constructs its vault inside the try whose finally re-derives the sink (the constructors say so). A hold in which an adopted vault inserts key material first asserts the sink is its own and otherwise refuses as locked, so a lock that landed while a create or import waited on the queue fails it before any irreversible step.
- A locked vault reported by a sign is recorded under the WASM lock hold the sign ran for, and `withWasmClientLock` carries it out on that hold's own rejection (`.reason = 'locked'`, the tag the offscreen path already sets per op); the transaction loop reads only the error. No ambient record: a dry run's or an earlier write's locked sign can no longer requeue an unrelated failure, and the SDK's `lastAuthError()`, which clears only on the next successful sign, is not consulted.
- Every E2E hook call on the shared client runs under a labelled hold spanning the call and its reads (the swap hooks, the store's guardian hook), asserting the hold is still current after each parking await and before each reach-through (never after a submit; `exportNote` gets the check through its own seam), and reporting the failing step's label; every Vault construction and insert hold is labelled too. Nothing on the accounts write queue waits unbounded (the guardian recovery lookup and the spawn's first client build are bounded like their siblings).
- The offscreen realm already kept one client with a per-op reverse-IPC signer and is unchanged.

<details><summary>Why realm-level callbacks</summary>

`MidenClient.create` fixes the SDK keystore at creation, so a per-write signer meant a per-write client, and in 0.16 nothing releases a client built in its own realm (#868, #869). Each realm has exactly one signer (the vault) and one insert-key sink (the vault's key), which is how the offscreen realm was already wired; declaring them per lock hold instead had two execute sites forget to (the dApp dry run, send speculation), a class of bug that installing once per realm removes. Sink ownership is by identity for `lock()` (a vault removes only the sink it installed, so a lock never clears a flow still constructing) and by the store at the end of every constructing flow (a failed unlock or spawn cannot leave its sink installed; a failed re-unlock over a Ready vault keeps the Ready vault's sink). The sign record is keyed by the lock hold because the mutex holder is the only flow inside a WASM call: a record nobody else can read replaces the realm-wide slot that two review rounds showed could bleed a dry run's or an earlier write's `locked` into a later, unrelated failure.
</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `miden-client.test.ts`: the singleton memoizes; the trampolines route to the installed callbacks and refuse before an install; uninstall drops only the callback it names; a locked sign rides out on its own hold's rejection and on no other, a later successful sign clears it, a refused sign on a replaced client touches nothing; a replaced client's trampoline refuses.
- `actions.test.ts`: init installs the signer (hex in, bytes out; a locked vault reaches the SDK classified); lock retires the vault it locks and nothing else; adopting a vault installs its sink; a failed unlock, spawn or import leaves the sink as the store has it; an import queued behind a spawn waits for it.
- `vault.test.ts`: spawn and import install the sink before their first insert; retire uninstalls that same sink; every create arm and the private-key import refuse as locked after a `retire()`, before any WASM step. `sign-callback.test.ts`: the classification the SDK boundary carries. `transactions.branches.test.ts`: the loop defers on the hold's tag with no locked text and fails an untagged rejection; `isLockedError` on the boundary's exact shape (`<context>: JsValue(Error: <message>)`). `miden-client-proxy.test.ts`: every inline write asks for the singleton with no options and never calls the per-write signer. `miden-client-interface.test.ts`: a client created with a signer alone gets named refusals for `getKey` and `insertKey`; the guardian recovery adopts each match under its own labelled hold, refuses a client replaced during the lookup, and stops before the cold-key insert when evicted mid-adoption. `test-hooks.test.ts`: eleven revocation cases, each proving the next client call never runs and the response names the hold and step, against the real poison error shape; every mocked record accessor requires the hold. `vault.test.ts` pins the spawn's exact hold sequence with no nesting.
- Fifty-one mutation proofs, each failing its named test: no install in init, trampoline ignores the installed callback, a replaced client still routes, lock does not retire, uninstall ignores identity, spawn constructs late, signer untagged, trampoline records nothing, the lock does not tag, no clear at the next attempt, a refused sign records under the successor, per-write options return, spawn flows off the queue, the three flows' missing resync, the insert assertion dropped or moved below the guardian arm, the identity predicate ignoring identity, the restore constructing late, the classifier's type guard and the loop's abandonment guard dropped, the getKey slot restored, the replaced-client insert judged by the latest retirement instead of its own build, a fresh id on every sink install, a hook unlocked, the poison path not stamping, the recovery lookup unbounded, the spawn acquiring its client outside a hold, the absent keystore members coerced with `!`, the flag-OFF consume calling the per-write signer, a hook's after-import or after-build check dropped, the recovery adoption outside or hoisted above its per-match hold or skipped, the hook error text without its cause, the vault read after `locked()`, the sink ignoring the store status, the spawn hold unlabelled, the sign refusal unlogged, the recovery inse

author: raeesnazeem-cpu
body:
## What

Adds a fourth run type, **`full_scan`**: a standalone QA pass triggered from inside a TED project. An operator enters a site URL and clicks **Scan**; QACC runs the **entire** check suite against that one URL and posts a single timestamped report to the project's `release.qa_post` parent task. A separate **Send to Fix** action runs the existing GitOps fix pass, and video recording runs as the last step of the fix module (proof of the final state).

## Behaviour (per the agreed spec)

- **Triggered from TED, URL is the input.** `POST /webhooks/ted/full-scan { trigger: { url, clientId?, clientName? } }` → returns `qaRunId`.
- **Test / Fix split.** The scan always publishes its own report (never deferred to the fix pass). Fix is on-demand: `POST /webhooks/ted/full-scan/fix { runId }`.
- **Ad-hoc.** No dedupe — may run any number of times a day; each run is its own record.
- **Never changes task status.** A full scan only comments on `release.qa_post`; it does not move it In Progress / Completed.
- **Video** runs as the final step of the fix module, to the parent task, without changing status.
- **All checks, graceful lapse.** Checks that need inputs a URL-only scan may lack (backend/WP, live-URL, woocommerce) self-lapse rather than fail.

## Safety / non-impact

Every behavioural change is gated on `run_type === 'full_scan'`. Pre-release / internal-QA / post-release runs are untouched — they build their own `enabled_checks` and keep their exact status/report/fix flow.

## Changes

- **migration** `20260914000000_add_full_scan_run_type.sql` — widen `qa_runs_run_type_check` to allow `full_scan`
- **packages/shared** — add `full_scan` to the `run_type` zod enum
- **apps/api/webhooks** — `FULL_SCAN_CHECKS`; the scan + fix receivers (no status changes)
- **apps/worker/tedSync** — don't defer the report for full_scan; "Full Scan" label + timestamp in the header; never complete full_scan task status
- **apps/worker/crawlPageJob** — full_scan scan closeout: report only, no auto-fix, release the run slot
- **apps/worker/aiFixRunJob** — full_scan: run the video barrier as the last step, no status completion
- **apps/worker/videoRecordingJob** — parent-only full_scan mode: post the proof to the parent, skip the sibling gate, never flip status

## Notes

- The fix module requires `AI_FIX_MODULE_ENABLED=true` in the worker env (unchanged).
- TED-facing contract (endpoints + payloads) is documented separately for the TED team.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` passes for both `apps/worker` and `apps/api` (the only two API errors are pre-existing, in unrelated `scratch/`/`scripts/` files missing `@google/generative-ai`).

author: kodawah
body:
Adds the one fact TCGplayer's own catalog never carries for this game -
artist credit - so a downstream matcher finally has a way to tell apart
two products that share a number and, once the qualifier folds into a
variant, an identical name.

## The gap this closes

Two rows in `ROS008` ("Aurora") both read `name: "Aurora (Marvel)"` -
`ros008_565391_coldfoil` (plain) and `ros008_565392_coldfoil`
(`promoTypes: [alternateart]`) - and nothing in the datastore said which
of SCG's two skus, sold as "Aurora (Asur Misoa)" and "Aurora (Ramza
Ardyputra)", was which. Guessing would have shipped a wrong mapping,
which is worse than the honest collision it was left as.

## The fix

`the-fab-cube`'s own dataset - already fetched for the `fabId` join -
carries `artists` per row, keyed by the same `tcgplayer_product_id` this
build already reads. This wires it straight through:

```json
{"id": "ros008_565391_coldfoil", "artist": "Ramza Ardyputra", ...}
{"id": "ros008_565392_coldfoil", "artist": "Asur Misoa", ...}
```

The credit is the **union** of every dataset row naming a product, not
the first row seen. A fused product's two rows each carry only one
face's artist ("Athiwut B." for Aether Ashwing's side, "Surya Prasteya"
for Ash's) - picking one would credit a two-sided token for half its
own art. Caught this the hard way: a first pass logged ~150 "artist
disagreements" that turned out to all be two-faced cards, not data
errors.

## Coverage

    fleshandblood: 0 -> 15331 of 17547 card entries carry an artist

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l` clean, `go test -race ./...` green.
- Rebuilt the full datastore against the currently-published TCGplayer
  catalog dump and diffed it against the live `output/fleshandblood.json`:
  identical on every card and every other field, 0 ids added or removed -
  purely additive.
- Loaded the rebuilt datastore through go-mtgban's real `fleshandblood.Load`
  and read `Artist` off live `CardObject`s for the Aurora pair, the fused
  Ashwing/Ash token, and Pleiades Superstar; the Pleiades value
  ("Livia Prima") independently matches the artist credit on SCG's own
  product page for that exact card.

Companion PR on go-mtgban: wires `DatastoreCard.Artist` through to
`mtgmatcher.Card.Artist`, which already exists and is populated for every
other game.

author: basgenix4u
body:
## What

Research records move from process memory to **PostgreSQL with row-level security**:

- `PrismaRecordRepository` — production adapter behind the existing `RecordRepository` port; every operation runs inside `withTenant` so RLS enforces the tenant boundary. Keyset pagination on `(updatedAt, id)`, opaque cursor, new composite index.
- Owner is the **authenticated principal** (`@CurrentUser()`), never a fixed dev actor or client-supplied value.
- Schema + migration: deposit metadata columns the API accepted but the table lacked (equipment, external partner, publication/patent refs, related records, supervisors).

## Verification

- 179 api · 29 contracts · 36 web unit tests
- **40/40 integration tests** against real PostgreSQL, including 5 new: durable create, round-trip, **RLS invisibility without owner/tenant context**, edit persistence, exact pagination
- tsc, lint, build, `pnpm audit` clean

## Security checklist

- [x] Every query path runs under a tenant context (RLS is the backstop)
- [x] No new tenant table (columns only, on an existing RLS-guarded table)
- [x] No scores introduced
- [x] Public projections untouched
- [x] Errors remain RFC 9457

author: moudabdelwahab
body:
PR منفصل لتأمين `create-api-token` كما طُلب.

## الثغرة

الدالة المنشورة (v5) تتحقق من الجلسة ثم **تُنشئ المفتاح لأي حساب مسجّل**:

```ts
const { data: userData } = await userClient.auth.getUser();
if (userError || !userData?.user) return 401;
const userId = userData.user.id;      // ← ولا فحص بعدها إطلاقًا
```

ولا فحص لرتبة، ولا لعلاقة بشركة، ولا لاستحقاق. و`ALLOWED_SCOPES` فيها تشمل `admin:full` و`settings:manage` و`oauth:manage` — أي أن **أي عميل** يقدر بنداء مباشر (`curl`) أن يصدر لنفسه مفتاحًا بصلاحيات مشغّل المنصة.

إخفاء هذه الخيارات في لوحة الشركة لا يمنع ذلك بحال. الواجهة ليست حاجزًا.

## `migrations/036` — القرار في القاعدة

| الدالة | الدور |
|---|---|
| `can_create_api_token()` | طاقم منصة، أو مدير شركة (الدور **و** العلاقة) باستحقاق `api_tokens` فعّال. `company_user` مستثنى صراحةً — العضوية ليست ترقية |
| `api_token_scope_ceiling()` | سقف الصلاحيات لكل نطاق سلطة. سقف الشركة **لا يشمل** صلاحيات مشغّل المنصة الثلاث |
| `api_token_issue_context()` | القرار والسقف والنطاق في **نداء واحد ذرّي**، فلا تنفصل الشروط ولا تُعاد صياغتها في لغة ثانية |

**ولا دالة من الثلاث تقبل مُعامل هوية** — فتزوير المعرّفات مستحيل بنيويًا لا ممنوع فقط. اختبار يفشل إن أُضيف مُعامل يومًا.

### التحقق من الإنتاج بعد التطبيق

الترحيل مُطبَّق ومُتحقَّق منه بانتحال هوية مالك الشركة داخل معاملة انتهت بـ`ROLLBACK`:

| الفحص | النتيجة |
|---|---|
| `allowed` · `actor` | `true` · `company_admin` |
| حجم السقف | **20** من 23 |
| `admin:full` · `settings:manage` في السقف | **false** · **false** |
| `tickets:read` في السقف | **true** |

## الدالة المُحصَّنة (في المستودع، **بلا نشر**)

- التفويض بنداء واحد للقاعدة بهوية المنادي. **ولا فحص رتبة في TypeScript** — إعادة بنائه كانت ستصنع نسخة ثانية من قاعدة الصلاحية تنحرف عن الأولى.
- **سقف الصلاحيات يأتي من القاعدة لا من ثابت في الملف**، وأي صلاحية خارجه تُرفض بـ`403`. فحساب شركة لا يبلغ `admin:full` مهما أرسل.
- رسالة رفض موحّدة لكل الأسباب: التمييز بين «لست مديرًا» و«لا استحقاق» يكشف حالة حساب الشركة لمن لا يملكه.
- تاريخ الانتهاء لا يقبل الماضي، وسقفه سنتان.
- السرّ يُعاد **مرة واحدة** ولا يُسجَّل في أي `console`؛ والمخزَّن بصمة مشفَّرة لا القيمة — فلا الخادم نفسه يقدر على عرضه لاحقًا.
- القيم الداخلية لصفّ Bearer عشوائية ولا تُعاد للمستخدم.
- **الافتراضيات لم تتوسّع** عن الإصدار المنشور: توسيعها كان سيمنح صلاحيات جديدة ضمنيًا لكل مفتاح يُنشأ بلا `scopes` صريحة.

## المصفوفة المطلوبة — كلها مُختبَرة

`tests/sql/api-token-authorization.test.sql` — **9 تأكيدات**:

| الحالة | النتيجة |
|---|---|
| مدير شركة مصرَّح له | ✅ يسمح |
| `company_user` | ⛔ يُمنع (ولا يرث المدير) |
| شركة بلا استحقاق `api_tokens` | ⛔ تُمنع |
| عميل بلا شركة | ⛔ يُمنع |
| مجهول الهوية | ⛔ يُمنع، وسقفه فارغ |
| تزوير المعرّفات | ⛔ مستحيل بنيويًا |
| طاقم المنصة | ✅ السقف الكامل، ولم يفقد شيئًا |
| `anon` على مستوى الصلاحيات | ⛔ محجوب |
| صلاحيات مشغّل المنصة في سقف الشركة | ⛔ خارجه |

`tests/api-token-function-static.test.mjs` — **15 فحصًا** على مصدر الدالتين تُثبِت الخصائص الأمنية من الكود نفسه (بعد تجريده من التعليقات، فالفحص ينظر إلى الكود لا إلى شرحه): لا فحص رتبة محلي، لا قراءة معرّف من جسم الطلب، لا تسجيل للسرّ، والسقف من القاعدة.

**478 اختبار node · 22 ملف SQL — كلها ناجحة.**

## ما لم يحدث

**لم تُنشَر أي دالة.** النسخة المُحصَّنة في المستودع فقط، والنشر قرارك.

حتى يتم النشر: السقف مفروض في القاعدة ومُعلَن في الواجهة، لكن الدالة المنشورة ما زالت تقبل ما يُرسَل إليها — وهو ما يجعل النشر خطوة **مطلوبة لا تجميلية**.

body: ## Description IssueOps `save_registry` wrote a bare agents array after registration/removal. Production `registry.json` is a LiteRegistry object (`version` / `updated_at` / `agents`). A successful IssueOps run demoted the file to an array; CI `validate_registry.py` still accepted arrays, so PRs could auto-merge. Python `discover_from_registry` / `LiteRegistry.model_validate_json` then fail for all SDK consumers, while the web app still works because it accepts both shapes. `save_registry` now always persists `{version, updated_at, agents}`, preserving an existing `version` when present and refreshing `updated_at`. ## User Value Keeps the public Lite Registry readable by the Python SDK after IssueOps registration/removal, avoiding a silent discovery outage for MarketClient and related tooling. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ## How Has This Been Tested? - [x] `uv run pytest tests/scripts/test_process_registration.py tests/scripts/test_process_removal.py --tb=short -q` (41 passed) - [x] Regression coverage: object envelope on save, preserve version, upgrade bare array → object ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes - [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules

author: victor-falcon
body:
The paywall passed `pinFooter` to `StepScreen`, which kept its footer `position: sticky; bottom: 0` with an opaque background at **every** width, not just on phones. That footer is 229.5px tall, so on any window shorter than ~900px it painted over the content underneath it.

Measured at 780×630, at first paint:

| Element | Covered by the footer |
| --- | --- |
| "Your AI assistant" row | 92% |
| "Monthly" plan row | 100% |
| "Yearly" plan row (the default selection) | 100% |

~229px hidden, 36% of the viewport. You landed on a screen titled "Choose your plan" with no plan on it.

Worth noting the same happened at **1280×720** — one of the two sizes the original pinning was measured against. The comment there reasoned that an inline footer would put the primary action 137px below the fold; what it did not account for is that pinning it instead hides the plans. On a plan chooser that is the worse half of the trade.

## The fix

Drop `pinFooter`. The footer falls back to the path every other step already uses — sticky on phones, inline from `md` up. Nothing else in the codebase passed the prop, so it goes too, which is most of the diff.

## The cost, measured

Scroll needed for "Start a plan" to be fully visible:

| Viewport | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1440×900 | 0px | **0px** |
| 1280×720 | 0px | **137px** |
| 780×630 | 0px | **227px** |
| 390×844 (phone) | 0px | **0px** — unchanged, still pinned |

So the fix costs exactly the 137px the original comment predicted at 1280×720. In exchange, both plan rows, both feature rows and "Continue with the free plan" are visible without scrolling at every size, and the footer can no longer intersect any row at any scroll position — it is in flow, permanently ~66px below the Yearly row.

## Before / After (780×630, first paint)

### Before

![Paywall at 780x630 before the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/694baa42-7d36-47d9-992e-9f5505c855b9)

### After

![Paywall at 780x630 after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43ad1d3f-efe4-46da-a6f9-1416612df5c0)

## QA

Browser QA on the soft gate at 780×630, 1280×720, 1440×900 and 390×844:

- Footer computes `static` at all three desktop widths and `sticky` at 390×844, as intended.
- No footer/row intersection at scroll-top or at full scroll, at any width.
- Mobile is untouched: footer still pins at 229.5px, both buttons inside the viewport with no scrolling.
- Plan selection still works — clicking Monthly/Yearly moves the check and updates the checkout href and the trial copy.
- An onboarding step that never used `pinFooter` renders identically before and after (sticky at 390×844, static at 1440×900), confirming the prop removal disturbed nothing else.
- No console errors or warnings.

## Tests

No new test: this is a layout prop removal, and what it fixes is a paint overlap that only exists once a browser lays the page out. `paywall.test.tsx` (jsdom) renders the page and is unaffected — it passes unchanged, along with the rest of the suite.

author: alexander-zimmermann
body:
## Why

The Discord agent answered "Wo ist das Licht an?" with nine lights, all off. `get_current_knx(function="Beleuchtung", only_active=True)` had returned `Dimmen-Absolut` = 100 % and `Ein/Aus` = true from days ago: on an actuator the suffix-less datapoint is the command, and its retained value is the last order sent, not the device now. The `-Status` siblings all said off. The docstring promises "which lights are on?", so this is the tool's job, not the caller's.

Neither `dpt` nor the catalog's `writable` flag separates the two reliably (`Dimmen-Status` shares 5.001 with its command; 32 `Ein/Aus-Status` GAs are writable). The naming convention does, consistently across `Beleuchtung`, `Beschattung` and `Schalten`.

## What

- Every state carries `role`: `status` (a `-Status` datapoint), `command` (the datapoint it reports on: the same name without the suffix, or one extending it with a dash — `Dimmen-Absolut`/`Dimmen-Relativ` for `Dimmen-Status`), `reading` (everything else: sensors, meters, `-Anomalie`).
- Siblings are looked up in the whole catalog per device (`name LIKE ANY(...)`), not in the caller's filtered match, so `name="Dimmen-Absolut"` alone still yields `command`.
- `only_active=True` keeps status and reading rows that are on and drops commands.
- Docstrings (tool and implementation), result `note`, README row.

## Tests

Seed gains a kitchen device with `Switch`/`Switch-Status` and `Dim-Absolute`/`Dim-Status`; five new tests cover role derivation, readings without a status sibling, `only_active` skipping stale orders and reporting status on, and the command role surviving a narrow filter. Full suite: 178 passed; ruff, format and mypy clean.

## Not done

Putting the role into the catalog itself (ETS export → `ga_catalog` column) would be the canonical place, but touches three repos and the schema for one field the name already carries.

author: dmihai91
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #165. That PR made the Docker site-runtime Caddyfile answer real 404s (`try_files {path} {path}/ =404` plus a `handle_errors` block serving the template's own `404.html` with the shared security headers), but the filesystem-mode snippet in `apps/deploy-agent/src/caddy-snippet.ts` — used when a site (or preview) is served directly by the front Caddy instead of a container — still carried the old `try_files ... /index.html` fallback, which silently served the home page for any unknown path.

- `serveLines`'s `'static'` branch now mirrors the runtime's rule exactly: `try_files {path} {path}/ =404`, `file_server`, then a `handle_errors` block that rewrites a 404 to `/404.html` and serves it, falling back to Caddy's own built-in error page if a build shipped no `404.html`. Trailing-slash and directory-index behavior for real pages is unchanged.
- The site's security headers (`renderCaddyHeaderLines`, from #134) are now reapplied inside `handle_errors`, so a 404 response carries the same CSP as every other page — the filesystem-mode equivalent of the Docker runtime's macro-imported headers.
- `buildCaddySnippet` and `buildPreviewCaddySnippet` both route through the same `serveLines`, so previews agent mode (`MODE=previews`) on the filesystem runtime gets the same fix without a separate code path. A `'proxy'` `ServeTarget` (Docker runtime) is untouched — that container answers its own errors via its own Caddyfile, which is #165's concern.
- Corrected the stale snippet template in the `flowstarter-deploy-site` skill's `api-contract.md`, which still documented the old `index.html` fallback.

Note: #165 is still open (not yet merged) as of this PR, so this branch is based on current `main` and does not yet include that Caddyfile change. Rebase after #165 merges.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` in `apps/deploy-agent` — 192 pass, 0 fail (18 in `caddy-snippet.test.ts`, including 3 new tests: an unknown path on a site's static target 404s via `404.html`; same for a preview's static target; the 404 response carries the site's security headers)

author: timurproko
body:
## Summary
Implements the accepted OpenSpec change `fix-response-copy-freeze` from specification PRs #359 and #365, initially based on `71e97ab6`, now rebased onto `26b51b0b` with the accepted rendering, compaction, timestamp, and right-edge selection changes preserved.

- Immutable selected-range snapshots; bounded copy coordination and killable native/encoding helper; destination-correct, bounded OSC 52 fallback through the existing writer.
- Independent native and terminal-provided paste; isolated acquisition/classification/image preparation, 5-second acquisition and 15-second insertion lifetimes, eight distinct reservations, cancellation and recovery.
- Prompt copy/cut and workflow/tree copying share the write fence. Later independent paste does not inherit a completed copy failure.
- Preserve chip/image/selection/undo semantics, fix provisional chip cleanup, bound fragmented input, and add opt-in payload-free diagnostics.
- Fix stack overflow in hyperlink tokenization with an equivalent linear scanner.
- User-approved compact-path refinement: budget individual path-chip presentation at 4,096 UTF-16 units per paste, including framing and a 20-unit suffix allowance per occurrence. Over-budget lists become one existing text-paste chip in the isolated preparer, retaining every expanded path in order. Small lists and the synchronous compatibility classifier remain unchanged.
- User-approved spec/code refinement: cap URL-chip OSC 8 metadata at 65,536 UTF-8 bytes per editor render, including framing and cleanup across repeated occurrences/rows. Reject oversized metadata before encoding/construction; preserve the full URL, chip, atomic editing, and exact copy/history/submission expansion.

## Ready for review at user request — physical acceptance pending, do not merge
The earlier near-16 MiB URL produced a ~16 MiB terminal write despite its compact chip, with a 305 ms synthetic application timer gap. The user approved updating this PR's planning artifacts and implementation together to omit oversized explicit hyperlink metadata. That refinement is now implemented and covered by deterministic byte/content/output tests. One augmented native/bracketed run recorded 6,563 maximum write bytes and roughly 48/55 ms maximum timer gaps; workloads include extra content/typing checks, and these are not physical acceptance measurements.

Tasks 1.2, 1.3, 2.3, 4.4, and 5.6 now have diagnostics/composition, generated baseline, copy-clear/cache, real helper capacity/exit/conversion, and session teardown evidence. Indexed owned atomic segmentation avoids enumerating discarded chip interiors without modifying pinned source.

**Compact fallback implemented (tasks 5.3/5.8):** the same 6,000 long-named paths now produce 30 editor characters instead of 1,014,006, with about 18.3/18.5 ms synthetic native/bracketed timer gaps instead of the earlier 1.39-second gap. All full classified paths remain behind the compact chip without additional separators or re-normalization. The former observational probes now assert compactness, exact content/history, following input, undo/redo, bounded writes, and no duplicate acquisition; near-16 MiB inputs also exercise safe original-text fallback when probes time out. Cold emitted helpers and invalid-prefix fallback are covered.

The integrated automated fault/content matrix passed (task 6.1). Latest-candidate CI and physical route/clipboard acceptance remain open. The user's actual Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V freeze cause is still unconfirmed. The planned code changes and automated regression matrix are implemented. The user requested removing draft status and running normal pull-request CI. Ready-for-review status is not physical acceptance or merge authorization; any observed freeze still fails acceptance.

author: ashishawasthi
body:
## What was wrong

This service read the caller's identity from `x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion` and nothing else.

`x-goog-*` is Google's reserved namespace, and the serverless frontend **removes that whole
namespace** from a request entering a service, so an embedding host behind IAP cannot hand a
downstream application the assertion its own edge was given: the host sets the reserved name, the
frontend drops it, and the service refuses *"request did not pass through IAP"* about a request
that passed through IAP one hop earlier. The broker already injects the same value under
`x-portal-iap-assertion` for exactly this reason.

So this service would have answered **401 to every authenticated caller the day it was embedded**,
with a green gate, a healthy console and a passing offline suite.

## Why nothing reported it

Three things hid it, and each is worth keeping:

- The unit suite **builds its own request**, so it could only ever choose the header the author had
  in mind. It was right about the claims it asserted and silent about the transport that failed.
- A browser walkthrough looked healthy, because **a console's first calls need no identity at all**.
- A literal always agrees with itself, so no gate could see a divergence.

It was found by deploying two applications on the same day: both refused a service-account caller
through the portal's IAP edge while a third, deployed a week earlier through the same hosts with
the same audience, answered it. The kit release, the audience, the host and the proxy were all
excluded by execution. The difference was one line.

## What changed

The read is now `hex_service_kit.federation.select_assertion`, the one reviewed selection function,
rather than another copy of an `or` chain. It examines both names, prefers the edge-injected one
(for diagnosis, not trust — both take the identical verification path), strips so a header a proxy
rendered blank is *absent* rather than malformed, and names **both** headers in its refusal so an
operator reads which hop dropped one instead of going to the load balancer.

## The proof, falsified first

`tests/unit/test_embedded_assertion_transport.py` is new and needs no cloud SDK, project or
network. With only the header read reverted, five of its cases fail — including the one that
resolves the contradiction between a passing claim suite and a live 401.

It also pins the parts that would let the defect back in silently: that the forwarded name is the
commons value and is **outside** the stripped namespace, that neither name buys a bypass of the
verifier, that the edge-injected name still wins when both are present, and that a blank value
under either name is an absent assertion rather than a malformed one.

`make gate` passes.

author: jasonluther
body:
## The bug, and the wrong diagnosis it produced

A subagent's shell inherits the parent's `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, so `cmd_status` resolves to the **parent's** row and `POST /sessions` overwrites its goal and step. Measured this morning with four workers on one machine: each overwrote the others, and the parent's own narrative vanished twice. Both sessions independently concluded that *"the board keys one row per host"* — a wrong diagnosis the symptom fits perfectly, and one that would have sent someone refactoring the wrong thing.

The `SubagentStart`/`Stop` nested label is right for a read-only Explore. But a subagent holding its own worktree, branch and PRs is a coordination peer in its own right — exactly what the board exists to make visible — so it should get a row, linked to its parent rather than replacing it.

## `--as-subagent LABEL`, and why one flag rather than two

Nothing exposes an agent's own id to its shell (`agent_id` reaches the hooks on stdin, not the subagent's Bash). My first cut was `--session-id <parent>:<label> --parent <parent>`, which works — and requires the parent to paste its session id into every dispatched prompt. That's the step that gets forgotten, and forgetting it silently restores the clobbering.

The subagent already *has* the parent's id in its environment, so one flag is enough:

```
standup status --as-subagent 'lane-d' --goal '...' --step '...'
```

It derives `<parent>:<label>` and `parent_session_id` from the inherited id. The `update_status` MCP tool takes the same `as_subagent` label — the skill offers it as the alternative to the CLI, so fixing only the CLI would have left the documented path broken.

## What `standup list` looks like now

```
agents:
  partygame	snoopy @ main — UI duplication program
    ↳ partygame	snoopy @ ui-dup/screen-h1 — #3109 OPEN — lane D screens
    ↳ partygame	snoopy @ ui-dup/resume — adopt + resume
  partygame	lucy — gamepad guard
```

Four workers on one machine read as four workers instead of four strangers. **A child whose parent is absent from the listing still prints at top level** (filtered by `--repo`, or ended early) — hiding live work is worse than an ungrouped row, and it's the collision the board exists to prevent.

## Lifecycle

Cleanup is the parent's `SessionEnd`: `deregister` cascades to rows naming it as parent, scoped to the owner. A subagent has no hook of its own and doesn't choose its own id, so without the cascade a finished worker's row sits there until the 12-hour TTL. Self-parenting is rejected — it would delete the row twice and render as its own child.

`parent_session_id` is a new column with the same `ALTER` migration pattern as `type` and `subagents`; its test writes the schema **as actually deployed** (type and subagents present, parent missing) so it exercises that one migration rather than all three at once.

## Verification

316 tests pass, 99% coverage (95% gate), ruff clean. **Every new behaviour is mutation-checked — 14 planted defects, each caught by a named test:** the cascade at both the roster and store layers, the parent setter, all three app validations, both client paths, both MCP paths, the nesting, and the orphan-visibility rule. Removing the migration call reds all three migration tests. The `list` rendering was also smoke-tested against a realistic four-row board (output above).

body:
Cablea el botón «Añadir otra» a `BitacoraBase.siguienteObjeto()` (el enabler de #300, hoy sin consumidor).

Hasta ahora el botón vaciaba el bloque de entradas entero, así que encadenar el objeto siguiente obligaba a reelegir ocular, reescribir el aumento y recalcular el campo real, aunque no se hubiera tocado el tubo.

## Qué cambia

- El manejador (`registro/resources/js/bitacora-formulario.js`) ya no decide qué se conserva: le pasa a `siguienteObjeto()` lo que hay en pantalla (`recogerEntradas()` + fecha, hora y exploración) y pinta lo que devuelve, por la vía «más tarde» (`mismoCampo: false`).
- La entrada nueva nace con ocular, aumento, pupila de salida y campo real heredados; el objeto, las coordenadas, el estado de resolución, la descripción, las imágenes y la exploración salen vacíos.
- El salto de 20 minutos ya vive en `siguienteObjeto()`, así que el manejador no llama a `sumarMinutos()`.
- Sin entradas que heredar se sigue creando una vacía.
- Versión del script del fragmento subida a `20260914_1200` (el .js va por FTP y el HTML se pega en WordPress: si no se sube, el navegador sirve el viejo).

## Criterios de aceptación de #297

1. Ocular / aumento / pupila / campo real heredados — sí.
2. Lo que quede en pantalla manda al guardar — sí: se lee del DOM al enviar, como siempre.
3. Objeto, RA/Dec y estado de resolución vacíos — sí.
4. Vía «más tarde»: título, descripción e imágenes vacíos — sí.
5. Vía «mismo campo» — fuera de alcance, es el botón de #298; la regla ya está escrita en `siguienteObjeto()`.

## Comprobación

`scripts/test_otra_observacion.js` ampliado: la aserción vieja sobre `sumarMinutos(..., 20)` se sustituye por el cableado nuevo (delegación, `mismoCampo:false`, herencia de la óptica). Closes #297

author: apojomovsky
body:
## What

Follow-up to #30, whose rebase-and-retry approach was itself hit by a
real race in the very next `epic-tasks ship pio` run: the `framework`
job's write-back was rejected (another commit landed on master mid-run,
same as #30's original bug), retried, fetched, and rebased as designed,
but this time the rebase itself hit a genuine conflict:

```
Auto-merging CHANGELOG.md
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md
```

Root cause: the concurrent commit was `toolchain`'s own write-back from
the same run, which also prepends to `CHANGELOG.md` (git-cliff's
`--prepend` always inserts at the top). Two concurrent write-backs
prepending to the same file's same region is not a special case, it's the
common case whenever `toolchain` and `framework` both run in one
`package.yml` dispatch (exactly what `epic-tasks ship pio`/`ship all` do)
plus any other agent's activity on this repo.

## Fix

Replace rebase-and-retry with reset-and-recompute: on a rejected push,
`git fetch` + `git reset --hard origin/master`, then rerun the entire
`sync_versions.py` / `git-cliff --prepend` / `rollup_changelog.py`
sequence fresh against the new tip, instead of trying to transplant the
stale diff. Every file this touches (`packages/versions.json`,
`packages/<name>/package.json`, `platform.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`) is fully
generated from current state, so recomputing is always correct where
rebasing a generated, order-sensitive file is not.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the exact race in a throwaway sandbox: seeded a minimal
      repo with the real scripts, had one clone run `finish_release.sh`
      for `framework-epichal` and push, then ran it again from a
      deliberately stale clone for `toolchain-epiccc` (the same shape as
      #30's failure) — first push attempt rejected, reset-and-recompute
      kicked in, second attempt succeeded with both packages' entries
      correctly present in `CHANGELOG.md`, `versions.json`, and
      `platform.json`
- [x] `bash -n scripts/finish_release.sh`, `epic-tasks takeoff` clean

Allow users to organize menu-bar cards and feature rows into up to five mixed panels, edited directly in the menu-bar popover.

- Add, reorder, and customize icon tabs with a built-in symbol picker. Keep both default panels non-deletable and return a deleted panel's entries to their original default surfaces.

body: # Qué hace este cambio Quien entra al sitio veía «Ingresar» aunque ya tuviera sesión, y sólo podía salir desde `/cuenta`. El menú ahora muestra el nombre, un retrato rectangular privado y cómo cerrar la sesión. La foto se sube desde la cuenta y **no se publica**. El HTML público sigue siendo el mismo para todo el mundo, para no romper el caché. `/cuenta` —la sección «mi cuenta» que ya existía— dejó de ser un formulario largo apilado. Ahora es un índice editorial con pestañas: reservas, cómo aparecer, acceso y borrar. Si hay reservas, esa pestaña abre primero. En el teléfono, la barra de «Ayudar a reconstruir» no aparece en `/cuenta`: tapaba los formularios. **Especificación**: FR-244–FR-248, SC-213, ADR-037. ## Cómo lo verificaste - `npm run typecheck`, `lint` y `format:check` en verde. - `npm run db:test` en verde: 281 aserciones pgTAP (chrome de cuenta). - E2E `cuenta.spec.ts` escritorio: 11/11, incluyendo abrir Acceso y Borrar. - E2E `catalogo.spec.ts` escritorio: 4/4; después de reservar abre la pestaña Reservas. - En 390 px, las cuatro pestañas y sin la barra de ayudar encima. La subida real del retrato no se afirma en local (ADR-013). [Cuenta en 390 px, pestaña Cómo aparecer](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-ad8c653c-a5d6-4d5e-a8aa-11031a70bd5e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcuenta_390_tab_aparecer.png) [Cuenta en 390 px, pestaña Reservas](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-ad8c653c-a5d6-4d5e-a8aa-11031a70bd5e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcuenta_390_tab_reservas.png) [Cuenta en 390 px, pestaña Acceso](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-ad8c653c-a5d6-4d5e-a8aa-11031a70bd5e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcuenta_390_tab_acceso.png) [Cuenta en 390 px, pestaña Borrar](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-ad8c653c-a5d6-4d5e-a8aa-11031a70bd5e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcuenta_390_tab_borrar.png) [Cuenta en 1440 px, pestaña Acceso](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-ad8c653c-a5d6-4d5e-a8aa-11031a70bd5e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcuenta_1440_tab_acceso.png) [cuenta_tabs_390.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-ad8c653c-a5d6-4d5e-a8aa-11031a70bd5e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcuenta_tabs_390.mp4) ## Definition of Done - [x] Cumple la especificación que se cita arriba. - [x] Tiene tests en el nivel que corresponde, y los vi fallar antes de que pasaran. - [x] `npm run typecheck` pasa. - [x] `npm run lint` y `npm run format:check` pasan. - [x] `npm run build` pasa. - [x] Accesibilidad revisada: axe en `/cuenta` con sesión. El menú abierto no se le pasa a axe: el muestreo de contraste toma la foto de detrás del overlay. - [x] Revisado en mobile de verdad (390 px). - [x] Seguridad considerada: el retrato es privado; `/cuenta/sesion` no crea el perfil; el HTML público no se personaliza. - [x] SEO considerado: las páginas públicas no se personalizan; `/cuenta` sigue en `noIndex`. - [x] Documentación actualizada (ADR-037). - [ ] CI en verde. ## Datos y contenido - [x] No hay ningún dato inventado. Sin foto, el espacio queda reservado. ## Base de datos - [x] El cambio de esquema llega por una migración versionada. - [x] Hay tests pgTAP de negación. - [x] `npm run db:test` pasa (281 aserciones). - [x] La migración no es destructiva: agrega `portrait_path` y el bucket `avatares`. ## Riesgos y vuelta atrás Quien está ingresada ve un instante de «Ingresar» hasta que hidrata el island. ### 1. 🔴 « le bouton Offre de l'embed KO : ❌ Aucun profil SigilOS dans cette guilde » (le dashboard fonctionne)

**Cause mesurée** (`src/app/api/discord/interactions/route.ts`, branche des **modales** `payload.type === 5`, `mkt:offer`) :
- `userId: member.user.id` = **snowflake Discord** transmis au service, alors que `resolveMemberContext` (`src/server/market/discord-interactions.ts:160`) lit `UserProfile.userId` = **`User.id` interne** (le **bouton**, lui, passait bien `account.userId` — d'où dashboard OK / embed KO) ;
- le gate RBAC (`DISCORD_PERM_MAP`, `mkt → market:trade`) vivait **dans** la branche `payload.type === 3` ⇒ **les modales n'étaient pas filtrées du tout**.

**Correctif (au bon étage, aucune règle métier dupliquée — §13.4)** :
- `DISCORD_PERM_MAP` en **portée module** + `ephemeralDiscordRefusal()` / `DISCORD_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` / `DISCORD_PERMISSION_DENIED` partagés ;
- **gate unique `isDiscordPrefixAuthorized(prefix, guild_id, discordUserId)`** (fail-closed : exception ⇒ refus) appelé par les **boutons ET les modales** ;
- la branche `mkt:offer` résout `findUserByDiscordId(member.user.id)` puis transmet **`account.userId`**.

### 2. 🧨 « +15975 Effet [15975] » (*Pestilence de Corruption*, carte + image OG + « Jet déclaré »)

**Cause mesurée** (sonde `_probe-effet-15975.mjs` + `api.dofusdb.fr/items/22412`) : l'`effectId` **1175** est un **porteur de capacité légendaire** — `diceNum` = **id du pouvoir** (`15975`), `diceSide` = 1. **DofusDB l'écarte lui-même** de son tableau normalisé `effects` (**17** entrées brutes `possibleEffects` / **16** `effects`) ; notre siphon copiant la forme brute, la ligne était **déclarable** puis affichée partout. **Portée : 334 fiches** (+ 6 autres `effectId` sans libellé référentiel : 971→61, 205→14, 721, 233, 2907, 2991).

**Correctif (règle pure, une source de vérité)** — `src/lib/market/effects.ts` :
- `NON_STAT_EFFECT_IDS = [1175]` · `isNonStatNativeEffect()` · **`isDisplayableNativeEffect()`** (métadonnée `0 → 0` **et** ligne « pouvoir ») ;
- appliquée au **siphon** (`toNativeEffects`), à la **lecture client** (`enrichNativeEffects`), à l'**éditeur** (`buildNativeStatDrafts`), au **catalogue** (`getItemCatalogEntry`) ;
- **miroir** `isStatBearingStatRow({ effectId, … })` pour les lignes **déjà persistées** ⇒ annonces existantes nettoyées à la **lecture** (écrans, image OG, payload Discord) — **aucune migration**.

### 3. 🖼️ « icône assets ko : +5 % Mêlée (%) » (+ « d'autres ko à signaler ? »)

**Audit mesuré** (sonde `_probe-stat-icons-audit.mjs` contre le référentiel siphonné `GameCharacteristic` / `GameEffect` = source de vérité) :
- `Mêlée (%)` (caractéristique **124**, asset `tx_resMelee`) et `Distance (%)` (**120**/**121**) n'avaient **aucun thème** ⇒ repli lucide ;
- **collision d'espaces d'ids** : `124` = *Sagesse* (`effectId`) **et** *Mêlée (%)* (`characteristicId`) ;
- **3 icônes fausses** : `82` = Retrait PA (était Esquive PA), `84` = Dommages Poussée (était Esquive PM), `88` = Dommages Terre (était Résistance Poussée) ;

### ✅ Vérification demandée — « les annonces des gens partis sont-elles supprimées ? »
**Oui** : `withdrawMarketListingsForProfileCore` (`src/server/market/lifecycle.ts`) est branchée sur les **5** chemins de départ (`archiveProfile`, `deleteProfileByAdmin`, `syncGuildMembers` `BANNED`/`LEFT`, `user-actions`) + `wipeUserProfile` + suppression RGPD (`S8.20`). Aucun correctif nécessaire ⇒ **fait vérifié**.

`src/temp/debug.md` (tableau complet) : **`Réglages → Marché`** (retirer 3 sélecteurs de rôles + panneau « Durées, plafonds & rappels » — le God est **déjà** global : `saveGodMarketSettings` écrit **toutes** les guildes en `updateMany`) · **timeline des offres** (emplacement **à trancher**) · **désistement depuis la fiche du dashboard** (l'action `cancelMarketReservationCore` existe) · **capacité légendaire** (texte du pouvoir **à sourcer** : `isLegendary` de `22412` = `false` en base) · **image OG** (titre `EFFETS` recouvert, ligne horizontale, pied « Annonce #… / vendeur »).

body:
## Summary

- The rv64 lane left every `main` that named a view of its own array (`whole: []u32 = view(&buf)`) or declared a record without an initializer to the C backend, while the AArch64 lane lowered both.
- A span or view local over an owned frame array now binds like a parked span parameter: the array's frame address (`addi sB, sp, off`) and its constant length (`li sL, N`) in two callee-saved registers, the length register serving as the raw and the normalized length, so the local reads and stores through the checker's guarded-index idiom, passes on as a `{base, len}` pair, and another named span aliases by copying the registers. A subslice stays with the C backend in this increment.
- A record local without an initializer is zero-filled from the zero register word by word (`90-backend.md` §6), and the verifier's Oak side holds every value-less aggregate local (array, record, sum) at its zero value where it refused a record or a sum.
- Lean model `Oak.SpanLocals`: a guarded element access stays inside the array's slots and below the frame, as an instance of the checker's span access rule; the word-by-word zero fill is the record's zero value.
- Docs: `94-assembler.md` §8 thirty-fourth increment (the RV64 stack-parameter paragraph renumbered thirty-third so the two read in order); `STATUS.md` row sentence.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./compiler -run TestE2ENativeRV64SpanLocals` (bare-metal QEMU on RV64 and the AArch64 host, exit 42)
- [x] `go test ./asm ./prove`

author: denisfrodrigues-pax
body:
## Corrige o balão de instalação do PWA mostrando nome/logo do sistema em vez da igreja

Bug reportado: ao abrir o site público de qualquer igreja de teste, o balão de instalação mostrava "Instale o app do Rede Conect" com o ícone genérico da plataforma — não o nome/logo da igreja atual.

### Causa raiz

`<PWAInstallBanner />` era renderizado em `App.tsx` como **irmão** de `<Routes>`, fora da árvore de rotas `/i/:churchSlug`:

```tsx
<Routes>...</Routes>
<PWAInstallBanner />   {/* fora da árvore de rotas por igreja */}
<PWAUpdatePrompt />
```

Estruturalmente, isso significa que o componente **não tinha acesso** a `useIgrejaSlug()` — o contexto que resolve a igreja atual pelo slug da URL (`/i/:churchSlug/...`), usado por todo o resto do sistema para tema de cores, logo, favicon e título da página (ver `IgrejaSlugContext.tsx`, que já resolve isso tanto para usuários autenticados quanto para o site público sem login). Como resultado, o banner sempre caía nos valores hardcoded de sistema: texto "Instale o app do Rede Conect" e ícone `/pwa-192x192.png`.

### Correção

Segue exatamente o mesmo padrão que `IgrejaSlugLayout` já usa para favicon/título dinâmicos por igreja:

1. **`IgrejaSlugContext.tsx`**: adiciona `churchLogoUrl` ao `IgrejaSlugContextType` (já expunha `churchNome`, faltava o logo) e move a renderização de `<PWAInstallBanner />` para dentro de `IgrejaSlugLayout`, ao lado do `<Outlet />` — dentro do `<IgrejaSlugContext.Provider>`, cobrindo toda a árvore de rotas por igreja (site público, área do membro, líder e admin).
2. **`App.tsx`**: remove `<PWAInstallBanner />` do nível global (ficou só `<PWAUpdatePrompt />`, que não depende de contexto de igreja).
3. **`PWAInstallBanner.tsx`**: consome `useIgrejaSlug()` para mostrar `"Instale o app da {nome da igreja}"` e o `logo_url` da igreja atual — com fallback para o ícone genérico da plataforma apenas se a igreja não tiver logo cadastrado (mesmo fallback já usado em `ChurchLogo.tsx`).

**Efeito colateral esperado e correto**: as rotas de superadmin (`/`, `/admin`, `/admin/igrejas/nova`) ficam fora da árvore `/i/:churchSlug` — não há "uma igreja" para instalar nesse contexto, então o balão simplesmente não aparece mais ali. Antes ele aparecia com a mesma mensagem genérica sem sentido nessas telas; agora não aparece, o que é o comportamento certo.

### Sobre a dependência circular

`IgrejaSlugContext.tsx` passa a importar `PWAInstallBanner`, que por sua vez importa `useIgrejaSlug` de volta de `IgrejaSlugContext.tsx`. Isso é seguro aqui porque ambos os usos acontecem em tempo de render (dentro do corpo de componentes React), não em tempo de avaliação do módulo — confirmado empiricamente: `tsc`, `npm run build` (Rollup) e teste real no browser (Playwright) não mostraram nenhum erro de runtime ou de bundling nas 3 igrejas testadas.

### Sobre o `manifest.json` (nome do app fixo)

Investiguei se dá para gerar/servir o manifest dinamicamente por igreja. **Não fiz essa mudança nesta PR** — é uma limitação técnica real, não uma escolha de escopo:

- O manifest (`name: "Rede Conect - Sistema de Gestão Eclesiástica"`) é gerado **em build-time** pelo `vite-plugin-pwa` (`vite.config.ts`), produzindo **um único** arquivo estático `manifest.webmanifest`, referenciado por **um único** `<link rel="manifest">` no **único** `index.html` da SPA — o mesmo `index.html` é servido para toda e qualquer rota (`vercel.json` só tem um rewrite `/(.*) → /index.html`, sem lógica por igreja).
- Não há infraestrutura de servidor no projeto hoje: **nenhuma pasta `api/`**, nenhuma serverless/edge function configurada no `vercel.json`. Um manifest dinâmico por igreja exigiria criar essa infraestrutura do zero.
- Mesmo com uma function dedicada (ex.: `/api/manifest/[slug]`), ainda faltaria resolver os **ícones**: o manifest exige imagens PNG em tamanhos exatos (192×192, 512×512, e variantes "maskable" com margem de segurança) — hoje só existe `logo_url` (upload livre, qualquer proporção/tamanho) por igreja, não um conjunto de ícones PWA pré-processados. Faria a instalação nativa (ícone na tela inicial do celular) ficar esticada/cortada sem um pipeline de redimensionamento de imagem.
- Uma alternativa client-side (trocar o `href` do `<link rel="manifest">` para um Blob URL gerado com o JSON da igreja) é tecnicamente possível, mas é uma URL efêmera (não persiste entre carregamentos), o que é frágil para o fluxo de instalação nativa do navegador e mais difícil de depurar do que um endpoint estável.

Dado que isso exigiria (a) nova infraestrutura de servidor, (b) um pipeline de geração/redimensionamento de ícones por igreja, e (c) mudanças na config de deploy — é uma mudança de escopo bem maior do que o bug relatado, que era especificamente sobre o balão em React. Documentando aqui para você decidir se vale abrir como um pedido separado.

### Testes

- **3 igrejas de teste** (Convergência, Radiação, Red): balão mostra nome e logo corretos em `/i/:slug/publico` (site público, sem login) e também dentro de área autenticada (`/i/:slug/admin/dashboard`) — confirmado via Playwright disparando `beforeinstallprompt` sinteticamente e inspecionando o texto/imagem renderizados.
- Zero erros de console/runtime em nenhuma das igrejas.
- Rota de superadmin (`/`) confirmada funcionando normalmente sem o balão.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: limpo.
- `npm run build`: limpo (confirma que o Rollup resolve a dependência circular sem problema).
- `eslint`: idêntico ao baseline de `origin/main` (só deslocamento de linha nos 3 avisos pré-existentes, zero problemas novos).

Sem merge — aguardando confirmação.
