body:
## Where this came from

Triaging CodeQL alert **#75** (MEDIUM, `js/http-to-file-access`, `scripts/prune-merged-branches.mjs:370`).

**That alert is a false positive at its sink.** The path is `process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, an Actions-provided variable, and every branch name reaching the summary is escaped — `shellQuote` for the restore command, `mdCode`/`escapeHtml` for names and reasons, `encodeRefPath` for URLs — with a live self-test that exits 1 if an escaper regresses. I also confirmed the ```` ``` ```` fence cannot be broken out of: a closing fence must be a line containing only the fence, and `git check-ref-format` refuses newlines and tabs in refs, so no branch name can produce one.

These four are what the hunt actually turned up. None is the flagged line.

## 1. `paginate` followed the `Link` header to any host, with the token attached

`url = next[1]` came out of a **response header** and went straight into `fetch(url, { headers })`, where `headers` carries `Bearer ${GH_TOKEN}` — a `contents: write` credential. No origin check. Observed leaving for `https://attacker.example/steal?p=2` with the bearer attached when the header was crafted.

This is the same untrusted-network-data class the alert names, with a worse sink than the file: the credential itself. Now pinned via `isSameApiOrigin`, and a `rel="next"` link off this origin throws instead of being fetched.

## 2. `b.commit?.sha ?? ""` turned the restore command into a delete

An empty sha renders `git push origin :refs/heads/'x'` — an empty **source** refspec, which git reads as a deletion. The "paste this to undo the deletion" line would have deleted the branch.

A missing field producing the *more destructive* outcome is the shape golden rule 2 forbids. A branch whose tip sha the API did not report is now kept as unrestorable rather than defaulted.

## 3. `if (b.protected)` treated an absent field as unprotected

An absent `protected` is unknown management state, and the branch was deleted. This is the server twin of the iOS `managedBool` rule in CLAUDE.md — *"never derive a policy default from the ABSENCE of managed configuration."* Now `b.protected !== false`, so unknown keeps, and the kept reason distinguishes "branch protection" from "protection state not reported".

GitHub always sends the field, so this one is latent rather than live.

## 4. The recovery record was written *after* the delete loop

The file header says *"REVERSIBILITY IS PRINTED BEFORE ANYTHING IS DELETED … this is the only moment that record can be made"*, and the summary array says *"emitted BEFORE any deletion"*.

Both were true of when the array was **built** and false of when it was **written**: the single `appendFileSync` sat after the entire delete loop. A run interrupted mid-loop — cancelled job, runner eviction, a throw on the forced-branch path — deleted branches and wrote no restore record at all. The claim held only when nothing went wrong, which is the one case it was not written for.

Split into `appendSummary`: the recovery record goes out before the loop, the result block after.

## Proof

Seven self-test cases added beside the existing escaper cases, covering the origin pin: the API origin itself, another host, a differing scheme, an `api.github.com.evil.test` suffix host, a differing port, a relative URL, and unparseable input.

**Falsified** by planting `return true` in `isSameApiOrigin` — the self-test goes red on all six negative cases and exits 1:

```
✗ escaping self-test FAILED — refusing to render untrusted names.
    got true want false
    (×6)
```

With the real check restored, the script runs past the self-test to its normal `401 Bad credentials` on a fake token.

## Gates, quoted

- `node --check scripts/prune-merged-branches.mjs` → clean
- `node scripts/check-doc-line-counts.mjs` → `0 drifted`
- `node scripts/preflight.mjs` → `Preflight PASSED — everything it runs is green.` 320 gates, 0 failed. 2 proofs SELF-SKIPPED (`backup-restore`, `db-role-split`) because `DATABASE_URL` is unset here — not run, not passed; CI's durable-persistence job runs them against a real Postgres.
- `pnpm run verify:breadth` → `Breadth lane PASSED — 56 breadth proofs green.`

The script itself is CI-only (the "Prune merged branches" workflow) and preflight lists it under gates this harness does not cover, so the self-test above is the executable evidence for the new behaviour.

## Owner-gated — do not auto-merge

Touches `scripts/**`. Auto-merge is not enabled; left for owner review.

## CodeQL #75 triage: FALSE POSITIVE

Dismissal needs the Mac lane's `gh` or the owner — the cloud lane has no code-scanning API. Suggested reason **false positive**, justification: *the write target is the Actions-provided `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` path, not attacker-influenced; every untrusted branch name reaching it is HTML-escaped or shell-quoted by helpers with a live self-test, and a ref name cannot contain the newline required to break the surrounding code fence.* The four defects the review found are fixed in this PR rather than dismissed.

author: queuecumber
body:
## Summary

Mail/calendar ports from the local aibs project: read-only IMAP and iCal, plus explicit SMTP email/invitation tools. This PR is stacked on `feature/graph-memory` to keep the memory prompting work untouched and the adapter diff separate. Outlook is intentionally not ported because the user now has a NVIDIA-provided replacement.

## IMAP

- Retains read-only mail searches, full details, and attachments. Searches are bounded and preserve folder case. Uses IMAPClient for UID-based commands and IDLE rather than implementing the protocol.
- Incoming messages generate passive `mail_received` events at the existing session-manager `/event` endpoint. Each watched folder has its own IDLE connection, with reconnect catch-up and adapter-side polling only when the server lacks IDLE.
- SQLite persists mailbox checkpoints and an event outbox in one transaction. Failed/ambiguous HTTP requests retain the notification for retry; stable `metadata.event_id` identifies repeats. First startup and UIDVALIDITY resets establish a baseline instead of replaying historical mail.
- Message IDs include account, folder, UIDVALIDITY, and UID, so stale IDs cannot fetch unrelated mail after a server reset. Existing aibs IDs must be reacquired by search.
- Attachment tools return MCP binary resources rather than container-local temporary paths. No read flags or mailbox contents are mutated.

## SMTP

- Sends real mail only on an explicit tool call. Uses TLS before authentication, a fixed sender mailbox, and a recipient allowlist that covers To, CC, and invitations. An empty allowlist denies all recipients unless the operator explicitly enables unrestricted sending.
- Attachments use bytes and platform resource URIs, never arbitrary file paths. Plain-text and HTML alternatives are included.
- Invitations retain absolute time, including daylight-saving folds, and have UID/DTSTAMP/METHOD/ATTENDEE fields and display alarms.
- Reports accepted and refused recipients separately on partial failure. No automatic send retries after potentially ambiguous outcomes.

## iCal

- Read-only `list_calendars`, `range_events`, and `get_event` tools over named private HTTPS feeds. Query output is bounded, carries freshness/truncation, and uses opaque feed/occurrence IDs rather than colliding provider UIDs.
- Conditional ETag/Last-Modified refreshes produce passive source-change events through a persistent SQLite outbox. First successful loading is quiet, failures retain the previous valid snapshot, and removed-from-feed is distinct from cancellation. Recurrence expansion alone does not generate changes.
- Uses the existing aibs recurrence library, bounded date windows, timezone-aware comparisons, all-day DATE preservation, moved/excluded/cancelled occurrences, and explicit stale-ID handling. The port fixes the old unbounded-series iteration and source-date serialization pitfalls.
- Private feed URLs come from a Kubernetes Secret and are excluded from tool status and HTTP request logs. One replica and a dedicated PVC retain cached feeds and pending events. Feed polling defaults to five minutes; this is adapter-generated push, not a provider webhook or an appointment reminder.

## Deployment And Compatibility

- All three services are disabled by default. Helm exposes account/transport/policy settings with external Kubernetes secret references. IMAP and iCal each have one Recreate replica and a dedicated state PVC; SMTP needs no volume.
- Adds workspace packages, locked dependencies, Dockerfiles, image build entries, Helm schema validation, and migration/configuration docs.
- HTTP MCP only. Legacy `MAILCAL_MCP_*` variables/CLI flags, plaintext login, arbitrary sender identities, filesystem attachment paths, and non-display invitation alarms are intentionally not carried over.
- The existing session-manager returns HTTP 202 after scheduling an in-memory handler. This PR guarantees retry until HTTP acceptance, not durable downstream processing or exactly-once delivery. IMAP flag/deletion events, sent-folder sync, invite edits/cancellations, calendar reminders, and Outlook remain outside this port.

## Verification

- Full suite: **578 passed, 0 skipped**, including 46 IMAP tests, 29 SMTP tests, 48 iCal tests, and 24 mail/calendar chart tests.
- New mail implementation modules have **100% line coverage**.
- Tests include real SQLite reopen/retry behavior, mocked IMAP IDLE/reconnect/UIDVALIDITY handling, MCP lifecycle/shutdown and resource round-trips, platform binary argument resolution, SMTP policies/partial failures, calendar timezones, and Helm renders.
- iCal regressions additionally cover conditional refreshes, private URL logging, stale reads, malformed/oversized/slow feeds, atomic snapshot/outbox rollback, duplicate UIDs across feeds, sparse cancellations, recurring exceptions, time-only metadata churn, and preservation of date-only versus midnight DATE-TIME values through storage.
- No real mailbox credentials were used, no messages were sent, and no cluster resources were deployed. Real provider authentication and IDLE behavior remain deployment smoke checks.

author: fre0grella
body:
## What this changes

Four strands, in four commits, all aimed at the same thing: the documentation
an examiner reads should describe the system that exists.

- **`chore(github)`** — issue forms and a pull request template.
- **`ci`** — `check` becomes three parallel jobs with cached toolchains, and the
  test suites stop running twice per push.
- **`docs(adr)`** — ADR 0004 now records the pipeline that runs.
- **`docs`** — a DDD building-blocks page, D1 as the described persistence
  target, and the exam report reordered around the exam's own criteria.

## Why

Three things were wrong rather than merely thin.

**The persistence story was inverted.** `wrangler.jsonc` aliases the MongoDB
driver to `driverAbsent.ts`, so the deployed Worker cannot reach it — yet nine
diagrams named MongoDB as the only store, including the first diagram of the
exam report, labelled "the game's store". Renaming participants was not enough:
two sequence diagrams were wrong about correctness, claiming a transaction for
sign-in where D1 does two separate inserts, and a `leagues.revision` bump for a
purchase, which is the Mongo mechanism. D1 is now the described target and
MongoDB is what it is — a second implementation that proves the repository
boundary holds, and keeps the choice of vendor a decision rather than a
dependency.

**ADR 0004 contradicted itself.** A banner said two mechanisms were superseded,
then ninety lines asserted them: the collector "writes scores/standings to D1 via
the REST API". Assembled into the single-page report the banner disappears into
the flow and the assertions remain. The Worker-limits analysis — which is the
part that still justifies the second platform — is now the centre of the
argument rather than a preamble, and Cloud Run and direct D1 writes moved to
"Alternatives considered".

**The CI had no cache.** Measured on run 34428567499: 6m03s, of which 60s was
re-downloading the Gradle distribution, with the three projects running back to
back. `coverage.yml` and `docs.yml` both had caches; the heaviest job did not.

## How it was verified

- [x] `cd docs/site && npm run build` — 54 diagrams rendered, 15 pages in 6
      sections, no dead links, no unresolved report paths
- [x] `./gradlew :frontend:check -Pcoverage` — run in full, produces
      `frontend/coverage/coverage-summary.json`
- [x] `./gradlew :backend:npm_run_test_coverage` — run in full, produces the
      summary and `lcov.info` for Codecov
- [x] `./gradlew :backend:check --dry-run` with and without `-Pcoverage` — picks
      `npm_run_test` and `npm_run_test_coverage` respectively
- [x] All ten workflow files parse
- [x] ADR claims checked against the code, not against other prose: the
      publish-images guard, `vars.SCORING_RUNNER`, the
      `ON CONFLICT(teamId, date)` upsert inside `db.batch()`, `CHUNK_SIZE = 100`

**The workflow changes have not run yet** — that is what this push exercises,
and the first run is cold-cache, so it will not show the improvement.

## Gates that are easy to forget

- [x] **Docs changed** and `cd docs/site && npm run build` passes.
- [x] **No route changed**, so `backend/openapi.yaml` is untouched.
- [x] **No domain rule changed.** The DDD page is a mapping and states no rule of
      its own; every rule it names is stated once under `docs/domain/` and linked.
- [x] **No new term**, so `CONTEXT.md` is unchanged.

## Anything left undone

- **The development process has no section in the report.** It is one of the five
  exam criteria, and the only one that cannot be assembled from existing pages:
  the practices exist (Conventional Commits via a Gradle-installed hook, the
  `master` ruleset, AGPL-3.0, Renovate) but no page under `docs/` describes them.
  Needs a new authored page plus a sidebar entry.
- **The docs build gate never runs on pull requests.** `docs.yml`'s only job is
  guarded `if: github.ref_name == 'master'`, so the dead-link and diagram checks
  run only after a merge. Pre-existing, not introduced here, and worth closing.
- **`semantic-release` is declared but not wired.** It is a devDependency with no
  `.releaserc`, no workflow invoking it, and zero version tags. Either wire it or
  drop the dependency.
- **`docs/deployment/deploy-strategy.md` is stale** — it documents `dispatcher.yml`
  and `build.yml`, which do not exist.
- **`docs/domain/what-are-model-entities.md` is a 147-word stub** written in a
  different register. It was dropped from the report bundle for that reason, and
  left otherwise untouched.

author: ashishawasthi
body:
## What was wrong

This service read the caller's identity from `x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion` and nothing else.

`x-goog-*` is Google's reserved namespace, and the serverless frontend **removes that whole
namespace** from a request entering a service, so an embedding host behind IAP cannot hand a
downstream application the assertion its own edge was given: the host sets the reserved name, the
frontend drops it, and the service refuses *"request did not pass through IAP"* about a request
that passed through IAP one hop earlier. The broker already injects the same value under
`x-portal-iap-assertion` for exactly this reason.

So this service would have answered **401 to every authenticated caller the day it was embedded**,
with a green gate, a healthy console and a passing offline suite.

## Why nothing reported it

Three things hid it, and each is worth keeping:

- The unit suite **builds its own request**, so it could only ever choose the header the author had
  in mind. It was right about the claims it asserted and silent about the transport that failed.
- A browser walkthrough looked healthy, because **a console's first calls need no identity at all**.
- A literal always agrees with itself, so no gate could see a divergence.

It was found by deploying two applications on the same day: both refused a service-account caller
through the portal's IAP edge while a third, deployed a week earlier through the same hosts with
the same audience, answered it. The kit release, the audience, the host and the proxy were all
excluded by execution. The difference was one line.

## What changed

The read is now `hex_service_kit.federation.select_assertion`, the one reviewed selection function,
rather than another copy of an `or` chain. It examines both names, prefers the edge-injected one
(for diagnosis, not trust — both take the identical verification path), strips so a header a proxy
rendered blank is *absent* rather than malformed, and names **both** headers in its refusal so an
operator reads which hop dropped one instead of going to the load balancer.

## The proof, falsified first

`tests/unit/test_embedded_assertion_transport.py` is new and needs no cloud SDK, project or
network. With only the header read reverted, five of its cases fail — including the one that
resolves the contradiction between a passing claim suite and a live 401.

It also pins the parts that would let the defect back in silently: that the forwarded name is the
commons value and is **outside** the stripped namespace, that neither name buys a bypass of the
verifier, that the edge-injected name still wins when both are present, and that a blank value
under either name is an absent assertion rather than a malformed one.

`make gate` passes.

## Summary
Extends the service worker's existing fire-and-forget failure containment to extension install/update and browser-startup initialization.

## Changes
- wraps install/update initialization in the same bounded `runSafely` path used by tab and alarm events;
- wraps startup initialization so storage or browser API failures cannot surface as unhandled promise rejections;
- preserves settings initialization, activity restoration, alarm scheduling, badge updates, and first-install options behavior;
- expands regression coverage to inject a storage failure into tab activity, startup, and install/update paths and assert each is reduced to an operator-visible warning.

## Why
Manifest V3 background workers are restarted opportunistically. Initialization paths should fail visibly but not leak rejected async listener promises when extension storage or other browser APIs are temporarily unavailable.

## Validation
The repository's existing test command runs the failure-containment suite together with startup, core behavior, manifest, and package validation in CI.

author: fabianocruz
body:
O documento servido declara 186 caminhos / 227 operações. O snapshot do repositório parou em 181 / 221, no refresh de 11/09. Faltavam seis, e nenhuma foi removida:

```
GET    /v1/charges                    List charges
POST   /v1/charges                    Issue a charge
GET    /v1/charges/{chargeId}         Read a charge
POST   /v1/charges/{chargeId}/cancel  Withdraw a charge
GET    /meta-tools.json               o catálogo de meta-tools
GET    /v1/meta-tools.json            o mesmo, sob /v1
```

As quatro de `charges` respondem **401** a uma sonda sem credencial, contra **404** de uma rota ausente: elas existem, e existiam. É isso que a [codespar-enterprise#1307](https://github.com/codespar/codespar-enterprise/issues/1307) descreve como "charge.get e charge.cancel existem só em REST" — o SDK e a CLI derivam do snapshot, e o snapshot não as conhecia.

## O que cai disso, tudo derivado

- `cs.api` e `API_OPERATIONS` passam a alcançar as seis.
- A CLI ganha o grupo `charges` com quatro subcomandos, por **uma linha** em `PUBLISHED_GROUPS`. Verificado contra a API viva: `codespar charges list` responde, `codespar charges --help` lista os quatro.
- O pino de comandos derivados foi **regerado da árvore**, não editado: 66 → 70, e o diff mostra exatamente as quatro linhas de charges, sem remoções.
- O pino de contagem de operações vai a 227, com a linha de história dizendo o que entrou.

## ⚠️ Uma subida de pino que precisa do seu aval

As duas rotas do catálogo de meta-tools entram como **exceção**, não como grupo de comandos. Razão: são documento servido, lido por um runtime que decide o que despachar; quem está no terminal roda `codespar tools meta`, que imprime as mesmas definições a partir do `@codespar/types` publicado, sem rede. É o precedente já registrado para `openapi.json`, que também está na lista com as duas grafias.

Isso sobe o `EXCEPTION_PIN` de 43 para 45, e o próprio portão diz que uma subida pede aval do founder no corpo do PR, nomeando a família e por que ela não tem uso terminal.

> **Aval do founder, 14/09/2026 (Fabiano):** as duas exceções estão aprovadas. A família é o catálogo de meta-tools servido como documento (`GET /meta-tools.json` e `GET /v1/meta-tools.json`), nas duas montagens. Ela não tem uso terminal: quem lê o documento é um runtime decidindo o que despachar, e quem está no terminal roda `codespar tools meta`, que imprime as mesmas definições a partir do `@codespar/types` publicado, sem rede. Mesmo precedente já registrado para `openapi.json`, que também está na lista com as duas grafias.

A alternativa considerada e recusada: dar um `codespar tools meta --remote` que leia a rota em vez do pacote, o que devolveria o pino a 43 — recusada porque é superfície nova, e esta rodada não amplia superfície.

## Versões

`sdk` minor (superfície nova), `cli` minor (comandos novos), e os 13 adapters em patch só para a faixa de peer aceitar `^0.14.0`. Portão de deriva rodado localmente: 16 pacotes publicáveis, nenhuma deriva nova.

## Ordem de merge

Há outros dois PRs abertos no `packages/cli` (#145, #146). Este foi cortado do `main`, então quem entrar por último rebaseia e reconcilia o número da versão da CLI — só ele conflita.

author: man8-octoflow[bot]
body:
## Summary

TargetProcess answers a query parameter it does not recognise, and a `where=` filter on a nested collection path it does not filter on, with HTTP 200 and the unfiltered rows, so the mistake is indistinguishable from success. The library now refuses both before any request is sent, and the refusal names the route to use instead.

## Changes

- `QUERY_PARAMETERS` in `request_handler.py` declares the eleven query-parameter names the handler's builders emit. `RequestHandler.get` and `RequestHandler.list` refuse a built parameter set carrying any other name with `ValueError` before the URL is formed. In `list` the check sits ahead of the `limit=0` short-circuit.
- `BaseResource.ignored_filter_paths` and `check_where` mirror `unhydratable_includes` / `check_include`: `list()` refuses a `where=` whose leading path segment is declared, in any casing, before any request. Quoted values in the filter are data rather than paths, so `Name contains 'Assignments.cs'` still passes. The one declaration, `ASSIGNABLE_IGNORED_FILTER_PATHS` (`Assignments`), lives in `resources/base.py` and is referenced by the six assignable managers: user stories, bugs, tasks, features, epics and requests.
- The generic `entities` path mirrors the refusal through `_IGNORED_FILTER_PATHS` for every spelling of those six collections and for the polymorphic `Assignable` / `Assignables` collection, reporting the caller's spelling.
- SPEC.md: an "Unrecognised query input" bullet under the API facts, a clause on the `where` bullet, and a new "Silently ignored queries" subsection holding the known set.
- CHANGELOG.md: an `[Unreleased]` / `Changed` entry.
- Two new test modules: `tests/test_query_parameters.py` and `tests/test_resources/test_ignored_filter_paths.py`.

## Testing

- Offline throughout. `ALLOW_PROD_RECORDING`, `TP_API_TOKEN`, `TP_BASE_URL`, `TP_DOMAIN` and `TP_TOKEN` were all unset. Every new test runs against `httpx.MockTransport` or a specced `AsyncMock` handler, and no cassette was recorded or touched.
- The two new modules: 43 passed.
- Baseline check: with `src/targetprocess` stashed back to `main` and the new tests left in place, the same run gives 28 failed, 15 passed. Every refusal test fails. The six assignable managers and every generic spelling let the filter through, the undeclared `sort` parameter reaches the transport on both `get` and `list`, and the allowlist tests fail on the missing names. The 15 that pass assert only baseline behaviour: valid filters, including quoted values, forwarded unchanged.
- After restoring the sources: 43 passed.
- Ceilings and callers: `SPEC.md` is 991 lines and `scripts/check_large_files.py` exits 0. `git grep 'Assignments\.'` hits only this change's files. No `where=` in `examples/` or `scripts/` filters on `Assignments`, and neither directory passes a sort parameter outside the typed keywords.
- Published-content checks: a grep of the changed files for internal names finds nothing, and `scripts/check_internal_refs.py` exits 0.
- `uv run ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- `uv run ruff format --check .`: 162 files already formatted.
- `uv run mypy --strict src`: no issues found in 53 source files.
- `uv run pytest -q --cov=targetprocess --cov-report=term --cov-fail-under=90`: 1179 passed, total coverage 99.06%.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` at the pre-commit and pre-push stages: every hook passed.
- The PR title passes both commit-msg hooks. A control title with no type fails `conventional-pre-commit`, and a control title carrying a tracker-shaped key fails `check-commit-message`.

## Context

- The refusal is `ValueError`, as for every other pre-send refusal in the library. `RequestValidationError` stays the mapping of an HTTP 400 response, so a caller can still tell "the server rejected it" from "the client never sent it".
- There is no caller-facing query-parameter passthrough: every parameter reaches the wire through a typed keyword, so the allowlist guards the builders themselves against a mis-cased or undeclared name.
- `Assignments.Count` is refused too, since nothing shows TargetProcess honours a collection count in `where=`. `order_by`, `include` and `AssignedUser.*` are deliberately outside the ignored set, being unverified; an entry is added only with live evidence.
- `RequestHandler.list` still passes `where` verbatim. The filter refusal lives in the resource layer, as the include refusal does.
- No post-merge steps belong in this description.

## Checklist

- [x] `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` pass
- [x] `uv run mypy --strict src` passes
- [x] `uv run pytest -q` passes and coverage stays at or above 90%

- [x] `uv run pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage pre-push` passes
- [x] New public functions, methods, and classes have docstrings
- [x] No real credentials, tokens, or PII are added to the diff
- [x] `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK`/`XXX` markers name an issue (e.g. `TODO(#123)`) — not applicable: the diff adds no such markers

## Özet

Hibe tasarım paketi **tur 18c · çağrı dönüşüm hunisi**: host hangi çağrının iş getirdiğini görüntülenmeden onaya kadar tek ekranda görür. Karar (2026-09-14): **görüntülenme sayacı eklenir, çift migration.**

### Veri
- **Yeni tablo `AppGrantCallDailyStats`**: host çağrısı başına gün + kanal (pargetto.com / platform) görüntülenme sayısı. Tek tek olay satırı yok; tekil indeks `(GrantCallId, Day, Kind)`.
- Sayım sayfa **açılışında** yapılır: pargetto `/Hibeler/Detay` ve kiracının `/Grants/Detail` sayfası. Ekran içi yenilemeler ve host kullanıcısının bakışı sayılmaz; var olmayan ya da kiracıya ait çağrı kimliği sayılmaz.
- Sayım **best-effort**: kendi iş biriminde, hata sayfayı düşürmez. Artış tek SQL güncellemesi; günün ilk iki görüntülenmesi aynı anda gelirse bir sayım kaybolabilir.
- Kayıt yöntemleri uzak API'ye kapalı (`RemoteService(false)`); üretilen JS vekilinde yalnız okuma uçları var.

### Ekran · `/Grants/Funnel` (yalnız host, menüde "Dönüşüm Hunisi")
- Çağrı seçimi (açıklar önce; planlanan ve kapanan etiketli) ve 30/60/90 gün penceresi. Seçili çağrı adreste taşınır.
- Altı aşama: **Görüntülenme** (pargetto · platform ayrımıyla) → **Uygunluk testi** (pargetto talepleri) → **İlgi** (platform "İlgileniyorum") → **Görüşme** (randevu tercihi bırakılan ya da randevu verilen talepler + danışmanın üstlendiği ilgi talepleri) → **Başvuru süreci** → **Onay**.
- Oranlar kanala göre kurulur: test pargetto görüntülenmesine, ilgi platform görüntülenmesine oranlanır. Payda sıfırsa ya da aşama öncekini aşıyorsa oran yazılmaz. Onay yoksa ve başvuru varsa "kurum sonucu bekleniyor".
- **Tek cümlelik içgörü:** test+ilgi → görüşme → başvuru arasındaki en büyük oransal kayıp ("En büyük kayıp: Test ve ilgi → Görüşme (137 → 24)."). Üçten az kayıtla oran yazılmaz.
- Pencerede hiç hareket yoksa boş durum; altta "sayım bu sürümle başladı" notu.

## Doğrulama
- `dotnet build Apya.Platform.slnx` → 0 hata
- `has-pending-model-changes` → **iki sağlayıcıda da "No changes"**; migration yalnız yeni tablo + tekil indeks
- Domain **334/334** · Application **269/269** · EF **364/364** (3 yeni) · Web (hibe sayfaları + genel/kiracı yüzeyleri + menü + Smoke) **116/116**
- Yeni EF testleri: iki pargetto + bir kiracı görüntülenmesi iki satırda doğru sayılar, host bakışı ve yabancı kimlik sayılmaz · huni: pencere dışındaki görüntülenme ve talep sayılmaz, randevulu talep + incelemedeki ilgi görüşme sayılır, onaylı başvuru onayda, pencere 45 → 60'a yuvarlanır, çağrı etiketi · kiracı bağlamında huni ve çağrı listesi yetki hatası
- İlk koşuda yakalanan test kurgu hatası: başvuru kiracı başına çağrıda tekil; onaylı başvuru ikinci firmaya taşındı
- Tarayıcı QA (sunucu çıktısı dökümü + ham Funnel.js/css, API taklit): altı aşama sayı/bar/oran, planlanan ve kapanan çağrı etiketleri, dönem 90'a geçince istek `days=90` ve başlık, hareketsiz çağrıda boş durum ve içgörü gizli, `?callId=` büyük harfle bile doğru çağrıyı seçiyor · kontrast (alfa kompozit): metinler açık temada en az 6,94:1, koyuda 7,18:1; bar dolgusu karta karşı 6,02 / 4,12 · 375px'te yatay taşma yok, aşamalar iki sütun · konsoldaki 404'ler yalnız döküm düzeneği (tema ikonu, tanıtım görseli, çerez/tur uçları). Pencere gizli olduğu için ekran görüntüsü alınamadı.

## Tasarımdan sapmalar

author: leanuzi
body:
Erro relatado na producao, no card do Hotel: RACAS[h.raca].nome com a raca undefined. A causa: excluir um pet dos Pets deixava as hospedagens dele apontando pra um cadastro que nao existe mais, e hospede() devolvia raca, nome, peso e tutor vazios. O Hotel parava de abrir.

Havia um segundo caminho pro mesmo estrago, pior: apagar uma raca em uso. O botao de remover ja era escondido pra raca em uso, mas o "em uso" so contava pets (nao contava irmaos nem hospede de hotel sem cadastro), e dava pra sumir com a raca so apagando o nome dela no campo. Com a raca de um pet da creche apagada, o app inteiro parava de desenhar (avatar le RACAS[].st).

- racaDe(): todo lugar que le uma raca passa por aqui e cai numa raca valida se a chave nao existir mais (23 pontos trocados).
- hospede(): reserva orfa devolve nome, raca, peso e tutor utilizaveis.
- excluir(): antes de tirar o pet, copia nome, raca, peso, tutor, telefone e irmaos pras hospedagens dele, que seguem no Hotel como visitante.
- usoDaRaca(): conta irmaos e hospedes sem cadastro tambem.
- Configuracoes de racas: apagar o nome de uma raca em uso nao a remove mais.

body:
### **User description** ## What Adds a skill that records what a working session is for, then answers "what's left" in under 100 words: what is done, what was deliberately deferred, what still needs doing. The goal lives in a file, so it survives a context reset. Every item has to carry evidence before it counts as done. Work that left the repository, a message sent or a ticket raised, can only be closed by the person who did it, never by an agent that watched a tool call succeed. Deferred work leaves the goal and becomes a follow-up, so the goal shrinks to what is genuinely still in play. A goal that grows too large becomes a plan instead, and is recorded as promoted rather than finished. Also adds `goals` to the curated typology set, so these files sort alongside findings and plans instead of landing in the index's catch-all bucket. ## Why Asking an agent what is outstanding currently gets an answer reassembled from whatever is left in the conversation. After a context reset there is nothing to reassemble from, and the answer quietly turns into fiction that reads exactly like fact. ## Notes - Audit 126/140 (A), zero errors, zero warnings. The first cut scored 82 (F); the second commit is that remediation. - Four eval scenarios, 18 instructions at 100% coverage. - Behaviour verified end to end: creation, summary rendering, and five distinct check failures including a self-attested external item. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Tests, Documentation ___ ### **Description** - Add `goal-tracker` skill for session tracking. - Integrate `goals` into project management typologies. - Implement validation script and goal templates. - Add comprehensive evaluation scenarios and references. ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR User["User"] -- "States session goal" --> GoalScript["goal.sh"] GoalScript -- "Creates / Validates" --> GoalFile["Goal Markdown File"] GoalFile -- "Promotes if overgrown" --> PlanFile["Plan File"] GoalFile -- "Parks deferred items" --> FollowUpFile["Follow-up File"] ```

body:
## 摘要 / Summary

**发布 `v1.5.0`** —— 本批次把 dev 上积累的 2 个变更（PR #100、#101）送入 main。

1. **收口发布 PR 的外部审查意见**（#100）：修复两处**真缺陷**（均非该次发布引入，是发布 PR 的 diff 面变大才照出的既有缺陷）——
   - **上下文档名判定不剥离合法 ATX 闭合标记**：`## 名称 ##` 是合法 Markdown，此前会把结尾的 `##` 一并存进段名，与模板段名比对落空，七段被整片判成缺失（`INIT-VALIDATE-FAILED`），**依赖上下文结构校验的正常路径被误阻断**；
   - **安装器把 `.gitignore` 的访问类读取故障当成「文件不存在」**：随即按空内容继续，并用默认覆盖写回，把用户既有 `.gitignore` **截断**为仅含受管条目（数据破坏；触发条件窄——读被拒、写允许）。
   另含：受保护路径三判据去重（收为单一实现，此前守卫自带一份逐字节相同的副本）、四处过时表述订正（pathBase 错误消息与注释 / dsh 平台的 npm 与 AGENTS.md 状态 / 本 CHANGELOG 的版本标识路径与一处已与事实相反的陈述 / 安全策略的第三方依赖边界）、三处技能描述与其机制对齐。**场景数 241 → 243**。
2. **版本面收尾**（#101）：`Unreleased` 落定为 `1.5.0`，九处版本面与 dsh 桥接版本戳（文件头标记行 + 导出常量）同步为 `1.5.0`。

**影响**：**无破坏性变更**。两处缺陷修复都是收紧既有判据——合法输入不再被误判为非法，故障时不再破坏用户文件；既有安装流程与产出不变。

**开发 PR 列表**：#100 · #101

## 验证（勾选已执行）/ Verification (check executed)

- [x] 回归测试 / Regression：`node .flow-comet/skills/flow-comet/scripts/guard-self-test.mjs` → ALL 243 SCENARIOS PASSED + `node .flow-comet/skills/flow-comet/scripts/system-test.mjs` → ALL SYSTEM TESTS PASSED

- [x] 如有未运行的验证项（说明原因）/ Not run if any (explain)：① **副本回归与三处分发属发布步骤**（本 PR 合并、打 tag 之后执行；版本标识需 tag 存在才解析为发布值）；② **端到端完整流程验证（dogfood）本轮不做**——已按维护者裁决；改动面已由两级基线 + 安装副本 CLI 冒烟覆盖。

## 自查（勾选）/ Self-check (check)

- [x] 提交信息为纯描述（无代号、编号、行话）/ Commit messages are plain descriptions (no codes, numbers, jargon)
- [x] 版本号 / 场景数与实现一致 / Version number / scenario count match the implementation
- [x] 行为变化已记入 CHANGELOG（Unreleased）/ Behavior changes recorded in CHANGELOG (Unreleased)
- [x] 向后兼容：无破坏性变更（如有已说明）/ Backward compatible: no breaking changes (explain if any)
- [x] 无无关文件或本地伪影 / No unrelated files or local artifacts

## 验证输出 / Verification output

```
$ node .flow-comet/skills/flow-comet/scripts/guard-self-test.mjs

ALL 243 SCENARIOS PASSED

$ node .flow-comet/skills/flow-comet/scripts/system-test.mjs

ALL SYSTEM TESTS PASSED
```

两处缺陷的回归场景在修复前因**正确原因**失败（原始输出见 #100）：

```
FAIL: 242 CONTEXT 段标题带 ATX 闭合标记 → 段存在判定通过（INIT-DONE）
INIT-VALIDATE-FAILED: CONTEXT.md 已存在但不满足模板（缺段 ## 项目概要；缺段 ## 技术栈；…）

FAIL: 243 .gitignore 读取访问类故障 → 中止安装且用户文件不被改写

{ "initial": "# 用户既有内容\nnode_modules/\ndist/\n",
  "after": "# flow-comet 运行时文件（不随仓库分发）\n.flow-comet/\n" }
```

安装副本 CLI 冒烟（在 e2e 载体上，用其安装副本自己的脚本；8 项全过 + 零残留）：副本内原位只读命令可用 / 空闲态写放行 / 闭合标记形态通过 / 缺前置空白的标记仍判缺失 / 改回后恢复通过 / 运行态越权写被拦 / 白名单内写放行。

## 基于版本 / Based on

`dev` @ `e52ad40`（领先 main 两个 change 级提交）。

## 审查注意点 / Review Notes

- **正式版发布不可撤回**：npm 只能 deprecate、不能撤回。本 PR 合并后依次执行：打 tag `v1.5.0` → 三处分发 → `npm publish` → GitHub Release → dev 同步。
- **发布顺序依赖**：必须**先 tag 再三处分发**——安装副本的版本标识取自源仓库的 `git describe`，tag 未建时会推算出开发态版本。

## Summary by Sourcery

Release v1.5.0 with context parsing and installer safety fixes, shared protected-path validation, synchronized version metadata, and updated documentation and regression coverage.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent valid ATX closing markers in CONTEXT headings from causing existing sections to be reported as missing.
- Abort installation on .gitignore access failures instead of treating them as missing and overwriting the user's file.

Enhancements:
- Consolidate protected-path validation and protected-file reading into a shared implementation.
- Align skill guidance, platform references, security boundaries, error messages, and release documentation with current behavior.

CI:
- Update regression references and checks for the 243-scenario guard suite.

Documentation:
- Finalize bilingual release documentation for v1.5.0 and update version references and regression baselines.

Tests:
- Add regression coverage for ATX closing markers and .gitignore read failures; retain full system-test coverage.

Chores:
- Finalize the v1.5.0 release version across package metadata, installed-version markers, and dsh bridge version identifiers.

author: deferredreward
body:
Closes #394.

`POST /api/tn-quick` answered `503 uhb_missing_for_verse` for every New Testament reference. `getVerseWords()` only ever read `data/hebrew_bible/`, which `fetch-tools.js` fills from `hbo_uhb` alone, so the verse map was empty and the handler returned before the model was called.

## Changes

- **Fetch the Greek NT.** New `fetchGreekNt` pulls `el-x-koine_ugnt` into `data/greek_nt/` through the existing `fetchDoor43Batch`, registered as `fetch_greek_nt` on both the MCP surface (`index.js`) and the CLI registry (`registry.js`).
- **Route by testament.** `BOOK_NUMBERS` numbers the OT `01-39` and the NT `41-67` (there is no 40) in both map definitions, and UHB and UGNT use the same `<num>-<CODE>.usfm` filename, so the book number alone picks directory and filename. Extracted as `sourceUsfmPathForBook`.
- **Generalize the quote normalizer.** Both sides NFC-normalize before comparing, and each script drops its own non-distinguishing marks via the new `foldSourceToken`: Hebrew cantillation/taamim as before, Greek accents, breathings and case. A grave/acute variant (`πολλοί` for `πολλοὶ`) or a decomposed quote still matches.
- **Split the failure modes** the old code collapsed into one 503, per the issue's point 4:

  | condition | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | unknown book code | 503 | 400 `unknown_book` |
  | verse absent from a loaded book | 503 | 422 `verse_not_in_source` |
  | source file genuinely missing | 503 `uhb_missing_for_verse` | 503 `source_verse_missing` |

  Only the last is transient, so clients no longer retry against permanent errors.
- **Renamed `no_rtl` → `no_source_script`** (422). The editor keys off `tn_quick_disabled`, so these codes were free to move; the request field stays `hebrewGuess` for wire compatibility.

`parseHebrewVerseWords` needed **no change** — UGNT marks words with the same `\w form|lemma=... strong=... x-morph=...\w*` shape as UHB. Verified against the real `43-LUK.usfm`: 1151 verses parsed, LUK 1:1 yields the expected 11 tokens.

## Verification

- New `test/tn-quick-source-verse.test.js` — 18 tests covering testament routing, `getVerseWords("LUK", 1, 1)` returning words, Greek quote normalization matching a verse word, accent/NFD variance, ` & ` discontinuity joiners, each distinct failure status, and Hebrew/ZEC non-regression. All pass.
- Fixtures are real trimmed chapter-1 UGNT LUK and UHB ZEC. They live outside any `data/` directory (`.gitignore` ignores `data/` at every level) and are staged into a temp workspace by the test.
- **Full suite compared against `origin/main`: identical set of 103 pre-existing failures before and after — this change introduces no regressions.** Those failures are environmental on this host and unrelated.
- Live `fetch_greek_nt` of `66-JUD.usfm` succeeded end-to-end (36 KB fetched, 25 verses parsed), confirming repo name, URL shape and filename convention.

## Deploy note

The code change alone does not populate the volume. `fetch_greek_nt` must be run once on the deployed instance before NT requests return 200; until then NT references answer the new `503 source_verse_missing`, which is the intended retryable signal.

body:
A Wolfenstein 3D clone for os8088 — raycast textured walls, pixel-art sprites, doors, a HUD — in NASM 8086 assembly, playable on a 4.77 MHz XT with a CGA or Hercules card, in colour on VGA, in a window and fullscreen. Built wave by wave; this PR grows with each wave and stays a draft until the last one lands.

**The plan**: `docs/plans/PIXELSTEIN-PLAN.md` — a scouting/design workflow (seven scouts, three competing engine designs, three judges, three adversarial reviews), Codex's independent research agreeing on the budget and the voxel verdict, the grafts from James Howard's WolfensteinCGA (the real Wolf3D engine converted for 8088), and the user's three directions: a graceful-degradation ladder (Wire → Flat → Textured → more rays by CPU tier, Auto by tier and by measured frame), the XT benchmarked fullscreen in the low-resolution modes, and "Low res" as a Detail-menu item.

**Wave 0 (this push)** — the instrument, the tables, the level tool and the reference renderer. `tests/pxsbench` measures every unit the plan priced, to the cycle, on MartyPC (CGA, Hercules, VGA); `tools/pxsframe.py` re-derives the frame; `docs/reports/PXS-FRAME-2026-09-13.md` is the measurement. The XT default written from it: Size 64 × Rows 80 × Low res (32 rays two bytes wide, full view width) at **9.4 fps scene A / 8.9 scene B** on CGA4, 9.5 / 9.0 on Hercules, promise ≥ 8.0 / ≥ 7.0. Full 64 × 80 reported at 6.3 / 5.9.

| unit (MartyPC, 4.77 MHz 8088) | plan D | measured |
|---|---:|---:|
| compiled store `mov [di+r*80],al`, RAM / CGA / Hercules | 25 / 31 | 24.3 / 30.1 / 32.1 clk |
| a DDA crossing | 130 | 128.2 |
| the column's setup | 516 | 1,094 |
| texel load + store | 48 | 46.0 |
| span copy to the card | 18.6/B | 19.4 / 19.3 clk/B |

Verified: `make` 38/0; `tests/pxsbench.py` ok on all three MartyPC machines; QEMU boot of `bench.img` with the 48 rows read back; kernel byte-identical. Four review lenses (8086 rules, frame cost, plan fidelity, Codex) over three rounds, then an independent verifier.

Waves to come: 1 skeleton + Wire/Flat on every adapter + windowed + the gate; 2 textures and the compiled scalers; 3 sprites, guards, doors, combat; 4 HUD, states, scores, sound, the episode; 5 the 16-colour window; 6 the dog, the map, the 86Box machines, the numbers.

author: yea-80y
body:
## What

Sub-ENS registry v2 and registrar v2, the one-transaction deployer, and both deploy scripts. Nothing is deployed.

**Registry (`L2Registry`, `L2Resolver`)**
- One rule for record writes: the name must exist, and the writer is a registrar or someone ERC-721 lets act for the holder (`_isAuthorized`). The signed record setters and `nonces` are gone.
- Every change of holder (mint, transfer, release, admin transfer, admin handover) moves the record version, so no record survives a change of holder.
- The admin seat (the base name) moves only through `nominateAdmin` + `acceptAdmin`. The admin can still rewrite any name's records by enrolling itself as a registrar - accepted and documented; the check on it is the Safe (later a DAO) and onchain visibility.
- Labels are 1-63 bytes with no `.`, `"`, `\` or byte below 0x20; a whole name is at most 255 bytes.
- `releaseWithSignature` tries plain ECDSA before the universal signature validator; `clearRecords` needs the holder's authority; `createSubnode`'s registrar branch is limited to the base name; `supportsInterface` reports `IExtendedResolver`; `addRegistrar(address(0))` is refused.

**Registrar (`WoCoRegistrar`)**
- The permit path is removed (`registerWithPermit` and all its state). One sponsor-submitted `register`, with one holder check after its last write.
- `Ownable2Step`, `renounceOwnership` disabled, mint window capped at 366 days, zero sponsor refused, `setContenthash` refuses a label nobody holds.

**Deploy**
- `WoCoSubEnsDeployer` creates the implementation, the clone (initialised in the same constructor) and the registrar in one transaction, with both admin roles on the Safe from construction.
- `DeploySubEnsRegistry` refuses an admin that is not Safe-shaped (no code, or an EIP-7702 delegated EOA), proves the clone runs this repo's v2 bytecode, and checks the deployed state: admin seat, registrar owner and registry, sponsor, reserved labels, and the `woco.eth` base node.
- `RedeployRegistrar` prints the Safe batch that enrols a new registrar and retires the previous one, and refuses a previous registrar that is not enrolled or not owned by the registry admin.

## Tests

- `forge test`: 562 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (`SubEnsV2CutoverFork` without `ARB_ONE_RPC_URL` / `MAINNET_RPC_URL`). `forge build --sizes` clean.
- Regression tests for the v1 findings from audits 924, 925 and 927 (`test/SubEnsV2AuditRegression.t.sol`), a model-based records invariant, and a cutover rehearsal on forks of live Arbitrum One + mainnet state.
- Mutation testing: 86 mutants across the registry, resolver, registrar, deployer and both scripts, each guard removed or weakened one at a time - all killed.
- Pre-merge review signed off; its findings are applied in 46a1245.
- The two v1 setter tests (`L2ResolverSignatureNonce`, `L2ResolverTextSignature`) are removed with the functions they tested.

## Next

An Arbitrum Sepolia rehearsal with a Safe as admin, recorded on this branch. The mainnet cutover waits on an audit of this code.

body:
## What

Mercury (xycloo Labs) gave us their own Stellar mainnet payout address. With the Worker var `MERCURYDATA_X402_ADDRESS` set, the four `mercury_*` routes become router-hosted x402 paywalls whose 402 names that address. The buyer's USDC settles to Mercury after Mercury's upstream answers 2xx and never enters the ROZO pool. The router keeps only its held JWT for the upstream call. Var unset = pooled path, byte for byte as before.

## How

- `PublicServiceRoute.directSettlement` (env-bound payout spec) on the four Mercury overlay entries.
- `services/catalog-direct-settlement.ts`: resolves the binding at request time into `operator` + `hosted`, reusing the existing hosted-paywall branch in `proxy.ts`. A set-but-invalid value yields an operator with no payouts, which the proxy answers with 503 rather than falling back to the pool.
- One shared `operatorCatalogFields` renderer used by `listPublicCatalog` and the overlay, so `/v1/services/catalog`, `/.well-known/x402` and the live 402 all name the same party.
- Proxy hosted branch injects `upstreamAuth` when the route carries one instead of loading a registry credential.

## Test

- `tests/mercury-direct-settlement.test.ts` (8 new, all pass): unset/set/invalid binding, route resolution, catalog fields and no leakage of the pool address, x402 header names Mercury.
- Full suite: 1407 passed. The one failure (`catalog-payment-gate` Option A timeout) fails identically on a clean `origin/main`.
- Address checked before wiring: well-formed, not on the blacklist, funded (4.99999 XLM) with a USDC trustline.

author: nick4man
body:
## Что это

Инициализация окружения для двух сред разработки, которых у проекта не было: облачных сессий Claude Code и GitHub Codespaces. Только конфигурация, кода приложения не тронуто.

Отделено от PR #90 намеренно: там разбор интеграции с CRM, здесь инфраструктура, ревью у них разное.

## Зачем

В облачной сессии Claude Code нельзя было запустить ни линтер, ни тесты — и это не мелкое неудобство: агент физически не мог проверить свою же правку.

| Препятствие | Как решается |
|---|---|
| Gemfile требует Ruby **3.4.10**, в образе 3.1/3.2/3.3 | `rbenv install` — но сперва надо обновить `ruby-build`: в образе он знает только до 3.4.9 |
| Гемы не установлены | `bundle install --jobs 4` |
| PostgreSQL 16 без PostGIS и pgvector | `apt-get install`, обязательно после `apt-get update` — индекс в образе протух и половина `.deb` отдаёт 404 |
| Кластер не инициализирован | `initdb -A trust` + `pg_ctl` с `fsync=off` |
| Redis не поднят | `redis-server --daemonize` |
| Спекам нужны 9 переменных | пишутся в `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, набор один в один с джобом RSpec в CI |

## Что добавлено

**`.claude/hooks/session-bootstrap.sh`** — зарегистрирован **вторым** в слоте `SessionStart`, рядом с существующим `session-start.sh`, а не вместо него: тот печатает routing и inbox за миллисекунды и обязан отрабатывать всегда, этот идёт минутами и только в облаке.

Гейт — `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE`: на машинах агентства (`/home/q`, `/opt/.openclaw`) скрипт выходит сразу, там свой Ruby через `bin/rb` и свои контейнеры, лезть туда с `apt` и `initdb` нельзя. Все шаги идемпотентны — на тёплом контейнере повторный запуск занимает секунды. Ни один шаг не валит старт сессии: отваливается, говорит об этом и пропускает зависящие, финальный `exit 0`.

**`.devcontainer/`** — `devcontainer.json`, `docker-compose.yml`, `post-create.sh`.

Переиспользует оба Dockerfile'а репозитория, и в этом смысл: база из `Dockerfile.postgres` — PG 15 + PostGIS 3.6 + pgvector, ровно прод и джоб RSpec; приложение из корневого `Dockerfile` — Ruby 3.4.10 с уже установленными гемами, без компиляции при старте.

Стек отдельный от корневого `docker-compose.yml`: тот боевой (`restart: unless-stopped`, `env_file: .env`, порт на `0.0.0.0`, volume'ы с прод-данными), а в свежем Codespace `.env` нет вовсе и compose упал бы на первой `${POSTGRES_USER}`. Боевой `ENTRYPOINT` перекрыт — он ждёт базу, гоняет `db:prepare` и поднимает Puma, а dev-контейнер должен просто жить.

## Расхождение сред — зафиксировано в шапке скрипта

Docker-демон в облачном контейнере **недоступен**, поэтому путь CI (сборка образа из `Dockerfile.postgres`) там закрыт и приходится брать системный PostgreSQL:

| Среда | PostgreSQL | PostGIS |
|---|---|---|
| Прод, CI, Codespaces | 15 | 3.6 |
| Облачная сессия | 16 | 3.4 |

Для прогона спеков это безразлично — `db/structure.sql` не пинит версии расширений, проверено. Но считать облачный прогон проверкой совместимости с прод-базой нельзя, последнее слово за джобом RSpec в CI. Записано в шапку скрипта, чтобы следующий читатель не обманулся.

## Проверки

Прогнано в облачной сессии на этой ветке:

- Полный прогон хука — `ruby:1 gems:1 postgres:1`, тестовая база готова. Повторный запуск на тёплом контейнере: «гемы на месте», «PostgreSQL уже поднят».
- `bundle exec rubocop app/services/topnlab/stages_cache.rb` → `1 file inspected, no offenses detected`
- `bundle exec rspec spec/models/property_spec.rb` → **29 examples, 0 failures** за 4.56 с — задействованы БД с PostGIS и pgvector, Redis, WebMock
- `bin/services-check` — зелёный
- Файлы Codespaces — синтаксис JSONC, YAML и bash

**Чего проверить не удалось:** фактическую сборку Codespace — docker-демона в облачной сессии нет, образы не собирались ни разу.

## Режим хука

Синхронный. Плюс — зависимости гарантированно готовы к первому запросу, агент не полезет гонять спеки раньше, чем поднимется база. Минус — первый холодный старт займёт минуты, в основном компиляция Ruby; состояние контейнера кэшируется, цена разовая. Переводится в async одной строкой, если приоритет — быстрый старт.

Действовать начнёт после мержа в `main`: все последующие сессии и Codespaces поднимутся уже с этим.

fagci
body:
## Контекст

После #10 (фикс фильтрации в многоступенчатой децимации) стало заметно реже прерываться на 2048k — но пользователь заметил регрессию: **по сравнению с изначальным (до всех этих правок) кодом прерывания появились и на 1024k**, хотя раньше 1024k работал вообще без затыков.

## Причина

#9 сократил частоту чтения для демод-режимов вдвое (20/сек → 10/сек, т.е. чанк вырос с ~50мс до ~100мс), чтобы вылечить перегрузку воркера от ДВУХ читателей, интерливящихся друг с другом (эффективный период доставки чанков в воркер получался вдвое короче номинального). Разумно на тот момент — воркер и правда не успевал.

Но это же изменение уменьшило гранулярность: тот же суммарный процент потерянного времени теперь размазан по вдвое более редким, но вдвое более крупным (и заметным на слух) провалам, вместо частых мелких. Это применялось ко ВСЕМ sample rate, включая 1024k, который раньше (до PR7-10) в этом изменении не нуждался вовсе — там воркеру всегда хватало запаса.

## Фикс

#10 сделал воркер заметно дешевле (дорогой канальный фильтр теперь считается на пониженной частоте, а не на полной sr). Значит, запас по CPU у воркера теперь больше, и можно вернуть частые мелкие чтения, не возвращая проблему интерливинга — тот чинится ИМЕННО одним читателем (не двумя), а не редкими чтениями. Поэтому:

- читатель для демод-режимов остаётся один (та часть #9, что реально чинила перегрузку — не трогаю);
- частоту чтения возвращаю обратно на 20/сек (как было ДО #9 и как сейчас в IQ-режиме) — чанк снова ~50мс вместо ~100мс.

## Как проверял

- `node --check` на `modules/sources.js` (изменение не в теле `RTL_WORKER_SRC`, туда не лезло).
- Playwright headless Chromium: все 65 встроенных пресетов — 0 структурных ошибок.

Это чисто про тайминг/расписание чтения USB, а не про DSP-математику — синтетическими тестами это не проверить, только на реальном железе. Жду обратную связь: пропали ли затыки на 1024k, и как теперь на 2048k (не стало ли хуже от возврата к более частым чтениям).

author: alexisvalotaire
body:
# Release steer 6.2.0

## Changes

- **Security: the five shipped workflow templates are hardened, and the zizmor
  tier over them is now a hard gate (closes #492).** They referenced actions by
  tag, declared no `permissions:` in `ci.yml`, persisted the checkout credential
  in every job, and gated Dependabot auto-merge on `github.actor` — which names
  the *last* actor to touch the context rather than the PR author, so a crafted
  HEAD commit can make it read `dependabot[bot]` while the rest of the branch is
  the attacker's. A tag is a moving pointer its owner can repoint at any commit,
  so every managed repo was running whatever that tag meant that day. All 25
  findings are resolved: every `uses:` is SHA-pinned with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment
  (resolved live via the API, cross-checked against this repo's own pins),
  `ci.yml` declares `permissions: contents: read`, read-only checkouts set
  `persist-credentials: false`, the auto-merge gate is
  `github.event.pull_request.user.login`, and `update-type` moves out of the
  `run:` body into `env:`. The two remaining `artipacked` findings carry
  `# zizmor: ignore[...]` with their reason: `claude-code-action` has no checkout
  of its own and writes through the workspace the step creates, so dropping the
  credential could break delivery in every managed repo. The `|| true` is gone
  from `mise run actions-security`, so a regression now fails the gate instead of
  being reported and scrolled past. A `MIGRATIONS.md` entry applies the same
  hardening to already-adopted repos — resolving SHAs live rather than copying
  them, and never moving a pin backwards past one Dependabot has already advanced.

- **Changed: CI skips draft PRs and cancels superseded runs; `/steer:work finish`
  marks the PR ready before watching.** The shipped `ci.yml` ran every job on every
  push to every PR, draft or not, and never cancelled a run its own next push had
  superseded — on an agent-driven branch that is where most of a repo's Actions
  minutes go, almost all of it on work still being written. `on.pull_request` now
  carries `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]`, every job
  (including the three advisory ones) carries a draft guard, and a `concurrency:`
  block cancels a PR's in-flight run on re-push — never on `main`, where each trunk
  commit keeps its own conclusive run. This is safe against branch protection
  because a *skipped* job satisfies a required check where an absent one does not,
  which is also why no `paths-ignore` is used. The trap it opens is on the skill
  side: a skipped check reads as green to `gh pr checks`, so `finish` could have
  reached `validate` with no test having run — it now runs `gh pr ready` **before**
  the watch, and treats a `skipped` check as a red flag rather than a pass.
  `/steer:work` gains the `gh pr ready` grant; a `MIGRATIONS.md` entry applies the
  four workflow edits to already-adopted repos, &&-ing the draft guard onto a job's
  existing condition rather than replacing it.

- **Added: a sub-second `mise run pre-commit` gate, wired to `.git/hooks/pre-commit`
  at bootstrap.** The scaffold had no commit-time gate at all, so the cheapest
  failures — a lint or format error — were only ever caught by a CI run. The new
  `pre-commit` task is `ci:hygiene` + `ci:lint` and deliberately nothing else: no
  typecheck (it needs an installed workspace) and no tests, because a tier that
  runs on every commit has to stay fast or it gets bypassed. `/steer:init` and
  `/steer:adopt` now run `mise generate git-pre-commit --task=pre-commit --write`,
  which needs no `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and no Python in a Node-only repo.
  `.git/hooks/` is not versioned, so the hook is per-clone state, not a committed
  file — a new `commit-gate` capability makes `/steer:sync` re-establish it for
  every teammate, and `/steer:adopt` reports-and-stops on a repo that already
  has its own `pre-commit` hook or sets `core.hooksPath`. Linked worktrees share the
  primary checkout's hooks, so `claude --worktree` needs nothing extra.

- **Added: the required `ci` check now runs as `mise run ci:*` tasks, so it runs
  on a laptop too.** The body of the shipped `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — stack
  detection, the "a detected stack with no test contract FAILS" rule, pytest's
  exit-5 handling, the changed-line coverage gate — lived only inside the YAML,
  reachable only by a GitHub runner. A contributor could not run the gate that
  decided their PR, and an org that exhausts its Actions minutes lost the ability
  to validate a managed repo at all. The logic moves to eight shipped
  `scripts/ci-*.sh` stage scripts (POSIX sh, shellcheck-gated, each self-detecting
  its stack and no-opping with a `::notice::` when absent), invoked by new `ci:*`
  tasks in the scaffold `mise.toml` and all sourcing a ninth, `scripts/ci-lib.sh`,
  that no task runs directly; the workflow's steps are now one `mise run`
  each. One definition, two entry points: `mise run check` (hygiene + lint +
  typecheck) is the fast local tier above the narrower `pre-commit` hook task, and
  `mise run ci` is the whole required check — a reproduction of CI rather than an
  approximation, which is what makes it a usable substitute when no runner is
  available. `build/SKILL.md` already
  allow-listed `mise run check` / `mise run ci`; the tasks behind that vocabulary
  now exist. Documented in `CONVENTIONS.md` -> "Standard mise tasks"; the
  `drift-gate` capability grows the scripts and the task wiring so `/steer:sync`
  repairs a half-installed gate; a `MIGRATIONS.md` entry re-takes the `ci` job's
  step region in already-adopted repos, carrying product-specific steps forward.

- **Fixed: a clean `/steer:questions` sweep no longer recommends busywork.**
  Its next-action table carried two rows that both matched a spine with nothing
  open — "All blocking questions resolved" (`Recommended`, re-run
  `/steer:spec validate`) and "Only non-blocking deferrals remain" (`Complete`).
  `Recommended` is level 6 in the shared safety precedence and `Complete` is
  level 7, so the follow-up won every time and `Complete` was unreachable: a
  sweep that found every question already resolved, nothing open, and wrote
  nothing still closed by prescribing a gate re-check over an untouched spine — a
  recommendation that contradicted the body directly above it. The two rows are
  now disjoint: the `/steer:spec validate` row fires only when the run actually
  wrote to the spine (and names the feature it touched, or `--all`), and a sweep
  that found no `open`/`investigating` question ends at `No action is currently
  required.` `/steer:doctor` had the same shape — "All green, repo already set
  up" prescribed `mise run dev:setup` unconditionally and buried its own
  `Complete` row; it is now conditioned on the run having installed or repaired
  something, with `dev:setup` kept as an optional continuation under `Complete`.
  `NEXT-ACTIONS.md` §3 states the underlying rule, so the next domain table
  doesn't reintroduce it: a `Recommended` row must name state observed as
  unfinished, never state that is also true when there is nothing to do.

- **Fixed: the scaffolded `ai-slop` CI job reports its findings instead of
  failing twice.** Both of its steps failed on a real consumer repo, neither
  because of the scanned code. The scan step: `aislop scan` applies the same
  exit rule as `aislop ci` — 1 on any error-severity finding or a score below
  `ci.failBelow` (default 70) — so under `bash -e` it died the moment the tool
  had something to report, which is the job's whole purpose. The upload step:
  code scanning is a **paid feature on private repos**, so `upload-sarif` ended
  at `Advanced Security must be enabled for this repository`. The job now writes
  `--json` and renders it as a step-summary table plus inline PR annotations —

author: bdart
body:
Last of the nine styling-primitive topics. The previous eight moved markup onto shared primitives; this one declares the contract that kits, themes and the add-in consume them through, and adds the tooling that keeps it honest.

## Why now

A component kit is a separately-deployed bundle that imports host values as **one flat named import**. If a single name leaves the surface, module linking fails *before* the kit's entry runs — so its version handshake never logs, and every override silently reverts to its default. `Tooltip` left the surface exactly that way once.

Six names reached the kit-facing surface only as a byproduct of an unrelated import graph, and three of them are **declared dependencies of shipped kits**:

| Name | Declared by |
| --- | --- |
| `MailIcon`, `PinIcon` | `component-kits/openwebui/kit.json` |
| `FileUploadLoading` | `component-kits/filesource-grid/kit.json` |
| `Card`, `ThreadMessageCard`, `ThemeProvider` | nothing |

Any refactor that stopped a registry-reachable component importing one of the first three would have taken that kit offline, silently. They are pinned now.

## What is in here

| Commit | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Declare the kit surface and the themeable host class names | Splits the hand-pinned half of `@erato/frontend/shared` into `shared/kit-surface.ts` with `ERATO_KIT_SURFACE_EXPORTS` as its string half; pins the six byproduct names, the nine library-only names and their prop types; adds the frozen 67-entry `ERATO_GEOMETRY_CLASS` record and exports it |
| Fail a component-kit build that imports host values off the shared surface | `component-kit/check-kit-manifest.mjs` — a kit may take **types** from `@erato/frontend/library`, never values. Wired into `component-kit-example`'s build and its own CI step |
| Document the host class hooks and which rule wins | Class-hook table, the layering rule, the `0` vs `0px` gotcha, and the `ModalBase` portal note. Fixes the Building Blocks table, which told kit authors to import from `@/…` — an alias a kit cannot resolve at all |
| Share the themable geometry lint rule between the frontend and the add-in | One `eslint/themable-geometry.mjs` instead of two hand-synchronised copies, moved out of the Lingui object whose `ignores` it was inheriting; three new selectors; a RuleTester suite wired to `test:eslint-rules` |
| Run the kit surface check under a symlinked package and warn on unpinned names | `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` is false through a pnpm symlink, which silently disabled the whole check when a kit invoked it by path |
| Share one default stub set across the add-in's barrel mocks | `createEratoLibraryMock` + the five largest suites converted, with a companion test asserting the stub set covers the declared surface so a future export cannot leave a mock hole |

## Visible delta

**None.** No component markup changed, no class value changed, no token changed. `ERATO_SHARED_SURFACE_VERSION` deliberately **stays 1** — both shipped kits compare it with strict `!==` in kit-side code, so bumping it would make every deployed kit log an error until rebuilt. Additive growth is carried by `ERATO_SHARED_SURFACE_MINOR`, 5 → 6.

No name left the surface. Verified with a TypeScript checker snapshot either side of the split: `/shared` 380 → 404 names, `/library` 1272 → 1283, zero removals on both.

author: zsn896
body:
The existing engine ranks candidates using its validation period and reports heuristic confidence scores. A score increase is not evidence of better forward accuracy.

Add a separate research model targeting four-plus hits directly. Use 60/20/20 chronological discovery/calibration/test boundaries; choose one to three precursor triples using calibration only. Score complete five-draw, non-overlapping episodes; shrink calibration estimates toward the exact chance baseline; report test Brier score, nominal lower confidence bound, and temporal halves. Abstain unless a predeclared historical gate passes.

Expose a read-only bounded archive analysis endpoint and an Arabic lab linked from the application. Include a clearly labeled frozen-legacy-candidate benchmark, not a claimed replay of production. The new model does not change production forecasts or write retrospective outcomes. Promotion requires real evidence and a prospective trial.

Tests cover fair-data rejection, planted-edge detection, untouched-tail invariance, missing windows, overlap, duplicate IDs and UI stale-result handling. Deployment validation will include the real archive.

## Production verification — 2026-09-14

All six original Strong Manual target sets were evaluated on the live archive (20,000 rows per target, fixed 60/20/20 split). Model commit: 70691d4365cb9e763a8734dd4b08fb90cdd25e06. Chance reference: 6.20845% per five-draw window.

|---|---:|---:|---|
| 9-17-37-51-56 | 11 / 87 | 12.64% | pass (exploratory) |

Only one of six targets passed the nominal historical gate. Multiple target testing and previous target selection mean this is exploratory, not a demonstrated prospective advantage. Production signals remain unchanged; no claim of improved production accuracy is supported yet. The lab is deployed at https://zsn896hotspottrackerlatest.vercel.app/signal-lab.html and its endpoint returned HTTP 200 for all six real-data requests. author: andste82
body:
An `enum` and a `bitfield` are bound by the **width their declaration implies** — for an enum the
smallest signed type holding every declared constant (`i8`..`i64`), for a bitfield the smallest
unsigned type holding its highest declared `pos` (`u8`..`u64`). A value inside that width is valid
even when the schema names no constant for it and even when it carries an undeclared bit; only a
value outside it is `INVALID` (§7.1). Undeclared bits are **not** masked away.

MESSAGE_SPEC §1, documentation `382159e` (doc PR #95).

## This is a partial revert, and the guard stays

#530 landed the closed-set reading nine days ago — an enum bound by its **set** of constants, a
bitfield by the **mask** of its declared bits — which MESSAGE_SPEC carried for six days (doc PR
#89, `a50db95`) before doc PR #95 withdrew it, after documentation#94 weighed the options against
the measured cost.

The pre-#530 state is **not** what this restores. That state was the defect: #513, where `1000`
into an `i8`-backed enum decoded as `-24` with the verdict `Ok`, and zig aborted the process on an
out-of-range `@intCast`. What changes is the **bound**, from a set/mask to an interval — which is
§1's own reason for the change: an array's elements are consumed inside the corelib loop, so a
bound has to cross that channel as an interval, and a width fits where a set does not.

So for the shared fixture (enum `{0,1,2,10}`, bitfield `pos{0,1,3}`):

| value | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| enum `5`, `-1` | INVALID | **valid** |
| enum `127`, `-128` | INVALID | **valid** (width edges) |
| enum `128`, `-129`, `1000` | INVALID | INVALID |
| bitfield `4` (undeclared bit 2) | INVALID | **valid** |
| bitfield `255` | INVALID | **valid** (width edge) |
| bitfield `256` | INVALID | INVALID |

## All eleven backends now enforce the same interval

Verified by generating one schema for every target and reading the emitted guard, not by trusting
the tests:

| backend | enum `{0,1,2,10}` | bitfield `pos{0,1,3}` |
|---|---|---|
| c | `int8_t` storage + corelib width check | `uint8_t` storage |
| cpp | `_v < -128 \|\| _v > 127` | `_v > 255ULL` |
| csharp | `value < -128 \|\| value > 127` | `value > 255` |
| dart | `value < -128 \|\| value > 127` | `(value & ~0xff) != 0` |
| go | `v < -128 \|\| v > 127` | `v > 255` |
| java | `value < -128L \|\| value > 127L` | `(value & ~0xffL) != 0` |
| kotlin | `value < -128L \|\| value > 127L` | `(value and 0xffL.inv()) != 0L` |
| python | `value < -128 or value > 127` | `(value & ~0xff) != 0` |
| rust | `value < -128 \|\| value > 127` | `value > 255` |
| typescript | `_v < -128 \|\| _v > 127` | `_v > 255` |
| zig | `value < -128 or value > 127` | `value > 255` |

The elisions agree too: a bitfield whose highest `pos` is 40 implies `u64` — the accumulator
itself — so **no** backend emits a guard for it.

## The bound is an interval, so it can travel

Three backends could hand it to the corelib instead of generating a per-element comparison, and
**deleted generated code** doing so:

* **go** — the width rides the matrix collector (`NewSignedMatrixSeq(..., -128, 127)`); the two
  generated wrapper types `_rowClosedMatElemElem` / `_rowClosedMbfElemElem`, each embedding a
  corelib seq and overriding its array callback, are gone.
* **dart** — `sofab.IntMatrixSeq(o.cmat, 2, true, -128, 127, ...)`; the generated collector
  subclass is gone.
* **python** — the whole bound is the `on_array_begin` interval; the array scan is gone.

## Where the bound comes from

`ir.EnumWidthRange` / `ir.BitfieldWidthMax` in `internal/ir/width.go`, beside `ir.NarrowRange` —
one derivation for the family. Both answer `ok == false` where the implied width is the 64-bit
accumulator and a guard would be dead code.

`generators/c/backend.go` used to re-derive the same widths by hand, which for the c target *is*
the bound (it emits no inline guard). It now calls the helpers. Proven inert: 26 schemas generated
before and after, `diff -r` over 52 files, no difference.

`internal/ir/closed.go` is deleted, together with `--legacy-closed-set`, `--hull-only` and the
legacy tables in the shared driver (renamed `check_declared_width_kinds.py`).

## Tests — family-wide, one case for every language

* `internal/ir` — width derivation at every edge (i8/i16/i32 boundaries, `pos`
  7/8/15/16/31/32/63), an enum with no constant, a bitfield with no flag, and the two values the
  withdrawn rule rejected and this one admits.
* Per backend — the six-position emission test (scalar, native array element, struct member,
  struct-array element member, union member, matrix row element × both kinds), plus the elisions,
  plus a test pinning that neither withdrawn form is emitted any more.
* **All eleven conformance suites** now run the shared driver — `c` was the one that never had
  this leg and now does, on both decode surfaces, `108 rows over 12 cells`, with **no**
  declension. Every config variant runs: cpp ×4, rust ×4, typescript ×3, python ×2 engines.

## Documentation

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` rewrote the enum/bitfield regions (+271/−341); three claims in it were
checked against code and found false — that corelib-c-cpp implements §1 at none of the six
positions (it passes all twelve cells), that kotlin rejects `5` (it accepts it), and that
`array<array<enum>>` does not compile on the C++ corelibs (#531 fixed that). `schema/README.md`
and the config schema's description text now separate the **authoring** rules (an enum `default`
must name a constant; an authored array-of-bitfield default must not set an undeclared bit —
both unchanged) from the **wire** bound, which is the width.

## Known, and deliberately left

* `cpp` still declines `matrix:enum` via `--skip-positions`. That predates #531 and is now
  broader than the target needs — a separate change with its own conformance run.
* `cpp`'s pure-corelib legs still decline `matrix:bitfield` beyond-width rows: `sofab::MessageSeq`
  reads a matrix row through an unbounded `readArray`, so `256` becomes `0` before generated code
  can test it. A corelib-side limit, not a codegen one.
* java and kotlin decline the corelib's bulk-element offer for both kinds. The rationale is
  restated (their `long`/`long[]` destination states no narrower width) but the decline itself is
  unchanged — it costs decode Ir (+4.2% java, +2.8% kotlin as measured in the migration commits)
  and is worth re-pricing now that the bound is an interval. Separate change, separate
  measurement.

body:
## Tóm tắt

Người dùng gửi mẫu biểu "Quy trình quản lý TS" (BM-TS01..06) và yêu cầu: đề xuất Sửa Chữa tài sản cần có ý kiến đánh giá của **Bộ Phận Chuyên Môn** trước khi người có thẩm quyền phê duyệt cuối cùng (đúng cột "Ý kiến của Bộ phận chuyên môn" ở Mẫu BM-TS02). Đã phân tích + gửi demo (mockup phiếu in) cho người dùng duyệt trước khi sửa code thật — người dùng xác nhận "Đúng rồi bạn làm đi nhé".

**Phần cấu hình (không cần code, admin tự làm)**: mọi quy trình nhiều bước đã hỗ trợ sẵn từ v22.6 việc đặt nhãn hành động riêng cho từng bước (VD "Cho Ý Kiến"). Admin chỉ cần vào **Hệ Thống → Quy Trình & Phê Duyệt → 🔧 QT Sửa Chữa**, thêm 1 bước "Bộ Phận Chuyên Môn" đứng trước bước phê duyệt chính thức.

**Phần sửa code (lỗ hổng phát hiện khi phân tích)**: phiếu in "Phiếu Phê Duyệt" trước đây CHỈ hiện ý kiến của bước duyệt CUỐI CÙNG (khối "Ý Kiến Chỉ Đạo Của Người Phê Duyệt Cuối Cùng" tách riêng) — nếu thêm bước ở giữa như trên, ý kiến bước đó sẽ bị rớt mất khỏi bản in. Đã sửa tại đúng 1 điểm dùng chung cho cả 3 loại phiếu (Đăng Ký Xe/Văn Bản Trình/VPP-Văn Phòng).

## Thay đổi

- `public/js/core.js`: `buildApprovalSignatureColumnHTML()` nay hiện ĐÚNG ý kiến (`history[].comment`) của CHÍNH bước đó ngay dưới chữ ký (khung `.as-sign-comment` nhỏ, chữ nghiêng), thay vì chỉ hiện của bước cuối.

author: brilhatex-dotcom
body:
Na tabela da **ESCALA DE SERVIÇO EXTRAORDINÁRIA**, a coluna FUNÇÃO DESEMPENHADA era texto livre. Numa operação com vários patrulheiros isso é digitar a mesma palavra dez vezes — e ainda sai `patrulheiro`, `Patrulheiro ` e `PATRULHEIRO` no mesmo documento, que vai impresso e assinado.

Agora é um seletor com **CMT · Aux. do CMT · Patrulheiro · Motorista**.

## O que foi preservado

- Função escrita **fora da lista** (de documentos já montados, ou uma função fora do comum) **não se perde**: aparece como opção própria dentro do seletor.
- **"outra (digitar)…"** volta ao texto livre para aquela linha, com um botão `▾` para retornar à lista. Ninguém fica preso às quatro opções.

## No papel continua texto

Caixinha de formulário impressa denuncia que o documento saiu de um sistema e fica feia no meio da tabela. Na tela o campo tem o tracejado e o realce que mostram que dá para clicar; na impressão perde borda, fundo e a setinha:

```
media print -> {borda: "none", fundo: "transparente", cor: "preto", aparência: "none"}
```

## De quebra, pelo mesmo motivo (velocidade)

**"+ adicionar linha"** agora herda **LOCAL, HORÁRIO e FUNÇÃO** da linha de cima. Numa operação essas três se repetem quase sempre; o que muda de verdade é nome, ID e CPF. Cada policial a mais passa a custar **três campos em vez de seis**.

## Verificação

`tsc`, `lint` e `build` limpos. Aparência conferida em navegador com o CSS real da folha, na tela e em `media print`. A folha publicada (somente leitura) já renderizava a função como texto puro — não precisou de mudança.

author: cod0216
body:
## 배경

간헐적으로 로그인이 풀려 온보딩으로 이동하는 문제를 재현하려고 한다. 이 문제는 refresh 로 토큰을 교체하는 순간 앱이 새 RT 를 잃어버릴 때 생긴다. ([BEA-306](https://linear.app/bean-zip/issue/BEA-306))

지금은 AT 가 15분이라 교체가 자주 일어나지 않아 재현이 어렵다. 팀원 두 명의 토큰만 짧게 발급해 교체 빈도를 높인다.

## 변경

`JwtTokenProvider` 에서 대상 사용자 두 명만 TTL 을 줄인다.

- `7dc0edad-f5ed-41a9-b828-4167c6646569`
- `c115f184-fbaf-4ec0-9fe0-66734c985b57`

| 토큰 | 기존 | 대상 사용자 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| AT | 15분 | **1분** |
| RT | 30일 | **10분** |

- 로그인(`issueSessionTokens`)과 refresh 가 모두 `createAccessToken` / `createRefreshToken` 을 거치므로 두 메서드만 바꿨다.
- Redis 세션 만료(`save` 의 `expire`, Lua 의 `PEXPIREAT`)는 RT 만료 시각을 그대로 따르므로 함께 10분이 된다.
- 다른 사용자의 TTL 은 바뀌지 않는다.

## 참고

- 배포 뒤 대상 사용자가 앱을 다시 켜면 refresh 가 일어나면서 짧은 토큰으로 바뀐다.
- 대상 사용자가 10분 넘게 앱을 쓰지 않으면 RT 만료로 로그아웃된다. 이때 서버는 `AUTH_REFRESH_EXPIRED` 를 반환하므로, 이번 버그의 `AUTH_REFRESH_REUSED` 와 구분할 수 있다.
- **임시 코드다.** 디버깅이 끝나면 이 커밋을 되돌린다.

## 검증

- 대상 사용자 두 명 모두 AT 는 1분, RT 는 10분 뒤 만료된다 (`issuesShortLivedTokensForDebugUser`, 파라미터 테스트)
- 기존 사용자는 15분 / 30일 그대로다 (기존 테스트)
- `userId` 가 null 이면 기존처럼 400 을 반환한다. `Set.of` 는 null 조회 시 NPE 를 던지므로 이를 고정했다 (`rejectsMissingUserIdAsBadRequest`)

전체 657개 통과.
