author: ovitrac
body:
## Harvest family and tender domain library

This PR moves into RAGIX the tools developed alongside the tender-response work, so that other projects can use them from the public package. It is a straight port. Each module is copied as it was, and the only edits are package imports, author headers, and removing any reference to the specific consultation the tools were developed on. No existing RAGIX kernel is modified.

### What is added

**`ragix_kernels/harvest/`, the harvest family, read-only over a `saqqara` document store:**
- `fr/`: French value readers, meaning typed values with units (grammars 1.5), dates, and cut detection for OCR digits split across lines (cut 1.1).
- `form`: the harvest form 0.8, with value substitution. Figures are read by the grammars and reinserted as markers, never written by the model.
- `runner`: the node, window and bake-off harvest runners, with bounded pools, refusal records, subset runs and resume.
- `derived`: the derived sidecar store, where anything computed is written (the source store is never written).
- Abstracts by recurrence on a word ladder (window, document, family, corpus), with provenance for every child used. Also the family rung.
- Node embeddings, where a node's vector at document grain and above is the mean of its children's vectors. Also the descent over the pyramid.
- The graph edges builder.
- The question-answering composer, with its fail-closed checker: a digit in a composed sentence must occur in a cited row, and reviewer corrections are applied at write time.
- Post-hoc re-scorers, and the brief checks.
- `registers/`: commitments, clauses, template slots and traps, where a traps register lists documents that contradict their family.
- `provenance`: the T0 manifest by content hash. `gold/`: the gold-by-blind-reading tools.
- `models/`: the Ollama Modelfiles that give Granite 4.2 its chat template, which the registry ships without, plus read-only resident-memory and concurrency monitors.
- `ragix_kernels/shared/journal.py`: a hash-chained event journal, which `activity.py` does not provide.
- `MIGRATION.md` maps every source to its target, with the source's sha256.

**`ragix_kernels/tender/domain/`, the tender domain library:** records, claims (ClaimRecord 1.1), contract, authority, routing, requirements, retrieval, pipeline, tagger, vocabulary, deadline slice, pyramid, agreement and substrate. It is also listed in `docs/KOAS_TENDER.md`.

### Tests

| | passed | skipped |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1 381 | 13 |
| this branch | 1 722 | 37 |

- `tests/harvest/` has 175 ported test items and 57 new ones. `tests/tender/` has 12 ported test files.
- Tests that need a reference store skip unless `HARVEST_REFERENCE_STORE` is set.
- The French readers, the form and the runner were also checked against their originals on the same input, with byte-identical output. The rest is covered by its ported tests.

### Public hygiene

```
check_forbidden: main..HEAD — 1137 blob revisions, 11 commit messages, 0 finding(s)
check_forbidden on the 101 added files: exit 0
diff grep (client and consultation identifiers, home paths, private addresses, redaction tags): 0
commit messages, attribution: 0
```

The AGPL guard tests pass. No added module imports a PDF library. The routing tests use PyMuPDF only to generate their test PDFs, and skip without it.

### To check before merging

- The consultation reference that tools matched in file names and headers is now read from `HARVEST_CONSULTATION`, which defaults to `REF-1`. Lab paths are read from `HARVEST_*` and `KOAS_JOURNAL_ROOT`. On a real corpus these must be set.
- Some data comes from a public consultation:
  - a vocabulary of 71 generic heading names, with buyer names neutralised;
  - a fixture of 50 claims;
  - the cue phrases in `authority` and `deadline_slice`, which are their matching logic.
- The scoped rules in `tools/check_forbidden.py` do not cover `harvest/` paths yet. They were run over every file of this diff by hand, with 0 findings. Adding the paths is an edit to an existing file.

### Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- KOAS kernel wrappers (`harvest_<verb>`), configuration and MCP tools over the moved modules, and a full `docs/KOAS_HARVEST.md` manual. The README lists the modules for now.
- A fix to the graph builder: « article N du CCTP » is resolved as a reference to lot N.
- Making every PDF read a port, with the permissive library as the default and PyMuPDF (AGPL) as an explicit per-deployment opt-in under the existing render guard. Today only rendering works this way.
- Changes to the store's own kernels, which need validation first: persisted spreadsheet cells, abstention on header bands that sit too deep, the roll-up seam overlap, and joining OCR leaves.

For the existing sequential instrument with known parameters, a single classical decision bit attains the full operational-memory optimum for every finite history length. A concrete two-weight example has exact classical score 5/2, while preserving a qubit gives sqrt(2) + sqrt(5)/2.

body:
Doorloop als leerling van het hele knapsack-hoofdstuk en de hand-out, daarna de fixes per patroon, daarna de toon; daarna de items van de hand-out vervangen zodat sorteren echt verliest, een kolom waarde per kilo bij de items, en een tweede doorloop en toonpas over het resultaat. Tien commits.

Preview: **[Knapsack 0/1 — het idee](https://knapsack-opknappen--algorithms.preview.coderius.nl/docs/knapsack/01-concept)** en de **[hand-out](https://knapsack-opknappen--algorithms.preview.coderius.nl/docs/unplugged/05-pak-de-rugzak-in)** (druk op Print deze hand-out voor de papieren versie).

## De hand-out: één blad

Was drie bladzijden plus antwoorden: vier knipkaartjes als codeblokken op pagina één, de tabel op twee, het teruglopen op drie. Nu is alles voor de leerling op de voorkant: links de items met waarde, gewicht en waarde per kilo en de twee sorteringen vooraf, rechts de drie regels met de formule, dan de invultabel over de volle breedte, daaronder teruglopen en nabespreken in twee kolommen. De antwoorden op de achterkant.

**Nieuwe items.** Op de oude hand-out gaf sorteren op waarde per kilo precies het optimum, dus wie zo sorteerde won van de tabel en leerde het omgekeerde van wat de werkvorm wil. De nieuwe set (2, 1 kg), (6, 2), (7, 3), (8, 5) komt uit een zoekscript: sorteren op waarde geeft 15, op waarde per kilo ook 15, de tabel vindt 16 met items 1, 2 en 4 die de rugzak precies vullen. De onderste rij verschilt nu van de rij erboven, dus het teruglopen begint met een echte stap. Een extra vraag laat de leerling uit de kolom van 5 kg aflezen wat de beste rugzak dan is: de tabel beantwoordt alle capaciteiten tegelijk, en bij 5 kg was sorteren per kilo toevallig wél goed.

Gecontroleerd door de build headless naar PDF te printen en te rasteren: twee pagina's, de voorkant compleet. Drie aanpassingen in de print-CSS raken ook andere hand-outs: de tussenkoppen van een compacte hand-out kregen hun 11.5pt niet (het thema wint op specificiteit, net als bij de H1), een overzichtstabel hoort smal en zonder schrijfhoogte, en rijkoppen die over drie regels braken maakten de invultabel te hoog. De kaarten-hand-out is ervoor en erna geprint: blijft twee pagina's, met koppen die niet meer afbreken.

## Sorteren verliest, en dat staat er nu ook

Het idee zei alleen in woorden dat sorteren niet werkt; nu laat het beide sorteringen op het eigen voorbeeld stranden op 35 tegen 40, en de itemtabellen in het idee, bij vul de tabel in en op de hand-out hebben een kolom waarde per kilo, zodat de leerling ziet waarop "sorteer per kilo" sorteert. Omdat het idee de sorteringen nu zelf weerlegt, waren stelling 1 en 2 geen voorspelling meer; ze vragen nu naar een eigenschap (zit het waardevolste item altijd in de beste rugzak, zit bij drie gegeven items het item met de beste waarde per kilo erin) met dezelfde tegenvoorbeelden.

## Wat de doorloop vond

Alle tabellen en optima heb ik met code nagerekend; die klopten. Wat niet klopte:

- **Stelling 2** antwoordde "Niet waar, niet altijd", gaf eerst een voorbeeld waarin greedy wél wint, en zei "gebruik recursie (deze track)" terwijl het hoofdstuk een tabel invult. **Stelling 5** was "Half waar". **Stelling 6** droeg O(n × W), en stellingen toetsen het idee, niet de notatie. `stellingen.test.ts` vangt nu ook "Half waar", "Deels" en "niet altijd".
- Onder de verwachte uitvoer van welke-items stond "Wacht, item 4 weegt 6, niet 7, klein typo hierboven", terwijl de uitvoer erboven gewoon 6 zegt.
- De **fouten-pagina** beloofde "crashes diep in de logica" bij een i-lus vanaf 0; het echte symptoom is een rij 0 vol waardes van het laatste item, dat daarna nog een keer meetelt (één item van 10 in een rugzak van 2 geeft 20). De test pint dat vast.
- Negen keer "de afbeelding van je docent" of "het image-voorbeeld": die afbeelding staat nergens. De categorie beloofde "recursief denken" voor een hoofdstuk zonder recursie.
- Zes pagina's hadden de oplossing als tip en geen Antwoord-blok; bouwsteen 2 gaf bij Voorspel letterlijk de code die eronder gebouwd moest worden (nu gaat het Voorspel over drie keer dezelfde rij in een tabel). De uitdaging van bouw zelf en het onderzoek van compleet hadden geen antwoord. `assert`, `enumerate`, `join` en `{c:2}` zonder uitleg.
- Twaalf keer "pagina 02", "pagina 5 en 6": het bestandsprefix, dat de sidebar niet toont. Nu links met de lestitel.
- Tweede ronde: de kop "twee vragen per item" boven een alinea over één vraag, "W = 11." los onder een tabel die de 11 kg al noemde, "de drie bouwstenen" waar het er vier zijn, en "de recurrence" in de cheatsheet als naam voor de drie regels.

## Tests

- `knapsack-oplossing.test.ts` (nieuw): draait per pagina de startcode met het Antwoord-blok erin en eist "Alle tests gehaald ✓"; de startcode alleen moet op een assert omvallen.
- `knapsack-tabel.test.ts` (nieuw): leest items en antwoordtabellen van vul de tabel in en de hand-out en legt er het algoritme naast; rekent de kolom waarde per kilo na; eist dat beide sorteringen op les én hand-out onder het optimum blijven, en dat het 5 kg-antwoord uit de tabel komt.
- Achterstanden leeg voor knapsack in `opdrachten`, `nummering` en `enumerate`.

## Om met de hand te checken

1. Print de hand-out en kijk of je in de cellen kunt schrijven en of de formule leesbaar is.
2. Het nabespreken: "Bij 5 kg pakte de tabel wél de items met de beste waarde per kilo. Wanneer werkt sorteren dus wel, en wanneer niet?" Is dat de vraag die je in de klas wilt stellen?
3. De nieuwe stellingen 1 en 2: voorspelt een leerling die het idee net las ze nog echt, of zijn ze te dicht bij het idee gebleven?

## Verificatie

- `pnpm test` — 1244 groen
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` — exitcode 0
- `scripts/draai-python-blokken.py algorithms` — 0 fouten
- `pnpm stijl --streng` en `pnpm spel` op hoofdstuk en hand-out — 0 meldingen
- build van de algorithms-site — exitcode 0; de hand-out als PDF geprint en per pagina gerasterd, ook na de kolom waarde per kilo

author: 27aaron
body:
修复容器部署时数据库无法创建的问题:`unable to open database file (14)`。

## 根因

v0.1.6 镜像以非 root 用户 `weread`(UID 10001)运行,但 bind mount 的宿主机
`./data` 目录通常由 Docker 以 root 创建——非 root 进程无法在其中创建
SQLite 文件,启动即 panic。

## 修复

- 新增 `docker/entrypoint.sh` 两阶段入口:以 root 启动时仅修复数据库目录
  与 SQLite 文件(db/-wal/-shm/-journal)的属主并收紧权限(600),随后通过
  `su-exec` 降权为 `weread` 运行应用
- 非 root 重新进入时校验目录可写,不可写时给出明确的中文错误提示
  (而不是 sqlite 的原始报错)
- Dockerfile:固定 UID/GID 10001(便于宿主机预先授权)、安装 `su-exec`、
  COPY 入口脚本、注入默认环境变量、`STOPSIGNAL SIGINT`
- README Docker 小节补充非 root 运行说明

## 验证

- `docker build` 通过
- 实测 root 属主的空数据目录:容器启动、`/readyz` 200、`weread.db` 连同
  WAL 文件正常创建
- `go build` / `go vet` / `go test` / `gofmt -l` 通过

author: kitten
body:
# Why

A follow-up change may introduce changesets for versioning, which currently would have to treat templates as separate targets. We can't publish from workspaces while `templates/*` aren't part of the workspaces, so this would retain manual publishing steps. Instead, it's easier to incorporate them, and introduce additional safe-guards instead.

The main steps this PR takes are:
- add templates to the workspaces, as regular parts of the pnpm monorepo
- move `expo/template.tgz` creation to `expo` scripts for consistency (and add to gitignore)
- Add script to validate `bundledNativeModules.json` against templates as safe-guard

# How

- Add `templates/*` to workspaces
- Add `prepack` script to `packages/expo` that creates `expo/template.tgz`
- Remove manual `updateProjectTemplates` due to switch to `workspace:~` specifiers
- Manually clean up `expo/template.tgz` in post-steps of publishing script
- Remove `templates` logic for workspace enumeration from `tools`
- Add validation script for templates against `expo/bundledNativeModules.json`

It's assumed that now as well as in a future changesets flow, `bundledNativeModules.json` is updated when packages are versioned (rather than it being switched to dynamic creation). However, this does mean that it can go out of sync for non-expo packages. To ensure it doesn't, templates dependencies are checked against it in its `test` script.

# Test Plan

- CI should run through as expected

author: sunrisepeak
body:
## Summary

**The defect** (read at `59068d6`, 2026.9.12.1): every download landed in
the shared runtime directory `<data>/runtimedir`
(`src/core/xim/installer.cpp` `runtime_dir_`, `task.destDir` near line
2575), every archive was extracted into that same directory
(`extract_archive_detailed(localFile, localFile.parent_path())` near line
2834, which returns the directory itself), and when `install_dir` was
still empty after hooks — always for a package with no `install()` hook,
and for a hook that does nothing — `stage_extracted_payload_(runtimedir,
install_dir)` (near lines 1121-1190, called near 3117) moved **every
entry** of the shared directory into that one package: other packages'
archives, their `.lock`/`.meta`/`.part.*` sidecars, and extracted trees.
Its branch that strips a single top-level directory (near line 1135) was
unreachable for a downloaded archive, because the archive file itself was
always a second entry beside the extracted tree — so the de facto layout
every hookless install has ever produced is un-stripped
(`<version>/<top-level-dir>/...`), and 55 mcpp-index descriptors (`mcpp =
"*/…/mcpp.toml"`) plus mcpp's `*/mcpp.toml` default lookup depend on that
layout. Measured on the reporting machine's mcpp registry: 221 of 401
version directories carried swept sidecars, 5.2 GiB of foreign archives.

**The rule** (new, `docs/spec/xpkg-manifest-v1.md` §6): a package that
defines no `install()` receives in its install directory exactly the
entries of its own archive, laid out as the archive lays them out (the
top-level directory is **kept**, never stripped), and nothing else; the
archive stays in the download cache.

**The change:**

- **X1** (`src/core/xim/installer.cpp`, `installer.cppm`) — a package
  without an install hook no longer extracts into `runtimedir` at all.
  When staging is actually needed (`!payloadInstalled` and `install_dir`
  has no entries), its archive is extracted into a private,
  per-installation directory
  (`<runtimedir>/.stage/<sanitized plan key>-<pid>/`, same volume so the
  final move is a rename; RAII-removed on every exit path via the new
  `ScopedStageDir_`) and staged from there. A package **with** an install
  hook still extracts beside its archive first — that is the hook's
  contract (xpkg-manifest-v1 §8.2's example derives the extracted
  directory from `install_file()`). If the hook leaves `install_dir`
  empty anyway (e.g. the patchelf case noted near the auto-stamp comment),
  the archive is extracted a **second time**, privately, and staged from
  there — the staging fallback never reads `runtimedir` again.
  `stage_extracted_payload_`'s single-top-level-directory stripping
  branch is **deleted**: with a private extraction it would become
  reachable and strip the very layout the spec now requires. Script
  (pkgType 1) and SubOS (pkgType 4) default installers are unaffected —
  they fill `install_dir` before staging runs.
- **X2** (`docs/spec/xpkg-manifest-v1.md`) — §6 states the rule above, in
  the document's own language (Chinese), as declarative sentences.
- **X3** (`src/core/xself/doctor.cpp`, `doctor.cppm`,
  `src/core/xself/repair.cpp`, `repair.cppm`) — `xlings self doctor`
  reports a payload whose top level carries the sweep's fingerprint
  (new `FindingKind::SweptPayload`, detected by the new
  `xim::swept_payload_marker`: a zero-length `<name>.lock` paired with a
  sibling `<name>`, a `<name>.meta` sidecar, or an entry ending in a
  download/archive extension). `--fix` repairs it by **reusing** the
  existing reinstall ladder (`repair_one` in `xself/repair.cpp`) — but a
  swept payload already reads as successfully installed (the version
  database agrees with it), so the ladder's cheap first rung (`xlings
  install` alone) would report the finding "healed" without touching the
  contamination. `repair_one` now skips that rung for the new
  `RepairKind::SweptPayload` and goes straight to remove-then-install, so
  the reinstall's `install_dir` is genuinely empty and reaches the
  private-extraction staging fallback. After `--fix`, the directory
  equals a fresh install.
- **X4** — two new e2e scripts and new unit tests (see Test plan).

## Test plan

Build and unit tests:
```
mcpp build     # Finished dev in 24.53s (after the version bump; fingerprint a42d990378affbe5)
mcpp test      # test result ok. 56 passed; 0 failed
```
New unit tests (all pass): `StageExtractedPayloadTest.*` (4, regression
guard for the deleted stripping branch), `PrivateStageDirTest.*` (3), and
`SelfRepairLadder.SweptPayloadSkipsReRegisterAndGoesStraightToRemoveAndInstall`
+ `SelfRepairLadder.BrokenPayloadStillTriesReRegisterFirst`.

New e2e (both need no network — a fixture archive is pre-placed at the
exact path the downloader would have saved it to, with a matching
sha256, so downloader.cpp's cache-hit path never fetches the URL):

```
XLINGS_BIN=<built xlings> bash tests/e2e/hookless_install_stages_own_archive_test.sh
  → PASS: hookless_install_stages_own_archive   (positive + layout)

XLINGS_BIN=<built xlings> bash tests/e2e/doctor_swept_payload_test.sh
  → PASS: doctor_swept_payload
```

Negative leg, run against the released 2026.9.12.1 binary (this repo's
own `main` checkout, commit `59068d6`, built separately):
```
XLINGS_BIN=<2026.9.12.1 binary> bash tests/e2e/hookless_install_stages_own_archive_test.sh
  → FAIL: hookless-multi-fixture install_dir has 8 non-bookkeeping entries,
    expected exactly 3 (bin, lib, README.txt); got: bin, hooked.tar.gz,
    hooked.tar.gz.lock, hookless-multi.tar.gz.lock, hookless-single.tar.gz,
    lib, README.txt, .xpkg-install.json, .xpkg.lua
    — the previously-installed hooked-fixture's archive (and its .lock,
    and a THIRD package's not-yet-installed archive) swept into an
    unrelated package's install_dir.

XLINGS_BIN=<2026.9.12.1 binary> bash tests/e2e/doctor_swept_payload_test.sh
  → FAIL at D2: self doctor reports rc=0 with only an unrelated warning —
    FindingKind::SweptPayload / repair_swept_ do not exist in that build,
    so the seeded fingerprint is invisible to it.
```

Nearest existing e2e (all pass against the built binary, no regressions):
`foreign_payload_reinstall_test.sh`, `self_doctor_test.sh`,
`doctor_fix_convergence_test.sh`, `doctor_removed_not_reinstalled_test.sh`,
`doctor_honest_verdict_test.sh`, `pkginfo_install_dir_test.sh`,
`install_idempotent_test.sh`, `install_refresh_on_missing_test.sh`,
`install_silent_failure_test.sh`, `config_install_no_implicit_dir_test.sh`,
`script_type_install_test.sh` (pkgType 1, confirms Script is unaffected),
`subos_xpkg_install_test.sh` (pkgType 4, confirms SubOS is unaffected),
`fresh_xlings_home_install_test.sh`.

Not run: `elfpatch_install_verify_test.sh` — its setup requires a packaged
`build/release.tar.gz` from the release scripts, which was not built here
(a plain `mcpp build` output does not satisfy it); the patchelf
hook-that-does-nothing path it would exercise is covered instead by the
unit tests above and by the design reasoning in the PR description.

`mcpp.lock`: `ftxui`'s entry moved from the `compat` namespace to
`mcpplibs` — the live xim/mcpplibs index has migrated it since this
repo's lock was last committed, and this repo's pinned dev-mcpp
(2026.8.8.4) re-resolves it that way on every fresh build regardless of
this change (reproduced identically, independently, by both `mcpp build`
after the version bump and by `mcpp test`). Included so a stale entry an
unrelated build step keeps silently rewriting does not surface in some
later, unrelated diff.

Refs mcpp-community/mcpp#636

## Summary

Adds the remaining twelve rows of the `survey_base` domain marker validator's
test surface to `tests/testthat/test-s7-classes.R`:

- Four further wrong types: double, character, factor, list.
- The two constructor routes (`as_survey()` and `as_survey_nonprob()`) given
  a data frame that already carries an integer marker.
- The rollback row: a failed write leaves the design with no marker column.
- The remaining accept rows: replicate with an all-`NA` marker, a logical
  marker carrying a `label` attribute that survives the write, the zero-row
  `logical(0)`/`integer(0)` pair, and two-phase with one `NA` where the
  design's own subset column is left alone.

## Why separate from #272 and #273

#272 shipped the validator and proved the reject path on all four concrete
classes. #273 proved the accept path. This PR is breadth: the remaining
type and shape coverage. Splitting kept each PR's entry inside the arc's
12-row and 8-criteria budget.

## Non-vacuity

Verified with the validator's type check temporarily disabled: exactly 13
expectations fail — the seven reject rows, the rollback row's two
assertions, and the four class rows from #272 — and no accept row among
them. The check was restored before commit; this PR changes no file under
`R/`.

## Test-only

- No `R/`, `man/` or `NAMESPACE` change.
- The shared `set_domain_marker()` fixture is read, not edited.
- No snapshot is added — Layer 1 S7 validator errors are asserted by class
  only.

## Scope note

PR 3 of 6 in the domain-marker-logical arc. The behavioural fixes —
`.apply_domain()` resolving `NA` to `FALSE`, and `.restrict_to_domain()`
dropping its coercion — follow in the next PRs.

- devtools::test(): 11825 pass / 0 fail (+20 expectations over `develop`)
- R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 pre-existing NOTEs

Flat coverage and any red `codecov/patch` reflect covr's inability to
attribute execution inside an S7 `validator =` closure — the control is
`R/core-classes.R:709`, a pre-existing guard nine passing tests exercise
that covr still reports uncovered. `codecov/patch` is not a required check.

author: jorgeesala
body:
## Qué cambia

Arregla el bug intermitente al editar una venta de remesa: "no hay ruta, las rutas no cargan y Guardar Cambios no aplica".

### Causa raíz

- `useRoutes()` cacheaba con la key global `["routes","list"]` y `staleTime` de 10 min, pero las rutas viven en el esquema de cada unidad y el endpoint depende del header `X-Business-Code`. Al pasar por otra unidad (ej. pollo) y volver a huevo, la lista cacheada era la de la otra unidad y no refetcheaba: las rutas no aparecían.
- El input visible de ruta tenía `required` nativo y **no estaba registrado en RHF** (el valor real va en un hidden). Si la lista no contenía la ruta de la venta, el input quedaba vacío y el navegador bloqueaba el `<form>` **antes** de RHF, sin mensaje: "Guardar Cambios" no hacía nada. Refrescar vaciaba la caché y funcionaba.

### Fix

- `routeKeys.list(business)` / `detail(business, id)` ahora incluyen el `slug`; `useRoutes`/`useRoute` lo leen de `useParams` con `enabled: !!slug`. Esto corrige también `TripInlineRow`, `FuelFields`, `RoutesTab` y los modales de pago que usan rutas.
- `EggMovementFields` y `ChickenMovementFields`:
  - Muestran la ruta guardada aunque no esté en la lista (`routeName` del detalle o `Ruta #id`), y el hidden conserva el `routeId`.
  - Se quitó el `required` nativo del input (y del alta rápida de ruta); si falla la carga aparece "No se pudieron cargar las rutas" con **Reintentar**.
- `BatchMovementModal.onValid`: si es una venta sin ruta, muestra "Ruta: Selecciona una ruta" en el modal en lugar de no hacer nada. En bajas/ajustes la ruta no se exige.

## TDD

- `routes.queries.test.tsx` (nuevo): key por unidad, dos unidades no comparten caché, sin slug no consulta, y el detalle también se scopea.
- `BatchMovementModal.test.tsx`: muestra la ruta guardada aunque no esté en la lista y guarda con ese `routeId`; venta sin ruta muestra el mensaje y no guarda; error de rutas muestra mensaje + Reintentar.

## Verificación

- `npx tsc --noEmit` OK
- `npm run lint` → 0 errores (160 warnings preexistentes)
- `npm run test` → 33 archivos, 258 tests OK
- `npm run build` OK
- `npx prettier --check` en archivos tocados OK

Solo frontend; PR a `dev`.

author: sger
body:
## Summary

**What changed?** Generics ship for the unconstrained case. An unannotated
definition that takes parameters and raises no class constraint is now generic
(G5) — `fn identity(x) { x }` is usable at `Int` and `String` with no
signature, exactly as `fn identity<a>(x: a) -> a` is. Tuple projection became a
real solver predicate rather than a shape guessed at the access site (0185
stage 5), type aliases resolve (G3/G4), binding groups are inferred and emitted
in dependency order (R1), and a generalized definition whose call sites all
agree on one instantiation is lowered under that substitution (B1).

Fourteen known issues close: KI-079, KI-082, KI-083, KI-087, KI-088, KI-091,
KI-092, KI-093, KI-094, KI-095, KI-096, plus KI-011, KI-069 and KI-070 marked
fixed by verification. `examples/generics/` lands as 48 snapshot-pinned
programs — 30 accepts, 4 rejects, 14 failing — organised by what the compiler
actually does with them, with every error code measured rather than copied from
the roadmap.

**Why was it needed?** The annotation was what made a function generic. That is
not the Hindley–Milner rule, and it is not what any of the proposals described;
`monomorphism_restriction` already existed and was already GHC-shaped, withheld
by one extra conjunct. The *constrained* half — `fn double(x) { x + x }` —
stays monomorphic without a signature, because there is nowhere to get the
dictionary. That is 0.0.8's B2, and it needs the evidence translation
underneath it (0186 stage 5).

**0.0.7 has open items, and one is caused by this branch.** They are listed
under *Notes for Reviewers* rather than left for a reader to find.

### Cache epoch: 43 → 53

Bumped per landing rather than once at the end. Every bump from 47 on is the
same reason — the change alters inferred types, so it alters what a cached
interface records. 47 R1, 48 KI-095, 49 KI-096, 50 stage 5, 51 G5, 52 KI-094,
53 the projection predicate no longer being retained on a scheme.

That last one is worth stating plainly: retaining a determined projection
predicate on a scheme made **every caller of `Flow.Array.update_many` an
`E490`**, because a `SchemeConstraint` cannot carry `TupleProjection`'s index,
so the re-raised predicate went looking for a literal field named `__tuple`. An
epoch-52 `.flxi` records that context, and a caller reading it is an `E490`
this compiler accepts.

KI-079's own fix deliberately took no bump: adding the compiler build to the
cache key changes every hash, so stale entries stop being *found* rather than
being read and mistaken for current.

## Change Type

- [x] Feature — G5, 0185 stage 5, G3/G4, R1, B1, `FLUX_DBG_EVIDENCE`
- [x] Bug fix — fourteen known issues
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs — proposals 0182–0187 restatused, the 0.0.8/0.0.9 split recorded,
      the GHC comparison re-verified
- [x] Release/Infra — `CACHE_EPOCH` 43 → 53, `examples/generics` added to the
      release parity sweep, `// requires:` added to the parity harness

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --all --all-features` — 3535 passed, 0 failed, 37 ignored,
      across 194 targets
- [x] VM smoke run — `parity-check examples/generics/working/accepts --ways
      vm,llvm` 30/30; `parity-check examples/guide --ways vm,llvm` 57 pass,
      0 mismatch, 2 skip (both platform-gated, see below)

**`generics/working/accepts` is what joins the release sweep**, not bare
`generics` — `failing/` is fail-on-purpose for the same reason `parser_errors`
and `runtime_errors` are excluded there.

### What this validation does not establish

**A sweep sees outcomes, not precision.** Parity and the snapshot corpus record
that a program compiled, ran, and produced a value. They do not record that it
was typed for the right reason. A wrong inference that happens to produce the
right value passes every gate here.

**KI-062 is why that matters.** The parity harness used to accept a fixture
that failed to compile on both backends — `expect: success` did not require
success. Fixing it found **7 of 133 fixtures had never run**. A gate that
cannot fail is indistinguishable from a gate that passes, and the only reason
it was caught is that someone checked the gate rather than its output.

## Release Impact

- [ ] No user-facing change
- [x] User-facing change — this PR's description is the changelog entry
- [x] Docs updated — `docs/versions/*`, `docs/roadmaps/*`,
      `docs/proposals/0182`–`0187`, `docs/internals/typeclass_vs_ghc.md`,
      `docs/known_issues.md`, `examples/generics/README.md`

author: imuromtsev
body:
## Why

A configuration key written as `myKey` instead of `my-key` was reported as a **warning**, next to genuine problems such as *Cannot resolve key property*. It is not a defect: Spring's relaxed binding resolves every spelling to the same property.

That is true for `@Value` and `Environment.getProperty` too, not only `@ConfigurationProperties` binding — Spring Boot puts `ConfigurationPropertySourcesPropertySource` first in the `Environment`, and its `getProperty` goes through the relaxed lookup:

```java
findConfigurationProperty(ConfigurationPropertyName.of(name, true));
```

`ConfigurationPropertyName` equality uses the **UNIFORM** form (lowercase, alphanumeric only, separators stripped), so `my_key`, `my-key` and `myKey` are one and the same property.

## What changed

**Severity → weak warning**, at all three sites: `SpringYamlInspection`, `SpringPropertiesInspection`, and the `@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = …)` check in `SpringConfigurationPropertiesInspection`.

The drop is **per descriptor**, not `level=` in `plugin.xml`. Those two inspections also report unresolved keys and a prohibited profile key; changing the registered level would have downgraded those too. They keep `WARNING` and `GENERIC_ERROR` respectively.

**Wording → "canonical form".** The check accepts a digit inside a word — `smart529` and `v4` are already canonical, since a dash is inserted only for a `-`/`_` separator or before an uppercase letter — so "kebab-case" describes it imprecisely:

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| quick fix | `Switch to kebab-case` | `Switch to canonical form` |
| problem | `Should be kebab-case` | `Key is not in Spring's canonical form` |
| prefix | `…must be in kebab case…` | `The prefix must be in Spring's canonical form…` |

Both inspection descriptions also said *"placeholders not in snake-case"* — wrong on both counts. Now *"keys not in Spring's canonical form"*.

## Verification

`./gradlew :spring-core:test` — **1491 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (exit 0), up from 1487 by exactly the 4 added.

`CanonicalKeyFormSeverityTest` is the test that fails if the severity is ever restored. It reads `HighlightSeverity` back from `doHighlighting()` rather than asserting a marker, and pins the contrast: the case problem is weak *while an unresolved key in the same file is still a warning*. Red phase, with only the `SpringYamlInspection` severity reverted:

```
AssertionFailedError: A non-canonical key must be reported as a weak warning, was WARNING(300)
  expected:<WEAK WARNING(200)> but was:<WARNING(300)>
```

Its first version was **vacuous** and said so: the fixture produced no unresolved-key problem at all, and the built-in guard `"The fixture must still produce an unresolved-key problem, otherwise the contrast proves nothing"` failed. An unresolved key is only reported under a prefix some class declares, so the fixture now adds a real `@ConfigurationProperties` owner.

`SpringCoreBundleRenderingTest` covers a separate trap found here: the bundle convention doubles apostrophes for `MessageFormat`, but `BundleBase.postprocessValue` **skips `MessageFormat` entirely when a message takes no parameters**. Writing `Spring''s` in these zero-argument messages rendered literally as `Spring''s` — caught by asserting the rendered text, not by reading the code.

## Note

The existing highlighting fixtures did already check weak warnings: `testHighlighting(vararg)` delegates to `testHighlighting(true, false, true, …)`. So the updated markers still constrain severity — a `<weak_warning>` marker fails if the problem is emitted as a warning, as the red phase above demonstrates.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## The problem

`proxy/dhan-cors-worker.js` has supported an `ALLOW_TOKENS` shared secret since it was added, and its preflight response already advertises `x-proxy-token` in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`. But **there was no way to send that header from the page.**

So following step 4 of `proxy/README.md` made the proxy unusable: every request came back `401 {"status":"unauthorized"}`, and the page dropped to paper mode with a generic *"Dhan connection failed: Dhan API Error 401"* message that gave no hint about the token.

## What this adds

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `dhan-live.html` | Masked **Proxy token** field in the 🔑 Dhan Account card, beside API proxy |
| `auto-trading/brokers/dhan-broker.js` | `proxyToken` config → `x-proxy-token` header, **only when a proxy URL is set** |
| `proxy/README.md` | Corrected step 4 |

The field is `type="password"` (matching the Access Token field), persisted in the same `localStorage` key as the rest of the connection config, and refilled on load.

**The header is gated on `this.usingProxy && this.proxyToken`.** A proxy-specific secret has no business being sent to any other host, so direct `api.dhan.co` calls never carry it — even if a stale token is sitting in the saved config.

Step 4 previously said *"Then send it from the page as an `x-proxy-token` request header"* — advice the page could not follow. It now says to paste the secret into the **Proxy token** field, and documents the 401 recovery path (re-`put` or `delete` the secret) plus a `curl` check that actually works.

## Two small additions serving the same fix

Flagging these explicitly as they go slightly beyond the field + header:

1. **`connectDhan()` refuses a Proxy token with no API proxy URL.** The token would be silently ignored — the exact class of confusion this PR removes. Mirrors the existing `https://`-format guard directly above it.
2. **A 401 from a configured proxy gets a specific alert** naming `ALLOW_TOKENS` and the Proxy token field, instead of the generic failure text. Dhan never returns that error shape, so it can only be the proxy's own token check.

## Verification

Driven through a real DOM (jsdom) against the served page, then page → broker → **the actual Worker module** → a stubbed `api.dhan.co`:

- ✅ Both fields render in the Dhan Account card; Proxy token is masked
- ✅ Round-trips through `localStorage`; refilled on load
- ✅ Correct token → badge flips to **LIVE**, Worker forwards to `https://api.dhan.co/v2/funds`, Dhan `access-token` + `client-id` intact
- ✅ The Worker drops `x-proxy-token` when forwarding — **the proxy secret does not leak upstream to Dhan**
- ✅ Wrong token → 401 at the Worker's token check, **never reaches Dhan**, new hint shown, stays in paper mode
- ✅ Blank token with `ALLOW_TOKENS` set → same (reproduces the original bug, now with an actionable message)
- ✅ Proxy set, token blank → header omitted, connects fine (Worker skips the check)
- ✅ Direct mode (no proxy) → `api.dhan.co`, **no** `x-proxy-token`, no regression
- ✅ Token + no proxy URL → refused with a clear warning, no request sent
- ✅ Trailing-slash / already-versioned proxy URLs still resolve correctly (`…/v2/funds`)
- ✅ Broker unit checks for `DHAN_PROXY_TOKEN` / `DHAN_PROXY_URL` env fallbacks
- ✅ Worker contract: Origin allowlist still evaluated **before** the token check; 403 for foreign/absent Origin even with a valid token; preflight advertises `x-proxy-token` (without it the browser blocks the real request)
- ✅ Existing `tests/full-market-stub-fetch.test.js` still passes; `node --check` clean on the broker and the page's inline script

No `package.json` in this repo, so the jsdom harness was kept out of the tree — no new dependencies.

author: bjmeetsfo
body:
`test_pre_retrieval_refresh_can_skip_pending_new_event_dirty_markers` has been red in
`python_suite_baseline.json`. **The control it guards is fine.** This is a negative result: the
test was the only thing wrong, and it had been red long enough to stop checking the lines below
its first failure.

WHAT THE CONTROL ACTUALLY DOES

Measured on the scenario the test itself builds. One `fast_async_hook_ingest` leaves five pending
markers -- four `new_event` up the session chain, one `profile_entity_promoted` on the profile
node. With the hook's own list, `skip_dirty_reasons=["new_event"]`:

    skipped_dirty_reasons   {'new_event': 4}
    refreshed               1  (the profile node, and only it)
    nodes marked ONLY by new_event that were refreshed:   none
    same pass without the list:  refreshes exactly those four, skipped_dirty_reasons {}

Every marker the list names was skipped, no node it held back was summarized, and the held-back
work was deferred rather than dropped.

WHY IT WAS RED

The two failing assertions were about the shape of the store, not about the control.

`refreshed_count == 0` stopped holding when the ingest began promoting profile entities, which
mark a node under a reason the list does not name. `assertFalse(any(context_summary))` stopped
holding when the ingest began writing its own `batch_l0` summary inline, before the refresh runs
at all.

Neither is the skip leaking. The same ingest commits its batch inline, so by the time the refresh
runs there are no pending session events left and the profile entity was promoted from a
COMMITTED event -- which is exactly what the test's own text says must not be summarized.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER READING

I first reported this as the event-count backfill at the end of `pending_dirty_node_records`
re-adding a node whose only marker the skip list had just excluded. That is wrong. Instrumenting
the callee shows the backfill never fires in this scenario; the one selected node carries a real
`profile_entity_promoted` marker. Recorded here because the wrong reading was mine and it was
plausible enough to act on.

WHAT THE TEST ASSERTS NOW

Both marker sets are read out of the store rather than written down, so a change in how many of
each the ingest emits cannot silently empty either claim; two denominators fail if either set is
empty.

The STORE is checked before the returned report. A pass that does the work and says it did not is
the shape worth catching, and the `refreshed` list is written by the same code that decided to
skip -- only the stored summaries are independent of it.

MUTATION TESTED

Each treatment verified applied by line number before the run, green again after each revert:

    skip never fires                     -> store check: "the skipped pass summarized ... anyway"
    counted as skipped, selected anyway  -> same store check
    skip swallows every reason           -> report check: the unnamed reason did not run

No production code changes. Suite: zero new failures; failing names diffed against main on the
same box, 79 -> 78, the single difference being this test.

author: oleksandrua
body:
## Why

The execution retention job failed on staging with a statement timeout. Its batch selects had a `LIMIT` but no cursor, so every batch read again the rows that earlier batches had already cleared, until one batch ran past the timeout. The CronJob then retried, and the rows the failed run had cleared were never counted, because the route records metrics only on success.

The plan-window pass had a second version of the same problem. It walked one organization at a time with the organization filter in SQL. For an organization with few runs, the planner answers that query by walking the whole run index for a page it can never fill, so a single page can run past the timeout.

## What changes

- Every pass pages with a keyset cursor on `(timestamp, id)`, so a page never goes back over rows behind it. The timestamp travels as text: a JS `Date` keeps only milliseconds, and a millisecond cursor made a page of one row return the same row forever.
- The plan-window pass walks each retention window once, over all runs in the window's date range, and checks each run's organization in code. A page is simply the next runs by `started_at`, so its cost does not depend on how many runs an organization has.
- An organization behind the window's front would drag that shared walk back. A new organization starts at the floor cutoff, a deferred one keeps an old watermark, and a stuck run holds one down. Each organization behind the front is probed through its own workflows for its earliest run that still has step logs and its earliest resumable run, and the walk starts it there. A probe runs under a short statement timeout; if it times out, that organization starts at its own watermark, which is slower but still correct.
- A run that can still resume holds its organization's watermark at its own `started_at`. A run that finishes after the walk passed it is picked up by a later run.
- The walk never starts below the floor cutoff. Everything older belongs to the floor pass, so a dry run no longer counts those rows twice.
- When the budget or an error stops a walk, every organization in that window records the last run handled, so the next run continues instead of starting the window over. Watermarks are written with chunked upserts.
- The dry run walks the same pages without writing, instead of counting the whole table.
- A failure inside a pass, including a lookup or a watermark write after pages have committed, comes back as that pass's `error` with the rows already removed. The run stops at that pass, and the route records those rows, counts a failed run and returns 500 with the partial result.
- The CronJob runs at 06:48 UTC instead of 03:48, clear of the nightly database backup, on staging and prod.

## How I checked it

- Real-Postgres tests in `tests/db`:
  - a cursor over timestamps with microseconds;
  - a dry run that matches the real run, including a run older than the floor;
  - a page failure in the output_raw pass;
  - a page failure in the plan-window pass with a pin below the stopping point and microsecond timestamps, where progress rounds down and the next run finishes the window;
  - an organization left behind by a plan-change deferral, caught up from its own oldest run on the next run;
  - the existing plan-window, watermark and run-row cases.
- I broke the floor clamp, the progress write, the text cursor and the probe on purpose, one at a time. Each time, the test that covers it failed.
- Unit and route tests cover the new control flow, including the probe timeout fallback and the partial-failure 500.
- I checked against a real Postgres that a statement timeout inside the probe transaction raises SQLSTATE `57014` in the shape the fallback reads, and that `SET LOCAL` does not outlive the transaction.
- I captured the SQL that drizzle generates from the Postgres statement log and ran plain `EXPLAIN` on a production-sized database, read-only.
  - The window walk page plans as an index scan on `idx_workflow_executions_started_at` under the `LIMIT`. The plan is the same for a first run from the floor cutoff, a page after a cursor, and a one-day steady-state range.
  - The probe plans as `idx_workflows_org_id`, then a backward scan of `idx_workflow_executions_workflow_started_covering` per workflow with an index-only check on `idx_exec_logs_execution_id`. For the largest organization it plans a scan of `workflows` first, which is the case the probe timeout covers.
  - The floor, output_raw and soft-delete pages, and the delete by `execution_id`, all use their indexes.
- Locally I ran `pnpm check`, `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm type-check:executor`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:unit`, `pnpm test:integration` and `pnpm test:db` on a freshly migrated database. One on-chain integration test cannot pass locally without the RPC configuration that only CI has.

author: sefalk
body:
Second batch for #280. Twelve of the 64 PowerShell-only `block-dangerous` cases were shared in the first batch; this one shares five more and lowers the ratchet ceiling from 52 to 47 in the same commit.

## What changed

Five deferral cases moved out of `test-hooks.ps1` and into `block-dangerous.cases.tsv`, where both dialects execute them against their own hook:

| case | command |
|---|---|
| a formatter run defers to the native assessment | `ruff format .` |
| creating a directory defers to the native assessment | `mkdir build` |
| package installs defer to the native assessment | `pip install requests` |
| conda environment changes defer to the native assessment | `conda install numpy` |
| non-terminal tool ignored | a `read_file` tool payload |

`Copy-Item a.txt b.txt` stayed inline on purpose. It is a PowerShell cmdlet, so running it through the bash hook would assert nothing about bash.

## Why `silent` is allowed in the table now

The table's header previously excluded `silent` outright. That was too broad, and the exclusion was never measured — it was a guess about where the two harnesses disagree.

Measured here: the bash hook emits exactly `{}` with exit 0 for all five commands, and both harnesses read exactly `{}` as `silent`. They disagree only when the hook emits **nothing at all** — PowerShell reads empty or whitespace output as `silent`, bash has no match for it. The header now states that measured condition instead of the blanket rule, so a `silent` case may move here once its `{}` output has been measured on both sides, and `notdeny` stays inline until that difference is closed.

## Correction to the first batch

The evidence comment on the first batch categorised roughly 14 of the remaining cases as *"policy-override and ask-reason cases depending on per-harness fixture setup"*, implying bash could not host them. **That was wrong.** Counted in `test-hooks.sh`: 16 policy-helper matches and 6 ask-reason assertions. The bash harness has both capabilities. Those cases are ordinary missing coverage, not exceptions, and they stay in the gap where they belong.

The largest real gap is elsewhere: roughly 30 of the 47 remaining cases are the `createAndRunTask` / `create_and_run_task` / `run_task` family, against about 5 such cases on the bash side. That is the target for the next batch.

## Evidence

| check | result |
|---|---|
| ratchet recount | `ps=97 sh=54 tsv=17 gap=47` — `ps` unchanged, so no coverage was dropped on the way |
| `bash -n test-hooks.sh` | exit 0 |
| `test-hooks.sh` | Passed: 342, Failed: 0 (was 337; +5 is exactly the new rows) |
| `test-hooks.ps1` | Passed: 467, Failed: 0 — unchanged, as predicted: five inline cases removed, five table rows added |
| no genuine `SKIP:` | confirmed; the six `FAIL|SKIP` grep hits are case *names* containing "fail" |

## Negative control

Prediction stated before the run: flipping the `expect` field of *a formatter run defers to the native assessment* from `silent` to `deny` must produce **exactly one** failure, named after that case, at 341 passed — the row-count floors stay green because the row is still present.

Observed:

```
FAIL  a formatter run defers to the native assessment -- expected deny, got: {} (exit 0)
Passed: 341
Failed: 1
```

The rows are executed, not merely counted.

## Not done

#280 stays open. 17 of 64 cases are shared; 47 remain. The roughly 4 genuinely PowerShell-only cases still have no recorded-reason mechanism, which acceptance criterion 1 requires before the gap can be declared closed rather than merely small.

No `local-check:` attestation: this branch touches `.github/scripts/` only, not `.github/hooks/`, and `test-hooks-integration.ps1` was not run.

author: dragonnite1221-lgtm
body:
## Summary
- `TestSuite.calculate_summary()` in `engineering/skill-tester/scripts/script_tester.py` set `overall_status = "PASS"` whenever `failed == 0 and no_tests == 0`, without checking `partial`.
- A batch where every script's own status was `PARTIAL` (some tests failed on each script, but none FAILed outright or had NO_TESTS) was therefore reported as a clean `PASS`.
- `main()` derives the process exit code directly from `summary["overall_status"]` (`PARTIAL` → exit 2, `PASS`/other → exit 0), so this misclassification made the CLI exit 0 for a batch that was not actually fully passing — silently swallowing the degradation for any caller that only checks the exit code.

## Fix
- Require `partial == 0` for the `PASS` branch.
- Route any `partial > 0` into the `PARTIAL` branch (covers both "some PASS + some PARTIAL" and "all PARTIAL" cases), which the existing exit-code mapping already treats as exit code 2.
- `FAIL` is now reserved for batches where nothing passed even partially.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `tests/test_script_tester_summary.py` with 5 cases (all-PARTIAL, all-PASS, mixed PASS+PARTIAL, all-FAIL, FAIL+PARTIAL mix).
- [x] RED: reverted the fix locally and confirmed 3 of 5 cases failed against the old logic (all-PARTIAL → PASS, mixed PASS+PARTIAL → PASS, FAIL+PARTIAL → FAIL instead of PARTIAL).
- [x] GREEN: all 5 new tests pass with the fix applied.
- [x] Full suite: `python3 -m pytest tests/ --tb=short -q` → 1935 passed.
- [x] `python3 scripts/count-repository-items.py --check` → inventory gate unaffected.

## What

The CCIP-Read gateway pins one L2 registry. Replacing the sub-ENS registry (yea-80y/WoCo-Contracts#21) switches L1 from the old registry to the new one in a transaction the server cannot see, so for a few minutes the gateway has to answer for both.

- `ENS_GATEWAY_REGISTRY_ADDRESSES` (optional, cutover only): comma-separated, must include `SUB_ENS_REGISTRY_ADDRESS`, at most two entries, every entry an address. The minting registry stays first and the set can never swap it out. Set but empty, a non-address, a set without the minting registry, or more than two entries disable the gateway with a named reason (fail closed).
- The handler reads and signs for the registry the request names when it is in the set. The memo key is sender + callData, and the callData carries the registry, so answers never cross.
- Health: `ensGateway.registries` and `cutoverWindowOpen`. The boot log warns while a window is open.
- With the variable unset, behaviour is unchanged.

author: benbou
body:
## Quoi

Nouvelle section **Activité** sur la fiche société, entre le tableau des deals et le fil « Reporting & communications » : qui a fait quoi, quand, sur les deals de cette boîte. Une ligne par geste, groupée par jour, 5 visibles puis « Afficher les précédentes ». Piste A (journal compact, style Linear) retenue après proposition ; les trois points tranchés : liste fermée de gestes, avant → après en clair sur statut / engagement / produit de sortie seulement, écriture agent au nom de l'utilisateur avec « via l'agent IA ».

Gestes journalisés : création, changement de statut (avec produit de sortie), conversion d'instrument, champs modifiés, valorisation ajoutée (y compris valeur d'un placement), virement pointé / dépointé (et la promotion term sheet → actif qu'un premier décaissement déclenche), document joint / retiré, échéance réalisée. Les intégrations qui écrivent seules sont des acteurs système : « Attio » (sync) et « Parallel » (pont VASCO), leurs rafales se replient.

Le journal est celui de **la fiche société** (table `companyEvents`, deal optionnel) : toutes les familles d'aujourd'hui sont ancrées sur un deal, les familles société (reports transmis, coffre, identité…) viendront dans une v2 sans migration.

## Comment

- **Table `companyEvents`** (`convex/schema.ts`) : journal en ajout seul, index par société / deal / clé de reprise. Les lignes d'un deal sont supprimées avec lui.
- **`convex/lib/companyEvents.ts`** : `logDealEvent`, `userActor`, et `diffDealPatch` (pur) qui réduit un patch à **un** événement par appel — priorité conversion > statut > champs, `null` si rien ne change (un webhook Attio identique ou un dialogue enregistré sans modif n'écrit rien).
- **Accroches** : `deals.create/update/remove`, `valuations.create/createInternal`, `lib/pointage.applyMatchToDeal/applyUnmatch` (couvre écran + agent), `documents.create/remove` (ancre deal), `forecasts.applyMarkEntryRealized` (nouveau paramètre `actor`, passé par les deux appelants), `agentTools.createDealInternal/updateDealInternal`, `attioSync.upsertFromDeal`, `vasco.applyInstrumentBridgePatch`.
- **Garde-fou CI** `tests/journalGuards.test.ts` : tout **bloc de premier niveau** de `convex/` (mutation ou helper) qui écrit directement une table de `JOURNALED` (`deals` pour l'instant) doit appeler le logger dans ce bloc, ou figurer dans `EXEMPT` avec sa raison (import Airtable, seed). Par bloc et non par fichier, pour qu'une nouvelle mutation dans un fichier qui journalise déjà ne passe pas. C'est lui qui a révélé le pont VASCO oublié. Ajouter une famille au journal = une entrée dans `JOURNALED`, le test nomme alors chaque bloc à brancher. Il vérifie qu'un logger est appelé, pas qu'il dit vrai : chaque nouveau type d'événement arrive avec son cas de régression (norme dans `CLAUDE.md`).
- **Lecture** : `convex/companyEvents.ts:listByCompany` (100 derniers, noms et titres résolus côté serveur, `requireOrgMember`).
- **UI** : `src/components/companies/CompanyActivitySection.tsx`, montée dans `participations.$companyId.tsx` ; i18n `participations:activity.*` fr + en.
- **Reprise du passé** : `convex/migrations/backfillCompanyEvents.ts` (`dryRun` + `apply` paginé par source, idempotent par `backfillKey`). Reconstruit créations, pointages, valorisations et documents. **À lancer une fois en prod après déploiement** (runbook en tête du module, ligne dans `MIGRATIONS.md`) — sinon la section démarre vide.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts` édité à la main pour les deux nouveaux modules (codegen indisponible hors déploiement, cf. `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` « Codegen Convex hors-ligne »).

## Vérification

- `pnpm lint` (tsc + eslint) ✅, `pnpm build` ✅, `pnpm exec vitest run` : 449 tests ✅ dont `convex/regression.companyEvents.test.ts` (10 cas : un événement par appel, patch identique muet, exit = un statut avec produit, conversion prioritaire, pointage + promotion sous la même main, écriture agent `viaAgent`, document joint puis retiré, lecture réservée aux membres, journal supprimé avec le deal, reprise idempotente), `pnpm test:unit` : 523 ✅ (dont le garde-fou, 11 blocs vérifiés), `sync:skills:verify` ✅.
- Manuel : `TESTING.md` SH26.

## Docs

`CHANGELOG_PRODUIT.md` v1.230.0, `docs/produit/04-participations.md` (fiche société), `TESTING.md` (B7, B11, SH26), `MIGRATIONS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (règle : tout nouveau writer d'une table journalisée appelle le logger, le garde-fou fait rougir la CI sinon ; chaque nouveau type d'événement arrive avec son test).

Hors périmètre, volontairement (v2) : reports transmis / rattachés / détachés, coffre société, identité société, KPIs, capital, prévisionnel, tâches ; fil sur la fiche deal ; filtres par type ; contenu des notes ; import Airtable.

author: timujinne
body:
## Problem

`mix precommit` (and the tracked `.githooks/pre-commit`, which mirrors it step for step) never compiles `test/**/*_test.exs`. `format` and `credo` only parse those files; `compile --warnings-as-errors` and `dialyzer` see `elixirc_paths`, which covers `test/support` but not the `.exs` test files; ExUnit is the only thing that compiles them, and only when `mix test` requires them. So a test file that is valid syntax but does not compile — the concrete case was two identical `describe` names in one module, which ExUnit rejects with `ArgumentError` at `defmodule` time — passes every precommit step and the hook, and only surfaces on the next `mix test`, which nothing runs automatically (AGENTS.md "CI/CD").

## Fix

- New `test.compile` alias in `mix.exs`, run in `precommit` between `deps.unlock --check-unused` and `quality.ci`. It compiles every `test/**/*_test.exs` with `Kernel.ParallelCompiler.compile/1` in a `MIX_ENV=test` subprocess (`System.cmd` with `env:`, no shell) — deliberately **without** `test_helper.exs`: no `ExUnit.start`, no database probe, no migration, zero tests run. It cannot go red from the environment, only from a genuine compile error in `test/`, so it does not reintroduce the "always-red gate" problem that keeps `mix test` out of `precommit`. Warnings from test files are printed, not fatal — same as under `mix test`. A subprocess because `MIX_ENV` is fixed for the whole aliased run once the VM boots (same reason `prerelease` shells out for its `MIX_ENV=prod` step).
- `.githooks/pre-commit` gets the matching `run_step` so a hook-approved commit cannot still fail `precommit` on this.
- AGENTS.md "Workflow" and CHANGELOG (Unreleased, no version bump) describe the step.

## Tests

- `mix precommit` on this branch: green end to end (compile, deps.unlock, test.compile, quality.ci, test.js); the pre-commit hook ran the same five steps on the commit.
- Negative check: a duplicate `describe "encode_pretty!/1"` appended to `test/phoenix_kit/utils/json_test.exs` — `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix credo --strict` on that file still pass (valid syntax); `mix test.compile` fails with ExUnit's `describe "encode_pretty!/1" is already defined in PhoenixKit.Utils.JsonTest`, `1 test file(s) failed to compile.`, `** (Mix) test suite failed to compile` (exit 1). Reverted afterwards; `mix test.compile` green again.
- `mix test` against an isolated `phoenix_kit_test` database: 42 doctests, 5085 tests, 3 failures — none touched by this change (`lib/` and `test/` are identical to `main`). Two are load flakes that pass in isolation (`probe_test.exs:99` 49 ms deadline vs 50 ms sleep; `common_unreachable_test.exs:20` sandbox owner exit). One is deterministic and pre-existing on `main`: `media_browser_test.exs:567` — `element("[phx-click='toggle_viewer_sidebar']")` now matches two buttons since bffac37f70 (2026-09-12) added a second toggle on the viewer/sidebar seam; the test still expects one. Left for its own fix.
- Rebased onto `main` at 5bc0f90b26 (phoenix 1.8.13 → 1.8.14 lock bump); the diff is byte-identical to the pre-rebase version. Re-run on the rebased head: `mix precommit` green end to end (test.compile → quality.ci → test.js 95/95); the duplicate-`describe` negative check fails `mix test.compile` again with the same `already defined` error and passes once reverted; `phoenix_kit_doctor_test.exs` (hooksPath check) + `json_test.exs` against the isolated test database: 72 tests, 0 failures.

author: lexasoft123
body:
Two field reports on 0.21.1, both on native desktop playback (the default on macOS and Windows since 0.21.0), plus what turned up while fixing them.

## What a singer gets

- **The count-in counts in on every Play**, from wherever the song is parked — after a scrub, after a Pause, and again after a Pause inside a count-in (to the same landing). It used to sound once per open and then every Play was a flat resume, which is the "count-in is broken" report.
- **The bar stays on the line you chose while the count runs.** A mid-song count-in drew the bar at the top of the song for its whole length, and a Pause inside it parked the bar there — the "seek bar jumps to the song start when I hit pause fast" report. The bar holds at the landing now, as the phones and the Web Audio path always did.
- **The count-in dots show under native playback.** They never had.
- **A control touched during a count-in no longer restarts the song at the top.** The click turned on mid-count brought the song in at 0.01 s from a count-in aimed at 60 s; paused inside a count-in, the same touch moved the bar to 0 and the next Play counted in to the top. Inside a count-in a change is now a rebuild anchored at the landing.
- **A double Play inside one restart adopts it** instead of stopping the count-in and starting it again.
- Silent runs are silent: the mute env now also clamps the metronome's cue volume in main. The clicks bypass the master bus, so a muted driver with the count-in on used to click out loud.

## How it is pinned

- Eight facade unit tests and an extended mute test, each failing against the old code.
- `tests/e2e/mac/count-in-e2e.cjs`, the only desktop driver that turns the count-in on: scrub before the first Play, Pause inside the count-in, Play after a Pause twice, a control change mid-count and another while paused inside it, Play twice inside one restart, a count-in-off control; `engine.position` sampled at 40 ms through every pre-roll, exactly one graph build per restart, any dsp warning a failure. Listed in the verifier roster.

## Verified

Silent and hidden on both desktop platforms, same driver, same shape on each — bar held at the landing through every count-in, dots 4/4, the song in within 50 ms of the spot, one build per restart, clean dsp log:

| leg | Mac (CoreAudio) | Windows field laptop (WASAPI) |
|---|---|---|
| first Play from a scrubbed spot | held, in at +0.05 s | held, in at +0.03 s |
| Pause inside the count-in | bar stays, core paused mid pre-roll | same |
| Play after that / after a pause mid-song | counts in again | counts in again |
| control change mid-count / paused mid-count | anchored rebuild, lands at the spot | same |
| Play twice, fast | one build | one build |

Also on the Mac: `transport-race-e2e` PASS, typecheck, `npm test` 1251/1251. The second commit hardens the driver for the laptop's hidden window (node-side polling, page-side presses), where its first runs had four legs race nothing while the change itself behaved on every leg reached.

author: ekenheim
body:
## Why
Three orphaned deployKF generate ClusterPolicies (source Secrets long gone) had accumulated **83,680 Pending kyverno UpdateRequests**, growing ~370/day. Every kube-apiserver watch-caches them: 13-14 GiB RSS and 0.6-0.8 core per master, the kyverno background controller OOMing at 4Gi ~14x/day, etcd at 1.39 GB. kyverno itself was an unmanaged ArgoCD leftover (chart 3.0.1 / v1.10.0), never in this repo.

## What
- **foreman**: the git-credential kyverno mutation is replaced by a HelmRelease `postRenderers` patch that mounts the same ConfigMap into the `foreman-agent` Deployment (where the reviewer/gate run). Coder Jobs are operator-created at run time and can't be reached this way; they revert to the harness's askpass auth, which is what they used before the policy.
- **datasci/kyverno-fixes**: removed (cert-manager + CronJob hack for kyverno's webhook CA).
- **cilium**: `hubble.relay` and `hubble.ui` off. Relay crashlooped every ~90s on a TLS handshake failure to hubble-peer (1780 restarts); nothing consumed it. Hubble metrics/dashboards keep working (they come from the agents). Gatus endpoint for the UI ingress dropped.

## Follow-up (manual, after merge)
Tear kyverno out of the cluster: scale controllers to 0, delete the webhooks, delete the `*.kyverno.io` CRDs (cascade-deletes the 83k URs and all policies server-side), then the namespace and cluster RBAC, plus the stale `hubble-gatus-ep` ConfigMap (cilium ks has `prune: false`).

author: 33kain
body:
## What

Replaces the flat fade-up on the four opening-intro elements (mascot, **CONTEXA** wordmark, tagline, and the "See how it works" button) with a **3D depth reveal**. Each element now starts large, blurred and tilted back in space, then settles onto the plane — it draws closer, sharpens into focus, and stands upright.

## How

- **New keyframe `introDepth`** — `perspective(1100px)` + `translateZ` + `rotateX` + `blur`, driven by per-element custom properties so each element arrives from a different depth for a layered cascade:
  - mascot: `--z: 440px`, `--b: 26px`, `--rx: 24deg` (deepest)
  - wordmark: `--z: 360px`, `--b: 20px`, `--rx: 20deg`
  - tagline / button: `--z: 300px`, `--b: 16px`, `--rx: 18deg`
- **Easing** swapped from the previous expo curve to an ease-out-quad (`cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)`), and the opacity ramp reaches full at **22%** of the timeline — so the depth is watchable the whole way down instead of snapping sharp almost immediately.
- The **~5s staggered timing is unchanged** (0.35s / 1.5s / 2.6s / 3.7s delays). The now-unused `introPop` and `introUp` keyframes are removed.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` now also resets `filter`, so it stays sharp and static with no animation.

## Verification

Inspected the running animations in-browser via the Web Animations API:
- **Mid-flight** (~30% through): elements are visible (`opacity: 1`) but still 8–12px blurred, enlarged and tilted (`matrix3d`, confirming true 3D) — the depth is clearly on screen.
- **Settled**: `blur(0)`, `opacity: 1`, identity transform — no leftover offset; rests exactly where the old animation did.

Website-only; no extension or worker changes. `npm test` (both suites) and `npm run build` pass locally.

author: norcalipa
body:
## What Problem This Solves Score writes deactivate superseded rows, but the read side consumed them inconsistently: - **Rankings** (`IndexView.fetch_results` raw SQL) had no `cs.status` predicate, so `AVG(cs.score)` averaged historical/superseded observations. It also omitted `ct.status = 1` (score type) and `cw.status = 1` (algorithm weight) — an inactive weight row duplicates the join and skews the weighted SUM. The completeness numerator counted any active score even for a deactivated score type, letting completeness exceed 100%. - **Company details** (`Organization.avg_scores`, served via `/api/organizations//scores/`) had no status filter either, so the detail modal contradicted the completeness subquery (which did filter) and rankings. - **Assistant explanations** (`default_score_summary_datasource`) were already correct but hand-rolled — the centralization gap this issue names. ## Why This Change Was Made A replacement observation must change ranking, detail, and assistant results identically, and historical values must never leak into averages. The fix centralizes one documented definition of an active-score read and applies it everywhere; the raw ranking SQL carries the same predicate set with a pointer comment (raw SQL cannot call the ORM helper without a rewrite, which is out of scope as performance-sensitive). ```mermaid flowchart LR W[score writes: deactivate old + create replacement
one active row per (type, source, target)] --> R[(crank_score)] R --> H["active_score_summary_rows
(single documented read predicate:
Score.status=1 AND ScoreType.status=1)"] H --> D[Organization.avg_scores
detail modal API] H --> T[default_score_summary_datasource
assistant score summaries] R --> S[fetch_results ranking SQL
cs.status=1 AND ct.status=1 AND cw.status=1
predicate set kept in sync with helper] S --> K[rankings + profile_completeness] ``` ## User Impact - Replacing a score now updates rankings, the company detail modal, and assistant score summaries consistently; a replacement of 1.0 → 5.0 reads as 5.0 everywhere instead of a historical 3.0 average. - Inactive weight rows no longer duplicate ranking joins; scores for deactivated score types no longer count toward averages or push profile completeness above 100%. - Missing-dimension semantics documented: an active score type with no active score counts as a missing dimension (numerator = active types with ≥1 active score, denominator = all active types), so completeness stays ≤ 100. - **Reviewer note:** user-visible ranking/detail numbers change where superseded rows previously skewed them — this is the intended correction. Read-side only; caches refresh within `CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS` or on the next score write's commit-time invalidation. Rollback restores prior reads with no data risk. ## Evidence All commands run in the worktree with the repo's configured env (`ENV=dev`, `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=crank.settings`, local Redis on 6379 matching CI): - **Tests (full suite, with coverage):** `coverage run -m pytest -q` → `1869 passed, 36 subtests passed` (baseline on origin/main was 19 failed / 1850 passed — all 19 failures were local Redis unavailability, not code). - **Changed-file coverage:** `coverage report --include='crank/services/scores.py,crank/models/organization.py,crank/views/index.py,crank/agents/job_search/tools.py' --show-missing` → tools.py / organization.py / scores.py **100%**; index.py 95% with missing lines `49-50, 130, 143` — all pre-existing lines outside this diff (this diff touches only comments and the SQL string inside `fetch_results`, which is executed by tests). Every new/changed executable line is covered. - **Regression fixtures added** (deliberately chosen 1.0 → 5.0 values that expose accidental historical averaging): superseded-only org excluded from rankings; weighted average `4.0 = (5.0×3 + 1.0×1)/4` with a deactivated weight row present; completeness `100.0` with a stray score on a retired type, `50.0` with one of two active types unscored; avg_scores / organization_scores API / assistant datasource each assert active-only results; superseded-then-active recompute exercised through the real `persist_score_observation` write path. - **Migrations current:** `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` → `No changes detected` (leaf stays 0029; no migration). - **License check:** `python check_license.py` → only flagged file is a generated `.pytest_cache` artifact, not part of the diff. - **Offline benchmark gate:** `python manage.py benchmark_job_pipeline --profile ci --seed 324 --assert-budgets` → passed. - **Diff hygiene:** `git diff --check` → clean; all 9 changed files end with exactly one newline. ## Plan deviations - The multi-active-row average tests use two distinct sources instead of two active rows for one `(type, source, target)` — the existing partial unique constraint (`unique_score_type_source_target_status`) forbids the latter by design. - Existing `test_organization_models.py::test_avg_scores` (unchanged) still passes under the new helper: its expectation `4.0` / `1.5` per type is preserved; the row-shape contract of `avg_scores` (keys `type__name`, `avg_score`) is unchanged. Fixes #461

author: rodneygagnon
body:
Connects #1219's last fix. `1.0.95` (OpusPopuli/opuspopuli-regions#85) replaces the LLM-generated manifest for the California AG propositions source with a declared `staticManifest`.

Without it the pipeline keeps regenerating that manifest every sync and keeps breaking a different field — v5 lost `proponent`, v7 lost `title`, both at 100% of items, with the sync reporting **success** throughout.

## Pinned exactly, not with a caret

The caret is what made #1253 necessary: `^1.0.93` already admitted `1.0.94` while the lockfile held `1.0.93`, so the build resolved the **old** manifest while `package.json` looked correct and nothing failed.

A range expresses *"any of these would do."* That's untrue here — this specific version carries the selectors this release depends on, and the next patch could regenerate them. An exact pin says what's actually meant, and makes silent drift impossible rather than merely unlikely.

## Verified, not assumed

- the **published artifact** carries `staticManifest` with all seven fields and the corrected text-based title regex — `npm pack` and inspect, not the version string
- the **installed** copy under `node_modules` carries it too
- typecheck unchanged at its 7 pre-existing region-service errors
- **855** region tests, **146** region-provider tests

## After this

Deploy, then re-sync. Extraction and mapping were verified end-to-end against the live page in regions#85 — 46/46 accepted, 0 warnings, first clean mapping since August.

I've said "this should fix it" twice already on this issue, so stating it precisely: what's proven is that the extractor and domain mapper handle all 46 items correctly with this manifest. Whether the collision clears depends on that running in production.

Self-review (SOC 2 CC8.1): sole author — needs countersignature.

author: mzahana
body:
## Problem

`pkgs_dep_keys` extracts `<depend>` tags from staged `package.xml` files with a line-based `sed`, which cannot see XML comments. A dependency a package has deliberately disabled, such as

```xml
<!-- <depend>mavros</depend> -->
```

still contributes its key, and the resolver then puts the corresponding apt package into `PKG_APT`.

This stayed invisible for as long as the resolved package existed in the apt repo: it was installed needlessly and nothing failed. On 2026-09-14 packages.ros.org stopped shipping `ros-humble-mavros` as a binary, and from that moment every `rrv build` of a pkgs set containing such a comment died in the image's apt step with

```
E: Unable to locate package ros-humble-mavros
```

— a package no staged manifest actually declares, which makes the failure very hard to trace back to its cause.

## Fix

Strip XML comments (including multi-line ones) from each manifest before extracting dependency tags, so only live declarations are resolved.

## Note for existing checkouts

The `PKG_APT` cache (`.cache/<profile>.pkgapt`) is keyed on the manifests alone, so a list computed by the old parser survives this fix. After pulling, remove `.cache/*.pkgapt` once; it regenerates on the next build.

Verified on a field laptop: with this change the same staged package set that failed as above builds clean, with the phantom package gone from `PKG_APT`.

## Summary
- Fixes an app crash on launch (reported from a real Simulator run on the native build):
  ```
  Uncaught Error: Cannot read property 'Steps' of undefined
  src/health/iosProvider.ts:27
  ```
- Root cause: `react-native-health`'s `HealthPermission` is declared as a TypeScript `enum` in its `.d.ts`, but the package's actual JS entry (`index.js`) is a plain `module.exports = HealthKit` default object with **no named exports at all**. `import { HealthPermission } from 'react-native-health'` therefore resolves to `undefined` at runtime — it type-checks fine (the ambient type exists) but crashes the moment `HealthPermission.Steps` is evaluated
- Fix: use the default export's own `AppleHealthKit.Constants.Permissions.*` instead — same string values (`'Steps'`, `'HeartRate'`, etc.), backed by a real JS object (`src/constants/Permissions.js`) rather than an ambient-only type
- Checked whether `react-native-health-connect` (Android) shares this problem — it doesn't; its compiled `lib/commonjs/index.js` has genuine named exports for everything `androidProvider.ts` imports

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx expo export --platform ios` — bundles clean

This fixes the specific crash that was reported; the rest of the HealthKit call sites in `iosProvider.ts` share the same callback-wrapped-in-Promise pattern and haven't each been separately exercised on-device yet, so worth watching for further issues as you test deeper into the flow (metrics screen, workouts, etc.)
