author: wdconinc
body:
### Briefly, what does this PR introduce? Please link to any relevant presentations or discussions.

Two actions were referenced **by branch**, so whatever those repositories point at when a workflow runs executes here without review:

| ref | where | secrets it receives |
|---|---|---|
| `eic/gitlab-sync@master` | `mirror.yaml` | `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_USERNAME` |
| `eic/actions/.github/workflows/list-open-prs.yml@main` | `build-push.yml` | none (called without `secrets:`) |

Both are now pinned to the commit those branches currently resolve to, with the branch and date in a trailing comment so the pin stays readable:

```yaml
uses: eic/gitlab-sync@975a67e4d71642c528c722bd5270ccd664e2dd11 # master as of 2026-09-14
```

**Behaviour is unchanged today** — both pins are the current branch heads, verified against `git ls-remote`.

One thing worth knowing: `eic/gitlab-sync`'s `v1` tag is **behind** `master` (`04d8559` vs `975a67e`), so pinning to the tag would have been a silent downgrade. Pinned to the commit instead. If the `gitlab-sync` maintainers cut a release tag matching `master`, switching to that would read better — and would let Dependabot bump it, which it may not manage for a commit with no newer tag behind it.

### Dependabot

The `docker` ecosystem is added, but **it buys less than it looks like** and the config says so in a comment rather than leaving a false impression:

- It reads literal `FROM` lines. The only one in this repository is `containers/eic/Dockerfile.spack-cache-cleanup`.
- Every other `FROM` is parameterised (`FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}`, `FROM ${DOCKER_REGISTRY}${BUILDER_IMAGE}:${INTERNAL_TAG}`).
- The images those actually resolve to — `debian:trixie-slim` in the build matrices, `nvidia/cuda` via `CUDA_VERSION`/`CUDA_OS`, and `docker:28.3.3` / `singularity:v3.11.5` in `.gitlab-ci.yml` — live in CI configuration Dependabot's docker ecosystem does not read.

So those still move by hand. Tracking them would need either a different mechanism or literal `FROM`s; I did not want to restructure the build for it in this PR.

### Not done here, for you to decide

Every remaining action is pinned to a **mutable major tag** (`actions/checkout@v7`, `dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v24`, `korthout/backport-action@v4`, `reproducible-containers/buildkit-cache-dance@v3`, …). Full SHA-pinning across all six workflows is the stricter posture and Dependabot maintains such pins fine, but it is a large diff touching every workflow and would collide with other CI work in flight, so I have left it as a call for the team rather than making it unilaterally. This PR fixes only the branch refs, which is the sharper edge.

### Verification

`actionlint` clean; `dependabot.yml` parses; both pinned commits confirmed to still match the heads of the branches they replace.

### What is the urgency of this PR?
- [ ] High (please describe reason below)
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

### What kind of change does this PR introduce?
- [ ] Bug fix (issue #__)
- [ ] New feature (issue #__)
- [ ] Optimization (issue #__)
- [ ] Updated documentation
- [x] other: supply-chain hardening

### Please check if any of the following apply
- [ ] This PR introduces breaking changes. Please describe changes users need to make below.
- [ ] This PR changes default behavior. Please describe changes below.
- [x] AI was used in preparing this PR. Please describe usage below.

One consequence worth stating: pinned actions no longer pick up upstream fixes automatically. If `eic/gitlab-sync` gains a fix on `master`, this repository must bump the pin to get it.

AI usage: the branch refs were flagged during a review of the CI configuration with Claude Code, and this PR was prepared with it. The ref resolution — including that `v1` is behind `master`, and that Dependabot's docker ecosystem would cover only one file here — was checked by querying the repositories and reading the Dockerfiles, not assumed.

author: loks0n
body:
## Problem

`getDevice()` builds a new device per request (and per project in the workers), and `utopia-php/storage`'s default S3 client sets `CURLOPT_FORBID_REUSE`, so every object call pays a fresh TCP and TLS handshake. `GET /v1/health/storage` does write, read and delete against four devices, so a single health call is twelve handshakes.

Cloud CI has been failing `Health\StorageTest::testStorage` (`ping < 100`) on main several times a day with 102 to 113 ms pings; see appwrite-labs/cloud#5830.

## Change

Hold one lazily built, process-wide pool of connection-reusing curl clients in `getDevice()` and pass it to every S3-family device (S3, AWS, DO Spaces, Backblaze, Linode, Wasabi). Curl options and the `S3\RetryStrategy` match the library default, so the only behavioural change is that handles keep their connection cache between requests.

Same shape as the existing `usageConnection` pool in this file. Pool: 64 handles, 30 s wait for a free one. Every entry point (HTTP, worker, CLI) already runs under Swoole coroutines, which the pool adapter requires.

## Testing

No unit test: the subject is a global function that builds a Swoole pool, and any double would only echo the wiring back. The red is the existing E2E: `tests/e2e/Services/Health/StorageTest.php` fails against MinIO in Kind at ~8 ms per handshake; with reuse the same twelve calls should sit well under the ceiling. CI on this PR runs it.

Étape 1 du lot 3 (« le cassé d'abord », arbitrage de Marc du 14/09).

La leçon §7 du `CLAUDE.md` prescrit depuis toujours de « rejouer (borné) tout ce qui n'est pas un JSON `ok:true` ». `appelerMoteur` ne le faisait pas : **un seul `fetch`**, et sur un non-JSON il jetait « panne transitoire Apps Script probable, **réessaie** » — il demandait à l'humain de refaire ce que le code n'avait pas fait.

## Ce que ça a coûté, mesuré

Le 14/09/2026, depuis une session Claude : `etat_moteur` répond « moteur illisible (HTTP 404) », puis « (HTTP 200) ». Deux appels, aucun rejeu — **et j'en ai conclu que le moteur DriveAI était cassé. Il ne l'était pas.**

Le 404 puis le 200-non-JSON sont la paire canonique d'un coup unique, déjà consignée **deux fois** dans ce dépôt (`CLAUDE.md` §7, `docs/LESSONS.md` incident du 08/07) : `/exec` répond au POST par une redirection vers l'écho, `fetch` bascule POST→GET, et `doGet` — qui ne connaît que le callback OAuth — rend le texte nu `DriveAI`.

Un faux diagnostic de panne sur l'app la plus complexe de la constellation, faute de trois lignes de rejeu.

## La limite est le vrai sujet, pas le rejeu

Un rejeu général aurait été la faute suivante. Quand Apps Script rend un non-JSON, **on ne sait pas si l'action a eu lieu** : la réponse est perdue, pas forcément le travail. Rejouer `mcp-intention` créerait une **seconde tâche** ou un second événement dans l'agenda de Marc, sans rien pour le signaler — un doublon silencieux, strictement pire que l'erreur qu'on évite.

D'où une **liste blanche**, et un défaut à `rejouable = false` : un oubli ne peut que **retirer** le rejeu, jamais l'accorder par accident.

`chat-assistant` en est exclu aussi, et ce n'est pas un oubli : il ne touche pas au Drive mais il **appelle un modèle**, donc il dépense. Un rejeu ferait payer deux fois une question posée une fois, sur un budget journalier plafonné.

## Deux sources de vérité, un test pour les tenir ensemble

Le moteur porte déjà l'information : `MCP_ACTIONS` (`src/Mcp.gs`) associe à chaque action un booléen « écrit ». La liste blanche côté serverless en est le miroir, faute de pouvoir l'importer — `api/` est zéro-dépendance par construction et ne lit pas de `.gs`.

**Un test analyse le fichier source du moteur et refuse toute divergence**, plutôt que de compter sur la vigilance : la première action ajoutée les aurait séparées en silence, et si c'est une écriture oubliée dans la liste blanche, elle serait devenue duplicable.

## Ce que ça ne soigne pas, et c'est écrit dans le code

Une indisponibilité de **plusieurs minutes** — celle du 05/08 a duré six minutes, et trois tentatives sur deux secondes n'y changent rien. C'est dit à l'endroit exact où quelqu'un serait tenté d'augmenter le nombre pour couvrir la seconde. Le message d'abandon ne dit donc plus « réessaie » : il nomme les trois tentatives et les deux causes qui restent.

## Un test existant a attrapé une vraie régression de mock

`mcp-endpoint.test.ts` échouait sur « Body has already been read » : `mockResolvedValue` rend le **même** objet `Response` à chaque appel, et un `Response` ne se lit qu'une fois. Échec du **mock**, pas du code — en production `fetch` rend un `Response` neuf par appel. Corrigé en `mockImplementation`, ce qui rend le test **meilleur** : l'ancienne forme affirmait en silence « appelé au plus une fois ».

## Fichiers touchés

- `api/mcp/_commun.ts` (+70-14) — rejeu borné, `TENTATIVES_REJOUABLES`, message d'abandon honnête.
- `api/mcp/index.ts` (+24-2) — la liste blanche `REJOUABLES`, et l'exclusion motivée de `chat-assistant`.
- `app/test/rejeu-moteur.test.ts` (**nouveau**, +180) — 8 cas.
- `app/test/mcp-endpoint.test.ts` (+12-3) — mock corrigé.
- `BACKLOG.md` (+1).

## Vérifications

- Tests moteur (racine) : **1149** passés. Tests app : **251** passés (+8). Build app propre.
- `secret-scan`, `check-structure`, `check-agents` : verts.
- `npm audit --omit=dev` sur `app/` : **0 vulnérabilité** (rien à corriger ici, contrairement à Hubperso et CarAI).
- **Discrimination prouvée par mutation** : rejeu rendu inconditionnel → les 2 cas « une action qui écrit ne se rejoue pas » échouent ; `mcp-intention` glissée dans la liste blanche → les 2 cas de non-divergence échouent.

## Points d'attention

- 🟡 **Latence ajoutée uniquement en cas de flake** : 1,6 s au pire, sur les seules actions de lecture. Un appel qui réussit du premier coup ne change pas.
- 🟡 **`SEUIL_MUET_MS` porte une justification fausse** (`api/hub/summary.ts:33`) : le commentaire dit « déclencheur à 30 min + marge » alors que le tick est à **5 min** — 30 min est `WATCHDOG_MINUTES`. La valeur de 45 min est cohérente avec le chien de garde, sa raison écrite ne l'est pas. Non touché ici pour garder cette PR sur un seul sujet ; ça vient avec l'étape 2 (les missions).

author: u9g
body:
Fixes #7208. Supersedes #7207.

## Problem

`RecognizeStream._main_task` gives a stream `max_retry` (default 3) reconnect attempts, and the only thing that resets `_num_retries` is a `FINAL_TRANSCRIPT`. A caller who never speaks never produces one, so a provider that recycles an idle socket on a fixed interval spends the whole budget on ordinary, successful reconnects. Cartesia closes an idle socket with `1001 Idle timeout` every ~3 minutes; after four of them the stream raises `failed to recognize speech after 3 attempts` and emits `recoverable=False`, even though every reconnect in between succeeded.

#7207 proposes resetting on any provider event. That covers Deepgram, which emits usage events every 5 s while audio flows, but not a provider that stays quiet during silence: Cartesia delivers nothing at all until someone speaks, so under #7207 the silent-caller case still dies. Its own description notes this.

Since #6418 the session tolerates unrecoverable STT errors and `_STTPipeline` recreates the stream, so on `main` this costs a socket rather than the call. It still burns one of `max_unrecoverable_errors` per ~12 quiet minutes, and that count only resets on a user transcript, so a long silent call dies at ~36 minutes.

Reproduced against real Cartesia with `cue-cli` driving a dispatchable agent started with `RoomOptions(audio_input=False)` on `main`:

```
12:48:20  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 0.1s
12:51:20  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 2.0s   ← counter never reset
12:54:22  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 2.0s
12:57:25  REPRO stt error recoverable=False
          APIConnectionError: failed to recognize speech after 3 attempts
```

## Fix

An attempt that ran longer than `conn_options.timeout` had connected, so its failure is not consecutive with the previous one: reset `_num_retries` before handling the error. `max_retry` now means "consecutive failures in a row" regardless of whether anyone was talking. No new option; reuses the existing connect timeout. The `FINAL_TRANSCRIPT` reset is left in place.

## Verification

Same `cue-cli` scenario on this branch:

```
13:21:54  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 0.1s
13:24:55  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 0.1s
13:27:55  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 0.1s
13:30:56  closed unexpectedly (close_code=1001, extra='Idle timeout')  retrying in 0.1s
```

Every retry is attempt 0 again and every error is `recoverable=True`; the stream never gave up and the session's unrecoverable-error count was never touched.

Unit tests in `tests/test_stt_base.py`: a flapping stream whose connections stay up for 180 s survives 9 drops with `max_retry=3`, and one whose connections drop after 1 s still gives up after `max_retry + 1` attempts. `mypy -p livekit.agents` clean.

JS counterpart: livekit/agents-js#2494 (which also ports #6418).

author: claude[bot]
body:
Two rounds of the animation redesign.

### T452 — The Animation pane is two tabs: Configure and Order
"the animation pane is not the right place for configuring the animation
details e.g. for things like the wobble and such. The animation pane is for
the order. Please do not mix them. Or perhaps put tabs on the pane."

T445 stacked one on top of the other, so the six numbers of a wobble sat
between you and the list of clicks. **Configure** is what the selected thing
does; **Order** is the list of clicks. Quick animate moved to Order, because
clicking things in turn *is* setting the order — arming it switches the pane
over and draws at the head of the list it is writing. Which tab you were on
is remembered; switching is a class flip, not a rebuild.

### T453 — A chooser opens its options in the ribbon, not over the slide
"each of these buttons opens up a horizontal display of all the options ...
instead of them all having a little horizontal thing of options, it just
appears for the one that you click on."

One shelf, in the bar itself. Clicking a chooser moves its whole row there;
another swaps; the same one or the ✕ puts it back. The row is never rebuilt —
the same element moves — so every listener and pressed state survives. It
takes a line of its own while open and no space at all while closed. Whole
slide and Build order moved to the right-hand end.

The hard part was keeping it open: every measuring pass unfolds the whole bar
and folds it again (once in `fitEditRibbon`, eight times over in
`ribbonMinW`), so the shelf shut itself on every selection change until
`rbnUnfoldAll` started remembering whose row it was.

And *"also what is disappear?"* — it was named for what it does to the object
rather than for the choice, under a label repeating the same word. It is
**Leaves early ▸ Send it away** now.

---

791 tests pass, ruff is clean, both driven in a real browser.

author: izzywdev
body:
## Summary

Fixes both defects in `.github/workflows/verify-consumer-credentials.yml` reported in #977, which caused the credential-verify check to file 18 duplicate issues into `izzywdev/MendysRobotics` (#325–#349, since consolidated).

**1. Duplicate filing (root cause).** The dedup query was scoped to `--label credential-drift`:
```sh
gh issue list --repo "$OWNER_REPO" --state open --label credential-drift --search "$id in:title" ...
```
but `gh issue create --label credential-drift` errors when that label doesn't exist in the consumer repo, and the step falls back to creating the issue **unlabelled**. The next run's label-scoped search then matched nothing, so a fresh issue was filed every 6h. Now:
- dedup searches by **hand-off id in the title** (label-independent), and
- the label is **ensured to exist** before filing via idempotent `gh label create --force`, so the labelled create always succeeds and label-based triage keeps working.

**2. Misleading title.** Only `auth-failed` is a real credential rejection. `unreachable` means the verify check could not port-forward to the datastore to test the value at all — a check-side/connectivity fault, not a bad credential — yet every mode was titled "does not authenticate" (all 18 MendysRobotics issues were mode `unreachable`). Title and body opener are now **mode-aware** (`auth-failed` / `not-delivered` / `unreachable` / `malformed`), and non-auth modes point the reader at check reachability rather than credential rotation.

No behavioral change to the happy path, the plaintext-safety guarantees, Telegram alerting, or the self-heal re-publish trigger.

author: abhinav-phi
body:
Fixes #16460

**Root cause.** On a multi-homed host, an HTTP/3 (QUIC) client pointed at `tri://127.0.0.1:20000` dials a different address: `AbstractClient.getConnectAddress()` runs the URL host through `NetUtils.filterLocalHost()`, and `isInvalidLocalHost()` treats `127.*` / `localhost` as invalid, replacing them with `NetUtils.getLocalHost()` (e.g. the docker0 address from the issue: `172.18.0.1`). The wildcard-bound `NettyHttp3Server` then answers from the kernel-selected source interface (`10.1.0.215` in the issue's tcpdump), not from the dialed address, and QUIC clients drop handshake packets that come from a different address than they dialed — so the handshake retransmits until timeout. TCP-based transports tolerate the rewrite because responses follow the established connection; QUIC's address validation does not.

**Changes**

- `Http3Helper.getConnectAddress(URL)`: loopback hosts (`localhost`, `127.*`) are dialed exactly as configured; anyhost/empty still resolves to the local host as before, and non-loopback hosts pass through unchanged.
- `NettyHttp3ConnectionClient` overrides `getConnectAddress()` to use it. The fix is deliberately scoped to the QUIC client: I did not change the shared `AbstractClient` rewrite, which long-standing TCP paths rely on.

**Testing**

- New unit tests (`Http3HelperTest`, 4 cases): loopback dialed verbatim, `0.0.0.0` still replaced with the local host, remote address unchanged — all pass via `./mvnw -pl dubbo-remoting/dubbo-remoting-http3 -am test -Dtest=Http3HelperTest`.
- Module compiles clean; spotless/checkstyle clean.

**Server-side half (out of scope here).** The issue also notes that a wildcard `NioDatagramChannel` answers from the kernel-routed interface when the client dials a *non-loopback* local address (e.g. `172.18.0.1`). Per-datagram source control (`IP_PKTINFO`-style) is not exposed by netty's QUIC codec today, so this PR fixes the reported end-to-end scenario (client honors the configured loopback address; on loopback the kernel answers from loopback, handshake completes). Cross-interface multi-homed dials remain a separate follow-up — happy to discuss direction.

body:
The measuring branch is deleted, so ADR-0014 must stop pointing at it.

`0014` cited `test/measure-legible-floor` for the screen that produced the numbers. That branch could never reach `main` — expo-router publishes everything under `app/`, so an instrument cannot live there — and keeping a branch alive only so a document can point at it is exactly the fragile reference #85 was re-scoped for calling out in #29's own citation.

So the design is written out in full instead:

- what it imports rather than copies, and why that was the prototype's undoing
- what one trial draws and asks
- that the row stays in view, with no clock and nothing to remember
- that cost is recorded alongside correctness
- that widths are shuffled, never named, and the shipped width is read from `dayCellWidth(useWindowDimensions().width)` as the positive control

That is what a second observer needs to rebuild it, and it outlives any branch.

Documentation only.

author: ursugit
body:
## Problem

`apps/signal-service/data/scout_state.json` was observed losing **all** of its channels — 16 down to `{}`, including the four hand-curated ones (ETM FX, Benjamin Cowen, Chart Fanatics, Straight Kim) — while its 569-entry `seen` list stayed fully intact. It was caught before commit and reverted, but it would have silently destroyed the curated list.

Two defects combined to make the loss permanent and silent:

```python
def _load(self) -> None:
    try:
        ...
    except Exception:
        pass          # any read problem -> channels = {}, no log

def _save(self) -> None:
    STATE_PATH.write_text(...)   # writes that {} over the good file
```

The asymmetry is what makes it severe: a curated channel is only ever added by an explicit human action, but could be removed by a background save.

**Likely trigger — the relative path.** `STATE_PATH = Path("data/scout_state.json")` resolves against the *process* cwd, so launching the service from anywhere other than `apps/signal-service` pointed it at a file that doesn't exist. Confirmed directly: importing the service from `/tmp` previously yielded zero channels; after this change it resolves absolutely and loads all 16.

## Changes

- **New `app/data_paths.py`** — resolves data files against the service directory rather than the cwd. Env overrides still win, and a *relative* override anchors to the service dir too. Adopted for scout state, the strategies store, the **cryptobot trade ledger**, and the YouTube OAuth token, which all shared the same fragility.
- **`_load()` is explicit** — distinguishes "no file yet" (normal first run, `info`) from "file exists but is unreadable" (`error`, sets `load_failed`).
- **`_save()` refuses to destroy data** — skips when the last load failed, or when an empty in-memory channel list would replace a populated file. `unwatch()` passes `allow_empty=True` so removing the last channel still persists correctly.
- **Atomic writes** — temp file + `os.replace`, so an interrupted write can't leave the truncated file that triggers the failure path above.

Behaviour is unchanged when the service runs from its own directory (the normal case); the path change only stops resolution from drifting when it doesn't.

## Test plan

- [x] 9 new cases in `tests/test_scout_state_persistence.py`, covering: corrupt file never overwritten, empty channels never replacing a populated file, deliberate unwatch still allowed, atomic write leaves no `.tmp`, and cwd-independent path resolution
- [x] **Verified the new tests fail against the pre-fix code** — stashed the fix and confirmed the empty-overwrite test reproduces the channel wipe
- [x] Full suite: **135 passed** (126 before + 9 new)
- [x] End-to-end: ran the real service for 30s with outbound HTTPS blocked (every scout fetch `403`) — channel list intact, no git diff under `data/`
- [x] Confirmed importing the service from `/tmp` now loads 16 channels instead of 0

## Done looks like

Running the signal service with the network blocked, for any length of time, leaves the channel list intact — and if the state file ever fails to load, the service says so in the logs instead of quietly starting with zero channels and then persisting that.

Closes #7.

## Plan

Triage's comment on #7 was accurate down to the line numbers, and this PR built it as drafted:

- The version row in `settings/+page.svelte` becomes a `<button class="row">` (was a plain
  `<div>`), matching the feedback row above it.
- `copyVersion()` follows `copyLink()`'s shape in `onboarding/invite/+page.svelte:32-44`:
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, a `versionCopied` flag cleared after 2s, try/catch around the
  clipboard call.
- `settings.version` in `en.ts`/`de.ts` becomes `{ row, copied }` — only the one call site, so no
  rename elsewhere.
- Triage's open question — "any visible confirmation beyond the label swap?" — is answered by
  **not adding a toast**: the row already reads label-left, value-right, so the transient
  confirmation swaps the **value** span to "Copied" in place, which is where the eye already is.
  That also means the comment above the row needed rewriting (it called the row "a fact, not a
  control", which stopped being true), and the SPEC §6 line was updated to describe the tap.
- Filed as **plan 19** (`docs/plans/19-copy-version.md`) since this is an `idea`, not a `bug`.

author: valovinnikov
body:
A newly provisioned tenant's home page renders instead of throwing.

db: the seeded `page_home` carried neither `headingBlock` nor `seo`, both of which `homePageQuery` marks `.notNull()` — so every tenant provisioned through the platform got a home page that failed to parse, while provisioning still reported success.

Both fields are now seeded from static copy sized inside the Studio's SEO bounds, so tenant-name length can't push them out of range. `verifyTenantSeededContent` now reads the seeded page back and fails the run on a missing or out-of-bounds value, so this class of gap can no longer reach a live tenant.

Closes #3193

author: onceuponarc
body:
Builds on #1. Switches Solana token creation from PumpPortal's trade-local wrapper to the official `@pump-fun/pump-sdk` (pinned 2.0.0), which is what actually exposes these features on-chain:

- **Pool pair**: SOL / USDC / custom quote mint, resolved + validated via `resolveQuoteMint` before building the instruction (rejects an unwhitelisted custom mint with a clear error instead of failing on-chain).
- **Mayhem Mode**: gated on `Global.mayhemModeEnabled`; blocked on custom (QuoteControl) pairs based on the SDK-reported quote source, not a hardcoded address check — matches pump.fun's own SOL/USDC-only restriction.
- **Creator rewards target (Creator vs Holders)**: `holderReward` flag, gated on `Global.isHolderRewardEnabled`; also written to the existing `stories.engine` column.
- **Fee % up to 3%**: `creatorFeeBps`, clamped to `Global.maxConfigurableCreatorFeeBps`. Only takes effect on a custom pair — pump.fun ignores it on SOL/USDC and uses its standard schedule there, which the UI now notes so it's not a silent no-op.
- Dev buy stays on PumpPortal's simple buy action as a separate follow-up tx (SOL pairs only) to keep bespoke token-quoted buy fee-math out of this pass.

Typechecks and lints clean (aside from one pre-existing unrelated error in layout.tsx).

author: quantumexplorer
body:
## Issue being fixed or feature implemented

`getDataContractsLatestVersions` (#4739) exists so a client can check that the contracts it already holds are still current without transferring them. Its proved form did not deliver that: it reused the multi-contract proof, and since GroveDB proves a matched key together with its value and the version number lived only inside the serialized contract, the proof carried every contract whatever `include_contracts` said. Proof-using clients (wasm-sdk, Evo SDK, the Rust SDK by default) gained nothing.

There was no query shape that could fix this on the existing state: contracts have no version-keyed layout (a history-keeping contract's revisions are keyed by block time, with key `0` a sibling reference to the latest), and a merk proof never emits a matched key without its value.

## What was done?

From protocol version 14 every contract carries its version as a four-byte big-endian item at key `2` of its root subtree (`[64, id] / 2`), beside the contract (key `0`) and its documents (key `1`).

**Storage (rs-drive)**
- `add_contract_to_storage` v1 writes the item on every contract create and update, for both the plain and the history-keeping layout, with the contract element's flags so its storage is paid for and refunded with the contract's. It is selected by the new `DRIVE_CONTRACT_METHOD_VERSIONS_V4`, which only `DRIVE_VERSION_V9` (PV14) uses; PV13 keeps writing nothing there.
- `Drive::add_version_items_to_all_contracts` backfills the item for every contract already in state. It pages through the contract ids, is idempotent (a repeat leaves the root hash unchanged), and runs at the end of `transition_to_version_14`.
- New `fetch_contract_version` (raw read of the item, `None` for a missing contract), `fetch_contracts_versions_query` (keys under `[64]` with subquery key `2`, shared by prover and verifier), `prove_contracts_versions` and `Drive::verify_contracts_versions` (verification with absence: a missing id verifies as `None`; unrequested, duplicate or malformed rows are rejected).

**Query (drive-abci + proof verifier)**
- A new query helper slot, `data_contract_query_helpers.latest_versions_read`, gates the behaviour with no wire change: `0` in the tables protocol versions 1 to 13 select, `1` in `DRIVE_ABCI_QUERY_VERSIONS_V3` (PV14). This follows the existing `document_query_helpers` pattern, since the query tables version the wire surface, not behaviour.
- Without `include_contracts`, the proved form now returns the version item proof, and the unproved form answers from the contract cache on a hit and from the item on a miss, never loading a contract into the cache. With `include_contracts`, or on a state without the items, both forms behave exactly as before.
- `FromProof` for `DataContractsLatestVersions` selects the proof shape from the protocol version the response metadata carries (covered by the quorum signature), not from the client's own version: the SDK seeds mainnet, testnet and regtest clients at protocol version 13 and only ratchets after a proof verifies, so a fresh client whose first proved call is this query must still accept the version item proof of an upgraded network, and a client already at 14 must accept the multi-contract proof of a network that has not activated yet. A wasm-sdk functional test pins a fresh local client to 13 and makes this query its first call.

**Docs**: proto comment, Rust SDK and wasm-sdk doc comments, verifier type docs, and the Platform Book bullet that names the contract subtree keys.

Proof size: in the tests the version item proof for three contracts is under a quarter of the multi-contract proof, and the bound is asserted; the savings grow with contract size (up to 16 KB per contract today).

## How Has This Been Tested?

- rs-drive: 17 new tests. Storage writer for both layouts including update, the stateless estimate path (estimate never undershoots the actual fee), a PV13 twin that pins that no item is written before PV14, the codec, the raw read, prove and verify for present, absent, duplicate, tampered and mismatched ids, the proof size bound, and the backfill including idempotence.
- drive-abci: 18 tests pass, including the version item proof verifying and reporting absence, the unproved path leaving the contract cache untouched, a PV13 twin where the proof is still the multi-contract proof and the unproved read loads the contract, the new transition test that checks every genesis system contract gets its item, and the existing v13 to v14 upgrade test, which now runs the backfill.
- proof verifier: 7 pass. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean on platform-version, drive, drive-abci, drive-proof-verifier and dash-sdk; `cargo check -p wasm-sdk --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- `packages/rs-drive/tests/deterministic_root_hash.rs`: the pinned PV14 app hash after applying DashPay moves because of the extra element under the contract subtree; re-pinned with a comment.
- Fee and hash baselines that moved with the extra element (all at the latest protocol version only, with protocol version 11 and 13 twins keeping their values): every document write under a PV14-stored contract costs 740 more processing credits (one more node of the contract's root subtree to rehash), a contract create or update 61,200 more (the item itself), and the query integration tests' pinned app hashes change. Re-pinned across rs-drive and drive-abci; the DPNS twin helper now stores its contracts at the protocol version under test.
- Also fixed, pre-existing on v4.2-dev (its own workspace test job fails on it): the specialized-funds voting strategy test still expected the 0.2 DASH contested document contribution that the PV14 fee schedule lowered to 0.1 DASH.
- Also fixed, pre-existing on v4.2-dev since #4746 (its functional tests job fails on it): the wasm-sdk `addKnownContract` functional test used `to.be(true)`, which the suite's callable assertions do not provide. v4.2-dev is merged into the branch.
- Also fixed, pre-existing on v4.2-dev since #4737 (its end-to-end suite job fails on it): the platform test suite still expected the pre-PV14 withdrawal deletion error message, which now also allows FAILED withdrawals.

## Breaking Changes

Consensus: from protocol version 14 the state layout under every contract's root subtree gains key `2`, contract create and update write one more element (so their storage fees shift by that item), and the first block of PV14 backfills the item for every existing contract. Devnets already running PV14 dev builds need a reset, since the first-block hook does not fire for them. No wire change: `GetDataContractsLatestVersionsRequest` and its response are unchanged.

## Checklist:
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have added or updated relevant unit/integration/functional/e2e tests
- [x] I have added "!" to the title and described breaking changes in the corresponding section if my code contains any
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation if needed

**For repository code-owners and collaborators only**

- **Documentation**

author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

Repoint the DeepGEMM pin from `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` `nv_dev` (2.6.1, `8b1392b`) to `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` at [`9a86ae2b`](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/9a86ae2b78991f1c8e6e95945a591e1ca3b19ce7) (2.8.0), and update the Mega MoE call convention that comes with it.

`9a86ae2b` is the tip of the fork's `dev` branch: the upstream 26/09 public release plus five fork-only commits — the SM120 (consumer Blackwell) port and the SM90 paged-MQA `kv_block=32`/`next_n=4` port that we were pinning `nv_dev` for, a Mega MoE task-info slot-release fix, configurable SwiGLU alpha/beta, and SiTU for FP8/FP4 Mega MoE. Staying on `nv_dev` means we cannot pick up the 2.8.0 release line without losing SM120 and SM90 paged-MQA coverage.

Both arch ports matter here. The 2.8.0 release line dropped the SM90 2-CTA KV multicast, which `next_n=4` and `kv_block=32` depended on — that support had only ever lived on `nv_dev`. An earlier revision of this PR therefore had to degrade H100: MTP=3 decode fell back to the flattened path, and the kpool indexer had to align to 64-entry pages. `vllm-project/DeepGEMM#7` ports that SM90 support forward instead, so this PR needs **no** vLLM-side SM90 changes — `native_next_n_supported`, `_paged_mqa_logits_schedule_slots` and the kpool page alignment are all untouched.

### Mega MoE call convention

2.8.0 replaces the SiTU-specific optional pair with a generic one on `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` (and adds it to `bf16_mega_moe`):

| 2.6.1 | 2.8.0 | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `situ_beta: float \| None = None` | `activation_alpha: float = 1.0` | SiTU gate tanh scale |
| `situ_linear_beta: float \| None = None` | `activation_beta: float = 0.0` | SiTU linear/up tanh scale; `0.0` leaves the up branch unchanged |

Under `swiglu` the same two floats now parameterize `gate * sigmoid(alpha * gate) * (up + beta)`, and the defaults `1.0` / `0.0` are exactly the previous behavior — so the DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 call sites need no change. Kimi K3 is the only site in the tree that passed the SiTU parameters through to DeepGEMM, so it is the only call site updated here.

Two related semantics, both no-ops for us in practice:

- `activation_beta` may now be `0` (meaning "no tanh on the up branch", matching an unset `situ_linear_beta` in FlashInfer). 2.6.1 asserted `situ_linear_beta > 0`.
- `activation_clamp` is now silently ignored under SiTU rather than asserted-unset. Kimi K3 already passes `None`.

Note that vLLM's own `activation_situ_beta` / `activation_situ_linear_beta` config names (`FusedMoEConfig` and the TRT-LLM / CuteDSL / AITER backends) are deliberately left alone; only the mapping at the DeepGEMM call boundary changes.

### Build plumbing

2.8.0 drops the `third-party/fmt` submodule in favor of `third-party/deep_jit`, so this updates `GIT_SUBMODULES`, the `_C` include path in `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py`, and the header glob that retriggers the `_C` rebuild. `docker/Dockerfile` gains `elfutils-devel`, matching #56266 / #56255.

### Second commit: masked grouped FP8 GEMM

Verification turned up a real breakage that the pin bump would otherwise have
shipped: 2.8.0 also drops the legacy `fp8_m_grouped_gemm_nt_masked` Python
alias. `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` resolved it via `getattr(..., None)`, so it
silently became `None` and every call raised *"DeepGEMM backend is unavailable"*,
taking out `BatchedDeepGemmExperts`. The second commit looks up the canonical
`m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_masked` with the legacy spelling as a fallback. Both
names alias the same `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_masked` binding, whose C++
signature and pybind defaults are byte-identical across 2.6.1 and 2.8.0.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR moves the pin to the vLLM fork. The closest neighbors are #56266 (Mega-Gate) and #56255 (Mega-mHC), which both pin `deepseek-ai@39d8c4ca` and carry the same `fmt` → `deep_jit` plumbing and the same `elfutils-devel` hunk.

That base is the same 26/09 release this PR sits on; what neither can reach from `deepseek-ai/main` is the fork's four extra commits, in particular SM120 and SiTU. So the build-plumbing hunks in this PR do overlap with those two, and whichever lands first leaves the others a trivial rebase — that overlap is stated here rather than papered over. The activation-parameter rename and the Kimi K3 call site are unique to this PR.

One caveat on `elfutils-devel`: I could not find any `libelf` consumer in DeepGEMM 2.8.0 or in DeepJIT (both are header-only, and `<format>` is what replaced fmt). It is included here to match the sibling PRs; if a reviewer knows it is unnecessary, it should be dropped from all three.

## Test plan

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1, driver 580.126.09, torch 2.13.0+cu130.

**Build.** `cmake --preset release` fetches `vllm-project/DeepGEMM@e49b29bb` with
the `deep_jit` submodule (no `fmt`), and `--target _deep_gemm_C` builds `_C`
clean. The vendored package then imports as 2.8.0 and exposes the new
`activation_alpha`/`activation_beta` signature. `_C` links without `libelf`,
which is why I flagged the `elfutils-devel` hunk above.

**SiTU convention (the load-bearing part of this PR).** Single-rank numerical
check of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe(activation='situ')` against a PyTorch reference
implementing `alpha*tanh(gate/alpha)*sigmoid(gate) * beta*tanh(up/beta)`, at
Kimi K3's own config values (`activation_situ_beta=4.0`,
`activation_situ_linear_beta=25.0`):

| run | `calc_diff` vs reference |
| --- | --- |
| `activation_alpha=4.0, activation_beta=25.0` | **3.56e-04** |
| alpha/beta swapped (control) | 1.36e-01 |

3.56e-04 is the quantization error floor — dequantizing the FP8 activations
alone gives 3.60e-04. The swapped control is ~380x worse, so a reversed
assignment would have been caught rather than passing silently.

**Unit tests.**

```
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py
tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_weight_loading.py
tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py
tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
tests/models/glm5next/                              -> 81 passed

tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py ................ 9 passed, 3 skipped
tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py  passed
```

`test_batched_deepgemm.py` is the regression test for the second commit: with
that commit reverted it fails immediately with the `RuntimeError` above; with it,
32 pass.

Note my hardware is SM100, so none of this exercises the SM90 paths. The H100
`nvidia-h100-deepgemm-kernels` job is the real gate there — it is what caught the
2.8.0 SM90 regression on an earlier revision of this PR, before the fork ported
the SM90 support forward.

**Pre-existing failure, not from this PR.**
`tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py::test_w8a8_block_fp8_deep_gemm_matmul`
fails on my machine with `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED (719)` out of
`cuLaunchKernelEx`, and the sticky context error cascades into ~254 downstream
errors in the same pytest process. This is **not** caused by the bump: I built
the old 2.6.1 pin's `_C` side by side and swapped it in, and the identical 719
reproduces there (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d` on 2.6.1, `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` on
2.8.0). Also ruled out: stale JIT cache, PDL, GEMM shape, and target arch (both
compile `sm_100f`; device is cc 10.0). Grouped DeepGEMM paths are unaffected and
pass. I believe this is local to my setup, but I could not get a clean signal on
that suite either way, so I am flagging it rather than reporting it green.

**Model eval.** Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, `hidden_act=situ`, mxfp4
experts) GSM8K with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enable-expert-parallel
--tensor-parallel-size 4`, which is the only path that exercises the changed
call site end to end. The engine log confirms `moe_backend='deep_gemm_mega_moe'` with EP enabled, so
the changed call site is genuinely on the path.

Because a single number proves little against a 75%-pruned checkpoint, I ran an
A/B on the same build and ide

author: erclx
body:
## Summary

Close four measured blind spots in `canon context audit` to catch drift the audit was reporting clean over.

## Key Changes

- Widen the change-provenance pattern in `src/context/audit.ts` from `#\d{3,}` to `#\d+`, masking displayed spans first so a heading's auto-derived anchor link and a hex color in a code span do not read as change numbers.
- Add whole-record and per-decision word counts plus a `## Risks / open questions` word weight to `measureArchitecture()` in `src/context/architecture.ts`, reported and never gated.
- Add `src/context/wireframe-states.ts`, which matches a wireframe's `## States` table against its evidence folders by header text, reporting a missing folder, an unlisted folder, and a `plaintext` sketch carried past captured evidence.
- Gate the states-mismatch finding under `--gate` in `src/context/gate.ts`, alongside the existing missing-section and index-drift facts. The sketch-with-evidence finding stays advisory under every mode, since it reads a whole entry against whether any state has evidence rather than one sketched layout against its own evidence, so a conforming file can still trip it.
- Wire the new reports into `canon context audit`'s console and `--json` output in `src/commands/context.ts`.
- Update `docs/agents/context-audit.md`, `docs/agents/context-audit-checks.md`, `docs/agents/commands.md`, and `canon/context/cli/audits.md` for the new reports and the gate boundary.

## Technical Context

- An evidence cell resolves as the literal path it names against the project root, per the operator's own answer to the matching question, since the standard puts the path in the cell and a detected root guesses wrong in a monorepo.

author: sonnguyen2914
body:
## The defect

`DECLARED` in `e2e/standing.ts` mirrors `api/main.py::watched_strip_standing_blocks()`
in the backend, and its own header names it *"the one thing here that can go stale"*.
The guard it pointed at asserts **every block moved something**.

That catches a **misspelled** key — a misspelling matches nothing, its block moves
nothing, the block drops out of the result. It does not catch a **missing** one.
Sixteen keys moving satisfies "every block moved something" exactly as well as
seventeen do, and the seventeenth rides on every match forever.

`DECLARED.read` listed **16** keys. The route hoists **17**. `a_rate_needs_time` was
never in the mirror — and measured off production for this PR it is **3,818 B on each
of 27 matches**, the second-largest hoisted key after `registered_holes` (5,245 B).
The suite was green the whole time, because nothing was looking.

This is the subset-blind shape this codebase found five times in one day — including
once in this very area (`standing.book_is_per_fixture` had no guard at all until
2026-09-13): **a guard that asserts a SUBSET moved, and therefore stops LOOKING at the
entry that was left out.**

## Why it could not be caught from inside the file

Every v2 fixture is produced **by `toV2()` from `DECLARED`**. Checking the mirror
against a fixture it generated only proves it agrees with itself, and a key absent
from both is absent from the question. Completeness needs a source the mirror never
touched.

## The source of truth chosen: the wire

`e2e/standing-wire.ts` records **key names only** off production's own
`standing_blocks`. Re-verified before trusting it: `version: "watched-strip-v2"`,
27 matches, `/api/ready` `code_revision 6eb14a1`.

The load-bearing fact is that `api/main.py` fills that envelope key from the registry
**verbatim** —

```python
standing_blocks = watched_strip_standing_blocks()
... "where":  watched_strip_standing_where(standing_blocks),
    "blocks": standing_blocks,
```

— *before* it walks a single match. `_hoisted()` consults it per match, but nothing
filters `blocks` by what any match happened to carry. So it is the **declaration**,
not the subset that moved. Had it been assembled from what moved, this recording would
have inherited the very blindness it closes.

**Names only, and that is a rule.** The strip is operator-gated because it carries
positions — stated size and price paid. The token was read at call time, never printed,
never written to any file, GET only. The committed file contains 33 identifiers and no
value of any kind.

## Two guards, neither subsuming the other

| | sees | blind to |
|---|---|---|
| `DECLARED` vs `WIRE` — **hermetic**, every runner | missing key, invented key, missing block, invented block; offender named | `WIRE` itself going stale (both halves live here) |
| `WIRE` vs **backend source** — freshness | the emitter declaring a 34th key | needs the other repo on the tree |

The cross-repo check walks the Python **AST**, not lines — the declaration wraps values
onto their own line, carries comments between entries and expands a `**`, three shapes
a regex reader gets wrong quietly. It reads `origin/main` rather than the working tree
because the backend checkout on this machine sits on a branch that predates #129, and a
check that went red over whose branch was out would be a red build about nothing.

**A skip is not a pass.** It reports SKIPPED *with its reason* when no checkout resolves
— never a quiet early return, which is the failure this repo fixed on 2026-09-13. CI
here resolves no backend and cannot (the backend repo is private), which is exactly why
the guard that catches the defect is hermetic and does not depend on this one running.
Every other condition **throws**: the extractor accepts exactly one `**`
(`live_read.STANDING`, by name) and exits non-zero on any shape it does not know, so it
can never quietly return a subset — which would have been this same defect wearing a
different hat.

## All six blocks checked — one disagreement

| block | wire | mirror | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | 17 | 16 | **`a_rate_needs_time` MISSING** |
| `model_live` | 4 | 4 | agrees |
| `states` | 7 | 7 | agrees |
| `shared_exit_book` | 2 | 2 | agrees |
| `coverage` | 2 | 2 | agrees |
| `state` | 1 | 1 | agrees |

An independent AST walk of backend `origin/main` returned the **same 33 keys over the
same 6 blocks** as the wire, key for key — two independent readings agreeing on what
the route declares. `read` was the only disagreement with the mirror.

Then `a_rate_needs_time` is added, and the mirror is complete.

## Falsification

Every mutation was **verified to have applied** before its result was trusted — a
mutation that silently does not apply reads exactly like a surviving assertion, and one
of mine did that on the first attempt (a `{` where the file has `[`), reporting a false
green until it was caught and redone. Files were copied aside explicitly and restored
by checksum; `git stash` was never used. Rebuilt between every run.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| drop `read.a_rate_needs_time` (the real defect) | **red**, names the key |
| drop `states.vocabulary` | **red**, names the key |
| misspell a key | **red**, names it INVENTED |
| delete the whole `state` block | **red** at the block set |
| empty `state` in mirror **and** wire | **red** at the count backstop — the lazy fix, where a red is answered by deleting from `WIRE` |
| no backend checkout | **SKIPPED with its reason**, not passed |
| backend present, function renamed | **FAILED**, not skipped |
| backend present, unknown `**` expansion | extractor exits non-zero rather than returning 3 keys for `read` instead of 17 |

No assertion survived its mutation.

author: seandillon1224
body:
## Summary

- **`src/lib/analytics.ts`** — `track(name, props)` fans one product event out to `Observe.logEvent` (it lands on the session next to its launch / TTR / TTI metrics) and a Sentry breadcrumb (so a crash report carries the last few things the user did). There is deliberately no "is telemetry on?" branch: Observe drops the call without `extra.eas.projectId` or from a debug build, and `Sentry.addBreadcrumb` drops it when `init` never ran, so `track()` is inert-but-safe in a bare checkout. `src/lib/sentry.ts` gains a one-line `addBreadcrumb` wrapper so `@sentry/react-native` still has exactly one importer.
- **One call site**, as the example: the fetch screen's error-state retry (`track('fetch_retried', { source: 'error-state' })`). Naming rule documented — stable `snake_case`, past tense, `<object>_<verb>`, never carrying a value.
- **`src/lib/storage.ts`** — the only file that imports `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage`. Two surfaces: typed `storage.get(key, schema)` / `set` / `remove` (JSON + Zod, where absent / non-JSON / off-schema all read as `null`, while a real backend failure still rejects), and `storageDriver`, the raw string API the TanStack Query persister serialises into itself. `query-client.ts` uses the driver; **the session store from #208 uses the typed helpers**, so the repo keeps one storage idiom rather than two a PR apart. The on-disk format is unchanged (`true` was already the stored string). Swapping to `expo-sqlite/kv-store` is one import line, documented in the file header and in `docs/conventions.md`.
- **Maestro tab selection** — took the *pin the locale* option, not `TAB_LABEL` from `common.json`. `TAB_LABEL` is already passed from every step file; sourcing it from the `en` catalog would only keep two English strings in sync, and does nothing about the actual failure mode, which is the device rendering a different language. `scripts/e2e-pin-locale.js` pins the device to `en-US`: it reads `persist.sys.locale` (falling back to `ro.product.locale`), does nothing when the device is already English (the common path — one `getprop`, no restart), and otherwise sets the property and restarts the framework, because the framework only reads it at start. It never exits non-zero. Called from `bun run e2e:android` (plus `-prop persist.sys.locale=en-US` on an AVD the script boots itself, so that path never needs the restart) and from a new `before_maestro_tests` hook on `maestro_android`. Node built-ins only, and added to the `builtins-only` guard's entry points.
- **No testID is achievable on the Android tab bar, and the docs now say why.** expo-router documents `NativeTabs.Trigger`'s `testID` as the item's view tag, which "Espresso-based drivers like Detox read but Maestro and Appium do not". The only selectable string left is `accessibilityLabel` (the item's `contentDescription`) — which is also what TalkBack announces, so buying a stable selector with it means screen-reader users hear "tab-settings" instead of "Settings", exactly what `bun run e2e:a11y` exists to catch. The label selector stays and the language gets pinned instead.
- **Docs** — `docs/native-e2e.md` gains a **Device locale** section (both call sites, why the restart, why iOS needs none of it) and the reasoning above; `docs/conventions.md` gains the analytics rule and a **Persistence goes through `@/lib/storage`** section; `CLAUDE.md` gains one line.

## Test plan

Full local gate, all green:

- `bun run lint` — clean (only the three pre-existing oxlint warnings)
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run test` — **39 suites, 413 tests**, up from 393. New: `src/lib/__tests__/analytics.test.ts` (both sinks, the propless `logEvent(name, undefined)` shape, and the no-DSN / no-project-id no-op path) and `src/lib/__tests__/storage.test.ts` (round-trip, `false` vs absent, non-JSON and off-schema reading as `null`, a backend rejection still rejecting) and `scripts/__tests__/e2e-pin-locale.test.ts` (the `sameLanguage` check that decides whether to spend 20 s on a framework restart)
- `bun run knip`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run env:check`, `bun run i18n:check`, `bun run docs:build`
- `bun run eas workflow:validate .eas/workflows/e2e.yml` — valid
- Web E2E loop: `bun run export:web:e2e` → `bun run serve:web` → `bun run e2e:web` — **6/6 flows passed** in 45s (session, updates, tabs, fetch, not-found, smoke)

The native lane cannot run here (no EAS build downloaded, no emulator), so the locale pin and the `before_maestro_tests` hook are unverified against a real device — the script is defensive about that by design (never exits non-zero, warns and continues).

Closes #181

author: lusoris
body:
## What

Raises the lint budget to `--timeout=30m` per step (65 min job) and gosec's cap to 45 min, keeping the three synced places in agreement: the job args, `run.timeout` in `tools/golangci.yml`, and the Makefile `_ci-module` target.

## Why

Lint and gosec fail on one specific ARC worker and pass on the others. That node sits on a Proxmox host carrying **26 vCPU across 16 threads**, so it loses 1–3 cores to hypervisor steal — and steal surfaces as neither CFS throttling (measured 0%) nor container CPU usage, so nothing inside the job explains the slowdown.

Measured 2026-09-14 on run `34886127607`:

| job | node | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lint | starved worker | `go/packages` load exceeded `--timeout=20m` **twice**, both at 1200.7 s |
| Security (gosec) | starved worker | ran 32.7 min against a 30 min cap, killed |
| Test (race + coverage) | healthy worker | **passed**, same window, same commit |

A lint timeout is additionally self-perpetuating: `setup-go`'s cache-save post step is skipped when the job fails, so a run that times out on a cold cache leaves the next run cold too. `setup-go` reported `Cache is not found` on both attempts. One green run warms it to ~2 min.

## This is headroom, not the fix

The correct sizing is already declared in the cluster repo's `terraform/vms.auto.tfvars` — 4 cores for the control plane and 10 for the worker, leaving 2 for the hypervisor — and has simply never been applied. A runbook for that apply is going up alongside this. **Revisit both budgets once the resize lands.**

Deliberately not done: lowering the work (e.g. trimming linters) or splitting the job, since neither addresses the cause and both change what CI actually checks.

author: aaronjcole
body:
## What

`src/components/ui` held 49 files. 19 are reachable from app code; the other **30 were scaffolding no importer ever referenced** — 2,828 lines, including a 627-line `sidebar.jsx` in an app that navigates by bottom tabs.

Removing them leaves **27 dependencies** with no reference anywhere in `src`, `tests`, `scripts`, `base44`, or the config files.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `src/components/ui/*.jsx` | 49 | 19 |
| Declared dependencies | 71 | 44 |
| `node_modules` | 330 MB | 317 MB |
| Bundle output | — | **byte-identical** |

The bundle does not shrink. These components were already tree-shaken, so the win is install time and supply-chain surface, not download size — worth stating plainly rather than claiming a performance improvement this doesn't deliver.

## How reachability was determined

A transitive import graph, not a grep — and that distinction changed the answer. `separator`, `skeleton`, `toggle` and `tooltip` all *look* used because `sidebar`, `menubar` and `breadcrumb` import them, but those importers are themselves orphans. A flat "does anything import this?" check reported 26 orphans; the graph found 30.

Roots were every non-`ui` file under `src` and `tests`, plus the five components tests pin directly: `button`, `input`, `dialog`, `sheet` (`touch-target-primitives.test.js`) and `adaptive-select` (`release-configuration.test.js`).

Each orphan was then cross-checked a second way — by exported identifier rather than import path — which flagged three for manual review. All three were name collisions, not usage:

- `progressPhotos.js` calls `new Image()` — the browser global, not `ui/image.jsx`
- `App.jsx` renders `Progress`, which is `lazyWithRetry(() => import('@/pages/Progress'))` — the page, not `ui/progress.jsx`
- The three progress charts import `Tooltip` **from `recharts`**, not `ui/tooltip.jsx`

## Dependencies removed

**19 Radix primitives** whose only importers were orphaned components: `accordion`, `aspect-ratio`, `avatar`, `context-menu`, `dropdown-menu`, `hover-card`, `menubar`, `navigation-menu`, `popover`, `progress`, `radio-group`, `scroll-area`, `separator`, `slider`, `tabs`, `toast`, `toggle`, `toggle-group`, `tooltip`.

`@radix-ui/react-toast` is in that list even though `ui/toast.jsx` is **kept** — that toast is built on `class-variance-authority` and `lucide-react` and never imported the Radix primitive. I checked this specifically because the combination looked wrong.

**8 others:** `@hookform/resolvers`, `react-hook-form` (only `ui/form.jsx`), `embla-carousel-react` (only `ui/carousel.jsx`), `react-day-picker` (only `ui/calendar.jsx`), `react-resizable-panels` (only `ui/resizable.jsx`), `zod`, `next-themes` (unused — `src/lib/useTheme.js` is a hand-rolled provider), and `eslint-plugin-react-refresh`, which was declared but never wired into `eslint.config.js`.

## Deliberately kept

Five packages show no direct reference but are not removable:

- `typescript` — `npm run typecheck` invokes `tsc`
- `postcss` — required by the Tailwind/Vite pipeline; `postcss.config.js` names its plugins, not postcss itself, which is why a naive scan flags it
- `@types/node`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` — consumed by `tsc`, never imported

And one on judgement: `baseline-browser-mapping` is an explicit devDependency pin with no reference and no recorded reason. Removing it gains nothing real (it resolves transitively anyway) and could undo whatever it was pinned to fix, so it stays. Worth someone deciding deliberately.

## Side effect

This retires the recurring dependabot PRs for components nothing imports — **#79** (`@radix-ui/react-context-menu`) becomes moot, and no future bumps will be opened for the other 18 removed primitives. **#112** (`react-hook-form`) also becomes moot.

## Verification

Every stage run locally against the change:

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| Lint | ✅ exit 0 |
| Typecheck | ✅ exit 0 |
| `test:security` | ✅ 164/164 |
| `test:fitness` | ✅ 124/124 |
| `test:contract` | ✅ 2/2 |
| `verify:android` | ✅ passed |
| `build` | ✅ 9.4s, output unchanged |
| `test:e2e` | ✅ 40/40 |

body: Live Best Odds on the owner-gated New Odds Board (Betstamp parallel board) no longer lets a book win when that number has not refreshed in 4 minutes. **Behavior** - Threshold is the named constant `LIVE_BEST_ODDS_MAX_AGE_MS` (`240_000`). - Gate uses the existing per-line `bookLineUpdatedAt` clock (same signal as the cell age badges). - Applies only when the game/quote is live (`game.is_live`). Pregame Best Odds is unchanged. - Stale book cells stay on the grid with their price and age. Only the Best column / best-highlight path skips them. - If no selected book is still fresh, Best shows the existing empty dash (`—`). - Public Odds Board is unchanged (it does not pass the freshness opts). **Tests** - `oddsBoard.test.js`: stale prices lose Best, next-freshest wins, all-stale / missing timestamps are empty, individual cells still render, pregame and ungated calls stay raw. - `betstampNormalize.test.js`: snapshot `bookLineUpdatedAt` flows through live Best; board wires `LIVE_BEST_ODDS_MAX_AGE_MS`.

body:
Cartograph v2.1.30 updates the supported ParadeDB image and exact pg_search contract from 0.25.7 to 0.25.9, refreshes all outdated direct Rust dependencies and compatible lockfile entries, and adopts the published Rust 1.98.1 Linux build images. This branch includes Dependabot PR #160's original commit for toml_edit 0.25.15.

The ArkTS 0.3 and OCaml 0.26 grammar updates also require a freshness transition: without it, unchanged V16 projects could skip indexing and retain older parser results. Append-only schema migration 43 admits V17, so those projects report stale, reparse and publish once, then return to no-op indexing. Migrations 1–42 remain byte-identical. Seven frozen digest expectations were independently checked against their original V16 values before changing only the digest domain; fixture content, projections, rankings and bounds are preserved.

Managed upgrade recovery covers 0.25.3, 0.25.6 and the immediately preceding 0.25.7, including backup, interrupted replacement, failures around extension catalog mutation, query preservation and repeat no-ops. author: themorgan
body:
## What this changes

The occasion index is loaded **in full by every session before it does any work**, and it had grown every day — 1,136 tokens on 08-31, 3,377 on 09-14, **3,812 today against this repo's own 3,600 cap**. Consumers are worse off, not better: a repo resolving five sources legitimately has a bigger index than this catalogue does, and one measured ≈5,586 against the 4,000 default. The cap was doing its job by refusing; nothing was reducing the thing it refused.

**The rule.** A practice whose `applies_to` names real paths is reached by `precedent_paths.py` when one of those files is edited. A practice declaring `gates:` is reached by `precedent_gate.py` at the moment it names. Either way its index line is a second copy of a channel that already works, so `build_views` omits it. A bare `["**"]` with no gate is untouched — that glob matches everything and therefore routes nothing, so the index is its only channel.

**The exception, and it is the whole reason this is not a one-liner.** Neither channel can fire on something a **person says**. A glob needs a file; a gate needs a moment, and `merge`/`review`/`push`/`reply` all arrive at the *end* of the work a phrase was meant to redirect. `Go merge` is the worked case and its own history is the citation: while its definition sat in a private set a session could not read, one went and asked what the phrase meant — the exact interruption the phrase exists to prevent.

So a spoken trigger is never dropped. A `command:` is one by construction; anything else says so with the new **`index_required: true`**. The judgment is made once, by a person, in the practice file — not re-guessed by a regular expression at every build.

## Effect

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| This repo's occasion index | 3,812 tokens (over its 3,600 cap) | **1,444** |
| This repo's `AGENTS.md` | — | 7,514 of a 12,000 ceiling |

The saving is larger for consumers, which is where the problem actually was. It is also self-maintaining: a new practice with a real glob or a gate no longer grows the index at all, so the daily creep this cap was invented to catch stops at the source rather than being paid down by whichever session happens to trip the ceiling.

## Two holes the harness caught

Both are real defects in the old model, not test friction — and both were invisible while every on-demand practice was named in the block:

- **`layered-practice-packs`' reachability model counted the index, gates and checks but not the path channel.** It was right by accident; the moment the index stopped naming routed practices, four correctly routed ones read as reachable by nothing. It now counts a real `applies_to` glob as the channel it is.
- **"the loader block renders every publishable source" required each source to be *named* in the block.** Under this policy a source whose practices are all routed contributes nothing to the rendered text while having resolved perfectly. It now requires a name only from a source with at least one practice that should appear.

`local/merge-target-is-beta-branch` takes `index_required: true` **on its merits**, not to satisfy that assertion — its occasion covers *opening* a pull request, and the `merge` gate fires too late for that.

Two fixtures now declare `index_required: true` rather than inheriting a line they relied on by default (`fixture-owns-its-state`); both assertions are otherwise unchanged and still prove what they meant to.

## Visibility

The generated block says what it no longer lists and points at **`precedent_show.py --index-omitted`** (new here), which names each omitted practice with the channel that reaches it. The footer deliberately carries **no count** — a count would be a second computation of the same set, printed for a reader who then runs the tool and resolves it again; the two disagreed by three on the first build.

## Gates

`verify_harness` **202 passed / 0 failed**, identical to the untouched tip measured before these changes. `doc_lint`, `doc_sync`, `leak_gate` clean; `precedent_check` 51 passed / 0 violated, including the new `index-required-is-declared` with its planted case and unplanted baseline.

Base is `precedent-beta-v01`, not `main`.

author: handys11
body:
## Summary

Second of three PRs from the Native AOT design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-native-aot-design.md`). The CLI and MCP server can now be published as Native AOT executables, and a new CI job checks every PR against the JIT build of the same commit. AOT stays opt-in: no project sets `PublishAot`, so `dotnet pack` and `publish.yml` are unchanged.

- **CLI (`ProjGraph.Cli`):**
  - `TrimmerRootAssembly` for `ProjGraph.Cli` and `Spectre.Console.Cli`, which Spectre reflects over for commands and settings.
  - Two `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]` attributes whose justifications cite the rooting and the smoke suite: IL3050 on `Program.Main` (`CommandApp`) and IL2067 on `TypeRegistrar.Register`.
  - `EnableTrimAnalyzer`/`EnableAotAnalyzer` on every build, and `IlcTreatWarningsAsErrors=false` so third-party ILC warnings don't fail publish.
- **MCP server (`ProjGraph.Mcp`):** the same analyzers and `IlcTreatWarningsAsErrors=false`. PR 1 already removed the runtime blockers.
- **`tests/ProjGraph.Tests.Smoke.Aot`:**
  - 28 parity tests, 18 CLI and 10 MCP, each running one input through the native build and the JIT build and requiring the same exit code, stdout, stderr, written diagram file, and MCP protocol results.
  - The tests skip unless `PROJGRAPH_SMOKE_CLI_NATIVE`/`_CLI_REFERENCE`/`_MCP_NATIVE`/`_MCP_REFERENCE` are set, so the existing matrix reports them as skipped. With `PROJGRAPH_SMOKE_REQUIRED=true` they never skip.
- **CI:** a new `aot-smoke` job on `ubuntu-latest` installs `clang`/`zlib1g-dev`, builds Release, publishes both executables with `-p:PublishAot=true`, and runs the suite. It has a 30-minute timeout.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` (including how to run the suite locally), and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

The branch also carries the implementation plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-native-aot-pr2-native-build-smoke.md`).

### Results (linux-x64, SDK 10.0.401)

- Native binaries: `ProjGraph.Cli` 36.6 MB and `ProjGraph.Mcp` 42.9 MB.
- Smoke suite, native vs JIT: 28/28 passed in ~20 s, both with and without `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.
- A clean clone running exactly the CI commands also passed 26/26. That run was before the two `--help` cases were added.
- The existing suites are unchanged: 1,178/1,178 passed, the build has 0 warnings, and `dotnet format` is clean.
- Harness self-checks:
  - JIT apphost vs JIT `.dll` passes.
  - A "native" binary replaced with `/bin/true` fails.
  - A missing variable with `PROJGRAPH_SMOKE_REQUIRED=true` fails instead of skipping.
- The first native publishes failed as the analysis predicted:
  - The unmodified CLI failed on IL3050/IL2067.
  - The CLI with suppressions but without the trimmer roots crashed with `Could not get settings type for command of type 'ProjGraph.Cli.Commands.VisualizeCommand'`, and the suite caught it.
  - The unmodified MCP project failed on third-party ILC warnings as errors.

### Deviations from the spec

1. **No `PublishSingleFile` condition on the MCP project.** With it left unconditional, the AOT publish succeeds and produces the same 42,946,344-byte binary, so the condition is a no-op. PR 3 removes `PublishSingleFile` entirely.
2. **The native publish uses `--artifacts-path`.** `ProjGraph.Mcp` is self-contained, so an in-place AOT publish reuses `bin/Release/net10.0/linux-x64`. That deletes the JIT apphost and rewrites its `runtimeconfig.json` with AOT feature switches, which corrupts the reference build.
3. **A reference variable can be a `.dll` or an executable.** A `.dll` runs through the `dotnet` host. The MCP reference is `ProjGraph.Mcp.dll` from the self-contained build output.
4. **A fifth variable, `PROJGRAPH_SMOKE_REQUIRED`.** Without it, a misspelled variable in CI would skip every test and leave the required job green.
5. **stderr is compared too, and `--output` runs share one path.** Spectre wraps the `Saved to <path>` stderr line at 80 columns, so both builds write to the same path one after the other.
6. **Reference outcomes are pinned.** Each CLI case asserts that the reference exits 0 (or non-zero for the two failure cases), and each MCP tool call asserts `isError != true`. Diagram cases also require non-empty output. A wrong path therefore can't pass as parity.
7. **Extra cases:**
   - a malformed project (`visualize`, `stats`, and MCP `get_project_stats` warnings);
   - a `.sln` that lists a project twice;
   - `ConcurrentDictionary`/`Barrier`/`[Required]` types in a class diagram;
   - `prompts/get`;
   - server capabilities;
   - `--help` and `visualize --help`.
8. **Parameter name.** The spec's `options.inheritance` is actually `options.includeInheritance`.
9. **Shared MCP servers.** Disposing an SDK 2.2.0 stdio client takes about 5 s, so each test class shares one native and one reference server, started lazily. The suite takes about 20 s instead of about 2 minutes.
10. **Legacy `.sln` fixture.** It also includes a solution folder, `NestedProjects`, and a classic C# project-type GUID.
11. **Output location.** Native outputs go to git-ignored `artifacts/native/*` instead of the spec's `out/*`, because `out/` isn't git-ignored.

### Found and fixed during review

- **ANSI under GitHub Actions.** Spectre.Console turns on ANSI color when `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`. The `stats` normalizer then missed the `Analysis time` row, and both stats cases would have failed on the first CI run; local runs couldn't show it. The normalizer now strips escape sequences before deciding which row to drop, and the local verification step sets `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.
- **Hangs.** MCP requests now carry a 2-minute cancellation token, and the job has `timeout-minutes: 30`, so a hung native server can't block CI for hours.

### Notes

- The native CLI publish prints an informational `ILC: Method '[Spectre.Console.Cli]OpenCli.OpenCliParser.Parse(...)' will always throw because: Failed to load assembly 'NJsonSchema'`. It comes from rooting Spectre's unused OpenCLI parser. It isn't a warning and doesn't affect any command.
- The plan's narrative still quotes 16 CLI and 26 total tests. The final counts are 18 and 28, after the review added the two `--help` cases.
- Deferred to the PR 3 plan:
  - capturing native MCP stderr in failure messages;
  - asserting the "native" variable isn't a JIT apphost;
  - narrowing the IL3050 suppression with a `CreateApp()` helper;
  - splitting the CI publish steps.

### Exit criteria (spec, PR 2)

- [x] No project enables AOT: `git grep -n "<PublishAot" -- '*.csproj' '*.props' '*.targets'` is empty.
- [ ] `aot-smoke` is green on this PR. Its first run on a hosted runner is this PR.
- [ ] **Maintainer:** after the first green run, add `aot-smoke` as a required status check on `develop`.

author: reeder-design
body:
## Summary

Connects Reference Library resources that are explicitly **Approved for Portfolio Use** into the guided Create Content Lab.

## Approved Sources → Content Brief

Content Briefs can now attach one or more approved sanitized derivatives as trusted source context.

- New briefs include an **Approved source context** selector.
- Existing briefs can add or remove approved sources.
- The Create Content workspace now describes Approved Sources as an active Content Brief input rather than a future feature.
- An approved Reference Library item now activates **Use in Content Brief**, opening a new brief with that source preselected.
- Unapproved items keep the action disabled.

## Private-original boundary

The source bridge never reads the private original into Create Content AI context.

Each attachment snapshots:

- Reference Library item id
- approved sanitized filename
- sanitized derivative SHA-256
- approval timestamp

When AI planning runs, Portfolio Manager extracts context only from the approved sanitized derivative. The private original stays outside the brief and outside the AI request.

## Stale-source protection

If an attached sanitized derivative is replaced, removed, or loses Approved for Portfolio Use status, the Content Brief detects that the saved source snapshot is stale.

- AI plan generation is blocked until the current approved version is reattached.
- Reattaching a changed source marks any existing AI plan stale.
- A brief therefore cannot silently use changed source material under an older approval/hash.

## AI planning boundary

Generate AI Plan now sends only:

- the saved Content Brief;
- public portfolio taxonomy;
- text extracted from selected approved sanitized derivatives that support safe local text extraction.

Non-text-extractable approved derivatives can still remain attached to the brief but are clearly shown as not included in AI text context.

The existing provider, authorization, sensitivity-preflight, proposal-only, and non-publishing boundaries remain in place.

## Validation

Adds `scripts/check-create-content-sources.py` and includes it in Full Validation and GitHub Actions. The regression test creates distinct private-original and sanitized text, proves only sanitized text enters Create Content context, replaces the derivative to trigger stale-source protection, then verifies reattachment refreshes the hash and marks an existing plan stale.
