body:
## What changes

This is the first of four slices of spec 009 T090 (research.md Decision 23, maintainer decisions): each full Prometheus destination scrapes the business services in its own namespace.

| Destination root | Business ServiceMonitors before | After | Canary ServiceMonitors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-dev` | `microtodo-dev` | `microtodo-dev` (now explicit) | `microtodo-prod`, unchanged |
| `infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-staging` | `microtodo-dev` | `microtodo-staging` | `microtodo-prod`, unchanged |
| `infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-prod` | `microtodo-dev` | `microtodo-prod` | `microtodo-prod`, unchanged |

The business ServiceMonitors are `auth-api`, `todos-api`, `users-api`, `frontend`, and `log-message-processor`. One JSON patch per destination replaces their `spec.namespaceSelector.matchNames`; the economical `infrastructure/prometheus` root does not change.

Also in this pull request:

- `research.md` Decision 23 records the four T090 slices and the maintainer's choices for all of them, and `tasks.md` lists them under T090.
- New `tests/platform/service-runtime-full.bats`, run by the `policy-contracts` job. Besides this slice, it pins what the full overlays already render: startup, readiness, and liveness probes and CPU and memory requests and limits on every container of the five Deployments, which the prod Rollouts reference through `workloadRef`.

## Why

The full destination roots take the economical Prometheus as their base, and its business ServiceMonitors select `microtodo-dev`, the economical cluster's business namespace (a T085 defect). A full cluster holds one environment, so full staging would scrape no business target and full prod no stable one: service alerts, the golden-signal dashboard, and the request-rate scaling planned for the third slice would all read nothing. The canary ServiceMonitors already select `microtodo-prod`, the only environment that composes the canary strategy.

## Tasks

- gitops `specs/009-full-platform-rollout` T090: first slice ticked as a nested item. T090 stays unchecked: three slices remain.

Commit order: `a0d76cc` design, `42c0480` failing test, `5d547b1` implementation, `5f7ab63` register.

- [x] The task register is updated in this pull request
- [x] Every task ticked here was verified by locating its artifact

## How it is verified

All runs are local, with kustomize 5.8.1 and kubeconform 0.7.0 from `scripts/managed/full-profile-toolchain.lock` (checksums verified), under `env -i` with only those tools, `/usr/bin`, and `/bin` on `PATH`, as in CI.

Test-first commit `42c0480`, before the implementation:

```
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor auth-api must select only microtodo-staging, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor todos-api must select only microtodo-staging, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor users-api must select only microtodo-staging, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor frontend must select only microtodo-staging, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor log-message-processor must select only microtodo-staging, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-prod: ServiceMonitor auth-api must select only microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-prod: ServiceMonitor todos-api must select only microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-prod: ServiceMonitor users-api must select only microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-prod: ServiceMonitor frontend must select only microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-dev
FAIL: infrastructure/profiles/full/prometheus/destinations/eks-full-prod: ServiceMonitor log-message-processor must select only microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-dev
10 failure(s)
```

The probe and resource pins passed already, as expected: they describe the current renders.

After the implementation `5d547b1`:

```
service-runtime-full.bats  exit 0  PASS: the five services render probes and bounded resources in every full overlay, and each full destination scrapes its own business namespace
observability-full.bats    exit 0  PASS: full-profile observability roots (prometheus, grafana) keep encrypted volumes on gp3 (aws) and managed-csi (azure) carry the full-profile alerts with their monitors, store Jaeger spans in Elasticsearch for 3 days, link Grafana traces to Elasticsearch logs, and name the cluster and environment of every alert
git diff --check           clean
```

`diff` of the `eks-full-staging` render against `main` changes exactly the five business `matchNames` lines, `microtodo-dev` to `microtodo-staging`. No recording rule, alert, dashboard, or analysis template names a business namespace, so none changes.

Each mutation below is applied to a copy of the branch; the unmutated branch passes:

| Mutation | Failure |
| --- | --- |
| `log-message-processor` dropped from the staging patch's target | `eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor log-message-processor must select only microtodo-staging, found: microtodo-dev` |
| `microtodo-dev` added to the prod patch's namespaces | `eks-full-prod: ServiceMonitor auth-api must select only microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-prod microtodo-dev` (and the other four) |
| the staging patch also targets the `-canary` ServiceMonitors | `eks-full-staging: ServiceMonitor auth-api-canary must keep selecting microtodo-prod, found: microtodo-staging` (and the other canaries) |
| `startupProbe` removed from `apps/auth-api/base/deployment.yaml` | `apps/auth-api/profiles/full/overlays/dev: Deployment auth-api must define startupProbe` |
| the economical `todos-api` ServiceMonitor moved to `microtodo-staging` | `economical infrastructure/prometheus must keep ServiceMonitor todos-api on microtodo-dev` |

The same canary mutation on the prod patch changed nothing and passed, as expected: prod's canary ServiceMonitors already select `microtodo-prod`, so it is an equivalent mutant, and the staging variant above is the meaningful one.

Documentation: the change is a Prometheus Operator `ServiceMonitor.spec.namespaceSelector` value, which neither `aws-knowledge` nor `microsoft-learn` covers; the field is already used this way by the vendored kube-prometheus v0.18.0 CRD (`infrastructure/prometheus/vendor/v0.18.0/setup/0servicemonitorCustomResourceDefinition.yaml`, `matchNames`: "the list of namespace names to select from"). `check-mcp.sh gitops .` passes: aws-knowledge answers with 5 tools, and microsoft-learn with 3.

Nothing was scraped in a cluster: none is reachable from this environment.

- [x] Infrastructure changes: the documentation consulted through the required MCP servers is listed above

## Risk and rollback

No full-profile root is active; T091 activates them. Once active, each destination's Prometheus scrapes the business pods of its own namespace. Revert the merge commit to roll back.

## What this PR does not do

- It does not add PodDisruptionBudgets, topology spread, KEDA ScaledObjects, or feature-toggle ConfigMaps (the next three T090 slices).
- It does not change the economical ServiceMonitors or the canary ServiceMonitors.
- It does not change how the canary ServiceMonitors tell canary from stable pods: in both profiles they select Services only by `app.kubernetes.io/name`, which the stable Service also carries, a question for a separate change.
- It does not record live evidence (T094).

author: viniciuspdre
body:
## Issue vinculada

Closes #78 

## Descricao da issue

<!-- issue-summary:start -->
### #78 - ci(pull-request): adaptar template e validações ao fluxo development/main

## Contexto

Atualmente todo Pull Request deve possuir uma issue vinculada através de `Closes`, `Fixes` ou `Resolves` e selecionar exatamente um tipo de release.

Com a estratégia `development → main`, existem tipos de PR com responsabilidades diferentes:

* branches de trabalho → `development`
* `development` → `main`
* `hotfix/*` → `main`

Um PR de promoção de `development` para `main` representa uma release e pode conter várias issues, portanto não deve ser tratado como um PR comum de implementação.

## Objetivo

Adaptar o template e as validações de Pull Request para reconhecer os diferentes fluxos de branches.

## Escopo

* [ ] Identificar o tipo do PR através das branches de origem e destino
* [ ] Exigir uma issue vinculada nos PRs de trabalho direcionados à `development`
* [ ] Não exigir uma única issue vinculada em `development → main`
* [ ] Exigir tipo de release em `development → main`
* [ ] Definir validação para `hotfix/* → main`
* [ ] Manter sincronização entre issue e PR para branches de trabalho
* [ ] Atualizar mensagens de erro das validações

## Critérios de aceite

* [ ] `feat/* → development` exige issue vinculada
* [ ] `fix/* → development` exige issue vinculada
* [ ] `development → main` não exige uma única issue
* [ ] `development → main` exige definição do tipo de release
* [ ] `hotfix/* → main` exige issue vinculada
* [ ] Os workflows atuais continuam funcionando nos respectivos tipos de PR

## Evidências esperadas

* Atualização do template de Pull Request, se necessária
* Atualização de `validate-pr-template.js`
* Testes ou execuções demonstrando cada cenário

### Observações

* Esta tarefa deve ser concluída antes das automações de release e GitHub Projects
<!-- issue-summary:end -->

## O que foi feito

- Ignorado o job `Commit messages` para PRs abertos por `dependabot[bot]`.
- Mantidos os demais checks de qualidade rodando normalmente para PRs do Dependabot.

## Evidencias

- `npm run test:github`
- Resultado: 17 testes passaram

## Checklist

- [x] Testei localmente
- [ ] Atualizei a documentacao, se necessario
- [x] Nao inclui segredos, chaves ou credenciais
- [ ] Conferi os itens concluidos na issue vinculada

## Tipo de release

Marque exatamente uma opcao:

- [ ] patch - fix/correcao compativel
- [ ] minor - feature/nova funcionalidade compativel
- [ ] major - breaking change/mudanca incompativel
- [x] sem release

author: muhammedakinci
body:
Closes #251.

## What was wrong

`index.js` answers a request the caller got wrong with 400, because a 500 tells a client to retry, an operator that the service broke, and a monitor to count it. But `validateRequest` only checked that fields were present, that the lists were lists of the right length, and the time window's shape and hours. The **format** of each field was first checked inside `buildCircuitInput`, after the gate. So eleven requests that are purely the caller's mistake came back 500, and each was counted in `square_proof_failures_total{reason="invalid_field"}`. The contract was inconsistent within a single object: `allowed_hours_end: 25` got 400, and `allowed_days: ['mondayy']` got 500.

## What changed

**`services/prover/src/prover.js`: `validateRequest` checks every field's format**

It uses the same helpers `buildCircuitInput` already calls, so a value accepted at the gate is one the build accepts, and the messages are unchanged: the field's name, never its value.

- `toFieldString` for `max_daily_spend`, `max_per_transaction`, `payment_amount`, `daily_spent_before`, `current_unix_timestamp` and `stripe_receipt_hash` (default `'0'`)
- `addressToField` for `operator_id`, `payment_recipient` and `payment_token`, and for every entry of `blocked_addresses` and `token_whitelist`
- the category rule for `payment_endpoint_category` and every entry of `allowed_endpoint_categories`
- the UUID rule for `policy_id`
- `daysToBitmask` for `allowed_days`, beside the hours it sits with

The order stays deliberate: missing fields, the salt, list types and lengths, then formats, then the time window.

**`services/prover/src/hash.js`**

The category and UUID checks were inside `hashCategory` and `hashUuid`, ahead of the Poseidon hash. They are now `categoryBytes` and `uuidHex`, which the hashes call, so the gate can refuse a bad value without paying for Poseidon, and each rule still has one home.

**`services/prover/src/openapi.js`**

The 400 description now lists the format errors it covers. The 500 description was already right: the prover failed after accepting the request.

`index.js` needed no change. The gate already answers 400 and leaves the proof metrics alone.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| all eleven requests answer 400 | `prove-route-validation.test.js`, `answers 400 for %s, naming the field`: the issue's eleven, each asserting the exact message it recorded and a `request_rejected` log with no `proof_failed` |
| none increments `square_proof_failures_total` | `counts none of the eleven as a proof failure`; `observability.test.js`, `does not count a malformed field as a failed proof` |
| `allowed_hours_end: 25` and `allowed_days: ['mondayy']` answer the same code | `answers an hour of 25 and a day of "mondayy" with the same code` |
| `observability.test.js` and `prove-route.e2e.test.js` pin the new behaviour | the malformed blocked address is 400, uncounted, and logged as a rejection in both |
| real prover failures stay 500 | `observability.test.js`, `counts a failed proof`: the service is loaded again with its artifact directory pointed at an empty one, and a valid request is 500 and counted |

The last row replaces what `counts a failed proof` used to send. It sent a malformed blocked address, which is now a 400. A valid request cannot stand in for a failure either, because the `prover (real proving key)` job has the artifacts and would prove it. Missing artifacts fail the same way on every runner, and each load of the service has its own metrics registry.

## Runs

`services/prover`, locally, on both setups CI uses:

| | |
|---|---|
| no artifacts, as `services/prover (hermetic)` | **185 passed**, 17 skipped (the suites that need the circuit) |
| with a proving key and wasm, as `prover (real proving key)` | **189 passed**, 13 skipped; the end-to-end suite proves for real, and its malformed-address case is now 400 |

The tests bite. With `prover.js` put back to `main`'s version, where the format checks are not at the gate, 14 of them fail: all eleven 400 cases, the "counts none" test, the hour-and-day test, and `does not count a malformed field`.

**Overlap to note:** #286 edits `services/prover/src/index.js` and `openapi.js`. This PR does not touch `index.js`; in `openapi.js` the two change different response descriptions.

author: j2msjadebot
body:
## Scope

Make answered check-ins visibly different from pending ones, without losing easy correction:

- Pending: original watch choices, No watch and evening Same as morning.
- Saved: date/slot and saved selection, with one **Change** button.
- Change: reopen offered choices with saved context; no record, timestamp or receipt mutation.
- Storage/validation rejection: retain controls and show a dismissible error alert.
- Post-commit Telegram edit/confirmation failure: keep the saved record; never report a failed write.

The UI reads current history rather than replay receipt text, so an old callback cannot put a superseded choice back on screen. Selection authorization is shared with the read-only Change operation, retaining exact owner/chat/topic and missing-topic message-binding rules. Telegram `/set` reconciles its known prompt; offline CLI stays offline.

No dependency or schema change. Message editing is best effort, not atomic with SQLite. Only the tapped duplicate is edited; no background reconciliation queue or full duplicate-message registry is added. These limits are documented in `docs/RUNTIME.md`.

## Verification

Verified clean commit: `b7416d1dfe0c939fe4c23c89bb4fbf5b9e70153b`.

- Full pytest: **40 passed** on Python **3.12.3** and **3.13.13**; no skipped tests.
- Ruff lint and format check: pass.
- Source distribution and wheel build: pass; isolated installed-wheel import: pass (PTB 22.8).
- Full base-to-head whitespace check: pass.
- New regressions cover saved/reopen/replay/restart projection, authorization and topic binding, commit-before-edit, network/edit failures, dismissible errors, snapshot semantics, and `/set` reconciliation including post-commit read failure.

## Acceptance evidence

See `docs/INVARIANTS.md` for regression coverage and `docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md` for the preceding baseline's live evidence. The baseline private-chat exercise demonstrated restart/correction/snapshot/backfill/export and injected write failure/recovery with synthetic data. It exposed the missing saved-state feedback and unreadable error toast that motivated this slice.

New UI live acceptance is still pending. No production deployment, migration or cutover. The temporary baseline bot is stopped. Reginald reviews independently; the repository owner retains merge/release authority.

Originating work: Tapkeeper project conversation on Buzz.

author: finger563
body:
Implements `IRammsActuationBackend::ReleaseMotor` for the MuJoCo backend. A MuJoCo actuator has no off switch (its ctrl is applied every step), so "release" parks it: a position servo (affine bias with a negative position gain) at the joint's **current** position — it stops pursuing its old target and holds where it is — and a motor / velocity actuator at zero. Returns `true` once the ctrl is staged, so `UMebotControllerComponent` can honestly mark a base-routed motor disabled on a MuJoCo chair.

Depends on the `bool ReleaseMotor(FName)` virtual from rammp-org/ramms-core#22 — **now merged** (`12afd92` on ramms-core `main`), so this is ready to go. Without the override, RammsCore's default reports "unsupported" and consumers keep the motor enabled — safe, just less useful.

Validated in PIE on `BP_LiftDriveHolonomic_Ramms`: `left_hip_front` commanded to 0.5 rad and released mid-travel parks at ~0.47 rad (small steady sag under load, as a held servo does).

author: carlosvinicius-ai
body:
## 📌 Resumo

Este PR conclui a **Phase 9 — Final Documentation & Submission** do framework analítico desenvolvido para a **SkillCorner Basketball Analytics Cup (Liga Endesa ACB 2025/2026)**, marcando a prontidão oficial do projeto para submissão pública (**Release `v1.0.0-submission`**).

Consolidamos toda a formalização matemática dos modelos BAV, SCI e FSPV, a transparência científica quanto a limitações e premissas, a revisão dos registros de decisão arquitetural (ADRs), a expansão dos testes de isolamento de domínio e a reestruturação completa do `README.md` como guia executivo e reprodutível de ponta a ponta.

---

## 🛠 O que foi implementado

### 1. Especificação Matemática Formal (`docs/SPEC.md`)
- **Ball Action Value (BAV)**: formalização do processo de Markov em tempo discreto, equações probabilísticas da chance ofensiva $\Delta P = P(\text{score} \mid S_t) - P(\text{score} \mid S_{t-1})$, vetor de 28 features espaciais e temporais no instante $t$, e formulação da taxa acumulada por posse.
- **Space Creation Index (SCI)**: formalização do grafo espacial dinâmico $G=(V, E)$ para 10 jogadores + bola, equações de agregação de mensagens do GraphSAGE em 2 camadas ($\text{AGGREGATE}^{(k)}$, convolução com ReLU e dropout), pooling global e método de atribuição nodal via sensibilidade de gradiente ($\|\nabla_{x_i} \hat{y}\|_2 \odot x_i$).
- **Full Spectrum Player Value (FSPV)**: equação de fusão ponderada padronizada em $z$-scores:
  $$\text{FSPV}_i = \alpha \cdot \text{BAV}_{z, i} + (1 - \alpha) \cdot \text{SCI}_{z, i} \quad (\alpha = 0.5)$$

### 2. Documento de Limitações e Transparência Científica (`docs/LIMITATIONS.md`)
- **Amostra de 10 Jogos**: impacto do tamanho amostral frente aos 327 jogos da temporada regular e risco de variância amostral em jogadores de rotação restrita.
- **Ruído e Interpolação de Tracking**: documentação de frames extrapolados/não detectados (17% a 24%) e sensibilidade a oclusões físicas no garrafão.
- **Sensibilidade de Hiperparâmetros da GNN**: escala de grafos, representação de arestas por raio euclidiano e suposição de estacionaridade temporal dentro da janela da chance.
- **Escopo Tático**: delimitação clara de que BAV foca na criação ativa com a bola e SCI foca na gravidade sem a bola, não incorporando diretamente esquemas defensivos de pick & roll (drop, hedge, blitz) no valor individual.

### 3. README Oficial de Submissão (`README.md`)
- Visão executiva completa do projeto alinhada aos 5 critérios de avaliação da banca SkillCorner (Relevância, Metodologia, Originalidade, Apresentação e Reprodutibilidade).
- Guia de instalação em um comando (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`).
- Instruções de orquestração via CLI (`run-all`, `run-bav`, `run-sci`, `build-report`).
- Seção visual com tabelas dos Top Performers da Liga ACB e print do relatório interativo HTML5 standalone.
- Citações acadêmicas e referências bibliográficas formais (VAEP / Decroos et al., Hamilton et al. GraphSAGE, unravelsports, floodlight, mplbasketball, skillcornerviz).

### 4. Atualização de Cardinalidades e ADRs (`docs/DATA-STRUCTURE.md`)
- Cruzamento e consolidação das contagens empíricas (71.984 eventos) com os schemas das 20 tabelas.
- Confirmação de status `Accepted` em todos os ADRs (0001 a 0005).

### 5. Auditoria de Clean Architecture (`tests/domain/test_zero_dependencies.py`)
- Expansão dos testes de AST e inspeção estática garantindo **zero importação** de bibliotecas externas na camada de domínio (`src/domain/`), preservando pureza arquitetural absoluta.

## What

Thirty bots on an owner's hours (D-77) show three or four dogs in the evening. The owner wants ten to fifteen, close to the centre, on a map that isn't already fully taken.

- **Roster of 120** in `services/botAvatars.ts`: ninety new hand-written entries (name, breed, five-part description), all names unique. An index keeps its name for good, so `bot:N`'s users row is untouched.
- **Ninety portraits** drawn with `pnpm bots:avatars` through the D-72 recipe into `server/assets/bot-avatars/30..119.png` (~2 MB, ~22 KB each, ink pass applied).
- **Homes 300 m apart** (`HOME_MIN_SEP_M` 420 → 300, ring 450 → 320) around the same ten central hotspots. Simulated: 120 placed with no fallbacks, **115 within 3 km of Maidan, 74 within 2 km**, farthest 3.4 km. At 420 m the pool spilled to 4.5 km rings; a first cut added fifteen outer-district parks and the owner sent it back ("close to my neighbourhood-district, center"). The first thirty bots' homes shift a little; with the wipe below that costs nothing.
- **`pnpm wipe:territory`** (`src/db/wipe-territory.ts`), built per CLAUDE.md: dry by default, `--apply` explicit, bots only unless `--all`, `--snapshot=<path>` writes the rows out first. The dry run prints what is held (marks, ground pieces, holders, km², raids per cohort, biggest holders) and exactly what the apply deletes: the chosen owners' marks, ground and raids, plus a reset of the last-mark spacing and home-ground flag on their companion rows so the first mark after the wipe isn't refused against a mark that no longer exists. Progression (points, XP, bones, happiness index) stays. Nothing re-seeds at boot (`botSeedMarks` is 0), so the city is claimed again from nothing at the new pace.

## After merge — the owner's steps, in this order

1. **Dry run** on production, read it: `fly ssh console -a shukajpes-api -C "node dist/db/wipe-territory.js"`
2. **Apply**: same with `--apply` (add `--snapshot=/tmp/territory.json` for insurance; `--all` if people's ground should go too, the dry run shows both cohorts).
3. **Raise the count**: the `MULTIPLAYER_BOTS` Fly secret to `120`. Doing this before the merge would put blank chips with repeated names on the map.

## Risks, named

- Territory is the load: 120 × 12 marks = 1,440 against 360, on one shared vCPU, read by every phone's sync. Watch `cron_slow` and sync timings after step 3; don't go past 120 in one step.
- Both leaderboards get 120 bot rows; capping or filtering bots there is a separate decision.
- The morning peak (~21 out) is below the 27 that ran fine before, so the tick itself isn't the risk.

## Docs

D-78 in `05-decisions.md`; `MULTIPLAYER_BOTS` row and a `wipe:territory` CLI row in `07-operations.md`; bots bullet in `02-architecture.md`.

author: andrew3019
body:
Closes #318 (part of #306, Wave 3: landing path).

**Why.** Opening a PR was a hand-run `git push` + `gh pr create` that an agent was trusted to have done, followed by `comment --pr`. v2 §4 makes `Open PR` a bundled step that Switchboard runs and completes itself, only once the whole operation succeeds.

**What it does.** `sb plugin plans open-pr <plan>` runs, in order:
1. the PR-open evidence gate (`change.verification`, `change.review`, `change.human_checks`)
2. the repo's LOCAL required checks (`[plans] required_checks`)
3. `git push -u origin <plan branch>`
4. find or open the PR
5. the marked summary comment

The `open_pr`-kind step is completed only when every part succeeds.
- **Refusals** leave the step untouched and nothing is attempted: the evidence gate, no checks configured, a step owned by someone else, the wrong branch, a dirty tracked tree.
- **A failed sub-op** (checks / push / pr / comment) sets `progress: failed` and `failure: {op, detail, at}`.

`sb plugin plans step retry <step>` re-runs a failed bundle. The retry is idempotent: it reuses the live PR on the record, or else an open PR for the branch, and never opens a second.

**Design calls** (lead-approved):
- **Checks setting:** `[plans] required_checks` ships EMPTY, and the verb refuses until a repo sets it. Switchboard can't know a product repo's test command, and "checks green" on zero checks is the claim this exists to stop.
- **`comment` unchanged:** it and its derive-on-first-post stay as the hand-run path, so nothing regresses. Removing that derive is a follow-up once `open-pr` is relied on.
- **Ownership:** an unowned open_pr step is taken implicitly by the caller, and the take is logged.
- **Remote CI:** not part of the bundle (#318 §2).

**Verification.** Full suite green on a97d703 (2513 passed). The `OpenPrBundleTest` tests cover:
- all sub-ops succeed → step completes
- comment fails → step `failed`
- retry reuses the PR

A read-only `gh api` call confirmed `{owner}` is substituted inside the open-PR search's query string. This PR itself was opened by `open-pr`, so that run is the live proof.

**Independent review.** Fresh reviewer on a97d703: no majors. Correct by inspection but untested: a dead recorded PR, and a crash between PR-open and record.

**Risks / limits.**
- Switchboard's own `required_checks` value lives in gitignored `.switchboard/settings.toml`, so each machine or fresh clone must set it.
- Check commands run with no timeout.

author: metanull
body:
## Summary

- `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` and `docker-compose.pgsql.yml` both define the `postgres` service's `image` key, and Compose resolves conflicting keys left-to-right with the last listed file winning. The ghcr header previously told operators either order was fine ("the two overrides touch disjoint keys"), which stopped being true once `docker-compose.pgsql.yml` gained its own `postgres` service.
- Listing `docker-compose.pgsql.yml` after `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` reverts `postgres` to the locally-built `appsec-scout-postgres:latest` (with its `build:` restored), and `docker compose pull` then fails with "pull access denied" — this is exactly what an operator hit on a fresh corporate-VM bundle install.
- Updated both override file headers to state the one valid order (`docker-compose.pgsql.yml` before `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`) and why, and added a one-sentence callout in `docs/QUICKSTART.md` section e right after the `COMPOSE_FILE=...` example, naming the "pull access denied" symptom so it's searchable.
- Comments/docs only — no functional YAML changes.

Closes #513

## Verification

Ran `docker compose config --images` with `COMPOSE_PROFILES=local-db` for both orders on this branch:

- `docker-compose.yml;docker-compose.pgsql.yml;docker-compose.ghcr.yml` → `postgres` resolves to `ghcr.io/metanull/appsec-scout-2/postgres:latest` (correct).
- `docker-compose.yml;docker-compose.ghcr.yml;docker-compose.pgsql.yml` → `postgres` resolves to `appsec-scout-postgres:latest` (reverted to the local build, matching the reported bug).

Also ran `docker compose config --quiet` (pgsql-before-ghcr order) to confirm the config still parses cleanly after the comment edits — exit code 0.

No PHP changes; Pint/PHPStan/Pest not run (not applicable to this docs-only change).

## Deviations

None — implemented exactly as specified in #513.

author: michel-zededa
body:
Files one bead, `harbor-oi3` (P1, bug): the New run **Dataset autocomplete shows no suggestions** on
the deployed viewer — reported against corello running `0.22.0-zededa-4.7` (`git_sha e0af478`), the
build that shipped the feature earlier the same day.

**Ruled out already**, all from outside an authenticated session:

- The route is deployed. `/api/run/datasets` answers `401 application/json`; before the 4.7 deploy
  the same path returned `200 text/html`, the SPA catch-all. A 401 to an anonymous caller is the
  launcher dependency working.
- The frontend calls it unconditionally — no launcher-mode branch, and no `/api/launcher/datasets`
  variant exists. Not the wrong-endpoint-in-kubernetes-mode trap.
- The token filter does not swallow the seeded `terminal-bench@2.0`: it tokenises on `@`/`.`/`-`, and
  those tokens match two registry rows, so the single-exact-match suppression does not fire.
- The registry is up: 80 datasets from the node using the deployed code.

**Leading suspect.** `list_registry_datasets` catches everything and returns `{"datasets": []}` by
design, but records the failure only at `logger.debug`. The viewer does not run at debug level, so an
in-cluster viewer that cannot reach the hub leaves no trace — and to the user that is the same empty
dropdown as "nothing matches what you typed". The pod's egress to the hub is *inferred* (no
NetworkPolicy in the namespace), not tested: `kubectl exec` there is refused as a production read,
and the endpoint cannot be called from the node because the viewer trusts proxy identity headers
only from inside `trustedProxyCIDRs`.

The bead carries the ten-second confirmation — in a signed-in browser, read the
`GET /api/run/datasets` response on the New run page; `{"datasets": []}` with a 200 confirms it, 80
entries moves the bug into the UI, a 401 means the proxy is not asserting identity on that request —
and asks for the degradation to be made observable (warning, not debug; possibly a
`registry_reachable` flag so the field can say so) plus a decision on what an empty query should
show, since `filterByTokens` deliberately returns nothing and ~80 datasets is a weaker case for that
than thousands of models.

No code changes — this is the issue record only.

author: cyber-g3
body:
💡 **What**: Pre-instantiate and cache `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances for English and Spanish locales and cache the `#timeline` DOM element in `app.js`.

🎯 **Why**: In `app.js`, `renderTimeline()` runs inside a 1-second `setInterval` loop to refresh timeline timers. Each invocation previously executed `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(...)` 3 times per second and performed a `document.querySelector("#timeline")` DOM query. Creating `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances on every tick incurs significant CPU and GC overhead.

📊 **Impact**: Benchmarking shows caching `Intl.DateTimeFormat` reduces date formatting execution time by ~125x (from ~356µs to ~2.8µs per formatting call) while eliminating repeated DOM query overhead and GC pressure.

🔬 **Measurement**: Benchmarked via Node.js execution loop comparing uncached vs cached `Intl.DateTimeFormat` formatters over 10,000 operations.

author: quntao-z
body:
Closes #2709

## The defect

`DEAD_LINK_ERROR_CODES` in `server/src/services/sourceLinkHealth.ts` listed `ENOTFOUND`, but nothing could ever produce it. `probeSourceLink` runs the SSRF guard before any request, and `isPublicHostname` swallowed the DNS error in a bare `catch { return false }`, so "this name has no record" and "this resolves somewhere we refuse to go" collapsed into one answer. The guard reported its SSRF refusal, `ERR_SSRF_BLOCKED` is not a dead-link code, axios never ran, and a host that had stopped existing was stored as `UNKNOWN`.

Serve-time suppression keys off `UNAVAILABLE`, so it never fired for any of them.

## The fix

`classifyHostnameResolution` reports which of `public`, `private-address`, `unresolvable`, or `resolver-failure` applies. `SsrfBlockedError` carries it as `reason`, and the health probe maps only `unresolvable` onto `ENOTFOUND`, which is what makes the classifier's existing branch reachable rather than adding a new one. `isPublicHostname` keeps its exact yes/no contract as a one-line wrapper.

**The security answer is unchanged.** Every non-public case is still refused; only the reported reason is new. Two properties are load-bearing and both are pinned by new `security:preflight` policies:

- Only a genuine `ENOTFOUND`/`ENODATA` reads as `unresolvable`. A `SERVFAIL`, timeout, or `EAI_AGAIN` stays `resolver-failure` and therefore `UNKNOWN`, so a DNS blip cannot retire a live citation.
- A private, loopback, or metadata resolution still classifies `UNKNOWN`, because that is a fact about our network position and not about whether the page exists. Reporting it as `unresolvable` would let a blocked internal host retire a citation.

This is deliberately the mirror of #2473. That issue stopped the lane over-retiring on inconclusive signals; this one stops it under-retiring on a decisive one. Neither direction may be traded for the other.

## Verification

Against the real corpus URL that surfaced this, not only a synthetic control:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| a served external website value whose host has no DNS record | `UNKNOWN` | `UNAVAILABLE` |
| a synthetic nonexistent host | `UNKNOWN` | `UNAVAILABLE` |
| a live Yale roster page | `HEALTHY` | `HEALTHY` |
| a 403 bot challenge | `UNKNOWN` | `UNKNOWN` |
| a loopback address | `UNKNOWN` | `UNKNOWN` |

Tests: 1,572 pass across the guard, link-health, rendered-fetch and scraper-util suites. `security:preflight` is 248 pass / 0 fail, up from 245 pass / 1 fail. The DNS-dependent cases live in a new hermetic file that mocks `dns/promises`, so CI never depends on live resolution or on a resolver that hijacks NXDOMAIN.

## Data operation this requires

Stored verdicts written before this fix still carry the wrong value, so merging changes nothing already recorded. Measured on Development:

- 13,406 stored `sourceLinkHealth` verdicts across 5,376 entities: 12,612 `HEALTHY`, 464 `UNAVAILABLE`, 330 `UNKNOWN`.
- Of the 64 distinct hosts behind an `UNKNOWN`, **15 do not resolve**, accounting for **18 stored verdicts, 8 of them on served rows**.

Those 8 are citations a student can reach and that suppression currently fails to hide. The correcting operation is `research-homes:backfill-source-link-health` against Development, and this is done when that has run and the served output has been re-read, not when this merges.

author: teknogeek0
body:
Four independent fixes found while running a live migration from a read replica.

**Stop CDC when the endpos is set on an idle source.** The feedback-timer guard in `pgsql_stream_logical` tested `cur_record_lsn`, which is declared inside the streaming loop and reset to `InvalidXLogRecPtr` on every iteration, so the test never passed. It now tests the position already streamed. Without this, setting the sentinel endpos on a source with no further WAL activity never stops the stream, and a replica source cannot be nudged with a write.

**Retry table COPY after a source connection failure.** Treats 57P01, 57P02 and 57P03 as connection errors and resets both connections between attempts, re-opening the snapshot when the source is the snapshot connection. Adds the `copy-source-reconnect` suite.

**Skip smoke tests on fork pull requests.** Runs them on pushes and same-repo pull requests only.

**Move the base image to Debian 12.** Debian 11 is on LTS and its security archive no longer serves the package versions its index advertises, so `apt-get install` fails with a 404 on the pgcopydb image. This broke the eight suites that build a `Dockerfile.inject` on that image. `tests/Dockerfile.pagila` was already on bookworm. This changes the published image. The same commit passes `PGCOPYDB_IMAGE` to the `exclude-extension` test service, which hardcoded `pgcopydb:pg16` and so failed the PG17 and PG18 cells.

## Tests

Full suite green at `PGVERSION=18`, all 34 suites. `citus_indent --check` passes.

The run needs Docker network pruning partway through: the default address pool holds about 30 networks and the suites leave one behind each, which is a local limit, not a CI one.

## Known gap, not addressed here

About eleven suites build their source database from a `Dockerfile.pg` whose `ARG PGVERSION=16` default is never overridden, because their `compose.yaml` passes no build args. The target follows the matrix, the source does not, so the PG18 cell of `cdc-wal2json` runs a PG16 source into a PG18 target. Pre-existing, and left alone because fixing it may surface real PG18 failures that deserve their own triage.

author: zprbot1
body:
Implements zipline#26 (V3): thread the existing `user.zpr.authority` through the connect and refresh paths into `derive_user_authority`, flipping the three zipline#24 V1 gate tests green.

## What changed

**RED** (`a6121ac`): removed `#[ignore]` from the three zipline#24 gate tests. All three failed against the `existing_authority = None` call sites:

```
test actor_attributes::tests::test_refresh_after_displacement_loses_user_record_and_tag_zipline24 ... FAILED
test actor_attributes::tests::test_refresh_of_decorating_store_keeps_google_authority_zipline24 ... FAILED
test connection_control::tests::test_oidc_connect_with_decorating_file_store_keeps_google_authority_zipline24 ... FAILED
  left: ["happyfile"]
 right: ["google"]
```

**GREEN** (`9b1d1ed`):

- **Connect path** (`vs/src/connection_control.rs`, `authorize_connection` loop): per-iteration owned extraction of the current authority from `authd_claims` (`find(USER_AUTHORITY).and_then(first().cloned())`), passed as `existing_authority.as_deref()`. Recomputing per iteration makes the first vouching source in `policy.list_services()` order win, and an authority stamped by the auth-blob arm before the loop wins over all trusted-service sources.
- **Refresh path** (`vs/src/actor_attributes.rs`): reads the actor's current authority via `actor.get_attribute(key::USER_AUTHORITY)`. The zipline#25 same-source arm in `derive_user_authority` lets the authenticating service re-stamp expiry on its own refresh; decorating sources never displace the stamp.

No changes to `derive_user_authority` itself (landed in #10), no schema change, no version-floor move.

## Behaviour change

With two CN-less file stores both vending `user.*` attributes, the authority winner changes from **last-wins** to **first-wins** in `policy.list_services()` order — and an authenticated identity (OIDC blob) can no longer be displaced by a decorating store on connect or refresh.

## Regression coverage

No new tests added — the connect single-store surface is already covered by `ts_user_attrs_install_user_authority` / `ts_two_sources_one_user_authority_value`.


author: richardthe3rd
body:
Opening search inserted the field as a third row of chrome, below the app bar and the festival banner rather than replacing either. While search is open the app bar now carries the field itself.

Fixes #664

## What changed

`SliverAppBar` while `_showSearch` is true:

- back arrow where the leading icon would be, field where `FestivalHeader` was, no overflow menu
- `FestivalBanner` sliver hidden
- `floating`/`snap` off, `pinned` on — a field that scrolls away mid-typing is wrong
- `titleSpacing` zeroed with a 16px right pad instead: the 56px leading slot plus the default 16px spacing left the field with a 32px gap on its left against a 16px right margin, reading as off-centre
- entry point unchanged: the bottom `SearchButton`

## Measured effect

At 400x800, the first drink card's top moves from **y=154 to y=56** — 98px of chrome given back to the list. The issue estimated the banner at 40–48px; measured it is 34px.

## The clear button changes meaning

Search here is a transient find, not a persisted facet like the category/style/visibility filters — so closing still clears the query, as before. A query left applied behind a closed field would be a narrowed list the user cannot explain, because the search button can only say that *something* is filtering, never which word.

That is what makes the in-field clear button's old behaviour incoherent once a back arrow exists: it was labelled "Clear search" but also closed the bar, and there would then be three controls all doing the same thing. Now:

| control | effect |
|---|---|
| `←` app bar | exit: close, clear, restore the app bar |
| `X` in-field | clear the text, stay in the field, keep focus |
| bottom `SearchButton` | same as `←` |

The `X` is rendered only when there is text to clear. That matters beyond tidiness: it, plus dropping the now-redundant prefix magnifier, is what pays for the ~56px the back arrow costs, so the hint's width budget from #659 survives. The 375px no-ellipsis test measures that rather than trusting the arithmetic.

`←` is labelled `'Exit search'`, deliberately not `'Close search'` — the bottom button already holds that label while open, and a duplicate node would make `find.bySemanticsLabel` ambiguous in the tests driving this screen.

## Expanding adopts the applied query

The provider's query outlives this screen: a tab switch goes through the shell's `context.go`, which disposes `DrinksScreen` without `_closeSearch` running. Opening search therefore adopts whatever query is applied instead of opening empty over a filtered list. `SearchButton`'s `hasQuery && !isActive` state is what signals this in the closed state, and this is the path that reaches it.

## Accessibility

A `TextField`'s accessible name is its hint only while it is empty — once the user types, the node carries the value and no label at all. That matters more here than in a form, because the takeover has removed `FestivalHeader` and this field *is* the app bar. Three approaches were measured: a plain `Semantics` wrapper and `InputDecoration.labelText` both fail (the label lands on an ancestor node the screen reader never focuses, or is dropped entirely); `Semantics(container: true)` sticks it to the field's own node while keeping the value and the `isTextField` flag. Pinned by a test.

## Accepted cost

The festival name, drink count, status badge and the overflow menu's three items (Browse Festivals, Settings, About) are unreachable while searching. Exiting is one tap, in three places. This is pinned by a test so losing it later is a deliberate act.

## System back: deliberately not handled

An earlier revision added a `PopScope` so hardware back would exit search. Verified under the real shell that this misfires: `DrinksScreen` sits inside `BeerFestivalHome`'s exit-confirmation `PopScope`, and `Navigator` invokes every registered handler for one back event — so back closed search *and* raised "Press back again to exit", arming the exit timer. Removed rather than papered over; coordinating the two scopes spans two widgets and belongs in its own change. Hardware back therefore behaves exactly as it did before this PR.

## Tests

+7 net (1492 → 1499). Rewrote the clear-button test to the new contract; added tests for the exit arrow, the header/menu/banner giving way and returning, the pinned app bar, the clear button's conditional rendering, the adopted query on expand, and the field's accessible name surviving text entry.

Two new goldens, `drinks_screen_search_active_{light,dark}.png`, both reviewed by eye. They need `EditableText.debugDeterministicCursor` — the autofocused field's blinking caret is an animation `pumpAndSettle` would otherwise wait on forever.

The six existing `drinks_screen_*.png` goldens are byte-identical: none of them opens search, so the change is inert for all of them.

## Reviewing note

Most of the `build()` diff in the first commit is re-indentation; the substantive changes are the `SliverAppBar` block, the `if (!_showSearch)` on the banner, and `_SearchBar` → `_SearchField`. The second commit is the review fixes.

## Not verified

No manual browser or device testing — an agent cannot do it. The Cloudflare Pages preview is the place to check the takeover by hand, particularly the field's look at real phone widths and with a soft keyboard up.

## Follow-ups, not in scope

- Coordinating the shell's exit-confirmation `PopScope` with a child scope, so hardware back can exit search without arming the exit timer.
- Search results have no relevance ordering — a match in the user's own note outranks an exact name match purely alphabetically.

author: gonzaloebiz
body:
Version bump and changelog. No code changes.

## What it releases

**#91 — the audience collection.** `observeList()` kept only the first audience a process saw, so an installation with several store views described one of them and nothing said how many existed. Coverage was a tautology, and the question that matters — has an audience nobody looked at changed — could not be asked.

The collection answers both halves in one response, and it is already fetched when the admin offers the audience dropdown, so nothing new is requested.

The roster is keyed by audience id, so a later reading completes an earlier one and a repeated id is impossible by construction. The account-wide count is never capped: a truncated roster beside an intact count still answers the coverage question, while losing the count loses the only figure nothing else can supply. The roster is bounded by both entry count and serialised size, trimmed one entry at a time.

**#90 — the account's billing arrangement.** `pricing_plan_type` sits on the account root beside the four fields already read there, and separates an account paying for a plan from one paying nothing. Kept as the string the API returns rather than mapped to a fixed set. **Not** the plan tier — nothing on that response carries it, and the docblock says so, because that is the misreading the field invites.

Both passive: no additional call, no quota, nothing added to any request.

`tools/no-deprecated-calls.php`: 64 files, 0 findings.

## Order

This is tagged ahead of the extension release deliberately, so the extension can raise its library floor to this version rather than pointing at a tag that does not exist yet. The ordering question that prompted it has been settled separately: a missing count is stored and displayed as unknown rather than zero, so neither order produces a misleading reading.

body:
Refs task-token-context-research

Purpose: record MEASURED context costs of ArggonManager's agent-facing surfaces (static docs, generated init tree, --json envelopes, MCP tools/list, comment growth) and propose ranked optimizations per operating principle 3.

Top findings:
- list --json (136 items) = 60.7 KB (~15.2k tokens); 6 fields null/empty on >=96% of items (~15-20% payload waste).
- next --json = 901 B vs list = 60.7 KB (67x) — agents should be steered to next-first.
- No arggon show <id> today; item files grow ~226 B per comment, unbounded per read.
- init --full emits ~43.7 KB; SKILL.md is 16.3 KB and duplicated in-tree.

Recommendation (ADR 0006, Proposed): compact JSON envelopes by default (opt-out --full), next-first agent guidance, new show <id> progressive-disclosure read path with --tail-comments N, and a generated-docs context budget (AGENTS.md <=2 KB, SKILL.md de-duplicated). MCP description trimming deferred. No product code changes in this item; implementation via follow-up items.

body:
## Why

Migrations **0012 and 0013 are now applied and verified on both Neon branches** (development `br-twilight-hill-ayffyd2b` and production `br-orange-feather-ayps8kep`): `result_persisted_at`, `player_request_limits` and the three serving indexes (373–375 MB) are present in each, and production was re-checked healthy afterwards.

The function bundles are still **not deployed**, so the bounded SQL selection, completion marker and per-player quotas from #83–#85 are inert in production and the new indexes are unused. Measured against production after the migrations: run start is still 11.0 s cold / 2.3–2.8 s warm, unchanged.

`BACKEND-RELIABILITY.md` asked to "obtain Neon deployment access or use an approved owner-operated deployment path." This adds that path.

## What

- `.github/workflows/deploy-functions.yml` — `workflow_dispatch` with an explicit `development` / `production` target, defaulting to development. Runnable from the GitHub web UI or mobile app; no local tooling required. Uses the `NEON_API_KEY` secret the backend gate already relies on.
- `.github/neon-functions.txt` — the slug-to-entry-point mapping, listed once and consumed by both the pre-flight and deploy steps.
- `docs/BACKEND-RELIABILITY.md` — records the applied-migration state, replaces release step 3 with this workflow, and corrects the rollback path.

Each entry point is bundled with esbuild, the same bundler Neon's own CLI uses by default. The workflow **refuses to upload a bundle that does not expose a default `fetch` handler**, then verifies the deployment by asserting the new `/health` coverage fields (`unrated_puzzles`, `missing_sets`) are present and clean — the old bundle does not emit them, so this proves the new code is actually live — and times two practice run starts.

The verification run is flagged `qa` and is never completed, so it writes no ranked result, no `game_results` row, and does not enter first-attempt player measurements.

## Verified before opening this PR

- All three entry points bundle for node24 ESM and load in Node exposing `default.fetch` (this is the check the workflow runs).
- Neon's documented deploy contract confirmed from their API reference: multipart upload, `index.mjs` entry, `nodejs24`, `DATABASE_URL` injected automatically.
- Bundle format proven live against a throwaway function on the dev branch, since deleted. No real function was modified.
- `npm test`: 114 JS + 72 Python passing.

## Not in this PR

Migrations are deliberately not applied by the workflow — 0012/0013 are already live, and a future migration should be applied before the code that needs it. Rollback is only available through the deployment history in the Neon console; the API exposes no bundle download.

## How to run it

Merge, then **Actions → deploy neon functions → Run workflow → `development`**. Check the health assertion and the two run-start timings in the log, then run it again with `production`.

body:
## Why

Every write tool worked inside an existing project, so a new user's only answer was "go to the web app first" (ezmodo task #322).

## What

- **`create_project`:** takes a title, a writing type (enum; the API rejects unknown ones with a 400), and optionally a synopsis, genre and nested `structure`.
  - Every `nodeType` is checked against `GET /api/v1/writing-types`, and the 500-node cap is enforced, **before** the project is created.
  - An unknown level returns `UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE` with the allowed levels.
  - If the node batch fails after the project exists, it returns `STRUCTURE_FAILED` carrying the `projectId`, so the agent retries rather than creating a duplicate.
- **`manage_outline add`:** a given `nodeType` is validated against the project's writing type.
- **`NO_PROJECTS`:** now an offer to create a project; `createProjectUrl` is kept.
- **`instructions`:** create a project only when the writer asked, after confirming title, type and structure.
- **Remote allowlist:** `create_project` added.
- **Version:** 0.2.0.

## Fix found by running it

`write_draft append` refused any section with an empty document and no blocks. That is every prose-level node the wizard, the kickoff and `create_project` plant, so no freshly planted chapter was writable from the connector. It now sends `adoptSectionProse` when the document has no content nodes. An image-only document is still refused.

## Checks

- **Tests:** 117 pass.
- **Mutation checks:** validate-before-create, the node cap, and the image-only refusal each fail tests when broken.
- **End to end over stdio against a local API:**
  - An invented level is refused and no project is created.
  - A nested poetry project plants correctly.
  - `chapter` is refused on poetry.
  - Appending to a created poem reads back.

**Depends on** EasyModeOnly/ezquill `feat/writing-types-registry` being deployed first. After merge, publish with `npm stage list` / `npm stage approve`.

author: carlosgutierrezmartin
body:
Recupera el trabajo de la PR #10 (se cerró sin fusionar cuando su rama base entró en `main` con la #9) y encima aplica el diseño del artefacto.

## Lo que traía la #10, ahora sobre `main`

- Detección automática de bordes: la pantalla de encuadre propone el recorte del ticket.
- Pestañas abajo (inicio, escanear, ajustes) y presentación de tres pasos la primera vez.
- Ajustes y banco de pruebas visual, que enseña qué leyó el OCR y por qué el parser aceptó o rechazó cada fila.

## El diseño

**Paleta con nombre.** Cada pantalla repetía a mano el par `bg-white dark:bg-gray-900`, y bastaba olvidar la mitad oscura una vez para que ese sitio se viera distinto al resto. Ahora el color se nombra por su papel (`surface`, `line`, `muted`, `faint`, `ghost`, `hair`, `canvas`, `ink`) y el modo oscuro se resuelve en un único bloque de `index.css`. Unas 180 utilidades sueltas pasan a token, y con ellas se van las variantes oscuras que faltaban en sitios donde el contraste ya era flojo. Lo mismo con los radios: convivían 16, 12 y 24 px sin criterio y ahora siguen la escala del diseño (24 paneles, 20 tarjetas, 14 controles).

**Portada.** Tarjeta principal con el botón de escanear dentro y un atajo a la galería que salta directo al encuadre. El historial muestra las caras de quien participa, el progreso del reparto y cuánto falta en euros, en vez de solo el número de artículos.

**Arranque.** Presentación que cuenta foto → lectura → reparto mientras la app monta, y dice que funciona sin conexión, que es lo que la distingue. Se ve una vez por sesión del navegador, se salta con un toque y no aparece para quien pidió reducir el movimiento.

**Renombrar vive en el título de la cabecera.** El reparto repetía el nombre del ticket justo debajo solo para poder llevar el lápiz al lado.

## Verificación

- 173 tests en verde (3 nuevos para la pantalla de arranque), typecheck y `vite build` limpios.
- Pantallas comprobadas en Chromium sobre el build de producción, en claro y en oscuro: arranque, portada, captura, ajustes y reparto.

Dos tests cambiaron de aserción a propósito y conviene mirarlos: el botón de escanear pasó de «Escanear ticket» a «Escanear» (y ahora comparte nombre con la pestaña, así que la consulta se acota a `main`), y el de renombrar comprobaba que el nombre saliera en **dos** sitios, que era justo la duplicación que este cambio elimina.

Lo único que sigue sin poder probarse aquí es una inferencia real del OCR: los hosts de los modelos (`paddle-model-ecology.bj.bcebos.com`, `huggingface.co`, `paddleocr.ai`) están bloqueados en este entorno.

author: davidnguyen-tech
body:
## Summary

Protect eligible managed-only cold activity launches with a bounded, transient `am set-debug-app <package>` transaction, without `-w` or `--persistent`. Keep the existing Java-debugging opt-in and MSBuild defaults unchanged.

Disabling `am start -D` avoids Java debugger waiting but does not mark an intentional early managed pause as debugging. AOSP distinguishes `DEBUG_ON` from `DEBUG_WAIT`; the former retains ActivityManager's per-process debugging/ANR exemption without waiting for a Java debugger. See [ActivityManagerService](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-16.0.0_r1/services/core/java/com/android/server/am/ActivityManagerService.java), [ActivityThread](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-16.0.0_r1/core/java/android/app/ActivityThread.java), and [ProcessErrorStateRecord](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-16.0.0_r1/services/core/java/com/android/server/am/ProcessErrorStateRecord.java).

## Behavior and safety boundaries

- Protect only Android 12+ forced cold, non-waiting, non-repeated activity launches targeting the sole device user, with an explicit component in the configured package and confirmed package process.
- Observe both restored global debug-app state and the matching process's `mDebugging=true` after attach. PID visibility alone is insufficient; no `am start -W` or application-code readiness wait is introduced.
- Serialize activity debugging per device serial within the host process; use independent bounded cleanup after failure/cancellation and preserve primary errors.
- Preserve legacy launches with explicit unprotected diagnostics for warm/multi-user/implicit/custom-process/unconfirmed-metadata/unsupported initial dump-layout paths. Keep strict ownership/layout errors after mutation. Check cancellation around each fallback.
- Preserve explicit Java-debugging, no-debug, null-command, broadcast and instrumentation behavior outside this transaction.

Android's debug-app command force-stops a package across all users, which is why protection is restricted to single-user cold launches. There is no atomic compare-and-clear API: unrelated adb clients, same-package concurrent external ownership, disconnection and late remote execution remain platform limitations. An observed different owner is not cleared.

## Validation

126 targeted tests pass against the real shared launch implementation and ADB transport using a private TCP fake server. Regressions were demonstrated red before corrections, including real `Stopping:`/`Starting:` output, custom-process eligibility, component-only launches, fallback cancellation, and gate diagnostics. Coverage includes PID-before-attach, timeout, cleanup/launch double failure, ownership changes, retries, malformed post-mutation state and pre-arm unsupported layouts.

The original reviewed implementation is commit `663060b22b02f872217f8c602db5671ad64ce03a`. Publication merge `06b2860e6fb1f6e9adc71de71aaa7b8a77946b59` preserves that commit and incorporates upstream main `00c4f3d99d4a138fc3c0818369126b18b80457ee`, whose sole additional change is nullable annotations in the installer's `Platform.cs`. The seven-file implementation patch is unchanged. All 126 targeted tests were rerun on the publication merge: 126 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

Built the supported netstandard2.0 product libraries and AndroidSdk netstandard2.0/net10.0 graph; net10.0 tests ran with configured major runtime roll-forward on .NET 11. Fixtures are source-shaped deterministic responses, not device captures. No live device/OEM breakpoint validation or full native SDK build was performed. This draft is not a production runtime sign-off.

author: matiaslujanw
body:
El descuento de una promoción se calculaba sobre el monto que se estaba cobrando, que es el saldo entero de la cuenta: alojamiento más consumos. Una reserva de $100.000 con $20.000 de heladera y un cupón del 20% descontaba $24.000 en vez de $20.000, así que la promoción del hotel terminaba regalando parte del minibar —que no está en promoción y que además ya se le pagó al proveedor—.

Ahora el descuento cae sobre lo que queda por pagar del alojamiento. Para saber cuánto es, lo cobrado cubre primero la habitación y después los extras: es la convención que ya usaba paymentState para distinguir "falta cobrar la habitación" de "la habitación está paga, faltan los consumos", y tenerla en un solo lugar evita que las dos respuestas se contradigan.

Con la habitación ya cubierta el cupón no tiene sobre qué caer, y eso ahora se dice: antes el código contestaba "código aplicado" y no movía un peso, y el recepcionista se quedaba esperando un descuento que no iba a llegar. En el resumen del cobro, cuando hay consumos, queda escrito sobre qué se aplicó: si no, el número descontado no es el porcentaje del monto de arriba y se lee como un error de cálculo.

El diálogo recibe la cuenta entera en vez del saldo suelto. Separar la habitación de los consumos es exactamente lo que no se podía hacer con un solo número, y el saldo sale de ahí.

body:
## 요약

사용자 지시("재기동 후 확인하고 잘되면 승인")에 따라 `docs/tasks/2026-09-14.md`의 **사이클 계측 요약 줄에 시장 세션 표기** 항목을 `[R]` → `[x]`로 마감한다. 구현은 [#130](https://github.com/CarpediemBDev/stockAuto/pull/130)(`661dda0`)로 이미 main에 있다. 코드 변경은 없다.

## 운영 확인

#130 병합 후 **05:25:13 KST** 백엔드 재기동. 첫 사이클에서 새 형식이 NY 장후 시간대와 일치하게 기록됐다.

```
[Cycle] Duration: 1022.8s (session=AFTER_HOURS)
[Cycle] Profile (session=AFTER_HOURS, 97 users, 1022.8s): …
```

## 인수인계에 남긴 단서

같은 요약에서 `cycle.simulated_unfilled_orders`가 **933.5s(사이클의 91%)**, `cycle.user_flows_wall`은 **89.2s**였다. 사용자 흐름을 시작하기 전에 97명분 모의 미체결 주문을 동기로 순회하는 구간이 사이클 회귀의 유력 후보다.

**다만 재기동 직후 워밍업 사이클 1건이라 결론이 아니다.** NY 정규장(`session=REGULAR_MARKET`) 표본으로 재확인해야 한다.

author: jumplink
body:
An `accessibility { }` block in a GtkBuilder or Blueprint file is typed by GTK's ARIA
table, not by the widget's ParamSpecs, and the two disagree.
`Gtk.Label { accessibility { orientation: vertical; } }` is legal and means the number 1
although `GtkLabel` implements no `GtkOrientable` and has no such property; `checked: true`
is a `GtkAccessibleTristate`, so it means 1 and not the boolean. A consumer typing those
slots from the vocabulary it already had got both wrong, silently.

The NAME half was already here: `ENUM_NICKS` lists every member of `GtkAccessibleProperty`,
`GtkAccessibleRelation` and `GtkAccessibleState`. Only the VALUE TYPE was missing, and the
received wisdom is that it lives solely in C, inside `gtk_accessible_property_init_value()`.
That is true of the FUNCTION and false of the table: each member documents its own value
type in its own doc string. So this is a read, not a derivation.

## What was measured

Two GIR files, independently:

| GIR | version | members | with `Value type:` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/usr/share/gir-1.0/Gtk-4.0.gir` | gtk4-devel-4.22.4-1.fc44.x86_64 | 53 | 52 |
| `girs/Gtk-4.0.gir` (what generation reads) | gtk4 4.23.3, GNOME 51 beta | 53 | 52 |

Both agree on all 53 — Property 20, Relation 24, State 9. The emitted table was generated
from `girs/Gtk-4.0.gir`.

Across the whole 718-GIR corpus in `girs/` the sentence appears on exactly those 52 members
and nowhere else, and only `Gtk-4.0.gir` declares any of the three enums. Six token shapes
occur: `string` (9), `integer` (9), `double` (3), `boolean` (11), `reference` (14) and five
`[enum@…]` links — to `GtkOrientation`, `GtkAccessibleAutocomplete`, `GtkAccessibleSort`,
`GtkAccessibleTristate` and `GtkAccessibleInvalidState`, all declared by Gtk-4.0 itself, so
every join lands in the same vocabulary.

Four members punish the obvious reading, which is why the capture takes the leading token
and strips a sentence-final period: `key-shortcuts` continues its sentence
(`string. The format of the value is…`); `expanded` and `selected` add `or undefined`, with
a line break in between because GTK wraps the doc; `pressed` adds the word `enumeration`;
`hidden` follows with a whole `See also:` line. A rest-of-the-line capture reads
`string. The format of the value is a` — measured, not imagined.

## The table

Two exports per vocabulary, keyed `<enum GType>.<nick>` the way `ENUM_VALUES` is, because
the ARIA names ARE enum members and one key parser reads both:

```js
ARIA_VALUE_TYPES['GtkAccessibleState.checked']  // 'enum'
ARIA_VALUE_ENUMS['GtkAccessibleState.checked']  // 'GtkAccessibleTristate'
ENUM_VALUES['GtkAccessibleTristate.true']       // 1
```

`AriaValueType` is a closed union of six: `string | integer | double | boolean | reference
| enum`. Two tables rather than one, the way `PROP_ENUMS` sits beside `ENUM_VALUES` — folded
together, the values would be six reserved words mixed with arbitrary GTypes and telling
them apart would be the consumer's problem.

## What the gate proves

The gate is the point, not the table. A member the generator cannot answer for fails
generation and names itself, because a missing row is indistinguishable from "GTK has no
such name" and the fallback a consumer reaches for next emits `true` where GTK means 1.
`tests/widget-vocabulary` grows three controls that must go the other way, on top of the
three it had:

- an ARIA member whose doc states no value type and no declared exception covers →
  `GtkAccessibleProperty.label: documentation states no value type`
- a declared exception that is no longer needed →
  `declared ARIA exception GtkAccessibleState.busy is no longer needed — its documentation
  now states a value type`
- `noComments` with `widgetVocabulary` → refused naming the flag, rather than emitting an
  empty table, because documentation is the only source these types have

The one member GIR does not answer for — `GtkAccessibleState.busy`, whose prose says "This
state has boolean values" — is a DECLARED exception carrying its reason, never an `if` in
the emitter. It is checked in both directions: the member must still exist and must still
lack the sentence, so the list cannot only grow. Reading `busy` out of its prose was
considered and refused: that phrasing occurs once in 718 GIRs, which is an instance and not
a convention.

Each of the three controls was broken on purpose and confirmed to report:

1. turning the refusal into a silent `continue` →
   `an ARIA member whose documentation states no value type: generated successfully`
2. capturing the rest of the line instead of the leading token →
   `GtkAccessibleProperty.key-shortcuts: value type "string. The format of the value is a"
   is not understood`
3. deleting the staleness check →
   `a declared ARIA exception that is no longer needed: generated successfully`

## What the gate deliberately does NOT prove

It does not check the table against a running GTK. The generator emits headlessly, so
whether `GtkAccessibleState.checked` really is a tristate at runtime is a question only a
consumer with a GTK installed can ask — which is why the facts ship as runtime data at all.
It also does not cover a `[enum@…]` link into ANOTHER namespace: today there is none, and
one would be refused by name rather than emitted as a key that joins to nothing.

Three enums are named by GType rather than detected. Detecting them ("any enum whose members
carry the sentence") is a subject that shrinks silently. A namespace declaring some of them
but not all is refused, so renaming one upstream cannot quietly cost a third of the table.

## Verification

- full 705-namespace run: exit 0; all 142 emitted vocabularies carry both exports, exactly
  one — `gtk-4.0` — is non-empty, with 53 rows and 6 enum joins
- walking `ARIA_VALUE_TYPES -> ARIA_VALUE_ENUMS -> ENUM_VALUES` resolves
  `orientation: vertical`, `checked: true` and `autocomplete: inline` to 1, which is what
  blueprint-compiler 0.20.4 emits for all three
- `gjsify run check` (lint, app, girs, pm, prereqs, docs, closure), `gjsify run test:tests`,
  `gjsify format` — all clean
- the emitted `.d.ts` compiles: `tsc --project` on the generated `mini-1.0` fixture package
  and on the real `gtk-4.0` package from the full run

## Notes

No example was added. AGENTS.md requires one for every type-generation PR, and the reason is
that an example exercises a previously-broken construct both at compile time and under GJS.
Nothing about the emitted TYPES changed here: this adds vocabulary DATA next to `ENUM_VALUES`
and `PROP_ENUMS`, and the two PRs that added those (#465, #467) added no example either. The
regression coverage that fits this shape is the gate, which reads both halves of the subpath
and has six controls that must go red.

`gjsify format` rewrote 125 files it had never formatted; those were reverted and are not in
this diff. Two previously-unformatted lines inside `assert.mjs` are, since the file is
already heavily edited here and leaving them sets the same trap for the next contributor.

body:
## Summary

Second-pass correctness/safety review: six hypotheses from the README/REVIEW.md docs were investigated against the actual source before changing anything. Two confirmed bugs, one real gap, one documentation-only disclosure, and two items that were already correct (now pinned with regression tests). No new services, frameworks, dependencies, or fuzzy/ML matching — all fixes are deterministic and fail-explicit, matching the existing architecture. Minimal diffs only.

## Findings and changes

| # | Finding in the actual code | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Confirmed bug.** A forced VAD/ASR-cap split (`"سی و" \| "پنج"`) was indistinguishable from a natural endpoint and each half parsed as a complete wrong value (`"30 و"` + `"5"`). `VADEvent` carried no forced flag; the pipeline treated every END identically | Forced cuts are tagged end to end (`VADEvent.forced` → `on_speech_end(duration, forced)` → engine queue item → `pipeline.end_utterance(forced=)`; ASR window resets count as forced too). New pure helpers `fa_numbers.open_number_tail` / `leading_number_span`: the boundary-spanning open phrase stays unparsed with a visible warning and a `forced_splits` counter, instead of completing into digits. Natural endpoints keep the documented per-utterance behavior; the residual "cut between two complete halves" case stays disclosed as undecidable without context |
| 2 | **Confirmed unenforced.** `commit_on_endpoint=false` (early-commit legacy mode) had no enforcement — only README wording — so it could run with injection or clinical persistence active | Hard startup refusal in `ShenavaApp.__init__` (`ValueError` → readable `error:` + exit 1), same fail-explicit pattern as the `require_streaming` / local-checkpoint checks. The mode still loads when no medical output path is configured |
| 3 | **Confirmed absent by design.** Crash/kill between injection and clinical persistence has no reconciliation on restart — `ClinicalWorker` is append-only, the injector keeps no journal, nothing replays or back-fills | Documented as an explicit accepted risk in README (clinical section) and `docs/REVIEW.md`, matching the existing disclosure style. No reconciliation system built |
| 4 | **Half-validated.** `--right-context` values outside `{0,1,6,13}` were already rejected at config load, but a *metadata*-unsupported yet set-valid value silently degraded to endpoint-only decoding with a warning | `NeMoASR._check_streaming_context` now fails at startup (`RuntimeError` listing the encoder's supported contexts) when a streaming-capable encoder lacks `[70, right_context]` — same "fail before the model stack does real work" pattern. Only checkpoints with no native streaming support at all keep the documented endpoint-only fallback |
| 5 | **Already correct.** `PostProcessor(extra_terms=...)` conflicts raise at construction time (`build_rewriter` → `TrieFST.add` during `__init__`), not lazily on first match | No source change. Added a regression pin: conflicting extra terms (against each other and against the built-in tables) raise `ValueError` at construction; an identical restatement is not a conflict |
| 6 | **Confirmed absent.** No dropout detection: the capture consumer blocked forever on `queue.get()`, so a silent/disconnected mic stalled the app silently (distinct from queue overflow, which was handled) | Capture heartbeat: the consumer polls with a timeout (`AudioConfig.dropout_timeout_s`, default 2 s, validated in `__post_init__`). A stall reports once per episode as a logged error plus `dropouts` / `last_error` statistics; an inactive stream reports immediately; an open utterance is aborted through the existing discontinuity path; recovery is logged when blocks resume; paused/stopping/closed states never false-positive |

Full table also appended to `docs/REVIEW.md` (existing entries untouched).

## Test plan

- [x] Before changes: `pytest -q` — 245 passed; `python main.py --self-test` emits `بیمار دوز 2.5 mg` and extracts the 2.5 mg measurement
- [x] After changes: `pytest -q` — **283 passed** (38 new regression tests; 3 existing test callbacks updated for the `forced` flag signature)
- [x] `python main.py --self-test` passes unchanged after the changes
- [x] `python -m compileall` and `git diff --check` pass
- [x] CLI-level check: early-commit + injection config exits 1 with the readable refusal message; `dropout_timeout_s` survives the JSON config round-trip
- [x] Real checkpoint/microphone tests: not run (no local weights/NeMo in this environment), consistent with the existing verification notes

body:
## Resultado final — pronto para revisão, sem deploy

[CI 34895993228](https://github.com/wpd159/topsv3/actions/runs/34895993228), tentativa 1, evento `pull_request`: **SUCCESS**, três jobs aprovados. Head `76c8d5edf4596e4923bfa79dcd0794dfda5177cc`; pai `e89d7ace8245da1a431e4e47d241dab3a66489fd`, filho da base `b7938731e545a7a64315f14e6167f199019ac506`. Checkout sintético `5014e3f9bb253b7a9ec6098f4422d99176081222`, pais base/head e árvore `22843e477bb867cd20d18b75787762ed31c75a87`, igual à candidata.

- Operação Linux: 41 testes Python, nove gates completos e 13 cenários de containers aprovados, sem skips. Reproduzido bloqueio da sequência antiga; callback HTTP real na fixture, ativação e recuperação aprovados; falha real de saúde rejeitada com erro original preservado. Cleanup `exit=0`, somente recursos próprios.
- Backend: 1.876 testes, zero falhas/erros, 29 skips opt-in preexistentes; suítes essenciais sem skips. Três JVMs frias e APPLY sintético não root aprovados.
- Frontend: auditorias, lint, TypeScript, build e regressões de navegador aprovados. Origem 451 Spring: recusa segura aprovada, sem escrita/storage real.
- Cinco uploads concluídos, não expirados: backend `10368432559`, preview não root `10369161373`, navegador `10368682263`, origem 451 `10368847071`, operação `10370497050`.

Worktree limpo; main local e demais worktrees preservados. Diff consolidado: sete arquivos, 189 inserções/22 exclusões; SHA256 `3D39A226BF508987751458B8AB6D8983A28FDED1E782DC8A0C8ED80987C3F9EB`. Logs e diff em `tops-startup-callback-20260914`, no TEMP local. Sem acesso ou mutação produtiva nesta tarefa.

## Correção focal

Resolve o ciclo de partida observado na ativação/recuperação: o registro do webhook depende do callback pelo gateway, enquanto um `compose up` conjunto aguardava o backend saudável antes de iniciar frontend/gateway.

Ativação e recuperação passam a iniciar backend → frontend → gateway por chamadas individuais, supervisionadas por `op_run`, com `--no-deps --force-recreate --no-build --pull never`. Não há alteração do Compose nem de snapshots/configurações de releases antigas. O smoke e as verificações finais continuam decidindo a aprovação; a janela de recuperação permanece em 300 segundos.

Preservados: Pix/registro automático, mTLS/autenticação, healthchecks, imagem física, mutex, journal, pending, regras de mídia e banco. Sem retry novo da aplicação, tratamento especial de HTTP400 ou aumento de timeouts. Isto não promete zero erro transitório durante a substituição dos serviços.

## Validação

- Local: sintaxe Bash, 249 checks do contrato PowerShell e contrato Node de saúde aprovados.
- Teste de stdin: assertions focais de ordem/supervisão passaram; execução completa no Windows parou em `install: cannot change permissions` de um diretório TEMP sintético. A suíte integral passou no CI Linux, sem contorno de permissões.
- Fixture operacional existente ampliada com `startup_callback` e `startup_callback_health_failure`: sequência antiga negativa, callback HTTP sintético atravessando o gateway, ativação e recuperação da base main-v1, falha real de saúde recusada. Os 11 cenários anteriores permanecem obrigatórios.
- Prova com containers reais: executada e aprovada no CI Ubuntu deste PR. Usa Node e callback sintéticos, não Efí/Spring produtivos; não representa validação em produção.

### Resultado da primeira candidata e delta focal

O run `34894739650` passou backend/frontend e origem Spring, mas reprovou o novo cenário operacional. Comprovou a sequência antiga bloqueada (backend unhealthy; frontend/gateway parados) e a partida inicial corrigida; a substituição seguinte esgotou a espera sintética do callback. A fixture Node PID 1 não tratava SIGTERM e o log mostrou parada de aproximadamente 10 segundos por processo; duas dessas esperas podem esgotar o laço de 100 × 200 ms antes da nova geração do gateway.

O commit `76c8d5edf4596e4923bfa79dcd0794dfda5177cc`, filho de `e89d7ace8245da1a431e4e47d241dab3a66489fd`, altera somente a fixture: trata SIGTERM nos dois cenários novos e preserva diagnóstico focal antes do cleanup em caso de falha. Não muda tentativas, intervalos, deadline de observação, assertions ou produção. A validação local do algoritmo extraído confirmou esgotamento em 20,837 s para disponibilidade modelada a 21 s; disponibilidade a 1 s foi aceita em 1,033 s. O handler fechou um servidor HTTP local; essa prova Windows não foi apresentada como prova Linux/PID 1.

Novo CI automático: https://github.com/wpd159/topsv3/actions/runs/34895993228 — SUCCESS. Sem rerun da candidata anterior. Logs anteriores preservados.

## Escopo e revisão

Base: `b7938731e545a7a64315f14e6167f199019ac506`, main remota conferida. Sete caminhos alterados: workflow de produção, helper de operação, fixture existente, três contratos diretamente afetados e um parágrafo do procedimento.

Mestre v1.0.0 lido integralmente e preservado, SHA256 `E381E31C2C599F8210042C15EABC25F218480FE73A38B67B29F9C67B037607DB`; tarefa compatível, sem mudança de SEO. Diagnóstico/evidências da recuperação anterior reutilizados, sem nova consulta produtiva.

PR em rascunho para revisão. Sem merge, dispatch, deploy, reinício produtivo, banco, backfill ou alteração de anúncios/fotos. Reversão do código por commit normal restauraria o comportamento anterior, incluindo o bloqueio conhecido; não constitui procedimento de recuperação produtiva.

## Correcciones de revisión (A.4r1, commit a3ddc7f)

- **Item 1 (CodeRabbit, mayor):** la rama de reintento de `_reconcilia_negativas` (ausente → POST → ack con id) también aprende: helper `_aprende_negative(conn, entidad, term, decision_id, platform)` llamado dentro del sello en las dos ramas que confirman `applied` (spec, decisión 5: todo negative aplicado en campaña de grupo; el "ausente/reintento no escribe" del brief era un error reconocido en revisión). Test ausente invertido a aprende (verificado que cae contra `dff25a8`); `ack_sin_id`, `ack_con_error`, señuelo, tope y ancestro siguen en cero filas.
- **Item 2:** esta descripción decía nota `ok|biblioteca_no_escrita` en el ledger; lo veraz es opción (b) — corregido en "Rastro durable" y "Fallo inyectado" arriba.
