body:
`packetMarkGeometry.ts` carries a line for each of the driver's twenty-two places — page, `x1`, `x2`,
`y` in page points — plus how the entry was established and what the page looks like.

### ⚠ A heuristic came first, and it is in the plan rather than the code

The model it found is real: the label's offset to its rule is cleanly bimodal, **−3** where the label
sits above its own underline and **+11** where it sits below the line as a caption. It still put four
marks on **21pt segments**, which are date boxes.

What kills it is that **the same geometry means opposite things on different pages**:

| | |
|---|---|
| **p13** `Signature of applicant` | caption **under** its line → the line above is the one to sign |
| **p25** `Driver/Owner Signature` | caption **boxed** by two short rules → the line to sign is the long one to its **right** |

Both are "a label with a rule above it". A rule separating them is a rule fitted to two examples, on a
document people sign.

### So every entry was looked at

Each candidate rule drawn onto the carrier's own page in colour, rasterised with `pdftoppm -r 85`, and
inspected. **Sixteen seen that way; six taken from a page whose layout is identical to one that was**
(p06/p09←p05, p19a/p19b←p18 & p20, p26←p25, p28←p27) — and the test pins that list **by name**, so a
later entry cannot quietly join it without somebody deciding it is true.

The packet uses at least four layouts for the same act:

| pages | the line to sign |
|---|---|
| p03, p18, p19, p20 | the long segment right of a boxed label |
| p13, p15, p17, p22, p31 | the line above the caption |
| p10, p25, p26 | the long line to the right, at the lower rule's y |
| p04 | signature and date **share one full-width rule** — its left portion |

⚠ **p04 is the one entry whose `x2` is not a rule's own end**, so it is excluded from the generic
assertion **by name** (not by a filter that could quietly grow) and carries its own: the rule must
contain the span, and the span must stop before the `Date` caption at x311.

### What the test can and cannot do — said in the file

It asserts every recorded line **exists in the template at that position**, so a re-export that moves
the carrier's paper fails the build rather than moving somebody's signature onto the printed text
beneath it. **It cannot check that the right line was chosen** — that is a judgement about a form, and
a test can hold a chosen line still but cannot choose one.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| nudge p20's line 4pt | `no rule near x 154..412 y 351.7 on p20` |
| revert p13 to the heuristic's pick | `p13 is 21pt wide: expected 21 to be greater than 28` |
| give p11b the same line as p11a | `p11a vs p11b: expected 0 to be greater than 20` |
| let p04 run over the Date caption | `expected 553 to be less than 310.8` |

⚠ The width guard (>28pt) is what catches the heuristic's own failure mode.

### Verification

28 assertions against the real document. All gates · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` green. No
migration, no runtime change — this is a table and its guard.

**Next:** draw the marks and field values onto the template with `pdf-lib`, and wire `renderPacket`
into `file.ts`. The geometry is no longer the blocker.

Adds `mnist/submissions/small-adam-nr-k8-20260912/` and one row to the MNIST-small (67%) table.

## Headline metrics

| Accuracy | Model time (ms) | Model energy (mJ) | Area (mm^2) | Time to score (s) | A100 time (ms) | A100 energy (mJ) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 67.35% (7,409/11,000) | 1,800 | 0.19 | 0.032 | 0.12 | 110 | 2,600 |

Rounded costs use two significant figures; exact values (1,798.760521 ms, 0.185228620462 mJ, 32,088 occupied cells = 0.032088 mm^2, 0.123 s, 106.9 ms, 2,560.3 mJ) are in the submission JSONs. Grid-model costs are provisional pending review of the scorer extension. Report: `mnist/submissions/small-adam-nr-k8-20260912/README.md`.

**Result:** 7,409/11,000 = 67.35% +/- 1.76 pp (sample SD) over the 11 draws (seeds 20261201-211), meeting the 67% target (7,370). Two-phase freeze/score evidence: predictions hashed before any evaluation-label slice was opened; per-draw seeds, indices and input hashes included; all 11 draws re-verified on GPU against the frozen predictions (params/scores/predictions bitwise-equal to the ordered CPU reference).

**Costs:** A100 2,560 mJ / 107 ms (median of 3, two sessions retained). Grid 0.185228620462 mJ / 1,798.760521 ms.

**Review request (merge condition):** this PR adds an Adam optimizer path to the grid scorer (SGD path reproduces the official score exactly, byte-identical program). Grid columns are provisional pending review of the Adam pricing: state initialization, bias correction, Newton-Raphson sqrt arithmetic (existing ISA ops only) and memory/tape accounting.

**Disclosure:** the A100 advantage over the published H32 row is largely the fused runtime; a same-container interleave measures the H32 learner at 44.5 ms / 1,062 mJ vs 106.9 ms / 2,424 mJ for this entry. No accuracy-superiority claim is made (+0.27 pp; +/-1.76 pp is a sample SD). Reproduce from the submission directory: `python run.py prepare/freeze/score`, `python verify.py`, `modal run gpu_benchmark.py`.

## Summary
Production-quality **StandOut** CV builder — guided + quick paths, privacy-first, live A4 preview, real PDF export.

### Core product
- **Two paths:** Quick (pick purpose/style/photo) + Guided (5 plain-language questions, always “I'm not sure”)
- **Recommendation engine** (`purpose × industry × experience × submission × style → template + warning`)
- **9 polished templates:** Classic, Executive, Modern Split, Contemporary, Creative Portfolio, Editorial, Academic Classic, Graduate, Professional Photo — shared data model, switch without re-typing
- **Conditional multi-step editor:** Goal → Personal → About → Education → Experience → Projects → Skills → More → Photo → Design; empty sections omitted, add/edit/delete/reorder
- **Photo:** upload <3MB, 4 styles, remove, honest guidance + ATS-photo warning
- **Live preview:** desktop split / mobile tabs, A4 scaled, `break-inside: avoid`, pill zoom controls
- **PDF:** `window.print()` + `@media print` / `@page A4` → selectable text, proper margins, no clip
- **Privacy-first:** client-only, `localStorage` (`standout:cv:v1`), no account, copy backup JSON
- **A11y + responsive:** labels, focus, keyboard, 44px targets, reduced-motion, mobile preview scaling
- **SEO:** semantic HTML, meta/OG/canonical, JSON-LD `WebApplication`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`

### Design — warm editorial refresh (Manus-inspired)
Inspired by `awesome-design-md`, `GeeQR`, and the **Manus/Candid** warm-paper reference:
- **Tokens:** `bg #fdfcfa`, `surface-2 #f7f3ee`, `border #e7e0d6`, ink `#12213a` + terracotta `#b65a2a`, softer `8/12/16/22` radii, warm shadows + `shadow-paper`, radial paper glow

- **Docs:** `DESIGN.md` documents warm direction, `index.html`/`favicon`/`og-image` warmed

### Tech
React 18 + Vite 5 + React Router 6 (HashRouter for GH Pages), modern CSS tokens, no UI framework, static deploy (`dist/`) via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`

- `npm run build` passes (33.38 kB CSS, 281.89 kB JS)
- `npm test` smoke passes
- `npm run dev` live on `0.0.0.0:5173` (allowedHosts)
- Tested scenarios: student no-exp, experienced, healthcare photo, scholarship, freelance, ATS vs creative, mobile

`arena/01a0a217-standout` → `main` — ready for Pages deploy.

author: sawyerhood
body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

Since #3325, `mergeLoadedTimelineWithLatest` replaces every loaded row whenever the latest page's `historySnapshot` changes, and the snapshot includes `maxSeq`, so each appended event unloads all older pages. When the previous conversation group is larger than the 1,500-event latest-page budget, it exists only on an older page. While a thread streams, each event removes it, the "Loading older messages" sentinel scrolls back into view, auto-load fetches it again, and the next event removes it again. The controller also discarded an older page still in flight whenever the snapshot moved. Separately, a page's older cursor used the group's first displayed row. Rows recorded after a request but displayed above its message, such as "Provider environment resolved", formed their own group with a higher sequence, so the first older request re-served the current group and merging it moved that row below the reply.

## What changed

- `packages/client-core` `mergeLoadedTimelineWithLatest`: when a new latest snapshot reaches the loaded tip, loaded older pages stay and only the rows the latest page covers are replaced. It still rebuilds from the latest page when the pages do not line up, when they share no rows and leave a gap, or when the server reports a later change to a row the page omitted. On a cursor tie it keeps the walk's cursor. `prependOlderTimelineRows` keeps the loaded order when an older page repeats loaded rows.
- `useThreadTimelineController`: an in-flight older page is applied when its request cursor is still the loaded `olderCursor`, instead of requiring an unchanged snapshot.
- `apps/server` pagination: new `timelinePage.olderRowsSourceSeqEnd`, the greatest `sourceSeqEnd` among rows the snapshot projected before the page's returned rows but omitted (`null` when none). That covers older conversation groups, owned groups a size cut left out, and the leaves a content cut dropped from the page's oldest group, so a command that completes before a content cut still triggers a rebuild. A row that keeps changing before a content cut therefore rebuilds on each refresh. Leading rows recorded after a group's message now join that group, and its cursor is the message row.
- `packages/server-contract`: the field is optional in `timelinePageMetadataSchema`, matching the other snapshot fields. No daemon wire change, so `HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is unchanged.
- `docs/timeline-pagination.md` describes the new rule. This relaxes #3325's "a new latest snapshot replaces loaded rows" behavior for refreshes that only append to newer rows; a later change to a row the page omitted still replaces them.
- One #3325 assertion changed in `timeline-event-budget.test.ts`. After a late append that sorts into the newest group, the merge must now equal the full canonical timeline rather than the latest page alone.

## How you verified

- New client-core merge tests: a streaming refresh keeps older pages, a tie keeps the walk cursor, a content-cut running turn keeps its head, a group starting right after the tip appends, no overlap with a gap rebuilds, a change to an omitted row rebuilds, and a repeated group keeps the loaded order. 5 of these fail against main's merge code.
- New controller test: an in-flight older page applies across refreshes that advance the snapshot, and older rows survive later refreshes.
- New server unit tests: the cursor anchors at the message row, and the rebuild value covers context-only older groups, owned groups a size cut left out, and rows before a content cut.
- Endpoint tests: walked history stays equal to the canonical timeline after an append to the newest group. A late command completion reports a rebuild both in an older group and before a content cut in the newest group; after the rebuild and reloading older pages, the rows equal the canonical timeline. The content-cut case fails with the previous pagination code.
- `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck` for `@bb/server-contract`, `@bb/client-core`, `@bb/server` and `@bb/app`, and earlier for `@bb/cli` and `@bb/mobile`.
- `pnpm exec turbo run test` for `@bb/client-core`, `@bb/server-contract`, `@bb/cli`, and `@bb/server -- test/services/threads test/provider-corpus test/routes`. The provider corpus correctness walk skipped because no corpus was available.
- App Vitest run directly for `src/components/thread/timeline`, `src/views/thread-detail` and `src/hooks/queries`, because the PWA icon check fails in this checkout.
- Browser, isolated source instance with `BB_FF_TIMELINE_WINDOW_EVENT_BUDGET=20` and real Claude Code turns sent from the composer. A MutationObserver recorded whether the previous assistant message stayed in the DOM while a follow-up streamed. With main's client merge it left and returned 8 times within about 4 seconds, and "Loading older messages" showed in 19 samples. With this change it never left over a 30-second turn.
- Replayed a real affected thread's events through the server at each of 49 consecutive sequences, feeding both clients. With main's client the previous message dropped on 49 of 49 refreshes; with this change, 0. The rebuild value stayed `null` throughout.
- The browser check ran before rebasing onto #3591, and the replay before the omitted-rows change. Tests and typechecks were rerun after both.
